Sparkling Beverage Maker is a Great Concept, But...... Carbonated beverages offer great refreshment. There is just something about the added bubbles that takes an ordinary cold beverage and makes it that much better and it isn't difficult to understand why so many people are so hooked on some of the popular soft drink brands.

So, with soft drinks tasting so refreshing, the idea of owning a small appliance that would make a great carbonated beverage tailored to one's own tastes has a definite appeal. What soft drink lover wouldn't like to create his/her own bubbly beverages? The concept is a good one and it has been done before but, unfortunately for the consumer, this Cuisinart appliance isn't as great as it first seems.

Let's start with the good aspects of the machine. It is simple to set up and use because it has only a few separate parts and it does make a good- tasting soda. You can add just a little bit of carbonation or a lot, so you can make the beverage as bubbly as you wish. Just add the carbonation, add your flavoring, and the beverage is ready to serve. The unit takes little counter space and is easy to store, too, so it is there when you need it and out of sight just as quickly.

Okay, so there are some reasons to like this appliance, but I'm afraid that the negatives are equal if not greater. For one, it should come with at least two bottles, but Cuisinart provides just a single, one- liter bottle and charges a high price to buy a second. One liter of soda doesn't last long at all in my house and that means constantly having to make more. It also doesn't make 16 bottles of soda, as it leads you to believe. Read the words carefully and you will see that the claim is that it makes up to 16 bottles. If you like your soda more carbonated like I do, then you can expect to get only about 12 bottles before you have to replace the CO2 cartridge.

And herein lies the greatest problem with this device: The cost of the replacement cartridges. At about twenty dollars a pop, with about 12 bottles created from a cartridge, the price of a single liter bottle of soda, just for the carbonation alone, is about $1.67! That's more than double the price per liter at a store and with the cost advantage eliminated, one of the greatest reasons to purchase a device like this is eliminated. Why go to so much trouble when you can get twice as much soft drink, straight from the store shelves, for the same money? I know, I know- the soft drinks you make yourself are more natural and you avoid waste because you reuse the bottles. But if the price is more than double, it is going to be difficult to convince people to make the purchase.

I like this idea in concept, but I cannot recommend the Cuisinart Sparkling Beverage Maker. The sodastream machine is better and costs less per serving, so if you really want to own a soda maker, that would be your best bet. It is nice that Cuisinart wants to help eliminate waste and help individuals consume healthier beverages, but they really need to work on the cost factor if they want this item to sell.

Nice Concept, but Manufacturing Flaw Spoiled the Party. Bars are useful when you like to entertain. I have a large backyard with a pool and spa and when we invite people over, we often need more ways to serve guests. This is when a portable bar can come in handy and this occasional need convinced me to add the 2L Lifestyle Southwood Folding Wine Cabinet Bar to our home.

With this portable bar, you get a pressed wood structure with a black finish. It features a drawer, shelf space, and a cubby hole with 9 small sections for storing bottles and other durables. It has three slots designed to hold wine glasses in a hanging fashion so they are there when you need them. The two side panels fold in and the flaps on the top fold down, making it possible to store this bar in a small space.

Everything about this portable folding wine cabinet sounds good, but there is one issue I had that forces me to lower my rating, and that is a design flaw that is going to take effort to fix. The problem is with the hinge on the right panel. It has an upper and lower stem that have to be placed into the hinges on the main cabinet and while this should be simple, the right panel has the stems facing up, not down like they should be. The left panel was manufactured properly, with the stem facing down and it fits perfectly fine. You cannot easily remove the hinges and turn them around because, while they are screwed into place, they are also apparently glued into place. It would require stripping them off, which will likely pull off the finish. And even then, if you turn the hinge around and re- fasten, it will require placing it just right so that the top of the bar fits into place.

I called the manufacturer to get a replacement piece but none are available because this product is no longer made! Lovely- now I have to decide whether I want to fix it myself, which may or may not work, or send it back in. I’m not happy with the situation, but at the same time, I did like the good customer service I received. The person on the phone tried everything to come up with a solution and I even sent him a picture so he could see what was wrong, and he admitted that this is, indeed, a manufacturing flaw. I also like how everything in the package was properly labeled. They even placed the hardware in separate, plastic bags with labels on each. This is much better than past experiences with similar products, many of which had all of the hardware mixed together in a single bag.

Portable bars are nice for those of us who entertain. The 2L Lifestyle Southwood Folding Wine Cabinet looks like a nice enough product and it would have worked out well for my home had it not been for the design flaw described above. Still, this is not something I can overlook so my advice is to purchase this at your own risk. You may get a perfectly designed product, ready to assemble and start using, or you may get a product with an obvious flaw, like I did. My experience convinces me to cut my rating to 1 or 2 stars, but I will go with 2, since the customer service rep went out of his way to try to correct the situation.

Small, Simple, but Only Produced Shakes for Me. [[VIDEOID:bb6709753499f3784cdd93e032970cd3]] My favorite snack, by far, is ice cream. This ice cream maker does make some noise, but all ice cream makers make noise and the decibel level here isn’t that bad. The mixture was still edible, but it was more like a thick shake, not the sweet, creamy ice cream I was hoping for.

I looked to this cheese slicer as a possible replacement. I would politely describe my experience with it as “disappointing”.

This is a guillotine-style slicer – it has a handle with a thin steel wire that is used to cut through the block when the handle is pressed down, making a clean, straight cut. The surface on which the cheese sits is a nice marble slab with a groove cut in it so that the wire can pass completely through the block without leaving an uncut lip.

In theory this works, and I have seen it work well in other similar slicers. However, for this particular slicer the wire is so flimsy and weak that it bends when slicing and I believe it’s a matter of time (not very long) before it breaks and I have to restring it.

Almost a Grill Pan. UPDATE 03/10/2018:
I initially rated this pan 3 stars. Having had this pan only about 5 months, large swaths of the Teflon are already coming off, and we've never scrubbed it with anything abrasive or used hard utensils in it. This is a new record (for me) for how quickly the non-stick coating comes off a treated pan. Based on this, I am dropping my rating to 1 star - stay far, far away from this pan. It's a poor product that will fail you sooner rather than later.

My original review follows.

---

I selected this pan for my wife, as she likes to use my cast-iron grill pans but she doesn’t like the clean-up afterward. I will confess that I am no fan of Teflon-coated pans, so I wasn’t too sure about this one. It has turned out to be a decent pan (if you don’t mind Teflon) but there are a couple of negatives that merit attention.

Farberware is not a high-end name in cookware, so I wasn’t expecting this to be a spectacular pan, particularly at the price. I was a bit surprised, though, when I received it – it seems to be very solid with a tightly-attached handle and it is very solidly balanced. This is a big plus, as I have had too many pans that aren’t quite flat on the bottom and as such will wobble on the burner and will heat unevenly. Being aluminum, it heats quickly and because it’s flat it seems to heat evenly. So far, so good.

Some of the other reviewers here have stated that the finish started coming off after the first washing. I have hand-washed this pan several times and so far the finish and the non-stick coating have not shown any signs of coming off. The pan is supposedly dishwasher safe; I have not tried it in the dishwasher so I do not know how well it will hold up in there.

My first issue with this pan is that the ridges aren’t really high enough to make this a proper grill pan. It does leave some grill marks when pre-heated and it does a good job of frying, but it is a poor substitute for most grilling surfaces. Because the ridges are wide and high, it does not grill foods like most other surfaces so the result is something that is more fried than grilled. That said, the ridges are high enough to allow some fats to drain away, so you will end up with moderately lower fat than straight frying, though that depends on how soft and amorphous the food you’re cooking is.

The bottom of the pan is textured and has a neat feel to it, but be careful when running your hand over it. The finer ridges on the bottom aren’t necessarily smooth and I nicked my hand when I ran it across the surface. This was an unpleasant (and unwelcome) surprise. It’s a minor point as most people are not going to make a habit of doing that, but it’s something to remember.

My wife is happy with this pan, though I am not. She has used it several times and it very pleased with how well it works for her and how easy to clean it is. I still prefer my cast iron grill pans and will continue to use them instead, even though cleanup is more work. If the goal is easy cleanup and some fat reduction, this pan is worth a look. If you want a proper grill pan, though, there are better choices available, even in the same general price range.

The one redeeming value of this cooker is that it keeps the mess contained. However, since the plastic melts so easily, there's not much motivation to use it in the first place. If the fins had been ceramic or glass, this could have been a much better product that would have cost marginally more.

Poor Quality for the Price. My past experiences with Mikasa products have been positive so I was expecting these to be good as well. Unfortunately, these fall very short, especially considering the price.

I received these packed in three nested boxes - a box inside a box inside a box, with appropriate padding to protect them. When I took them out of the box, two of the three were bent, like they has been dropped and hit on the handles before they were boxed up since the boxes in which they were packed were pristine.

I was able to bend them back into shape by hand which presents another complaint - these are very lightweight and flimsy. I've worked with galvanized steel buckets on a farm and those were darn near indestructible; these trays are much less sturdy and the fact that I can bend them up by hand without any real effort leaves questions about material. And, these certainly are not up to the same standard of other Mikasa products I have used in the past. At the price point I would expect solid, heavier trays that are not easily bent; instead, these compete with the quality of items you'd find at the local large discount department store.

I am very disappointed in these and cannot recommend them. They're functional and they're attractive, but they're poorly made.

Received a Pan Damaged Prior to Shipment. I was excited to try this 13”x9” baking pan as all of the ones I have are glass and often are more difficult to clean and maintain. A metal non-stick pan would be great! Unfortunately, the one I received was damaged. Worse, it is clear it was damaged even before it went into the packing box.

This is a nice, heavy pan that has a good non-stick finish on it. It doesn’t appear to be Teflon which is good. It should work well for things like casseroles, cakes and other recipes that call for this size baking dish.

Right out of the box, my pan was dented up. All four corners have been dented enough to be obvious in both sight and touch. The box in which it shipped was completely fine, though, which tells me that it went into the box already damaged before it was sealed and shipped. The damage was consistent with being dropped at an odd angle and under load, or having been inverted and having heave things stacked on top of it. I do not know if this occurred where it was manufactured or if instead it happened prior to retail shipment. Lack of scratch marks on the finish suggests the former.

I think I can pound it back into shape with a mallet and wooden dowel, but that’s not an acceptable solution. I should be clear, it does not impact usability, but it’s enough to impact the shape of some things baked in the pan.

I really wanted to like this pan but receiving an item that is damaged (and was likely damaged where it was manufactured) is a serious problem. I hope I am the only one who had this issue, but I cannot rate it higher based on a hope or an assumption. It’s a shame; it’s otherwise a nice baking pan.

Very Small and Doesn't Cool Well at All. I selected this mini fridge with one idea in mind - keeping a carton of creamer cold in the office, away from the kitchen so I can always be sure to have creamer for my coffee when I am in the office. I have been sorely disappointed in this unit.

It has two functions, heat and cool. I have little use for the heating function but I have tinkered with it, and it seems to work reasonably well. I have not measured the temperature, but it does keep an open cup of coffee warmer for a longer period of time and it does a reasonable job of working as a cup warmer which is a nice thing if you don't like pouring hot coffee or tea into a cold cup.

The first issue I have with it - and it's a major one - is that it just doesn't get all that cold. It does well enough to give a canned or bottled drink a slight chill but nowhere close to that of a typical refrigerator. This is all right if you don't like drinks that are really cold, but that somewhat defeats the purpose. In this case, a freezer pack in an insulated bag works better for me at cooling a bottled drink down. It is enough to raise some concern in my mind about food safety if leaving anything of consequence in this little fridge for more than a couple of hours. I certainly would not trust an open jar of mayo that was kept in this fridge overnight.

The second problem is that this fridge is too small to accommodate a quart-sized carton of cream, totally defeating the purpose for which I got it. It almost fits, but not quite. This is probably my fault for not measuring, but it's unfortunate nonetheless.

I have real difficulty recommending this little fridge. It's better than nothing I suppose, but there are better options if you're willing to spend a little more.

132Q leaves a LOT to be desired in quality. Please note - this review is for the MACHINE only, and has nothing to do with any particular seller. Seller reviews are in a separate area when you click on the seller. I just want to be clear that this is a PRODUCT review.

I have owned a couple of sewing machines now, and my mother always had Singer machines. I was pleased when I found this one for a very reasonable price, as I wanted to learn to quilt (the "Q" is for quilting on this model). I used it a grand total of four times before it broke. Now, it does a veey nice job, WHEN it works!

I was making pillows when it broke - I had stitched up 2 items, and was on my third. I'd finished the other seams, and was going back over the last seam when it caught and stopped running. Used to bobbins getting linty, I took that apart and blew out any fuzz, and tried the seam again. This time, it caught and I heard a snap. Now the entire machine was frozen up. I couldn't get it to budge, and neither could my husband. He had taken the machine to make sure all the parts were properly greased (they were - after all, it was new). I took the entire bobbin shaft out and made sure there wasn't thread caught where I couldn't see it right away - it was fine.

We took it to a sewing machine repair shop. Apparently, there is a plastic (yes, PLASTIC!!) gear that runs the bobbin gear, and it was stripped out. The thing is, they couldn't find a replacement part for it. We finally took our machine back home, unfixed. So, a grand total of maybe FOUR uses from it before it stopped working. Those are the most expensive pillows I ever made!

Of course, when I wrote to Singer, they gave me a canned reply, stating that if it was within the 90-day warranty (and it wasn't - I'd had it for a few months before I needed to sew anything), then they could help. Otherwise, take it to a repair shop. Gee thanks. This will be my last Singer. Neither the company nor the customer service is what it apparently USED to be. Maybe it is time to try a Brother machine. I also couldn't take it back to the store where I'd purchased it, because I had already used it. It would be dishonest to take it back and say it was broken, when it was working for a short while.

So, save yourself the headaches, and either get a different model, or perhaps consider a different brand. If this is the direction Singer has decided to head for home models - inexpensive low-quality parts in their machines - then choose another brand. They might also be made with lots of plastic, but it won't cost what the Singer machines cost.

UPDATE: We did order replacement parts and were able to get metal to replace the plastic. This is how Singer should have done it in the first place! I went to set it up to try and sew with it. You still need a liner! This won't do the job alone. Well, the mystery of how my daughter flooded our bathroom floor has been solved.

I bought this liner (clearly marked LINER, note) to go with a new fabric shower curtain
I had also purchased. Previously, we had just a vinyl curtain only. We have your basic bathtub - nothing
special or oversized, and we hung the liner and curtain like we always have.

First, the positives -
this curtain is beautiful - it really is. It has a light striped effect in shades of beige,
and it looks great on the hooks. It is very well made, and the weights in the bottom are exactly
what we had been looking for to keep the liner from billowing up and sticking to our soapy selves.
This is hanging on the INside of the tub, as liners should, with the new curtain on the outside of the tub.

After the first shower with the new curtains in place, we had a soaked floor, soaked rugs, etc.
We couldn't figure out what she did, and thought maybe water was hitting shampoo bottles and "leaking" out that way.
We even had blamed her for being careless with the handheld shower head.
Then I took a shower this morning.

I, too, had a flooded bathroom floor from a 10-12 minute shower. What the heck?!
I had made doubly sure that the corners/edges of the tub were covered with the liner.
Then I noticed what was really going on -

THIS LINER IS NOT WATERPROOF!
Nope - at least mine isn't!

This beautiful shower curtain "liner" should be considered a curtain ONLY.
It does not even repel water! It keeps shower spray in for a short while, but if water bounces off you and on to
the curtain, or you aim your shower head at the curtain to rinse off some soap, you will have
a soaked floor. This does NOT act like a liner at all, and in fact creates a wet mess.

Now, I know it said this was a fabric shower curtain liner, but wouldn't you think if it states
it is a LINER that it would be waterproof?!? I know I sure did! But it isn't.
At the end of my relatively short shower, my liner was soaked through, and had several places of
my new separate actual shower curtain soaked as well, and water puddled on the floor from where it dripped down
off the soaked fabric shower curtain. My rugs were soaked, as was a cardboard box of cat food packets I'd sat
on the floor, waiting to be put in the cupboard.

I've already discarded the packaging or I would return it. This is pitiful!
I like how the weights keep the curtain down in the tub, so my plan is to get a REAL liner that is
actually waterproof, and add it to the rings INBETWEEN the new curtain and this fabric liner.

Seriously - this was so disappointing! I really thought anything that called itself a liner
would act like one, but I was very wrong. I gave it two stars ONLY because it is very well made.

I would advise anyone thinking about getting this item (in any color) that they should consider it to be
ONLY a curtain, and to use a vinyl liner of some sort with it. It will keep someone from seeing you
"nekkid", but that is all it will do. It is not water repellant or water proof.

Just goes to show you that beauty does not mean brains - this looks a lot better than it works!

Very glad we bought it at the time. I wasn't really sure what to expect with this little heater.
We have an upstairs bedroom in a rental place (where we can't do major changes), and it
is very chilly in the winter. Add wind, and it gets freaky cold inside! We've actually had
ice on the closet walls before.

So, I wanted to get a small space heater that wouldn't require us running the central heat
if only our bedroom was cold.

This little guy does the job very well.
I don't find the noise annoying - it is like a computer running, with slight magnification.
It is not as noisy as a fan. I don't mind it a bit, and it can be like white noise, blocking
out other small annoyances.

This is so completely adjustable, it makes it great.
I've used both the high and low power settings, and don't see a huge difference between them.
I guess the high technically heats up faster, but again, I didn't really notice.
The other dial is how warm you want the air to be that comes out.
I've used it on many of the settings so far. Yesterday, for example, had 30-40 mph winds here
and it was very cold in the bedroom - cold enough I had a hard time sewing something by hand!
I put the little heater aimed at my desk, and within 1/2 hr, the room was very comfortable.
The room is about 12' x 10'. By the time my daughter got home from school, it was too hot,
and we had to turn it off for a while!

All in all, I'm very happy with it. We bought two different kinds, one for downstairs and one
for upstairs, to try to cut back on our utility bill. The other brand works just fine too, but
I think this one is a little better! : )

All in all, I would definitely recommend it. It won't heat a 2-story house, but it does 2 or 3 rooms
to a pleasant temperature (I don't like it super hot anyway, but it gets to 72 pretty easily) very well.
Upstairs, we have two bedrooms and a small bathroom. I can put this in the hallway, and, although it
takes a little longer, will have the upstairs comfortably warm in an hour or so. The bedroom alone
with the heater in the room takes much less time. I've even had it near the desk when my hands
were freezing while typing!

Not sure how great the fan alone will be - I'll try that when it gets stuffy some day.
But I bought it for heating, and it does exactly what it says, and does it well.
Very pleased with the purchase.

UPDATE:

Well, we had our first problem with the heater today!
We have used it probably ten times this winter, and it has done a wonderful job of warming
the bedroom/hall area. HOWEVER - today, March 29, we went to unplug the heater and box it
back up for next winter's use. This is where the problem began!

I tried to unplug the heater, and couldn't do it! I tried and failed, tried the other hand and failed.
When my son got home, had HIM try and he failed! It took the two of us to get the heater disconnected
from the plug, and when we finally did, the prongs came out of the plug!! OMG.
Well, THAT was an interesting development!

I checked on the website, and the heater has a one-year warranty on parts. So, I contacted
Lasko via their customer care center, and we'll see what they will do about it!
I could hardly believe it! We've had it plugged in since December, so around three months,
but I really don't think that's long enough to create a stuck plug problem!
I'll update about how Lasko customer service is once I hear back, and we find a resolution to the problem.

Until then - unplug carefully! You can see the glue on the end of the plug on ours!

UPDATE:
No response from Lasko yet, so it is looking like I'll be buying another brand
of small space heater for next winter. What a shame. I really did like this one.
My husband has another brand, however, that did equally well at heating the room.

oversight. I've had it too long to ask Amazon to handle the problem - it isn't their fault
the plug was faulty - but sure wish I could send it back for a replacement!
I am dinging it one star both because of the plug, and because of the lack of support over
a product that was only a few months old and allegedly still under warranty.

UPDATE OCT 2013:
Here it is, late 2013, and Lasko never bothered to respond to our concerns.
The heater has been sitting in the hallway since the plug pulled out several months ago.
Now that winter is getting closer again, I am back on Amazon, looking for another heater.
It will NOT be this one - it worked like a champ, UNTIL we needed to unplug it!
Note that it is STILL UNDER WARRANTY, and they won't respond to the problem.

What the worst part was was Lasko ignoring our request entirely. No replacement heater,
replacement cord, credit towards another one, nothing at all.
So, we will be looking at other brands. Most have similar wattages now, so there is no
reason to be brand loyal, when they didn't care a bit about us.

This Vacuum Disappointed Me -- And Not Easy To Glide Over My Carpet As Advertised. Considering its very high price and the positives touted by Oreck in the description, I am very disappointed with this vacuum.

They claim it glides easily over carpeting, as if we are using one of those self-propelled vacuums. While it feels this way while using it over bare floors, it in no way feels like this when pushing over carpeting. In fact, it's a definite slightly strained physical push over carpeting when the power is set to high (and I have low pile carpets). It is less of a hard push when the vacuum is set to low power, but it is in no way an easy glide as advertised.

The clip to hold the cord at the top rear of the vacuum and the light at the bottom of the vacuum is a joke. The cord easily pops out of the clip with very little effort while vacuuming. And the light has almost no illumination power.

Yes, the vacuum is very light weight, the swiveling works as advertised, and the suction is very good.

Bottom Line: It's very good for bare floors and zero-pile carpets (as it's a pleasure to glide along the floors and the suction is good). But for carpets, it's way too expensive to be as disappointing as I found it.

DO NOT BELIEVE THE HYPE OR THE CLAIMS. Editing my initial review (which is still below this revision), on September 16, 2013: So, the description here at Amazon for this vacuum has been changed from "NO MESS" to "LESS MESS." Much better description, as there is plenty of mess to clean up inside the vacuum dirt collection tray area. Also, a price drop, from $350 to $299.95. Over at Brookstone's Website, the "NO MESS" description has also been removed and changed to "Less Mess." I feel the fact the "NO MESS" description has been removed validates my original review. And I thank Brookstone for coming clean (no pun intended). And for those who accused me of lacking credibility with my review because it doesn't say "Amazon Verified Purchase," I'd like to reiterate here that I purchased this vacuum direct from Brookstone and not here at Amazon because at the time of purchase Brookstone had a coupon available, which lowered the price for me a bit. I still own and use the vacuum.

Original Review:

This vacuum (at $350) is so overpriced, it is insane.

First, let me warn you: Should your $350 Gtech Airram's battery ever fail, there is no way to use the vacuum. It would just be a brick. For that much money, they should allow, just as an emergency backup, the vacuum to be used with the charging cable plugged in. But no. If the battery is drained or dead, even with the cord plugged into it, the vacuum is useless.

But the above is not why I give this vacuum 2 stars.

They claim no mess? There is mess. In fact, you might need another vacuum to clean out the mess (dirt and dust and stuff vacuumed up) that accumulates into the collection area (even immediately after first use). Yes you will! (Yes, you can grab a cloth and wipe out all that dust. You will want to and have to. The video showing how the collection area has no mess, along with the written claims of same, are utter bs.)

I bought this vacuum direct from Brookstone, and am very disappointed. I really thought that for $350, there would be no mess (or at least, a tiny amount). One big complaint about bagless vacs is the mess in the collection areas. So, Gtech, in an effort to make the cost so high, claims "lightweight, clean, and cordless...no mess." It is lightweight. It is cordless. But it ain't clean. Not in the least. And there is mess.

So, if you got a lot of extra money to spend and you want cordless, light, and powerful, buy this vacuum. But do not expect clean. The only thing "clean" about this vac is that after you open up the cover, you're gonna have to CLEAN the inside.

To summarize: This vacuum is in no way worth $350, in my opinion...and you will have to clean the dust and dirt out of the collection area (with a rag or paper towels) just like you would with any bagless. There is mess and particles to manually empty seperate from what they call the "bales of dirt." Their so called "bales" after pulled out, stuff is still stuck to the underside of the cover, which you will have to pick out with your fingers. (This vacuum is not worth anything over $180, in my opinion.)

Positive: Convenient for quick touch ups since it is cordless. Light weight. Maneuvers fine. Seems to have good suction. Noise not too loud for me.

P.S. I doubt you would want this as a primary vacuum for your home. Better for quick touch-ups.

Easily Damaged & Fragile. The mast (or "sails") is paper-like and way too fragile considering how expensive this product is. You can see from the pictures the damage/defect. I do not recommend this product at all.

I Bought Two Of These: They Both Failed. I Bought Two of these: one in February 2016 and one in December 2015. They both failed completely in about 6 months. The pump motors died. I tried several sets of batteries (testing them with a great battery tester first, to make sure the issue was not the batteries).

It is mind-boggling that in this technological age, Simplehuman cannot get this product right, especially after the countless reports of failures. (Both this model and the rechargeable model which costs $10 more have so many reports of failures in a relatively short time.)

Yet Another Product With Bad Adhesive Residue Left Behind From Their Label. As everyone knows, One Star on Amazon equates to the feeling of "I Hate It."

They put a sticker on the long metal vertical front "wire rod" that is so difficult to remove, and that left two inches of terrible crap and sticky residue behind! (And I hate it!) There is no reason whatsoever this has to occur in 2016! They make adhesive that leaves behind no residue. For $50+ for this item, this company can afford labels that leave behind no residue. But let's say they do not wanna spend the extra money for the residue-free adhesive for their stickers. They could put a tag on it that is attached to string or plastic tie you simply cut off.

(And I bet when they ship this during a heatwave, it can make the adhesive issue even worse.)

Yes, I know full well I can buy that goof-off stuff to assist in trying to remove the crud. But I just spent enough money buying the rack. Why do I have to spend more money buying a crud remover, and then have to spend time scraping and rubbing?

Regarding the rack: I am disappointed the left and right sections, which swing in and out, have no locking mechanism to keep the arms open in one spot without them moving at the slightest touch, for folks who might not wanna screw down the base into a countertop (especially people at home who might wanna use this product).

Poorly designed, in my opinion.

I only recommend this item for folks who will screw it down into a counter, and who do not mind having to spend time and effort scraping off two inches of adhesive residue.

Also, this item is overpriced, in my opinion.

Heavy Perfume-Like Smell Right Out of the Package. Oh my gosh, I am not exaggerating. As soon as I opened up the package I was hit with a strong perfume smell from the product. Maybe perfume combined with laundry detergent smell. The scent permeated the entire room. I kid you not. It was so powerful, so annoying, and so unnecessary.

I couldn't take it. And because Amazon would have just said wash the darn thing to get the smell out, I would have had to pay the shipping to return it.

I was so disappointed and upset that this company would perfume the mattress cover, and because the smell was overwhelming me, I just immediately threw it away in the outside garbage bin.

I have no idea why this company would think people want a heavily perfumed mattress pad, especially knowing there are many people sensitive to smells. (The scent was making me cough.)

I Did Not Like This Blanket At All. I Did Not Like the following:

The size was way off with the dimensions seemingly reversed. The sides were way too long, and the length from head to too way too short.

The Satin trim at the top edge felt cheap, and not a nice feeling on the underside.

The blanket did not feel as soft and cozy as expected.

I decided not to use it immediately.

I absolutely do not recommend this blanket.
Painful to Open. It hurts my fingers to open up the lid. Terrible design. I do not recommend this bottle because of its lid mechanism.

It's a Thicker/Denser Norwex Towel But Without the BacLock Antibacterial Silver. This so-called "bath mat" is just a thicker and denser Norwex microfiber towel made of the exact same 70% Polyester and 30% Polyamide as the Norwex bath towels.

The Norwex bath towels, however, also have what Norwex calls "BacLock" (which they say is silver that makes the towels antibacterial). But for some reason, Norwex decided not to put this same BacLock in what they're selling as bath mats, even though the bath mats are as expensive as the larger bath towels. I find this to be unacceptable and quite disappointing.

Who wouldn't want the Norwex bath mats to be as antibacterial as the Norwex towels? I certainly would.

Norwex's big selling point for their towel products is that they are antibacterial with the addition of what they are calling "BacLock" (you'll see the word "BacLock" on the tag sewed into the towels). I expected this microfiber bath mat to include the BacLock since it's made from the same exact 70% Polyester and 30% Polyamide material.

This so-called bath mat is soft and it does absorb water well. I would have given it 5 stars had it contained the Norwex BacLock.

This bath mat is absolutely not worth the $38 I paid for it since it does not include the Norwex BacLock silver antibacterial protection.

Very Thin. First, they advertise here at Amazon that this towel is "As soft and silky as cashmere" ... this is just not true. Rub your hand back and forth over the side with the color and maybe you will agree with me that it is not as soft and silky as cashmere.

Second, this towel is extremely thin. Disappointingly thin. And while it absorbs okay, it does not absorb nearly as well as some other cotton towels, keeping in mind this towel's very high price.

3 Quarts of Water Taking 17 Minutes To Mildly Boil Is Not What I'd Call Fast. I used a "Duxtop Whole-Clad Tri-Ply Stainless Steel Induction Ready Premium Cookware SaucePan" (so please do not reply with a comment that I need to make sure I am using the correct cookware, as you did with prior reviews).

It took 17 minutes to bring 3 quarts of water to a boil (the water started out at room temperature...I used bottled water that was at room temp to conduct my test). And it wasn't even a rolling boil at 17 minutes. It was a mild boil.

I was so disappointed at how long it took.

Either this product is underpowered, or the claims that induction cooking is so much faster than other methods are exaggerated.

Yes, I had the Gas One Induction Cooktop turned up all the way up to its highest settings regarding both temperature and power.

The Gas One is easy to operate and seems nicely built, but sadly I am sorry I bought it due to the fact it doesn't deliver the cooking speed I expected.

Great Concept, Horribly Executed -- Expect Your Microwave To Get Very Wet. This absolutely needs to be taller. If you put in the recommended amount of water, the water will boil over into the microwave.

Yes, I guess you could place the pasta cooker on a thick towel inside the microwave, but then the towel will get soaked, and we shouldn't have to be required to do this.

This pasta cooker is one of those great ideas that is really poorly executed. What a terrible design. Also, it is extremely difficult to see the second line, aka the water fill line. The pasta fill line is easy to see...so I cannot understand why they made the water line almost impossible to see when you are adding the water.

I absolutely do not recommend this microwave pasta cooker.

Yes, perhaps one could put in less pasta and thus much less than the recommended amount of water, but then that would give you a much smaller serving when the serving is already small even if you put the pasta up to the pasta fill line.

Does a Poor Job Straining All The Water Out of the Bottom. The holes at the bottom are too small, in my opinion. The water does not fully drain out. It is frustrating. Because the holes are so small, I cannot recommend this.

It Really Needs More Suction Power. First, to the Livion Company, please do not write a reply to my review stating that I would get more suction power out of the vacuum if I use the batteries instead of the USB cable. I never even unwrapped the USB cable. I immediately put in 4 AA batteries that I assure you have full power, as I have a high quality battery tester and I test all batteries before I use them, even fresh ones out of a sealed package.

I realize that this vacuum is only $20, but still I expected/hoped for more suction power. It makes noise like it should have decent suction power, but it does not.

Also, the way it feels in the hand is not as comfortable as I would like. It it quite wide in the rear. Perhaps it could use a handle, etc. But I could absolutely live with its awkward/uncomfy shape if the suction power was better.

Disappointing For the High Price I Paid. $139 paid for a vacuum where the tube disconnects so easily while vacuuming! Shame on Oreck for not designing this better. It is upsetting. Do they not test this stuff first before putting it out there for sale?

Unless you buy this only for use with the small attachments connected to the hose, I would recommend you look elsewhere.

Sure, it's lightweight, and suction power is good (especially when using the smaller attachments connected to just the hose).

Overpriced For A Rug So Thin. This thing is so thin, and so overpriced for what you get.

The color is nice. The feel is soft to the touch.

But it feels very cheap due to how thin it is.

Strong Lingering Bad Smell. Bad smell that just won't go away, even after owning it a month. It's a strong smell and one that really is bothersome. I took the cover off and let it air for quite a while, and the smell is still the same.

It's a nice looking pillow and the cover is soft, and it might be an effective pillow for some. But with the bad lingering strong smell, I cannot recommend it.

Frustrating Lid Closing & Pour Spout Design. As other people have stated in the reviews, the lids are frustrating to put on, where often you’re not even sure all sides are snapped closed fully, and the pour spout is very disappointing.

I am sorry I bought these, and should have listened to the negative comments.

No BacLock. For years, Norwex has advertised that their microfiber bathroom products contain BacLock, which is a trademarked name for their exclusive silver-based antibacterial agent built into Norwex's microfiber products.

Unfortunately, this Norwex Bath Mat, which is quite expensive, and which is more towel-like than mat-like, does not contain BacLock.

Ineffective! Waste of Money!. I bought these cups via their original crowdfunding campaign. Please heed my warning: These cups are awful. They absolutely will not make you think you’re drinking flavored water. I also tried both the orange and the apple. Awful. Ineffective. Waste of money. You will see lots of similar opinions over at the crowdfunding comments page.

Poor Quality - Defective & Deformed. Unfortunately, and as you can see from the photo, it is badly deformed. And the location of the deformity makes it defective. These are of poor quality, obviously way too easily damaged.

Way Overpriced. This clothing rack is way, way, way overpriced. I paid $150 for this. I would have been happy to pay it if it truly was as great as the description made it appear.

The rack is not as easy to fold back up as they state. The middle rack does not easily slide up and down, and you have to slide it all the way up to fold the rack. One end of the middle pole often gets stuck while trying to raise it back up. I wish they gave the option to just remove the middle pole for those who would never need to use it, but the middle pole cannot be removed. I think it's a pain to have to lower and raise it every time you wanna unfold and fold the rack.

To charge $150 for the materials used is outrageous, in my opinion Also, the rack is only 50 inches high when set up, so any bedding over 100 inches is gonna touch the ground. The instructions that come with it are completely in a foreign language.

Disappointing Head Cushion. I am disappointed in the head cushioning. There really isn't much cushioning when resting my head against this headboard. While the headboard looks decent, the lack of comfy cushioning makes me not recommend this.

I Love the "Bagged Cordless Vac" Concept -- Very Unhappy With The Attachments. As of the posting of this review, the cost for this vacuum here and at Oreck is $569.99. That's quite a premium for the wonderful new concept of making this kind of cordless hand vacuum with a bag (they call them "Pods") rather than the always messy and dirty and dusty collection containers. (I am surprised it took this long for someone to invent a "bagged" cordless hand vacuum...and bravo to Oreck for being the first to do it. Yes, one has to buy the replacement Pods--Oreck includes 5 with the vacuum--but they're only $15 for a 5-pack.)

While I love the bagged-cordless concept, I was disappointed with this vacuum overall, mostly having to do with attachments to be used when using it has a hand-held, and with its heavy weight, which can make it feel a bit uncomfortable rather quickly for those who are not as strong as some. (Please keep in mind that my primary use for this Oreck vac is as a handheld, and not for use as a floor vac.)

The worst attachment by far is the "Soft-Bristle Dust Brush tool. The black bristles shed immediately upon first use, and shed very badly. (And the first use was just over soft bed sheets.) The soft bristles have stretched outward/become deformed in several places, as well, and just won't stop shedding.

The second worst attachment is the small "AirPower Pivoting Brushroll Tool." The vacuum stops working when using this tool way too often and way too easily, where a red light comes on, as if the vacuum thinks the suction is being blocked. And I assure you I am not applying too much pressure when using this tool.

The Crevice Tool works as it should, but because the two release buttons are so far back, it is not the easiest to eject the tool right away, on the first attempt.

I do like that one does not have to hold the power button down for this to work. Turn the dial to power it on, and it stays on.

Suction in low power mode is a bit weak, but adequate for some easy-to-vacuum-up stuff. Suction in high power mode, which will make the battery power drain faster, of course, is very good.

And finally, I am disappointed they could not make this vacuum work while the a/c cord is plugged in charging the battery. This would have been a great emergency backup if the battery was dead and you wanted to still use this vacuum. But no, when the the electrical cord is plugged in, the vacuum will not turn on.

Edit 8-29-2018: Oreck sent me a 2nd soft bristle dust brush. And after I reported that that brush also shed and had deformed bristles they sent a 3rd. The 3rd brush also immediately shed quite badly just by very gently rubbing the brush over very soft material.
It Smells Bad. It really smells quite bad. And with my head so close to it, there's no way to avoid the unpleasant smell. This thing is too expensive to be smelling this bad.

Damaged Product (Times 3). I ordered three of these at one time. All three--yes all three--had damaged wood inside the boxes. Bent wood. Chipped wood. Peeled wood. Damaged corners. Damaged edges. My gosh...all three! And multiple damaged pieces in all three boxes. These cabinets are some of the most awfully packed cabinets I have ever encountered. Do not buy these unless they are going into a garage, where you won't care that the wood pieces are damaged.

Absolutely Terrible. This curtain does not feel 20 Gauge at all. It does not feel thick or heavy. In fact, it billows in a lot, which makes it uncomfortable to take a shower.

There is no weight at the bottom to keep this from billowing in and hitting you as you shower.

I have used 10 Gauge clear shower curtains before that feel thicker than this so-called 20 Gauge curtain.

I am sorry I bought this and cannot use it because of the billowing.

Another Love-Hate Relationship With A Dyson Vacuum. Should Be Different For Its High Price. I bought the V6 Absolute cheaper elsewhere, and not here via Amazon.

There are two suction levels: Low and Max. There is a remarkable difference between the suction power between the two. If you doubt this, simply attach the dust brush and hold it at the bottom of your shirt. On low, your shirt will not be held on by the suction. On Max, your shirt will be held onto the suction quite nicely, and as you'd expect.

I am extremely disappointed by the low suction power when the vacuum is not on the Max setting, I do not wanna use it. It just is not good enough. But on the vastly superior Max setting, you get a measly 6-minutes of battery power.

For its high price Dyson could have rectified this situation by designing the vac with a removable battery, and then include a second battery you can keep charged. When your 6 minutes are up, simply swap the second battery...putting the first battery into a charger.

Also, disappointingly, you cannot use this vacuum while the battery is being charged. This might have been a helpful feature if one ran out of battery after the 6 minutes but really needed to finish up a job right away.

For this whopping price, to only get 6 minutes using the desired Max suction setting is extremely upsetting to me. Again, I find the low setting suction level to be way to weak.

I realize battery technology is still limited...which is why I suggested they could have made this vacuum be able to swap out the battery, etc.

I do love the soft roller brush. I do love the handling of the vacuum. I do love the suction when it is on Max (and only on Max). Filter cleaning is easy. So, like I said, Love/Hate.

Again, this is a vacuum that they MSRP'd and originally sold it at their site for $599. Right now, as I write this review, they discounted it to $479.99. That is a lot of money for just 6 minutes of battery life for the suction I expect and the suction power I want. (And they could have easily fixed this situation by designing it with a swap-able battery, and including a second battery.)

On a side note: Hopefully one day Dyson will make a Cinetic cordless that has no filters to clean, just like with their wonderful Cinetic Big Ball Animal + Allergy. Once Dyson can give us a Cinetic Cordless with no filters to clean and more than 6 minutes of battery life on Max suction setting...my feelings will go from Love/Hate, to just Love.

One and Done. It seemed to work fine for the first week...but then after toasting just one item it would stop working for quite a long time, which meant I could not do another one in a decent amount of time. Maybe the thermostat was malfunctioning. I was using it with a quality 120v to 100v 1000w transformer, so whatever was happening had nothing at all to do with USA vs Japan power. The transformer was working perfectly, and I never used the Mitsubishi without the transformer.

Extremely Overpriced. As of this writing, these pants hangers are approximately $6 per hanger. I say the value just isn't there with these hangers to justify this price.

They do their job as far as holding the pants and keeping them from slipping out. I wish I had done more searching at Amazon where I just saw an almost exact design for a lot less money.

Not Comfortable Under the Feet. I am generally a fan of Norwex microfiber bath products, but certainly not this bath mat. It's just not comfortable at all under my feet. Yes, the microfiber itself is soft, but the mat lacks any kind of cushion. In addition to it not having the cushion you'd expect, it feels like it has somewhat hard areas under my feet.

Also, the mat does not contain BacLock, which Norwex puts into most of its other microfiber bath products to inhibit bacterial growth.

Since I do not like how it feels while standing on it, I cannot recommend it at all.

Cloudy. They call it Clear, but the two I received are both cloudy. These are unattractive because they are not clear. Yes, I wiped them down with warm water and they are still not clear, and unpleasant to look through them, either from the outside of the shower or while showering inside.

I recommend looking elsewhere if you want nice-looking clear shower curtains.

Chemical Smell. The 20 oz. mug arrived with an unpleasant chemical smell inside. After repeated washings, I can still smell it, even though the smell is not as strong as when first arrived. I do not recommend this 20 oz. mug until the company can find a way to send these out with no chemical smell.

Message To Panasonic: Stop Putting On Tape That Leaves Marks!. I am rating this one star in the hope that someone at Panasonic will read this. It is inexcusable to put tape on Stainless Steel (or anything) that is going to leave a noticeable blemish or mark or discoloration when removed! Why would you do this?

So, Panasonic puts two separate long pieces of tape to hold the door closed during shipping. When I carefully and slowly peeled this tape off, it left behind discolorations...and I mean large and noticeable discolorations where the tape was. I tried washing it...and while it faded a bit, the discolorations/blemishes remain. This is infuriating to me. An expensive and very nice looking microwave marred because they choose to put crap tape on the stainless steel to hold the door closed.

I hate it! And Amazon "One Star" means "I Hate It." So, that justifies my one-star rating.

I am going to keep the microwave because I fear replacing it will end up with the same result. And because there is only one other similar model in size that has the desired situation of no spinning plate necessary because there is rotating bottom energy feed, etc. (And that other model, also listed at Amazon, is a generic name and not a brand name like Panasonic. So, if I want the exact features the Panasonic offers, I have to tolerate the discoloration.)

To review the actual microwave itself: This is a very small capacity microwave in both interior height and width. (Perfect for a single person.)

I bought the model with the "non-traditionally-formatted" digital keypad. Yes, it requires either some thinking or the reading of the instruction manual to figure it out. But I found it easy to figure out rather quickly.

Heating times seems fast enough. (I boiled one cup of water in exactly two minutes...If you want to test your existing 1000-watt microwave to compare the time).

I like the no spinning plate. Easier to keep the interior clean.

There is an odd cover over the light that could be the cause of concern if there ever is a food explosion in the microwave. It might be hard to clean under that cover.

The microwave looks nice. The few things I have heated so far seem to have come out evenly heated. I am of course hoping for longevity. (I saw some reporting theirs did not last a long time. My last microwave, an LG Intellowave, lasted 15 years. I do not expect this will last as long.)

Again, to all companies out there: Stop with the labels and the tape over items that when peeled off leave behind gunk or discoloration! Thank you.

Massively Uneven Cooking. The description claims this toaster oven provides even cooking. The unit I received provides massively uneven heating. The second photo shows the top of the waffle. The first picture shows the bottom of the waffle. The bottom is hardly cooked, and the inside is cold.

Overhyped and Extremely Linty. The amount of lint these towels put out, along with shedding, is astounding. Do not even think about washing these with anything else. Horrible quantity of lint...a massive amount.

These towels are also overhyped. While they feel soft to the touch, when you are drying yourself off they don't really feel any softer than most other nice cotton towels. The seller describes these as "extremely soft," but they're not extremely soft when you are drying off.

They absorb a nice amount of water while using, but the lint and shedding makes these towels a complete non-recommended from me. The company says just keep washing them over and over, and eventually the lint and shedding will stop. Sure...I wanna pay so much money for a towel that needs so much pre-washing over and over again just to stop the lint and shedding? And this is assuming they are even right that the lint will stop.

I do not know if all the similar towels made in Imabari are as terrible as these. I certainly hope not, but I think they might be.

Two Gold Cups Had Problems. Two separate Gold cups had to be returned due to paint job issues. The first cup's problem was on the outside of the cup, while the second cup's problem was on the inside of the cup. The inside issue was that the CARIVINO letters were not completely white.

After seeing the inside of the cup I have become skeptical that the interior is actually ceramic. Maybe it is ceramic coating sprayed over the stainless steel that is used, which could explain why I can see the darker color on some of the areas of the CARIVINO letters. If it's ceramic coating, that could also explain why the inside layer is so thin.

I have decided not to try for a third Gold cup.

Unnecessary Adhesive. The maker of this product attaches a big label inside the colander. Pulling off this large circular label left behind sticky adhesive residue. For a long time I tried to clean it with soap. No success. It was still there and sticky. I then tried vinegar. No success. The only way to clean it was using Goo Gone. Keep in mind, however, that this is a product to use with food. It's not a pleasant thought to have to use Goo Gone on something you'll be using with food you're gonna eat.

I had to spend way too much time removing adhesive on something that should not have had any adhesive on it in the first place.

Loose Powder. I do not know if you can see the black powder on the countertop in the picture since Amazon typically shows pictures as smaller size. However, I assure you there is a lot of black powder. When I unwrapped the plastic I gently set the filter down on my counter. I then discarded my old Alen filter. When I picked up this new filter off the counter I immediately saw it left behind a lot of black powder.

The genuine Alen filters do not leave behind any black powder. I bought this generic one because I wanted to save the $30. I should have just spent the extra $30. This generic replacement filter is way too inferior.
Too Small to Be a Cereal Bowl. This bowl is way too small to be used as a cereal bowl.
Tissue Thin. These wash cloths are way too thin. When wet, they are seriously as thin as tissues. I do not recommend these wash cloths at all.

It is Not an Over-the-Door Mirror as Advertised. They listed this as an over-the-door mirror. It is not at all a mirror you can hang over any door with hooks. It was a major mistake and waste of time. Of course I returned it.

Too Thin and Uncomfortable Under Feet. Disappointing Maximum Heat Output. Not USB.. This is too thin, where if you rest your feet on it, it is uncomfortable because you can feel the hard wires under your feet.

Also, this does not produce the stated heat of 119 degrees. It only gets to 105 degrees.

Also, at the time I purchased this, the details stated USB charging. It is not USB at all.

Poorly Thought-Out Over-Door Lighted Mirror. A few negatives, where to begin.

The mirror must be plugged in at all times to utilize the light bulbs feature. Most closet doors, assuming you want to use this to hang over your closet door, do not have electrical outlets close by. But even if you did have an electrical outlet close by, the provided cord is way too short.

The cord, besides being too short, has a round tip on one end and USB-A on the other. They do not include a USB power plug adapter.

They put the electrical port on the left side of the mirror 4 inches up from the bottom edge instead of at the bottom underside. So, you have a cord awkwardly sticking out the side higher up, instead of coming out on the bottom. This also is annoying because the cord is too short. You will need to buy a USB Extension Cable or use a regular power extension cord to use this mirror.

The lights flicker at lower brightness setting. This could be a defect, of course.

Dangerous Razor-Sharp Corner Tips. All 4 corner tips at the top are razor sharp. Please put your fingertip on the pointy-ends of the 4 top corners. Sharp as a knife and dangerous, especially with kids.  Uncomfortably and scary sharp at the 4 top corners.

The Top of the Lid Ruined by an Unnecessary Adhesive Label. I have attached a picture of the adhesive label they stick on the very top. I am not exaggerating when I say it cannot be easily removed. It is stuck on there so powerfully, it just will not peel off without destroying it and leaving behind discoloration and scratches and marks.

I do not recommend buying this unless the manufacturer either utilizes easily removable adhesive labels, or decides no adhesive labels at all. They could simply attach a tag to the handle with either plastic or rope.
It is not nonstick. This pan is not nonstick. Food will stick to it. The pan is heavy, and it looks nice, but it proved to be nonstick immediately.
Sized Wrong. The pad I received was too small, and not easy to stretch on. My queen mattress is 60x80x9, and thus not unusual in any way. I returned the pad right away.

Multiple Defects. At two separate places on the outside of the top ceramic section, there are defects, as you can see from the pictures. And at the underside of the cup, there is permanent white paint all over.

The paint job is terrible along the rim. Also there is an imperfection inside the cup where the ceramic looks bad.

I received a refund from Amazon. I do not recommend this cup at all.

Arrived with a Small Defect. Update After Receiving Replacement: The second set was worse than the first, as this time both pans had small defects. I uploaded 3 pictures of the second set. On the 12" of the replacement set, there was a sharp edge along the rim which you can easily feel if you run your finger across.

Original Review: The bad first. The 10" Pan arrived with a small defect on its rim. At this expensive price, the pans should be absolutely perfect immediately out of the box. The Zavor company was very nice about it and communicated with me fast. I boxed up the pans and ordered a replacement via Amazon...and you gotta love Amazon for their service, of course.

The good: The pans are very nice, and the fact they offer removable handles which makes the pans not take up as much room in your cabinet as other pans, is really a welcome and useful feature. The handles are soft to the touch. The pans feel like the perfect weight...not too heavy.

Initial setup was fairly straightforward. After collecting several days worth of data I decided to delete them just because I was trying out features. Somehow deleting all sleep data caused the app to malfunction and close the moment it was started. I had to delete the app, reinstall and reregister everything. That took a few tries. Several days later the cable was accidentally unplugged from the adapter. I went through the setup procedure, nothing, several times. I read the help file and found out how to do a factory reset. I had to perform this seven times before the app would connect to the sensor again. I used the device for another week and suddenly it stopped collecting sleep data. For four days it sat under my mattress doing nothing. I tried contacting support and have not received a reply yet. An earlier question was answered fairly quick but I had to provide the serial number (adding a full day to the exchange) to get a simple data meaning question answered. On the fifth day the unit once again began sending data to the app. Is it defective? Perhaps. I'm unsure. But that leads me to my deepest concern. . .
I don't trust the veracity of the data collected. It's supposed to be able to tell how long it takes you to fall asleep, when you're lightly or deeply asleep or in REM sleep as well as tracking when you snore, your pulse rate high, low and average through the night and how long it takes you to get up when you awake. I was impressed with all these bar graphs and data until I started looking closely. Every night I go to bed early due to pain and will spend up to a few hours reading or watching video on my tablet. when the bar graph said I was lightly asleep, I wasn't. When it said I was deeply asleep, I wasn't. I have no idea how, without seeing my eye movement, it can know I'm in REM sleep. I think one time it said I took a while to get to sleep but most nights while I lay there reading it was logging it as some form of sleep and my falling asleep taking only a few minutes. I know I snore, my scouts once dragged me out of the tent because I was so loud, so I guess the snoring detector is accurate. It can also, some times, tell if you've taken a nap during the day and add that to the day's data though it appears there needs to be a susstantial time between getting up and going back for a nap otherwise the time gap gets logged as simply a really long interuption in your night's sleep. I tend to spend quite some time in bed on bad days and that seems to seriously confuse the device and app.
It's a slick idea, nothing to wear, nothing to start or stop manually. Just stuff it under your mattress as directed and hey presto, sleep data. Too bad it's dreadfully inaccurate has connection issues and stops and starts recording data for no good reason. It would be great if it were even 80% accurate but I know for a fact it's no where near.

Prettiest hunk of plastic junk I've ever owned.. My wife picked up this Bissell on sale at a local store, we needed a new vacuum and wanted a bagless model that "specialized" in pet hair. What we got was a complete waste of money (nobody listens to me when I say do a little research first). There isn't one thing this vacuum does well - not one! I could say that the candy apple red paint is a nice touch...but I buy vacuums to clean my house, not to look nice when I open the hall closet.

If you like a LOUD vacuum with the suction power of TWO drinking straws, this is the vacuum for you. I think Bissell says in the manual that you have to remove the insert above the canister and clean it every once in awhile. We have one dog and one cat, and have to remove that insert about 2-3 times a month. This isn't a 'bang around the trash can' cleanout, either; I have to take it into the garage and blow it out with the air compressor. Do YOU have a compressor in your garage? There's so many nooks and crannies in the insert that it's pretty much a requirement to blow it out to clear the air passages. I know, I know...the engineers didn't expect this thing to be moving DUSTY AIR through its MULTI CYCLONIC SYSTEM.

That pet brush you see up on the handle? That is a junk extension of a junk device. It falls off at the slightest tap of the main vacuum chassis, and stopped working after 3 uses (you could hear the high-quality plastic bearings making noise during the first use). Right now it lives in the bottom of the closet, because it's useless and just falls off anyway.

There is another brush head on the body of the removable canister, which falls off 50% less than the pet brush. This one actually collects the pet hair so you can pick it out by hand and spoon-feed it to the vacuum. In fact, you'll be hand-feeding this hunk of crap more than you think - it needs a LOT of help. Find any hair/crumbs/glitter/anything on your carpet? You'll be making at least two passes before Ol' Faithful even considers picking it up...and then you stand a good chance of the offending item getting dropped out of the vacuum head as soon as you turn it off. It doesn't even pick up pet hair, which is what seems to be a selling point judging by all the dumb stickers on this thing. It's like an auto body guy from NASCAR works in Bissell's marketing department - STICKERS EVERYWHERE.

The hose itself is pretty inflexible and just about long enough, and the hose extension is another quality design by those Bissell MBAs...I mean, engineers. The extension has a twist lock in the middle, which will crack after maybe 6 months of use...rendering it useless as well. I've checked multiple times, and there are no blockages in any passageways; this thing is just very poorly designed.

Overall, keep looking right past this thing. It may look nice, but that's about it.
