F+ -->What was Bissell thinking?. I have a Bissell Spot Bot and I purchased a Bissell 9400 ProHeat 2X Select Upright Deep Carpet Cleaner for my boyfriend; both are superb products! However, I cannot phathom what Bissell was thinking when they produced this carpet cleaner. I tried it on an area of carpet that was only slightly dirty; but the results were very disappointing.

What they got right:
- Easy assembly
- Sleek vacuum design
- Useable power tools (power nozzle is good)
- Easy carry handle
- Excellent power cord holder
- Nice power cord release mechanism (no need to unwind cord from power cord wrap because you can just release the latch to drop the cord to the floor)
- Vacuum powers itself nicely along the carpet so there is hardly any pushing action required by the user

What they got terribly wrong:
- The soft PowerRoller doesn't clean; it's excellent on hardwood floors but that is not what this vacuum was designed for.
- The carpet does not dry in 30 minutes as stated UNLESS you hardly use any solution. Without using much solution, you might as well blow on the carpet with your mouth to try to dislodge the dirt because the results would probably be the same--which is no cleaning.
- The solution tank leaks around the cap when filled appropriately. I tried several times to reseal the cap but there was always some solution seepage.
- The dirty water collector tank also has water seepage even if you don't go above the fill line.
- I tried for 45 minutes to clean about a 6 x 7 area of carpet and it still looked as dirty as when I started. I then used the power tool and some elbow grease and tried again which gave me better results but still not good enough. My Bissell spot bot can clean the same area wonderfully but not this vacuum.
- By the time the hot water reaches the carpet it is either lukewarm or too cold to be of any cleaning use.

In summary, if the Bissell didn't leak all over, this vacuum would be excellent (but perhaps overkill) for cleaning a wood floor because the cleaning pad buffs up things nicely (I tried it my wood floor). However as a carpet cleaner, you would get better results by wetting a washcloth with warm water, applying some soap, getting down on your hands and knees and using some elbow grease to clean your carpet.

Decent vacuum for those who don't have pets or allergies but not for me. My first impression of this vacuum was that it was a four-star product. However after a full evaluation, in my opinion this is a three-star vacuum for non-pet owners and those without allergies. Although this Bissell has a lot of PROS, it is a two-star vacuum for my purposes because I have pets and allergies to dust.

PROS:
- Easy and intuitive assembly without reading manual (requires long Phillips screwdriver to tighten screw in handle which is a little awkward to tighten in the long hole)
- Incredible suction
- All tools fit snugly into their holders on the vacuum
- The Model 58F8-3 comes with a combination dusting brush/upholstery tool, a crevice tool, extension wand, and TurboBrush
- Retractable cord
- No need to purchase bags
- Has a bright headlight
- The internal filter is washable; all except for the HEPA Media Filter which has to be replaced
- Vacuum components are easy to disassemble without tools except for the headlight and drive belt replacement
- 25-ft power cord (according to the product description online; but this is not mentioned in the manual)
- Height adjustment knobs and other controls such as on/off switch and handle release pedal as easy to operate and locate
- Easy to empty dirt container and remove filter cup
- Has clean filter indicator and clean carpet sensor
- Vacuum has a three-year limited warranty

CONS:
- Vacuum was difficult to maneuver due to incredible suction
- Vacuum is very loud
- If the hose falls out of the hose wand base during vacuuming, a lot of dust escapes through the hole filing the house in a cloud
- Hair from pets clogged the filter cup even before the filter cup was full rendering the turbo brush in operable until everything was cleaned out
- Filter indicator light didn't change to red even though I had to clean out the filter cup
- The clean carpet sensors did not appear reliable to me. Many times it would show a steady green to indicate the carpet was clean, then it would turn to red when I went over the same carpet again and again; yet the carpet was clean.
- Emptying the filter cup and cleaning the filter was VERY MESSY
- Instructions don't give any recommendationos on when you should wash or replace filters
- I don't understand the meaning of a HEPA filter when so much dust escapes the vacuum if the hose falls out of the wand base or when emptying the filter cup
- The floor brush continues to rotate when you use the vacuum attachments which could wear out your carpet or mark up your floor while you are using the tools with the hose.
- I would have liked a cord that was about 2-3 feet longer

My arm hurt after using this vacuum because no matter how I changed the height adjustment knob, the Bissell required a lot force to push around. I was actually sweating after I vacuumed my rug. Also, the pet hair I picked up got caught in the upper filter area requiring a cup cleaning and filter shaking before the filter cup was full. In addition, the filter emptying process (although very, very easy) was incredibly messy. By the time I was done, I had to re-vacuum the area where I emptied the filter cup. In addition, there was a cloud of dust around my house similar to the type of dust kicked up by a Shop Vac. Of course, I used a carpet powder on my rug which only exacerbated the problem. I also didn't like how the floor brush on the upright continues to rotate while I was using the wand tools. To me this was unnessary and could result in excess wear on my carpet or scratch my floors.

In summary, this vacuum does pick up a lot of dirt and is easily assembled, which is excellent. Its interesting features are average. However, I can't recommend this vacuum for someone who has pets or has allergies to dust for the above reasons. Instead, I recommend buying a vacuum with a bag that isn't so loud or so messy to clean.

Beautiful to look at but with some design flaws. This is a gorgeous little tea kettle and is much smaller than I expected. This kettle is only for heating up water and nothing else. Below are the PROS and CONS including some design flaws.

PROS
- The unit is so pretty to me.
- There are five temperature settings - 212 (best for black and pu-erh teas and tisanes such as rooibos and herbal teas), 195 (best for oolong teas and some herbal teas; can be used for yellow teas if left to cool slightly), 175 (best for white teas), and 160 (best for green teas although I brew these teas around 175). The fifth setting is for 100 degrees to keep the water warm.
- Cord storage is hidden underneath the unit.
- The kettle fits nicely into the base as long as you line up the matching dots correctly.
- I like the push button feature of the dial to turn on the unit and the blue light on the dial.
- The lid on the carafe snaps nicely into place.
- It reaches the desired temperature pretty fast.
- Anywhere between 16 ounces and 48 ounces (2-8 cups) of water can be heated.

CONS:
- There are no in-between temperature settings; it must be dialed into 212, 195, 175, and 160 for brewing or 100 for keeping the water warm.
- There is no audible signal to tell you when the water has reached its desired temperature; the only way to tell is to watch the light go out. To me this is a design flaw because now I have to watch the water reach its temperature and there's no "automatic keep warm" feature.
- The lid is difficult snap into the upright position when there's hot water in the carafe.
- The neck of the carafe is so tiny that it is impossible to get a hand in the carafe to dry the inside unless your hand is small. I am able to get my hand inside when I am not using a towel; but as soon as I introduce a towel it's impossible for me.
- The other design flaw is that when there are 16 ounces of water in the kettle, the unit feels hotter to me and it was almost impossible not to burn myself when pouring the water because of the steam and heat emanating from the top of the unit. Of course, wearing an oven mitt or holding a towel will prevent this possibility.
- The lid is not removable.
- At the current price of $79.99, I think this is too expensive a purchase for what you are getting.

It is important to read the manual for this unit. For instance, the carafe has to be seated correctly before turning on the unit or the power light will blink and the unit will not work.

This unit should not be washed because all components, including the carafe, are electric. Only dry the inside and wipe down with a damp cloth. Although this Capresso does the job it is supposed to do, the two design flaws that made me rate this 2 stars instead of 3 was that there was no audible signal to tell you when the water is heated to the desired temperature and the fact that the water is too hot to pour when boiling unless using a mitt or towel to hold the very hot carafe. Other than this this is an average kettle. I cannot vouch for its longevity as I've only heated water 4 times in this unit so far. I will post an update if things change. If this unit were priced in the $29 range, I would have given it 3 stars despite its flaws.

If you are a real tea connoisseur, it is better to pay $170 more for the [[ASIN:B003LNOPSG Breville BTM800XL One-Touch Tea Maker]]. I personally purchased and own two of these. If you only make teas with boiling water and want to make tea for company, then you might consider the [[ASIN:B007UEEJVK Nesco TM-1 Teamaker, 1-Liter]]. I also own this one and although it is average, at least you can make tea in it. I've attached my reviews to the other tea makers in the comment section of this review for those who are interested.

In summary, I would pass on this Capresso.

Update November 2013 - This kettle stopped working so now it's headed for the garbage. This is not the life expectancy I would expect and had I purchased it I would be very disappointed.

Washcloths are of good quality but heavy when wet and not for washing. This washcloth is of good quality and actually feels double-ply in thickness. Since it is white with a stripe it appears very hotel-like in looks.

However, what I don't like about this washcloth is that it gets heavy when wet and the soap seeps into the cloth like a sponge so there is no lather. I don't consider this washcloth useful for washing for this reason (it is not a high-pile towel which tends to lather better) and for that I give it 1 star.

No towels ever look new after they are laundered and these are no different; however, they (I received 2) still launder nicely but seem to have shrunk just a wee bit.

I'm going to use these washcloths for other purposes. To me they make good finger towels, trivets for hot plates, and are nice to double up when lifting up a pot lid if I don't have a pot holder handy. Nevertheless, I would not buy them for this reason.

The current price of $9.99 is very steep for this towel even if it were a five-star product. I hope the price listed is for two washcloths as Amazon does not say this currently in the advertisement. I received two washcloths in the package that arrived for review.

Personally I would not buy these because it makes a good towel but is heavy when wet and prevents soap from lathering.

Some butter always sticks on the inside. I purchased these at Home Goods a while back because I was attracted to the beautiful colors and the idea that I would not get my hands dirty when buttering corn.  They are functional, but I'm not as enthralled with them as the other reviewers are. The reason is that some butter always gets left behind in the spreader. Also, it is a pain to clean the butter out of the edges. I'm actually disappointed with these and had I known this, I would not have purchased them.  The only plus to me is that they are colorful; however, I still wind up with butter on my hands during the washing process.

Slices garlic thin if I'm slicing only a couple of cloves otherwise the blade clogs; also requires lots of pressure to slice. I purchased this at a Pampered Chef party because I wanted to replace a sliding garlic slicer and this one appeared to work wonderfully at the party. However, after using this over 5 times, I absolutely hate it. I tried several types of garlic including the hard redneck variety and it slices some of the garlic very thin but if I'm slicing more than two cloves, the garlic clogs the blade at the bottom. In addition it requires brute strength to press the top and bottom together to get this to slice. I thought it was just me, so I had my boyfriend try this and he hates it as well. He said, "where did you get this garlic slicer, it's awful"?

I purchased three of these at TJX; they are super thin and tear easily; holds a lot. I purchased three (3) of these bags at TJX for $4.99 each plus tax (one in espresso color, another in grey, and one in dusty blue). They each are 24 in long x 18 in front to back x 12 in high.

The zipper extends around on both sides and there is a peek-a-boo window in front. There is also a handle on each side but I recommend it not be used.

The one I attached a picture of is in the espresso color. They hold a lot and because of that are heavy when moved. I was able to store one full shelf of shirts from my armoire in this one bag (about 40 tee shirts).

The problem with this bag is that it is made of a thin material that is like those free shopping bags supermarkets sell or different companies give out. Mine ripped immediately. It is just good for storage in place (without moving it).

Since I only paid $4.99 plus tax for each one, I feel it is okay for one time use as long as I gingerly carry it to its storage location or pack it at its exact storage location. However, this might rip the first moment used (as mine did by the handle). I would never pay $14.99 for this bag since it almost feels like tissue paper. I prefer thick plastic storage bags instead.

This are too big on the bottom to easily pick them up from a hot water bath canner. I purchased these jars at Walmart for canning at a comparable price to Amazon. They look pretty and I am able to use them in the quart-sized section of the [[ASIN:B007QT4GO4 Prepworks by Progressive Reversible Stainless Steel Canning Rack]]. However, what I do not like is that they are too bulbous (round, fat, etc.) on the bottom that it makes them very difficult to pick up from the hot water bath with my [[ASIN:B00FRQVKRY Progressive Ckc-100 One Handed Jar Lifter]]. In fact I find it dangerous because the jars feel like they are going to slip out my grasp. Other than this they are beautiful jars but not ones I will purchase again for water bath canning.

One pan arrived pre-chipped; pans are thin and not worth the price. The interior coating of the square pan arrived pre-chipped in two places so my first impression was not good. The pans are light and not of good quality. I consider them only slightly stronger than foil pans.

I used these on my electric grill and the veges I grilled in them (with a little oil in the pan) came out perfect. The handles are sized well making it easy to carry from grill to table (using gloves of course). I also, like the small size because I can use them in my toaster oven as well as the oven. However, I don't like the ceramic coating which tends to chip and it also does not clean well. I do not use a dishwasher so I soaked and hand washed the pans. The clean surface looked splotchy after only one use.

Personally I cannot recommend these, I expected better from Cuisinart. They are not worth more than $4.99 for the pair in my opinion. I personally think purchasing two [[ASIN:B0017T6O26 Lodge LMSRD Round Mini Server, Black, 14-Ounce]] is a better deal than these.

Barely strips herbs and barely cuts. I had high expectations for these shears but was sorely disappointed and here is why:

- The shears don't cut well at all unless I put the herb stem all the way to the base of the shear (that's the intersection of the cutting blades) . The tip has minimal cutting power unless the item being cut is delicate -- like cutting chives.

- The handle lock requires force to close.

- The herb stripper slot is awkward to use, especially for items with bigger leaves that have to be "fed through the handle" in order to reach the slot. Although I was partially successful in removing thyme from its branch that only worked when the branch wasn't delicate enough to break on its own.

The only thing I like about these shears is that the rubberized handle feels good in my hand and provides me with a non-slip grip when the shears are open.

I cannot recommend these and would purchase kitchen shears instead. This is another item that will eventually head to the landfill. I will continue to use my thumb and forefinger to strip herbs as I always do and will use my standard kitchen shears to do all the cutting work.

Pretty color as long as I put nothing in them; however, the color gets lost when used to store jam & makes some jam look sickly. This review is for the [[ASIN:B01AAHHB9A Ball Regular Mouth Elite Collection Half Pint Jars, Blue (4-Pack)]].

I purchased these jars at Walmart for canning at a comparable price to Amazon. These jars are absolutely beautiful. I used them in the pint-sized section of my [[ASIN:B007QT4GO4 Prepworks by Progressive Reversible Stainless Steel Canning Rack]] to can some jam. Because they are tall and narrow, they do tend to slip around on the canning rack so beware of that if using the same rack. What I really do not like is that once the jam is in the jar, the color of the jar gets lost. It made my peach jam look sickly and although the blueberry jam looked great, it did not look any better than in a clear jar. For this reason, I would not spend the extra money to buy these.

Note that I also purchased the [[ASIN:B01AAHHB5E Ball Jelly Elite Collection Jam Jar (4 Pack), 8 oz, Clear]] as well and love those jars and would purchase that version of the Elite collection but not these colored ones. In addition, I also purchased [[ASIN:B001DIZ1NO Ball Mason "PINT" Jars Wide-Mouth Can or Freeze - 12pk (by Jarden Home Brands)]], which I would purchase again. I love the wide mouth version the best because they can be put in the freezer. In addition, I purchased a dozen Kerr Wide Mouth Half-Pint Mason Jars from Walmart which are similar to the Ball Wide-Mouth Jars in that they can be used for freezing. I also love those.

I sent this back for a refund because the holes in the curved base were too small for the dowels provided. My boyfriend has a kneeling chair and I love it. I could not find the one he has so I decided to order this. Based on the look of the parts, the chair would probably have been a good one. However, the holes in the curved rocker part are too small to fit the dowels provided. I'm not interested in having to do woodworking to make the holes bigger so I returned this for a refund.

I probably would have liked or loved this chair otherwise. The instructions were pretty simple to me as I have assembled a lot of furniture before. In fact, I probably could have assembled it in 30 minutes. I already worked on it for 10 minutes when it came time to insert the dowels into the curved based. It was at that point I took it apart to send it back.

At first this was the best soap dispensing dish brush I ever used; but then it failed after a few weeks. REVISION OF REVIEW IS IN THE UPDATES AT THE BOTTOM

I am really impressed with this soap dispensing sink brush. It fact it is the best I ever tried but I only started using it so time will tell.

WHAT I LIKE

- This is so easy to fill. I just lightly pulled up the plug in the handle to fill it with dish detergent and then pressed down to seal the plug in place.

- One push on the center button and a 5 to 25-cent-sized dollop of soap is dispensed.

- The handle is long and has a nice grip for ease of use.

- The brush bristles are slightly stiff for moderate cleaning.

- The brush head is removable by twisting it to the left to dislodge.

- There's a scraper on the underside of the brush; it's not something I would likely use but it's nice to know it's there if needed.

- The brush comes with a limited lifetime warranty but one has to pay to ship the brush back to them for a replacement.

WHAT I DISLIKE

- I do wish that I could dispense a smaller quantity of soap for the times I'm just cleaning one plate.

- The brush head is not stiff enough for heavy-duty cleaning as the advertising states. I actually like that it's not heavy duty because then the bristles would be too stiff. What I don't like is that they advertise it can be used for that.

- I do not understand why the brush head needs to be replaceable. Perhaps I am wrong, but I seriously doubt the sealing ability of the plug in the handle will outlast the brush head. I would think this whole unit would have to be replaced after a year of use but only time will tell.

If this brush continues to work as it does now, I plan on ordering another one if the price is right. At the time of this review there is no price listed on Amazon. This brush allows me to clean most of my dishes without even getting my hands fully wet. It's great for moderate cleaning. It's not so great for heavy-duty cleaning or for cleaning small items like baked-on-cheese-covered utensils or greasy items like a butter dish where a sponge covers a better surface area. However, I never expect any dish brush to clean items where rubbing with a sponge would normally be required.

UPDATE Feb 8 - I've been using this brush daily all day long and I decided to lower my rating from 4 to 3 stars. Yesterday was the first time I was unable to dispense the soap. It appears that it might be due to too many soap bubbles in the handle but I can't be sure. After playing around a bit I got it to work. Until yesterday it was working beautifully all day long.

UPDATE Feb 11 - I've decided to downgrade this to 2 stars. Today the soap dispensing ability has mostly stopped working. I had to keep opening and closing it to try to get the soap to squirt out using the air in the handle which they call "air displacement" technology. Unfortunately, I can no longer recommend this.

A gorgeous fireplace that is partially non-functional. [[VIDEOID:fc1e9bcb5d0203dbb23da4974b4c9270]] I both love and hate this fireplace. As you can see from the video and picture, it is absolutely gorgeous in white. It is also small. I am 5'5" tall and it stands a few inches below my knees. It has three settings - lights only, 750W heat, and 1500W heat. This "cat-sized" electric fireplace was everything I wanted. I also was only interested in the ambiance of the real-looking log fire made by the lights. However, the entire unit should work whether I wanted it to heat a room or not.

Set-up was easy. There is no assembly. I just took it out of the box and plugged it in after reading the manual. Reading the manual actually makes one wonder whether it should be plugged in or not because there are all sorts of overheating and fire warnings that made me nervous. Nevertheless, I tried it. The fireplace was gorgeous and realistic when lit. However, the 1500W heater would not go on. The 750W heater worked. As a result, I had my boyfriend return this as defective and decided against a replacement.

I am so disappointed but after reading the manual, some of the other reviews, and having experienced a defective unit on my first try; it is best I not get a replacement. It is too bad this is low quality. It may be truly stunning and perfectly tiny but it is operationally imperfect.

Bare bones almost powerless cordless vacuum; picks up light dust and wisps of hair only. I am very disappointed in this cordless vacuum because it lacks any “pick-me-up.” I was only able to pick up tiny wisps of cat hair and dust and was barely able to pick up any cat litter sprinkled throughout the carpet or bare floor. If I uncoupled the hand vac from the floor head, then it had a bit more suction but still not enough. However, there is no way I am vacuuming a floor on my hands and knees with a hand vac even if the suction were great. This vacuum is too weak to be useful to me.

FACTS:

- Assembly of the four parts (floor head, hand vac, extension pole, top curved handle) is required.

- The fifth part is the charging cord that plugs into the hand vac portion of the vacuum.

- The floor head has no beater bar (meaning no rotating brush).

- There is no charging light on the vacuum or the charging cord.

- A charge of 16 hours before first use is needed and it is safe to leave on the charger indefinitely.

- The curved handle and pole are not removable once assembled; however, rest of vacuum comes apart for configuring into the various combinations.

- This is a 4-in-1 vacuum meaning there are four vacuum component combinations:
1) with floor head and hand vac attached (short handle)
2) with just the hand vac (meaning no floor head or pole handle)
3) with just the hand vac and long pole handle
4) with floor head and long handle attached to the hand vac – note that this is the typical upright full vacuum.

LIKES:

- Self-standing design with ability to hang from handle hole as well. There is also a wall fitting available for purchase according to the instructions in case one wants to hang the vacuum on the wall.

- Dust bowl and filter are easy to empty and wash.

- Swivel steering.

- "Ease of glide" along my bare floor.

- Two-year limited warranty

- Cordless with lithium ion battery (wall charger cord included)

DISLIKES in order of importance to me:

- There is limited suction, especially when fully assembled as an upright vacuum.

- The vacuum feels cheap like the plastic will break after a while.

- The floor head and hand vac are difficult to couple and uncouple.

- There is no charging light.

- The assembly instructions are not clear when it comes which way to line up the holes in the handle.

In summary, this is truly a bare bones vacuum. To get four stars, it would have to be able to pick up the tiny granules of cat litter sprinkled throughout my floor and carpet. To get five stars it would also have to feel sturdier than it currently feels.

Brews a good cup of tea but so many steps & a separate timer are needed; NOT worth it. I am a tea connoisseur that loves loose leaf teas to be brewed correctly and at the right temperature. Unless one brews only black or pu-erh tea or herbal tisanes, then a brewer that brews at different temperatures is required in order to extract the correct flavor profile of that tea. This is where this Breville BTM500 Smart Tea Infuser is supposed to shine. After having tried this brewer, it does brew the tea correctly but it is so cumbersome to use and there are so many steps involved that it is not worth the price, in my opinion.

Before I go into the PROs and CONS of this particular teapot, I want to explain a little bit about the tools I use now to brew tea.

My favorite pot is a [[ASIN:B003LNOPSG Breville One-Touch Tea Maker]]. I originally purchased one of those at $250 and then purchased a second one for $199.99 because I felt I could not live without it if the first one broke. It is is the only tea brewer I know of that does a phenomenal job of brewing tea that is to be enjoyed to the last drip and brews with the least hassle. However, if I only want one cup of tea, I use the much simpler [[ASIN:B00DHLAC66 Frigidaire Professional Programmable Water Kettle]] to heat water to the correct temperature for one cup of tea.

I also occasionally use a tea kettle to just boil water to brew one cup of black tea with a tea infuser. When I want more than one cup of black tea, I use the [[ASIN:B007UEEJVK Nesco TM-1 Teamaker, 1-Liter]] which acts like a coffee pot but for tea and only brews with boiling water.

Although this Smart Tea Infuser does produce a high quality brew, there is just not enough good about it compared to the bad.

WHAT I LOVE:
- It brews a good cup of tea of varying kinds at the appropriate temperatures.

- Water can be boiled in this.

- There is a cord storage underneath the base.

- This is an attractive tea maker that looks great on my counter top.

WHAT I DISLIKE (in order of my biggest hate):
- Brewing the tea requires several steps. First the kettle needs to be filled with the desired amount of water. Second, the lid rim and top need to be inserted. Third, the tea type / temperature need to be selected. Then the unit needs to be turned on (a.k.a. started). Fourth, once the unit beeps (which takes several long minutes), the tea basket has to be inserted with the correct amount of tea. Fifth, the steeping time has to be set and then the START TIMER button pressed to start steeping. However, there is no light on that button to indicate it was even pressed. Once the cycle is complete, the tea maker is supposed to beep three times. I was unable to get it to beep. This means I now have to time how long I am steeping it for with a separate timer or sit and watch until the other lights on the pot go out. Now the tea can be enjoyed but it is important to remove the tea basket first so it does not over steep. After the tea is poured, I have to follow more steps to keep it warm. I have to return the tea kettle to power base and press and hold the TEMP / KEEP WARM button for two seconds. This will keep the tea warm for 30 minutes unless I remove the kettle, after which I have to reset.

- The long brew basket makes it difficult to remove the spent leaves from the basket.

- The unit does not remember the last settings chosen after a power off.

- Custom programming is not possible as there is only a set selection of temperatures.

- There is no auto start option. This means one cannot wake up to a freshly brewed cup of tea. For the price of this unit, I would have expected this.

- The current cost of $149 is way too expensive for the cumbersome features of this brewer. I recommend spending $50 more to buy the [[ASIN:B003LNOPSG Breville One-Touch Tea Maker]]. Perhaps this is Breville's way of getting people to buy their one touch by making a substandard tea infuser.

- There is no secondary strainer at the spout of the carafe to catch any wayward leaves from escaping into my cup; although, this is unlikely given the tight "weave" of the brew basket.

- The base (obviously) and the carafe itself (that needs special care of wiping down or rinsing gently inside only) cannot be washed. This is the same with their one-touch tea maker.

MORE DISAPPOINTMENTS
- The quick start guide and instruction manual contradict each other. The quick start guide says to leave the tea basket in when cleaning for first use; the instruction manual says to remove it. The quick start guides forgets to tell you about selecting the steep time and has you just starting the timer.

- The instruction manual contains erroneous tea information. Most tea is oxidized (exposed to air) and not fermented (converted via use of microbes). Although some use those words interchangeably, they do not mean the same thing and there is a lot of misinformation out in the tea world about this.

In summary, this is definitely not worth the purchase. There are entirely too many steps required to achieve the perfect brew. The tea basket is too long and narrow which makes it difficult to empty. In addition, the unit does not beep three times when the steeping time is over as the manual says. If you just love different loose leaf teas and want to experience the various subtleties in the liquor of these different brews, then save for the [[ASIN:B003LNOPSG Breville One-Touch Tea Maker]] because that tea maker is worth it and this one does not even come close.

Attractive, large soap dispenser that dispenses too little soap for my tastes. I really like this dispenser except for the fact that it dispenses just too little soap even on the highest setting. I attached four pictures. The second photo shows the dispenser bottom removed with instruction booklets. The third shows the top battery compartment removed. The fourth shows how much the dispenser actually dispenses. From left to right is the largest to smallest amount released.

The bottom of this unit holds the soap and the top holds the batteries and controls how much soap will be dispensed. There is an on/off switch under the cap in case one wants to turn the unit off for moving. The instructions are written by someone who has English as a second language and it is not well written, yet they are still understandable.

In order to get the air out of the unit, I dispensed water. It does dispense water generously. However, due to the thickness of any soap, dispensing slows down. I do not want to water down my soap. I got this to release dish detergent and it comes out in a tiny dribble at the highest setting. I would have preferred twice the amount.

In summary, the unit is attractive and large and it does what it is supposed to do when dispensing nothing thicker than water. Nevertheless, when using soap, the dispensing action slows to a mere tiny trickle. Note that this will not dispense into clear glass. In other words, if I want soap to release into a glass container, it will not work. It actually has to see my hand or sponge to release. However, this is to be expected because glass acts like nothing to the sensor but I did not think of this because I often bring up the dish to the soap to dispense.

UPDATE December 6, 2018: I have been using this daily and noticed that it takes about three times to get soap to dispense if it has not been in use for about 30 minutes. This is very annoying. It is as if air gets in the line or the soap goes back down to the bottom of the straw and takes time to come to the top again.

UPDATE December 12, 2018: Although this is operating the same as I described in my update above, I am getting increasingly annoyed with this dispenser. As a result, I have lowered the ranking from 3 stars (a.k.a. 2.5 stars) to 2 stars. Every time that the dispenser has not been in continuous use, I have to try 3 or 4 times to get it to work before it starts dispensing again. At this point I am beyond annoyed.

UPDATE December 22, 2018: I tried so hard to use this soap dispenser and it just dispenses too little soap to be useful. I threw it in the garbage today.

More like an imperfect tapestry than a throw; hate the smell, texture, and design. I am very disappointed in this throw. First of all the texture is rough. Second, it smells like rubber. Third, the stitching has imperfections in it. Fourth, the design is not very pretty or western to me. Also, the texture reminds me a bit of sisal rope that my cats like to scratch. There is not one thing I like about this; I'm sorry I ordered it.

Dry cleaning is recommended but it can be machined washed on delicate as per the label.

Photo 1 shows the front; Photo 2 the back; Photo 3 the imperfections in back; and Photo 4 the imperfections in front.

The one I received does not oscillate but it heats fast; it's partially broken right out of the box. [[VIDEOID:fc5aec08f1488661939e768e5ce82915]] I actually ordered this for its oscillating feature and am extremely disappointed. This heater is sleekly designed and has a carry handle. There is supposed to be both an oscillating feature from 120 to 270 degrees and a non-oscillating feature. The LOW/HIGH dials to the left are used when the heater oscillation is not wanted. The LOW/HIGH dials to the right with the circular arrows are for the LOW or HIGH heat and the oscillating feature as well. There is supposedly a tip over button on the button, although I did not find it.

I feel uncomfortable using this because part of the unit is broken. I had high hopes and decided to order this based on other reviewers. That was my mistake. I cannot recommend this heater.

I see other have posted negative reviews since I last looked which tells me this is a substandard unit.

Very cheaply made; shipped inappropriately; lights are bright but lanterns are not built to last. There are two lanterns improperly shipped in a plastic envelope. Each lantern comes with three AA batteries already installed. However, one of mine had the cap fall off and the batteries spilled out with the tape removed from the batteries. In addition, that one sounds like there is a broken piece in the unit as I can hear it shaking around. Nevertheless, they both work.

There is both a side light and front like like a flashlight. The sides have to be expanded until the carry handle is stretched out all the way to expose the light. When the unit is compressed, it can be carried by the handle and used like a flashlight. The button at the base of the handle needs to be toggled on and off to get either the side light or front light to show. Note that there are no light modes (high, medium, or low) on this and no strobe.

I like that the lanterns can be carried and that it is versatile enough to stand up on its own. Inserting the batteries are also easy.

What I hate about this is that the units are not packaged appropriately for shipment. These are VERY CHEAP lights that I do not feel will last a long time. Also, the screw top that holds the batteries in the flashlight easily pops off. On one of mine, it kept falling off.

Like a $1 store blanket but super soft and pretty; thin as a sheet. This blanket is as thin as a sheet. Had I paid the current price of $23.90, I would have been extremely upset. I do not feel this is worth more than $8.

This is best to hang up on the wall. There is no warmth or heft in this blanket. It is very soft and super attractive as can be seen from the third photo, but not worth the money. It is best used as a privacy curtain or wall hanging or as a thin wrap or to lay out on the beach as a large super thin "towel." However, a towel is thicker and this is not what I expected to receive when I ordered a blanket.

There is no label on this which is good and bad. I assume it has to be washed in cold water but I would expect it to disintegrate in the laundry. This is disposable to me.

Low quality, low-end cookware. This is a 14-piece non-stick aluminum set that includes:

One 5 qt / 4.75 L Covered Dutch Oven
One 2 qt / 1.9 L Covered Saucepan
One 1 qt / 0.95L Covered Saucepan
One 10.25 in / 26 cm Covered Fry Pan (has Thermo-Spot heat indicator)
One 8 in / 20 cm Fry Pan (has Thermo-Spot heat indicator)
One "One Egg Wonder"
4 Plastic Measuring Spoons

The package states these pots have a safe non-stick coating with NO PFOA, NO LEAD, and NO Cadmium. It also indicates that the set can be used on a gas, coil/solid electric, ceramic, or halogen stove. It is made in China and comes with a limited lifetime warranty. I tested my set on a gas stove.

What I like about this set is that it has a large covered fry pan. Most fry pans do not have covers. I also like the brick red color, the handles on the pots, and the tops on the lids which are easy to grip. The pots also wash well. However, I dislike a lot about this cookware.

- The lids do not fit snugly on the large pot or fry pan because the pans are sort of misshaped (not fully circular) causing a gap. The two saucepan covers fit snugly, however.

- The cookware does not hold heat well.

- The 1 qt saucepan easily tips just by touching the handle unless the contents inside are heavy.

- I saw no change in the Thermo- Spot heat indicator of the two fry pans even after heating them up for 5 minutes; so that feature does not work.

- The package says this is oven safe up to 350 degrees (177 C). Personally that is useless to me because I cook at 350 or above. Since many oven temperatures are not exact, it would be easy to go over 350 and the handles would most likely be destroyed.

- For those who use a dishwasher, it says dishwasher safe on the box but the instructions say hand washing is recommended for the non-stick pots.

- The egg I cooked stuck to the non-stick coating of the "one egg wonder" although it did clean up pretty well after soaking.

- The pots also do not stack well because they slip around a lot.

As a side note, since the pots have a non-stick coating, those with pet birds have to be careful using this around them or they could die from the toxicity. The fumes the heated non-stick coating gives off are toxic to birds.

Had I purchased this cookware I would have been extremely upset and sent it back for a refund. This set is just barely serviceable and I cannot recommend this cookware. It is both low end and low quality in my opinion. In fact, I am stunned that others find this cookware favorable to them.

This denim apron gives me a serious neck ache due to the design; otherwise it would have been perfect for me.. NOTE: Amazon is combining reviews for several different types of aprons, so please be aware that this review is for the cotton denim apron being sold.

I have several aprons but I wanted one that came below my knees. This cotton denim apron fits that bill. I love how it protects the front of my clothing when cooking or cleaning. The apron pockets are chest high in front; I usually prefer apron pockets a little bit lower in the front so I am unlikely to use ones that are so high.

It washes well and any shrinkage is imperceptible to me. Also, it barely wrinkles after coming out of the dryer and the little that it does wrinkle is not visible after cinching it back around the waist. The only serious wrinkling is the folding of the straps; those will have to be ironed to sit flat. I chose not to iron mine.

The BIG NEGATIVE for me about this apron is the design. There is only one long strap holding the apron on. There's a channel on each side of the chest area through which the one strap is looped through like an upside down U going from one side of the body to the other. As a result, to enlarge the neck strap, I just have to pull up on the strap and that reduces the tying ability of the remaining length along the back. The strap is long enough so that does not matter, but what matters is that any movement after it's tied has a strong potential to pull down in the neck area. After wearing this apron for a while, I absolutely hate it because the strap around the neck which adjusts with how you tie it in the back, causes me to have a neck ache EVERY SINGLE TIME I USE THIS. It is only for this reason that I rated this 2 stars. If there were four straps (one on either side of the neck and one on either side of the back), this apron would have received 4 stars from me. It would have received 5 stars if they also put the pockets lower. This apron as it stands now is not usable to me.

Very thin throw that feels scratchy like sisal rope and is poorly made. This throw is thin, scratchy, and poorly made. It feels like it is weaved of sisal rope. I have cats and they would love to scratch this if given the chance.

The throw arrived with pulls already in the fabric--see first picture. In addition, the stitching is loose and disheveled as can be seen from the second photo.

Although the color is an attractive pale blue and the tassels add a decorative touch, I cannot recommend this and think even $5 is too much to pay.

What I received is super large and does not have vented lids as specified but it's functional. I ordered this because the XL shape of these was supposed to be more taller than long. Also the lids were supposed to be vented. Even though this is a great set, it is not what is advertised.

Note that I already have two of the smaller long containers and they are fantastic for holding soups and then squeezing it into the fridge on top of other stuff as a result of the low profile size (meaning not that tall). The larger bin is large enough to store a pair of boots and is great for holding batches of cookies, pasta, etc.

I would have rated this 1 star because it was not what I ordered. Nevertheless, this does not take away from the functionality or quality of this set even if it is not as advertised. Note that it is a bit difficult to secure the lids and they fasten tightly. If it were as advertised, I would have given this 4 or 5 stars.

This teapot arrived without a lid and there is no customer service or manufacturer to contact. This teapot seems nice but it arrived without a lid and I cannot use it effectively as a result. Also, there is no customer service. I tried the warranty and support section of the Amazon product page but only got a message to "Please contact the seller directly for warranty information for this product. You may also be able to find warranty information on the manufacturer’s website." I was unable to find a manufacturer site and have not had any luck contacting Amazon--at least not yet.

I will update my review if I have any resolution to this missing part but as it stands now, this is another item that is ready to be thrown out and a loss of money. I am thoroughly dissappointed because this looks like a nice pot.

I have some food storage containers that are Miocaro and they are five stars. Unfortunately, if a product is shipped with missing parts, no matter how good the product could be, it becomes a useless or almost useless product when pieces are missing.

Fragrance is overpowering and headache producing; this is liquid free. This is totally not what I expected. First of all, I thought it was a liquid diffuser but I did not read the label correctly.  Secondly, the scent is so overpowering, that I have a headache as a result and the reeds are in a different room.

This comes with a small white loop which looks like a napkin ring. There are a total of six reeds which is equivalent to "two servings" with each serving of three reeds lasting up to 40 days. When the reeds lose their fragrance, throw them out and insert the next set.

I do not know if I am going to throw this out or not. Right now the fragrance has not dissipated after 24  hours. One more thing, when inserting the reeds into the holder, it is impossible not to touch them. My fingers felt irritated (burning) just from setting this up. I immediately washed my hands with soap and water. Since I have cats, I put this in a place far away from them. I attached a picture of the ingredients which has a skin irritation warning associated with it.

The only thing this has going for it is the stylishness of the diffuser with the reeds. Other than this, I hate this.

Utterly disastrous poached eggs; this gets an F minus from me. I cannot believe I have to pay for this. This is not worth more than 50 cents.

This comes in three pieces. The yellow silicone cover on the handle, the frame itself with the egg well, and the silicone "bowl or rim." 

After washing for first use, submerge this poacher in boiling water up to rim of poacher and pour egg from a prep bowl into the egg well once the water begins to swirl. Cook for 2-4 minutes, drain, and serve.

It seems easy (see first four photos for instructions) but it is not.  First of all, when the water was ready, I poured the egg into the poacher and after a few seconds white foam (from the egg white) coagulated in the water. Once the egg was cooked, I gently lifted this from the pot. However, the yellow silicone handle kept sliding off so I had to keep re-attaching it. I finally squeezed it tightly while lifting the handle so it woud not fall off again. After the "egg well" drained as I lifted it from the pot, I turned over the poacher to release the egg.

Good luck. The egg is stuck relatively solid to the egg well. Only the yolk and top part of the egg white slipped out. I had to use a spoon to extricate the rest and it left some concrete residue behind.

I wanted to do another egg but the previous event clogged all the vents in the poacher.  It took me a couple of hours of soaking the poacher in Dawn Platinium and scrubbing it for about 15 minutes to remove the "concrete" residue. Not only was this a tremendous amout of work but it was not easy to remove the silicone rim from the poacher for washing and re-assembling.

In summary, this is an absolutely awful poacher. It would be best to just crack the egg into boiling water with vinegar and then removing it with a slotted spoon. I am glad I used a non-stick pan or I would have been scrubbing that into the wee hours.

THE VERDICT - This gets an F minus. Use only if you want to spend hours extracting one poached egg and working on the cleanup.

Sizing is all wrong and sham does not have a large enough lip to cover the pillow correctly. I am utterly disappointed in these pillowcases. First of all, I have a king-sized bed with king-sized pillows and some standard pillows. I ordered these in a king. However, the fit is a small standard and it is not even a good fit because the flap of the sham has too tiny a pocket to fit over the end of the pillow. Another negative is that these show and hold onto a lot of lint and cat hair.

Per my Internet search, these are the typical pillow sizes and the cases should be equivalent.

Standard Pillow Size 20" x 26"
Super Standard Pillow Size 20" x 28"
Queen Pillow Size 20" x 30"
King Pillow Size 20" x 36"

The box says these are King sized at 20" x 26" which is a full 10" shorter than needed. As can be seen in the photo, my king-sized pillow comes beyond the case. In the other photo, my standard pillow is even peeking out due to the cuff pocket being way too short.

The only thing good about these cases is the color and the feel. However, these are not functional due to the odd sizing and lack of correct pocket size for the end of the sham. The current price of $29.99 is outrageous for a substandard product. If it were perfect in sizing and sham pocket, then I would have rated this 5 stars and considered the price competitive.

Low quality throw with bald patches. This red and black plaid throw is pretty and it feels velvety. It is thin like all other throws. Unfortunately, I am so sorry I ordered it as it is not worth what I will be paying for it.

This is a standard-sized throw but there are bald patches and lint throughout the entire throw as can be seen from the photos. I personally feel this is not worth more than $12 as the quality is substandard. I am sorry I believed the five star ratings of other reviewers at the time I decided to order this.

Terrible design; otherwise tape picks up lint as good as others. I hate this set of rollers. There are two handles and six rolls. The two handles are installed in two of the rolls and have to be removed once the roll is done to use on the other rolls.

The handles themselves are delicate and I can see the bottom breaking before all the tape is used up.

What I absolutely hate about this set is that it is practically IMPOSSIBLE to remove the label on the roller. I had to remove mine in pieces and had to actually use a scissor to start cutting it off. It took me about 5 minutes to get the label off and it wasted a couple of sheets.  Second, once the label is off, there is nothing to cover the roller for storage.  The Scotch-Brite lint rollers always have a label that can be slapped back on when the roller is not in use. It kept sticking to everything as I have nothing to cover it with. In addition, the handle kept coming apart (see photo). The handle actually has to be seated well within the tube for this not to happen.

I did use the tape and it works very well. It picks up just as good as my favorite brand (Scotch-Brite). I also love that the tape removes on an angle. It is a lot easy to peel off the used tape that way. In this sense, it is actually a better design than my favorite brand.

There are supposedly a total of 120 sheets over 6 rolls, which means there are 20 sheets per roll. This would have gotten 4 stars from me if the label peeled off easily and was used to protect the tape when not in use. As it stands now, I hate this set.

Wall mounted soap dispenser will not dispense soap; it went into the garbage. About two years ago I ordered a $28 automatic soap dispenser. For weeks I tried to put up with it but It barely would dispense soap that I eventually threw it out. I had such a bad experience that it has taken me a couple of years before I decided to try this one that came up for review. After trying to get this to work for over 30 minutes, this also went into the garbage as per my experience below.

This is a wall-mounted dispenser. A key is needed to keep the top closed. Two keys, two mounting screws, and 3 extra nozzles come with this dispenser. It requires 4 AA batteries (NOT INCLUDED). The batteries get inserted in the back and there is an ON/OFF switch below the battery compartment. This means it has to be taken off the wall to change the batteries or turn the unit ON or OFF (should one be going away for a while and want it OFF).

I decided to test this before mounting to a wall and lucky I did. After inserting the batteries, I filled it partway, struggled to get the key lock to work to keep the lid closed, turned the unit ON in the back after inserting the batteries, and then engaged the unit. Since air can be in the line, I tried about 30 times to get the soap to dispense and nothing would come out. I even pulled out the nozzle and reinserted it. I had to pull out the nozzle with an open scissor because it was impossible to remove. The green foaming nozzle would not insert into the hole so I just reseated the one that came with it. At one point soap started to leak out of the seam in the back but it would never dispense it through the nozzle.

The instructions are not great but they are still somewhat understandable. After trying for over 30 minutes, I gave up. Besides not dispensing soap, the key lock is difficult to operate and very sticky and there does not seem to be any way to insert the green foaming nozzle if that is desired. The exit hole is just too small. However, these are moot points since after flushing all air from the lines, the soap would not dispense and then started to leak out of the seam in the back. It went right in the garbage.

Like tying my hair with telephone cord. There are eight spiral ties in this package. They also do not look exactly the same size and one of them is a different color brown. However, these do not work like the great [[ASIN:B08HQYH3H Goomee Spiral Hair Ties]] I love.

These feel like I am tying up my hair with telephone cord. It is difficult to use these and not that easy to remove. Also, they do not hold well. I personally do not like these at all.

Fragrance is subtle; guess these are not large enough because they do nothing for me. There are 32 rounds in this package and all but one had a hole in them for installation on a hanger. I think the one without the holes was a mistake. The cedar is so subtle that I have to put it directly under my nose to smell it. I have to put one on every hanger in order to get the full cedar effect. I expected a stronger fragrance. I had a cedar closet years ago and the fragrance was overwhelming but that was probably because the entire closet was made out of cedar. I guess I expected the same.

These can be put in boots, clothes drawers, etc. However, I tried them in all of my drawers (about five to a drawer) and there is no smell or aromatics at all. I am very disappointed in these and am sorry I ordered three boxes.

Barely does the job pitting cherries; although pits Bing cherries better. The purpose of this "industrial-sized" Leifheit cherry pitter is to be able to pit many cherries quickly without having to "reload" a cherry into the pitting chamber. I figured the need for a lot of pitted cherries when making pies or a large fruit salad would make such a gargantuan unit worthwhile. I already have the exceptionally designed and almost flawless [[ASIN:B000NQ925K OXO Good Grips Cherry Pitter]] but when this unit came became available, I felt it was worth trying out.

The unit comes with two rubber washers; one is a spare. What I had to do was remove the cardboard piece holding down the plunger arm and insert the rubber gasket into the slot. This gasket is needed to prevent the cherry pit from coming back into the cherry after I pulled up on the plunger. For my test, I tried to pit both the firmer Rainier cherries and the less firm Bing cherries with this cherry pitter. Even though the instructions do not mention pitting olives with this cherry stoner, I decided to try small black Kalamata olives as well--since my other cherry pitter can pit soft olives like this.

I loaded the Rainier cherries into the hopper and they didn't really line up in the pitting chamber; sometimes they had to be pushed into the hole for pitting. Once I pushed the plunger, I had to pull up fully to release the pitted cherry into the exit shoot. Of about 50 Rainer cherries I pitted many were damaged on the exit (partially squished or broken) and all but about 4 had the pits remain in the cherry. For the cherries that exited into the waiting bowl, I had to pry open the cherry to remove the pits. I then tried pitting about 50 sweet cherries and they pitted easier since they were softer cherries. However, I still had some squished cherries exit the hopper and about 6 of the cherries that exited had pits that had to be pulled out by hand. Since I also wanted to know if olives would work, I tried about 4 of them and found out quickly this unit cannot pit olives.

As I was washing the unit I noted that the washer was destroyed just from pitting these few cherries. It appears the plunger not only pitted my cherries but also chopped out part of the washer. When I inserted the washer, I made sure it was centered and that the pitter blade passed cleanly through the center of the washer's hole. However, with all the cherry pitting activity it probably moved around and caused large holes in the washer. Not only does this reduce the effectiveness of the pitting but I had to throw out the washer and put in the spare.

In summary, I cannot recommend this cherry pitter to anyone. The only redeeming quality it has are the rubber feet on the bottom of the unit that keeps the cherry pitter base firmly in place during pitting. Other than this, the unit is too huge. The pitting chamber so enormous compared to the hopper you put the cherries in. Also the plunger cannot be locked down for storage and stands at attention like a rocket about to take off. The pitter barely pits Bing cherries (the dark colored ones with a firm but softer flesh) and has a 95% failure rate when pitting Rainier cherries. I had high hopes for this cherry stoner and was sadly disappointed. I was going to give this unit 1 star but since it did pit the Bing cherries somewhat, I rated this 2 stars. I have not decided yet whether I'm going to send this to the recycling bin or keep it as a conversation piece, but I doubt I'll ever use this to pit cherries again.

Urn is the size of a thimble; will only hold a small fraction of ashes; inscription is too tiny. One would think this is a necklace with how small this urn is. This will only hold a thimbleful of ashes. The inscription on the front is microscopic and definitely not as clear as the Amazon site shows. It says "God has you in his arms I have you in my heart" and there is a heart image on either side of the word "heart." 

In this package are three cleaning cloths, a plastic spoon to scoop in the ashes, a  pouch for the urn, and the tiny thimble-sized urn. Also, the urn is not shiny and clear as pictured on Amazon. It is not great at all.

To me this is not worth the purchase.

Great idea but does not work well in practice; I’m sorry I ordered this. The idea behind this clip is to insert the cup like rim into a plastic bag and then wrap the bag around it and clip it closed. However, in practice this does not work well at all.

This separates into two parts. I followed the instructions as per the video but found that the clip is almost impossible to close once the bag is wrapped around it and I tried a thin biodegradable bag. Also, the flip top is almost impossible to snap shut. In addition, unless the bag has a very narrow top, the act of folding it causes the contents to be difficult to dispense because of all the creases in the bag.

I think this is a great idea but is just not functional in practice and is way too cumbersome to use. This is another item for the garbage. I am so sorry I purchased this, even though my purchase winds up being at a discount. I am so disappointed.

Easy to assemble but super flimsy and rips easily. There are 24 boxes in 4 designs with 8 of each design. Assembly is easy but there are no instructions. Unfortunately, the boxes are so flimsy that they do not even hold themselves up. They are not airtight. In addition, the locking mechanism broke immediately as can be seen in the photo. These are NOT worth the purchase in my opinion. They are somewhat usable but they will have to be taped around all the sides. The current price of $16.79 ($23.99 minus 30%) comes to $.70 cents per box.

This pepper mill needs improvement. This pepper mill is not only for wealthy consumers looking for another way to spend their money. It can be a medical aid in some cases for those with hand problems. I have no objection to a high-priced automatic pepper mill because those who have hand problems (arthritis, carpel tunnel, one arm or hand, etc.) will find it possible to now grind pepper and coriander without difficulty or pain. After all I purchased a $200 [[ASIN:B000A76VCY Breville 800CPXL Die-Cast Stainless-Steel Motorized Citrus Press]] just to reduce the hand stress I was experiencing with squeezing lemons and limes which I absolutely love and believe it was money well spent.

However, this pepper mill is not in the same league. I expected an elite "machine" that worked simply and well and here's what I got.

In the box is one large pepper mill that is mostly all motor. It comes with a small container of peppercorns and what looks like a square base on which the pepper mill should rest when not in use. (NOTE - It slips easily off this base if that is what it was designed for.) There are also 6 AAA batteries included.

The pepper mill has to be disassembled to load the peppercorns and also to extract the motor and load the batteries. Extracting the motor was incredibly cumbersome. There are 2 sliding levers on the inside plate that have to be shifted toward the inside of the motor with a pencil or file. In the process, my levers bent and almost broke off (so they are shoddy levers). Once the levers are no longer holding the motor in place, the unit has to be lightly shaken to dislodge the motor. It took a while for it to dislodge. Once the motor is removed, the batteries were easy to insert and the direction of insertion (negative and positive) were clearly marked.

After battery installation, I had to reverse the entire process. Inserting the motor is tricky as well as I had to line up certain parts, then push down the motor, and re-seat the levers out and under the base lip.

The top of the vessel holding the peppercorns that came with this product also acts also like funnel. I had to unscrew the top and punch out the center piece then lay this over the peppercorn reservoir to fill it. Once that was done. I screwed the holder to the base. (NOTE - Save the container that came with the peppercorns because it is a measuring cup for refilling the reservoir.)

As per the manual, only black, white, and green (dry) peppercorns of 5 mm (0.2") or less should be used in this mill for optimal performance. It also grinds pink peppercorns as long as the pink ones are no more than 15% of the peppercorns being ground. In addition, it grinds dry coriander seeds.

There are six (6) gradations of grind (from fine to coarse) marked on the bottom dial. Based on my tests (since the instructions are not clear on this), it appears the single horizontal line indicates a fine grind and as the lines increase in number to six (6) lines that indicates a coarser grind. The grind level is set by turning the dial to line up the desired grind lines with the letter P written on the reservoir (which is difficult to see).

To dispense the pepper, I just lightly touched the "button" on the top of the base to activate the motor. A light comes on and then dispenses the pepper according to the grind level set. The mill grinds quickly and well. Since the unit engages the motor easily, it means if one of my cats touches the top, the pepper will also grind.

In summary, had I paid for this product, I would have sent it back for a refund. The batteries are too difficult to get to, the levers holding the motor in place are poor quality and easily broken, there is no shutoff for the motor once the batteries are installed so the slightest touch of the button grinds pepper, and it does not feel like the elite "machine" I expected. Also, the lifetime warranty is on the motor only and no other part. If this grinder came with USB or other rechargeable and easy to insert batteries, had the ability to turn off the motor, felt like a quality kitchen tool, and the instructions were clearer (five languages follow each instruction) then I would have given this 5 stars. As it stands now, I consider this a working prototype only and not a kitchen tool that should be sold for such a high price.

Horrible canning experience; rims are "sticky"; golden lids don't seal; stick with Ball. This is a 40-pack set of mason jars with:
- 30 sliver lids with rims
- 10 golden lids with rims
- 1 tiny brush
- 40 chalkboard labels with chalk marker

I only ever used Ball jars, lids, and rims in the past and now I know why. I had an opportunity to try this and CANNOT recommend them.

I spent hours water bath canning only to discover that the golden lids DO NOT SEAL at all--that is 25% of the jars. In the fourth photo, the gold rim and lid is to the left of the picture. The silver lids appear to seal but the rims on about 90% of the jars are almost impossible to screw on. They are very sticky. After having the bad experience with the golden lids and using 14 of the jars with lids and rims, I decided to use my Ball canning set instead . When using a Ball rim, they glide on these jars. I have a funny feeling that because the rims are so bad, that the seal is broken periodically as a result of unscrewing the rim and checking if the lid is holding. For the golden lids, they just do not seal at all, whether the rims are good or not.

I see no reason for the tiny brush. The 40 chalkboard labels are very nice as they cover the entire lid and peel off and stick on easily (seventh photo). The chalk marker is okay. The jars themselves are good. If you find yourself stuck with this garbage, just go out and buy Ball lids and rims that will fit these jars and they will become usable. I do not trust these lids and rims at all--TERRIBLE.

If sealing a jar during canning is not a concern, then these jars, lids, and rims are usable even if the rim is hard to screw on. However, I only use canning jars for hot water bath canning, so I have to throw out all these lids and rims.

I would personally never buy this set after having tried it. The free brush, labels, and marker can always be purchased separately. Stick with Ball which is priced not much more than this and works every time.

Good Ziplock bag organizer ruined by etched in company logo; also back has a crack; PRICEY. This is what could have been a good four-compartment organizer for different types of Ziplock bags (quart, gallon, sandwich, and snack) except that the vendor label is etched into the bamboo just like the bag labels are etched into the bamboo. This is a BIG NEGATIVE for me as it makes the unit look like garbage. Second, there is a crack along the backboard of the unit (see photo).

This organizer opens via a hinge from the clip in the front so that the bags can be loaded easily in addition to being able to load them through the holes. This can be hung on the wall or be placed in a drawer that is large enough to hold it. Rubberized circles are provided which I installed. This keeps this from sliding around or scratching a drawer or wall. Three screws with plastic mollies are also provided for hanging.

Overall, this is a good organizer that does away with all those squished and ugly boxes in my cabinets. I would have rated this 4 stars but the vendor name etched into the bamboo, the crazy price, as well as the crack in the back, has me taking off two additional stars. The vendor label irks me the most as the crack is small. They should have a removable stick-on label on the back instead if they need to advertise their product. Also, the current price of $39.99 is also ridiculously expensive. In fact, this price is about $10 more than comparable units sell for on the market.

There are many other Ziplock bag organizer options available such as this [[ASIN:B09KMNHM2J one]] or this [[ASIN:B09VGP1WRL one]]. For one full unit only, then I recommend this [[ASIN:B09RF759BM rustic organizer]]. For a more modern look, I recommend this [[ASIN:B09WN5PZ6Q one]] or an individual heavy plastic set like [[ASIN:B09THNTBGX this]]. For a cheaper unit that has room for foil and plastic wrap, then I highly recommend this [[ASIN:B0B1TPD21S one]] but no screws are provided with that one. I tried all of these and the style purchased is based on what one desires. I personally like these other ones a lot better than this one.

Poorly made bag organizer; strips of edging peeled off. This is a poorly constructed four-compartment Ziplock bag organizer with one opening each for different types of bags such as quart, gallon, sandwich, and snack bags. The unit is hinged, so it can be unlocked in the front. This can be hung on the wall or be placed in a drawer that is large enough to hold it. There are two screws with plastic mollies provided but I only recommend securing it to a stud. There are also some rubberized "circles" on the bottom to keep it from sliding around a drawer. The clip closure allows one to open the entire unit to install the bags. However, I find it is just as easy to insert the bags through their holes as long as I am not filling with too many bags.

Unfortunately, this is so poorly made I cannot recommend it. First, the interior has gouges on the inside. Second, they put their lousy name on the front and it isn't even done well. I do not want the name Fozobaiy on the top of the gallon compartment. In fact, I don't want to see the name at all. Third, the edging of the container peeled off. It is as if this is laminate instead of wood. This is an embarrassment.

Overall, this is a lousy bag organizer of substandard quality. The current price of $39.99 is outrageous for this quality. Other options that are available are this [[ASIN:B09D5Y63D1 one]] if one is looking for four separate compartments. For a variety of organizers (separate and one unit), then I recommend this [[ASIN:B09KMNHM2J one]] or this [[ASIN:B09VGP1WRL one]]. For one full unit only, then I recommend this [[ASIN:B09RF759BM rustic organizer]]. I tried all of these and the style purchased is based on what one desires.

Terribly designed Ziplock bag organizers to put in a drawer or on a counter; cannot be hung. This is a terribly designed Ziplock bag organizer that comes in four separate compartments with one each for quart, gallon, sandwich, and snack bags. Since this is not one unit, it cannot be hung on the wall. There are felt feet on the underside of the boxes for when it is placed on the counter or in a drawer. However, the beauty of this design is that each compartment can be configured anyway one desires. They can go in several separate drawers or in an L shape in one drawer, or side-by-side, etc.

Unfortunately, the design is terrible. First of all, I can easily load the bags through the large opening but it is designed for the bottom to slide out. This means if I turn over the compartment to load the bags from the bottom, the bags start to fall out of the top. In addition, the bottom is so loosely seated, it slides off if I am not careful when I pick up the compartment. If the bottom does slide off, they also have to be put back a certain way. If I accidentally use the top end and slide it in using the bottom side, it only slides halfway because each end is cut differently.

Personally, this set is a disappointment. No wonder it is so cheap at $17.99. Even though I love the way this keeps all my plastic bags in order, I cannot recommend it. Other options that are available for organizers like this are this [[ASIN:B09D5Y63D1 one]] if one is looking for four separate compartments. For a variety of organizers (separate and one unit), then I recommend this [[ASIN:B09KMNHM2J one]] or this [[ASIN:B09VGP1WRL one]]. For one full unit only, then I recommend this [[ASIN:B09RF759BM rustic organizer]]. For a more modern look, I recommend this [[ASIN:B09WN5PZ6Q one]]. For a larger unit that has room for foil and plastic wrap, then I highly recommend this [[ASIN:B0B1TPD21S one]]. I tried all of these and the style purchased is based on what one desires. I personally like these other ones a little better than this one.

Functional but FLAWED Ziplock bag organizer to hang on a wall or put in a drawer; hardware incl. This would have been a great five-compartment organizer to store different types of Ziplock bags (quart, gallon, sandwich, and snack) and a roll of either foil, plastic wrap, or wax paper. Unfortunately, it has three design flaws.

FLAWS

- First, mine arrived with a crack in the base (see photo).

Produces mild heat on highest setting; arrived with black smudges on top; initial use has heat smell. This deep pocket heated mattress pad for a king-sized bed is like a heating pad. There are two controls that plug in on the top of the mattress cover and have settings for warm, low, medium, and high heat. The warm setting is the default. I could not feel much heat from any of the settings except for the high setting. The high setting provided a very low and very nice warmth. There are two controls; one for each side of the bed. There is a slight heat smell during first use.

I have a king sized bed that has a tall mattress with a topper. I require 16" deep pockets and the pockets on this are large enough to handle that even though there is nothing on the packaging that says that. This cover works (longevity unknown) but the CONS make this a pass for me.

PROS
- It provides a nice light heat on the highest setting that apparently shuts off after 10 hours. I did not test the 10-hour shutoff as I'm rarely in bed for more than 6 hours.

- There are two controls for both sides of the bed so the other bed partner can select a different heat setting.

- The mattress pad is attractive and comfortable to lay on (except for the area with the plugs).

- It has deep pockets for a tall king-size mattress and fits up to my mattress pocket size of 16".

CONS
- The electrical connection should have been located on the headboard side of the pad and only on the rim (meaning pocket side) of the pad. Currently, the connection is located at the foot of the mattress pad (based on the label). Of course, I can turn the label upside down and face the connection toward the top (which is what I did to access an electric socket); however, the plug on both sides is on the top and can be felt as a lump if laying down in that area.

- The pad I received arrived with black smudges as if someone walked on the mattress pad. When I order a new product, I expect to receive it in pristine condition.

- There was some cotton sticking out of the trim (see photo). This is a minor detail and can just be cut off, but it is another sign of sloppiness.

- Although the elastic section (pockets) fit over my mattress, the elastic is not gripping enough. This means, it is easy for the mattress pad to slide off the mattress unless I sandwich the remaining cloth between the mattress and the box spring.

- There is a bit of a heat smell during first use; not much but is to be expected.

- This unit has to be unplugged daily as there is no shutoff except for the claim that it shuts off after 10 hours, which I did not test.

- I would not count on being able to wash this successfully. It says I can wash this in a machine for 5 min but I personally wouldn't do that. I would suggest spot cleaning if needed.

In summary, this mattress pad works to produce very low heat on the highest setting. It will fit a king-sized bed with 16" to perhaps 17" deep pockets but the elastic is too loose to keep it on the bed unless it is wedged between the mattress and box spring. The location of the plugs is a problem and the dirty topper I received is an utter disappointment. The current price of $33.99 ($39.99 minus 15%) is very reasonable for this. A mattress pad without any heat for a king-sized bed is usually priced much higher. My recommendation is to pass on this pad and buy flannel sheets for the winter that keep one warm and toasty under the blankets. If a heated mattress pad is desired, I would say to look elsewhere.

Meater plus. UPDATE below: Original review - I have longed to try one of these of many different brands. After research and reading dozens and dozens of reviews, I landed on the Meater Plus. One thing I would note - I was going for a medium rare - and "upped" the suggested temp of 135 to 140 because I was nervous... the Meater Plus counts the resting time in the finished temp! So, I ended up with a little to the medium than to the medium rare. I am going to trust the Meater Plus next time. It notifies you of when to take your food out and then reminds you when the resting is done. You can follow the progress on the app on your phone. Nice long wide slots, but only toasts one side. T-fal customer service confirmed toaster not functioning properly.. Original Review 4/29/2015: This toaster has huge slots. Very easily fits 4 slices of American supermarket sliced bread. Would be great for bagels. I want the long slots for toasting longer, thicker pieces of decent bread. As other reviewers have stated, the cord does come out from the right side of the unit near the front. That placement is a bit odd. See third photo.

In all likelihood, you will have to flip your toast around to get the machine to toast both sides of your bread. The heating elements only glow red on the sides of the toaster. The heating elements on the inside panel don't come on, regardless of heat setting. See first two photos - taken at highest heat setting of 8.

I have not encountered any issues with beeping or smoking. The lift feature just lifts the bread a fraction of an inch. I still use wooden toaster tongs to grab my bread. If the heating elements on the center panel actually came on, I would probably give this 5 stars ---- so far...

Updated Review 4/30/2015: I was concerned about the one sided toasting and called T-fal customer service. The customer service representative informed me that the heating coils on the inside panel should come on unless the toaster is set to bagel. The toaster I received (and probably some of the units received by other reviewers) is defective. I have changed my rating to one star.

In addition, it seems that I am not the first person to receive this particular toaster. The toaster was only cushioned by foam on one end and there was space in the box for cushioning on the other end. There was an extra plastic bag in the box and there was no manual or warranty information inside the box. Looks like Amazon shipped out a toaster that had been returned by another customer.

There are 10 heat settings that range from 68-122 degrees as well as 10 auto-turn off energy saving settings that last from 1-10 hours.
