Our Bad Tasting Water is Still Bad...No Improvement While Using the Brita Pitcher. 10 years ago, we moved into a new home. At our old home, we had the BEST tap water ever. There was absolutely no need for us to buy bottled water, our tap water was that good and refreshing. At our new and current home, we had a different water provider. Gone was our delicious tap water. It was replaced with awful tasting water. Our home has a whole home water softener. But its a waste. It doesn't help at all. Our tap water is still awful. It leaves blue-green rings in the toilet bowl, bathtub and on the dishes back when we still used the dishwasher. (Dishwasher broke, never replaced it as I don't mind doing dishes by hand) Of course the water company says the water is at an acceptable quality. Less than two years after we moved into this home, our normally healthy dog got terribly sick and had to be put to sleep . He was in full kidney failure. He never had any problems before. We've gone through 3 hot water heaters in the 10 years that we've lived here. When we moved to this home, we brought our almost 3 year old washing machine along. It stopped working less than 2 years after moving here. All of these things could, of course, be coincidence. But its my belief all of these things are due to our terrible water. Weeks after we lost our dog, a spring water stand was built close to our home. From that moment on, we completely stopped using tap water for drinking/cooking and began to use ONLY spring water. (Still had to use tap water to bathe, etc) And we only give our pets spring water to drink as well.

I was anxious to try the Brita pitcher. I hoped that it would make our tap water taste better and we'd be able to drink it. I had no problems whatsoever with the pitcher, it was easy to use. But we just did NOT notice any kind of new or better taste to our tap water that was in the Brita pitcher. My husband and I think the tap water from the pitcher tastes the same way our tap water has always tasted . There is no improvement. The Brita pitcher didn't work for us.

I have owned two of these microwave ovens. The first time, the doorlatch failed after 16 months â€“ four months beyond the warranty period. The second model just failed this week, four months after purchase. The problem was exactly the same both times â€“ a doorlatch that becomes increasingly difficult to engage when you close the door, finally failing entirely to engage. The result is that the microwave will not turn on no matter what you do.

I just did a broad Internet search, and I have learned that Panasonic microwaves of various models are absolutely plagued with door latch failure. Sites from Consumer Reports to Panasonic's own review site are all choked with complaints about precisely the kind of doorlatch failure I experienced twice.

It is astounding that Panasonic continues to manufacture microwaves with this faulty design. It is also astounding that Panasonic has never recalled its microwave doorlatches and replaced them at its own expense, regardless of warranty period (although this would likely be economically disastrous for the company, given how many of these defective devices is it has sold).

Both times I have owned this model, I have admired every aspect of its performance except for the fact that the lifespan of the model is measurable in months. A Panasonic microwave would be a good choice for you only if you are fine about replacing your microwave (or going through the hassle of a warranty repair, if you are lucky) at least once a year. I am now investigating commercial models. These have fewer bells and whistles, but are built for hard use and long life.

Learn from my mistake. Don't do it! Read all of the innumerable other reviews regarding the defective doorlatches on Panasonic residential microwave ovens. The Internet is literally clogged with bad reviews relating to this issue. And when the doorlatch fails, the oven is inoperable, period. You will find those reviews not only on Amazon but also on many other websites, including Panasonic's own website. On my first Panasonic residential model, the Prestige Genius model here, the doorlatch failed after 16 months. On my second Panasonic (identical) residential model, the doorlatch failed in only four months. To get a sense of the extent of the problem, simply google the following phrase: "Panasonic microwave door latch."

Panasonic residential-level microwave ovens are a good choice only if you want to replace your oven frequently. All of the very wonderful features of this oven end up meaning nothing, because the door latch is junky and destined to fail early. (Planned obsolescence?)

After spending hours researching other residential microwave brands and finding other serious problems relating to durability, and after learning that literally 50% of residential microwaves, regardless of the brand, are made in just one factory in China -- with virtually identical or identical internal parts -- I have moved on to commercial grade. The ordinary pull handle on most commercial models is much more reliable than a push-button system. A commercial grade microwave will not have all of the bells and whistles of a residential model, but it will be built for durability, and you can get a good one for $250 - 325.

After numerous bad experiences with residential models failing way too soon, durability is all I care about at this point.

Good Quality Heater- Not as good as I was hoping. When my two 21 year old ceramic heaters started showing signs of failing I started hunting for new ones. After a long and arduous search I decided to give this one a try. I am very glad I did. We have a living room that is about 400 sq ft. that opens to both a sun room and the kitchen, about 900 sq ft total. This heater was able to keep the entire area in the upper 60s when it was below freezing outside, no sunshine. It took 1 hour to heat this area from 58 to 68. I do believe if this was utilized in a closed area of 400 to 500 sq ft., it would be more than adequate.

The construction is pure and simple. It uses a small blower similar to what is used in your furnace to distribute the heat. It is much quieter than fan driven heaters, has a higher cfm (cubic feet per minute) output and the delivery of the heat is very warm, and "softer" than fan driven models. It tends to make a sizable area around it feel cozy as best as I can describe it. When plugged in and turned on high it doesn't seem to have any more loading on the circuit than a standard hair dryer. It is much more efficient in producing and distributing 1500W worth of heating than anything I've ever seen.

The unit does remain cool to the touch except one small area above the heater core on top where you might describe it as barely warm. The filter on the back is basically a hair screen, not a dust filter. The power cord is 6 foot long, adequately sized, with a standard 3 prong outlet connection. The casters are adequate for hard flooring, not carpet. But the unit itself does not feel like it is over 20 lbs. to me. The remote is cute.

I'll be curious to see the electric bill. We are now successfully using this one 1500W heater to warm the same area it required two 1500W ceramics to heat previously. My only last concern would be with longevity. With a 3 year warranty I expect with normal care and maintenance (cleanings) this heater should be around a long time. I will update if I run into any problems.

UPDATE 2-17-2014: This unit is now failing. It still produces heat on the Lo setting, but produces much less on the Hi side then when new. Now the high and low side are producing an equal amount of heat. The unit has been subjected to no rough handling whatsoever. The filter has been cleaned exactly as recommended. I can only conclude that something inside the unit has failed. Considering this unit has a 3 year warranty and has displayed a failure within 4 months is quite irritating. I will be inquiring how much this would cost me to ship it back to the manufacturer for repairs, but no matter what the cost I find failure within this short of a time span pathetic, thus I have revised my rating on this product. With this kind of performance I could NOT RECOMMEND purchasing this product based on longevity.

Problem #2: the seat fabric is not "grippy" they way it should be on a chair with strong back support. This means when the back support presses against your back (as it should), the result is predictable: you slide forward on the seat. This is *really* uncool. The only way to fix this is to adjust the tension in the back support (how strongly the seat back pushes against your back) to the point where it is no longer supportive. This would be almost manageable if the seat depth were sufficient, which is sadly is not (see next paragraph).

Problem #3: Seat depth. This is by far the biggest issue. The seat depth is listed as adjustable and if you go to the Steelcase site they have videos showing you how to adjust everything. The thing is, the normal seat depth adjustment does not apply to the big and tall version of this chair, which they do not tell you in the product listing. The seat depth adjustment control mechanism is simply ...not there. But wait - it gets better...

As the depth adjustment mechanism is apparently not installed on the big & tall version of this chair, it came with a card attached explaining that to adjust the depth on the seat, the chair has to be flipped over so you can remove the screws holding the seat to the base and reposition it to another of the available pre-drilled hole locations--a very manual process involving lifting up and inverting a 74 lb chair onto a work surface without damaging the arms. Once this feat is accomplished (careful you do not hurt your back; I recommend using use a narrow armless chair to flip it over onto so the arms can hang down over the sides), it becomes apparent there is a serious depth problem. The line of pre-drilled holed only allow you to move the seat cushion backwards, not forwards. This means the seat is adjustable in only one direction: you can make it shallower, not deeper. The seat is attached to the base at the furthest forward setting at the factory--there is nowhere to move it to, except further back, which is not helpful.

Net result: If you are 5"11 or more, and have average-length legs (as do I), the seat depth will be insufficient. Add this to the fact that the fabric is not grippy enough to hold you in place, and yes, you guessed it--you slide forward off the seat, repeatedly, all day long. Even if you adjust the seat cushion angle to tilt rearward to help offset the forward slide, as I have, the lack of depth is still a big problem (and this is not ergonomically sound anyway). I slide forward all day unless I wear pants which generate a lot of friction (forget about wearing dress slacks).

Additionally, and this is a little odd, I think my chair is defective in another way: the line of holes on the bottom of the seat where you screw the base onto the seat is not straight--they are not at a 90-degree angle to the front/rear direction of the seat, and seem to be a couple degrees off to the right. The net result here is the seat cushion is not facing directly forwards, but turned slightly to the right. The effect is the seatback presses more firmly on the left side of my back than the right, as it is obviously attached to the base of the chair, not the seat.

Additionally, the seat back cushion is separating from the back, as though it is coming unglued (photo attached).

End result: this chair is a disaster, and while it seems very sturdy, it is very uncomfortable. Definitely not recommended for anyone who properly qualifies as big & tall. Or who expects a high quality chair commensurate with the price of this one. I just got it and I already need to replace it. :(

Bilt by stoopid enguneers. The basic things I need in a toaster are:
1. Four slice at a time capacity
2. Wide enough slots for bagels or thick slices of bread
3. Cancel button to stop toasting when necessary
4. Cool-touch sides
5. Crumb tray for cleaning
6. Aesthetically pleasing design

This model has all of the above, so I should be ecstatically happy, except:
1. Due to a design oversight, the toasted product doesn't pop up far enough to allow you to remove it without risking burns or serious injury. Forget toasting smaller items like English muffins or waffles that are slightly bent out of shape.
2. The "frozen" feature is designed to evenly brown items like waffles that you use straight out of the freezer. This doesn't work - period. Waffles toast with burned middles and untoasted ends, or vice versa.
3. The bagel feature needs some experimentation with the settings before you get it right. The lower settings don't really do very much, and the higher settings can make charcoal.
4. Due to another design oversight, thin slices of bread or small items can get trapped by the inner grill thingy, causing the food to get jammed in the toaster.

Summary:
If regular machine-sliced bread is all you need to toast, then this toaster will work for you. The "cancel" button is a definite plus, and it fills all the basic needs as above.
For all else - fuggedabouddit.

Amanda Richards, October 7, 2011

more cons than pros. I've had this vacuum for 3 months, and got it off of QVC with more attachments than on here, but I never use the microfiber mop anyway. I'll put brackets around reviews for the attachments that don't apply to this amazon package but for someone who was wondering about the extra pieces (which you can see here on the QVC website [...]

This vacuum sucks a lot of stuff out of our carpet. With a dog and two cats we have a lot of pet hair around, and every time I'm done vacuuming the canister is full of dirt and hair.

The cord isn't a long or short length. I use a vacuum extension cord anyway, but if I don't then I need to change the outlet once or twice while vacuuming my main floor.

[I use the bare floor attachment for my kitchen. It works okay, but when you run it parallel to the wall, it won't get any dirt or crumbs against the baseboard. Instead, you have run it at a perpendicular angle, so that's a little annoying since I have to often run over the same floor twice in two different directions just to make sure I get all the dirt/crumbs around the edges, and it forces you to slowly make your way down the wall a foot at a time, only as wide as the nozzle. It's irksome to say the least. I think I'll just start sweeping before I vacuum, which is pretty annoying.]

[I haven't used the dry dust mop attachment (microfiber pad) because I haven't had any real use for it when I have the bare floor attachment. The kitchen is high-traffic area and for the amount of crumbs from food and dog food that land on the floor, I'd rather use the bare floor piece rather than the dust mop. If I had a wood floor without as much traffic I might use it, but the rest of my house is carpeted!]

The regular "motorized floor brush nozzle" works well. I have to cut out the hair from the spinning brushes every few uses--it's amazing how much of my own long hair ends up on the carpet (gross, I know). I don't think it gets the edges of my carpet very well either, but I didn't seriously expect it to.

I wish the turbo brush could have somehow been motorized, but it wasn't with my last vacuum either so I didn't really expect it to be. I use it on my carpeted stairs, and it works ok but could definitely work better and more efficiently if it was motorized.

The vacuum is very tippy, [especially with the bare floor attachment. It almost can't stand up on its own with that attachment], so I always lean it up against a wall anytime I need to stop vacuuming (that goes for both floor attachments I use, [but the bare floor one hardly stands up at all without tipping over).]

My biggest issue with this vacuum is the "stretch hose." On the vacuum itself, it is 22" long. When fully extended, it's as long as 65". They want you to detach the floor attachment and use just the handle with stretch hose (with other attachments), OR you can detach the extension wand and use it with a floor attachment (like the dust mop piece in the pictures on QVC, turning the vacuum into a canister vacuum rather than upright).

However, the resistance of the hose is so strong that you can't extend the hose without holding on to the vacuum itself or else the vacuum gets dragged along with you (or tips over at the very least). If I wanted to use the vacuum as a canister vacuum rather than an upright, it'd be nearly impossible to do so since you can't tow the canister along with you. I have the biggest problem while using it on the stairs. I wish I could leave it at the top or the bottom of the stairs and use the handle with the turbo brush, but I can't go more than one step without the vacuum falling over because the resistance is so strong on the hose once you stretch it in the slightest. Instead, I detach the canister from the floor piece and extension wand, and just try to hold it in one hand while using the nozzle handle in my other hand. It's a big pain that I wasn't prepared for with this vacuum.

Overall, I don't think I'd recommend this vacuum just because of the inconveniences I have with it. I'm not very excited that I know I'll be stuck with this vacuum for a least a few years before I can try something else. All of the attachments make you excited about it, but I don't think they make up for the cons. The high ratings really made me think it'd be fantastic, but unfortunately I just don't think it's all that it's worked up to be.

11/7/2012 Edited to Add: I forgot to mention that this thing is a pain to empty. The bin holds very little until it is at is "max full." But if you have any sort of pet hair then it gets all clumped up in the top of the bin instead of the bottom. The bin is shaped so that all the hair/dust/dirt gets caught way up inside it and you have to reach your fingers up to pull it all out. I can't imagine this being possible for anyone with bigger fingers than I have, and my hands are fairly small. Another reason I'm very disappointed with this vacuum. Cannister vacuums are supposed to be easy to empty--just tip the bin upside-down and everything pours out. This vacuum is the opposite of that scenario.

"Dim" is too bright!. I already knew the noises on it would suck, but I sent my phone alarm to sound at the 7:15 so I wouldn't need to set sounds on the clock. It has a BRIGHT light.. This humidifier is ok for what it is. I used it in Montana and it seemed to be ok for a large room--small or medium would be more effective though. Now I'm in Arizona and I think it's even drier, and I don't think it works as well even in a smaller room, but I'm not 100% sure. It's a fine mid-range humidifier, I think.

Despite the "cool mist" advertisement it's not actually a misting humidifier. You're paying for a fan that sits over water.

It's easy to use, easy to clean, and I don't mind the noise. I prefer a fan sound at night so this does the job of my noisemaker when I use it.

I only have two complaints.

First, I'm annoyed at how expensive the filters have gotten. I used to be able to buy them at Target for like $8 (I've had this humidifier for years), but now I can't find them anywhere so I have to resort to Amazon where they're $12? Geesh. I've switched over to a different brand for filters (Fette Filter, filter A). To make the filters last longer, flip them over every time you add water (I usually did it every other day). I also put one of those Protec humidifier cleaning fish and it keeps the filter and tank clean for longer. Doing those two things, I would clean it about once a month while changing the filter when it got too crusty (maybe every two or three weeks?).

My second complaint is the blue light. It's BRIGHT. It's always on if the machine is on, no matter what. I have rolled up a hand towel and put it in front of the clear water gauge where the light is brightest, but because the machine is a light color it still makes the entire thing glow (and the wall or anything else around it!). I like a dark room at night, and sometimes I just don't have the determination to ignore the glowing blue light in my room so I don't always turn it on.

I've now switched to a BAYKA humidifier that really is a cool mist humidifier and it lets me turn the light completely off while running it. On top of that, I can put essential oils in a sponge ring where the air comes out, though that part isn't that effective like a real oil diffuser. I still like it more than this fan humidifier.

It cooks extremely hot, and the low setting makes soups boil. The outside of the crock pot gets so hot you can't touch it or risk really burning yourself (I say this because I saw a question & answer up above about it not getting too hot on the outside). It's a safety hazard for how hot it cooks!

It must run so hot that it probably cooked the roast in an hour or hour and a half, tops. What's the point? I might as well cook my meat in the oven instead of trying to be efficient while at work. I'm getting rid of this piece of garbage. I've had enough of costly ruined dinners thanks to this thing.

Not powerful enough, slow, designed badly- not a good product. I bought one of these due to my 18 year old VitaMix unit needing a part that would cost more than this system. I found it for a price more than 1/2 off Amazon's price at a brick and mortar store so I took the plunge.

PROS: It is an elegant looking system with the chrome front on the motor unit. I like having 16 oz. individual smoothie cups that the blade unit attaches to for making single serving smoothies. Cleanup is easy if there are no 'complications' (see CONS).

CONS: This thing simply isn't strong enough to really make a decent smoothie in a short time (350 watts motor). If you are using the 16 oz. cups I would advise only putting about 12 oz. in it or it will bog down. The motor will shut off if it gets to be too much (all the blue lights will flash... after this happens 3-4 times you will have to wait 3-5 minutes before you can use the unit again- who has time for that?!). And most of that better be liquid- this thing cannot handle a lot of ice, fruit or veggies. If you decide to fill one of the cups be prepared to 'steady' the cup as the smoothie is being made while the motor shuts down repeatedly. If you don't 'steady' the cup it will wobble and cause the motor to shut down even quicker- terrible design flaw!

The 32 oz. cup needs the same advise- don't fill it up or you will be making smoothies for about 15 minutes! Pulsing the ingredients in a full container (whether it be the 32 oz. or 16 oz.) before you go full bore at making a smoothie in either container helps but not a lot.

The design of this unit is so poor that any leakage coming out of the 32 oz. container will go right into the motor unit. There is a drain hole in the motor unit to allow for such occurrences yet maybe Cuisinart should design the unit so nothing goes into the motor unit. It would appear that having liquids in that area is not a good thing. It is nearly impossible to get out any liquids that leak into the spinning area of the motor unit.

I have not used the dry items cutting cup... I don't think it will be much better.

BOTTOM LINE: I will use this unit until I get my part for my VitaMix unit. Once I get that part I will only use this for mixing powdered drinks- I cannot see this thing lasting very long making smoothies on a daily basis. Maybe I am spoiled by my VitaMix being able to handle anything thrown at it without shutting down or bogging down. After owning a VitaMix for 18 years (and replacing 3 parts over that time) I would say if you are serious about making great smoothies please spend the money on something similar to the VitaMix and avoid this Cuisinart.

NO COMPARISON to standard dehumidifiers in high humidity situations.. Anyone who has rated this as getting the job done has probably never owned a true dehumidifier.  I ordered for a very VERY small bathroom (50 sf) that has a stand up shower.  We've just moved in recently, and this one bathroom doesn't have an exhaust fan.  I have a regular dehumidifier (50 pint capacity, I believe) and I've had whole house dehumidifiers; with those, I could get in the hot shower and when I stepped out the bathroom would be fog-free.  First time I used the Eva-dry I left the bathroom door open and when I stepped out, the whole bathroom was layered in moisture...literally! droplets were forming on the bottom of the wall cabinet.  I left the Eva-dry running (we never turned it off from the night before, when we'd first plugged it in) and after an hour and a half the bathroom was finally dry.  (Don't assume:  This period is the normal dry time without ANYTHING in the bathroom.)  The next time I got in the shower, I closed the bathroom door and kept it closed.  It took over 3 hours for the Eva-dry to dehumidify to the point that there were no longer droplets on the bottom of the wall cabinet, but the mirror was still coated in thick, wet 'fog'.  I've since replaced the Eva-dry with our huge (to me, and certainly by comparison) Hauer 50 Pint and when I get out of the shower the bathroom is dry and I don't have to wipe the mirror dry. *** Might be worth mentioning that I live in Georgia and I purchased/used the Eva-dry in August, which is possibly the most humid month of the year here.

Original review:
Almost a five star. The finish of the wok is truely high class, compared with a lot of the 'non'stick' varieties out there. After a couple of heavy duty sessions with our wok, including a dinner party of 6, we love it. the only grip is that we wish it could be 2 inches deeper, as per traditional wok. hence you can toss and stir fry like in a traditional wok, but we are living with it as it as the food is not sticking/burning and the cleaning is a dream. Note that there is a 25 years warranty on this product so scan a copy of this invoice, note down the address that is attached to the wok and save it in your email box! If it serves me for 25 years, I think I certainly got my return on the cost! The 12 inch is not that wide, and I would highly recommend for a family of two to a party up to 8.

Makes me laugh & curse, but doesn't actually vacuum well at all. See photos. For ten days I have laughed out loud, cursed and finally just ignored this little robot vacuum cleaner for my own sanity. It seems like a great idea and if you live in a tiny house with nothing but tiny dust bunnies on slick floors then it might be a good idea. However, back here in my world... a big house with pets and a mix of tile, wood and carpet on the floors this machine is next to useless in most applications.

Where to start? It charges very fast and is relatively easy to operate once you read the instruction book and figure out the buttons & codes. The error codes are super easy to memorize and that's good because you'll see them often. The collection bin is easy to remove and clean out and this is also a good thing because it's tiny and you'll be emptying it multiple times per room. Well... multiple times assuming the machine actually picks anything up for you. The wheels are strong and it does actually move over surfaces pretty easily. Of course the brush that sweeps the debris up into the collection bin doesn't really make the transition as well from wood or tile to carpet. More on this in a bit.

The charging dock is a problem unto itself. It weighs far less than the vacuum unit. When the vacuum tries to set itself up to charge it can bump the dock and cause it to move. If your dock is on a wood floor and the vacuum gets in a robot induced spin of confusion this becomes a Monty Python type skit. I watched my Bissel robo vac chase it's charging dock down my hallway yesterday trying to park & charge, whacking the dock hard enough to cause it to slide a few inches away on the wood floor each time they touched. This silliness repeated over & over until the charging dock actually became unplugged from the wall! I laughed so hard I had tears in my eyes. I kept thinking "Dude! She's just not that into you."

The actual vacuuming is a problem here as well. On a basic tile floor with nothing but dry mud from our barn boots, the Bissel does fine - see the first two photos. If I could leave this unit in just the mud room and kitchen it would be fine. Using it in the foyer and dining room yields similar results - again simple wood floors and very little dog hair & some random dry shoe dirt, just the usual. The problems become very obvious on carpet. Transitioning from wood to carpet means the brush on the bottom of the machine rubs onto the carpet and deposits all the gathered dirt & hair & debris in a tidy little pile ONTO THE CARPET. You know... so I can use my real vacuum at my leisure later. See the last two photos.

The business of dropping piles of debris all over my carpet and any area rug it crosses had gone on every single time I have used this machine. I have cleaned it, I've checked to be sure the roller brush underneath is working properly, I've vacuumed with the big Dyson immediately before setting the little Bissel loose and it still happens. Despite having a big banner over the top that proclaims it's designed for pet hair, it is not suitable in any way shape or form for a house with any quantity of dog hair. I am giving this machine two stars - one for the simple amusement factor (my dogs think it's an indoor turtle and watching them stalk it cracks me up) and a second star because it is pretty good on bare tile floors with very limited amounts of dry dirt. Minus three stars for limited capacity, inability to reliably self dock & charge, and failure to actually vacuum more than just dry dusty dirt or actually do everything it claims.

Coming apart after two washings. Sizes are too small. These pillow cases are soft and they are comfortable to sleep on. However, the sizing is way off. Our standard pillows fit length wise, but the cases are too narrow and we have to force the pillow fully in. Plus, after putting these through our laundry with the rest of the bedding twice, both cases are already losing stitching at the seams. They just are not constructed well. There are just too many good linen brands available to waste money on these.

Too small for a standard queen mattress & a hole in flat sheet. See the photos. Low quality.. I love high thread count pure cotton sheets as a rule and if you get truly good ones that are actually made well from good quality cotton then they will last forever. These are not those sort of sheets. These are very soft and the dye is a true deep navy. However, these sheets are poorly constructed and they do not fit properly at all on a standard size queen mattress. SEE THE PHOTOS. The ends of the fitted sheet do not cover the entire mattress and leave a portion exposed. Plus the corner pocket seams are pulled so tight that the stitches are threatening to separate. My mattress is not extra thick or a pillow top and it doesn't have a topper on it.

Additionally, you need to make sure you wash these BEFORE you even think about using them. I always do, but some folks don't. Removing these from the package revealed a flurry of strings and excess threads of various colors and some dust. There is also a hole at the top of my flat sheet where the hem stitch wasn't finished correctly. See the photo. In time, with repeated use, this will rip. I washed them immediately according to the directions on the tags and they did survive that well with minimal shedding in the dryer. At best these are guest room sheets that will see little use a few times a year, but I will continue to spend my money on a known high quality brand for my master suite in the future.

Sharp edge on top lip, unfinished inside. Exterior arrived with scratches on three sides.. On the one hand, this box does exactly what it says it will do....it covers a standard size tissue box and it is the stainless steel look. It blends with my kitchen appliances and looks fine sitting on the corner of the island. As long as you don't look closely at it. It arrived with scratches and marks all over three sides. The inside of the box is rough to the touch, almost as if they forgot to finish it during production. The top, where the tissues are dispensed, has one actual sharp edge on the underside of the lip. It's not a big deal with just adults around, but when my young nieces visit, I will have to put this thing away so they don't accidentally nick themselves.

Heavy, well constructed, knife handle is awkward and clumsy. Spoon shape is small. Forma is my fourth set of Mepra flatware so far. After listening to my husband rant about how much he dislikes our 20 year old silverware, I made a list of what he wants in good utensils. To that end, I have decided to try several of the Mepra designs until we find one we both love that we can afford and then I will buy a full 16 person collection. So....Forma isn't the one.

The utensils are well made and have a substantial feel to each piece when you hold them. These also have that beautiful intense shine that Mepra is known for. However, the spoons have a sort of tear drop shape to them that looks nice, but is actually inefficient for eating. The coffee/tea spoon is fine for those two things, but for eating ice cream it's a pain. It just feels wrong. The larger spoon is shaped wrong for twirling pasta into.

Finally, the knife. I dislike the design of this knife so much. The handle is angled differently than a traditional table knife. It does not lie flat on its side. Instead, it rests on the back of the handle with the serrated edge upright or the opposite direction, with the edge touching the plate or napkin surface. I get that this is a design or artistic thing, but it drives me nuts because in the real world after two meals, this knife is in the way - constantly.

High pitched whine, ineffective on rugs, canister doesn't reattach easily. Ok...This machine is not the same as my other Dirt Devil stick vac. This one is very light and easy enough to physically use. The comparison ends there because my three year old Dirt Devil is so much better.

My first issue the high pitched, very loud whine the motor makes as soon as it turns on. It does this constantly. Secondly, the power and roller brush are both weak. Trying to use this on a low pile area rug is essentially useless. It's better on tile and hardwood flooring, but barely. Third problem is the canister. It comes off correctly, but doesn't reattach easily - mine clicks and looks attached, but it falls out when I restart the vacuum. This is seriously obnoxious. The one good thing is the plastic pet hair attachment - it does pull cat hair out of fabric surprisingly well. However, in the end, this vacuum really doesn't work well for me.

Absolutely impossible to drink out of cleanly. Spills all over you. This cup is an absolute disaster waiting to happen. Do not even think about drinking hot coffee or hot tea with it - you will get burned as it sloshes out onto your face. Cold drinks aren't any better.

The problem is the 360 degree access on the lid. This is badly engineered and essentially useless for actual drinking. The multiple openings are long and narrow all the way around the lid and you cannot insert a straw to minimize the spillage. Once you tip the cup to drink you initially get a tiny trickle and then a full face flood as the liquid reaches the rest of the lid openings and rushes out. (See photos) For Heaven's sake, do not drop or tip it as you walk or you'll be cleaning a mess - totally not useful in a car.

The container part is a really pretty deep red and it does keep drinks cold. My only choice now is to just use this cup as a thermos rather than trying to drink out of it. I'm giving it an extra star for being useful in at least one way.

Primary floor head rollers do not power on. Small canister, top heavy. I'm a vacuum expert at this point. We've never had fewer than four house dogs at once in the past twenty years. That means I vacuum daily and mop floors & dust every other day so we don't live in a hair ridden, dog smelling hovel. There's no excuse for a home to smell like dogs or for dog hair to cling to people's clothing. A really good vacuum or two is a necessity in this house.

I typically burn out a vacuum cleaner every year. The only ones that haven't succumbed to the daily dog hair and regular dirt are the shop vac, the big Dyson and the Dyson cordless. I actually prefer the cordless flexibility of the two year old Dyson and hoped this Hoover Fusion would work as well. Not even a little bit.

The direct comparison is like having a toy next to the Dyson. First thing is that the Hoover is top heavy and not well balanced. No way do I want to hold this thing upright and try to clean the ceiling fans or upper corners. The second problem is that I have to remove the battery to charge it up - my Dyson cordless plugs in directly in the hanging cradle with one step. Third issue is the small canister - it's suitable for random, light dirt quick pick up only.

My main problem though is the non-operational rollers. They will not turn on and the digital status light on the handle shows a constant yellow warning or is blank. The machine powers on and can be used with the small attachments like the crevice tool etc. But the primary floor head does not work on mine.

Flimsy, wobbles and pieces missing. Plastic parts cracked immediately. This is one of those things you think will be helpful in the kitchen, but it is a disappointment. The first problem is that one of the poles in my kit is a hair shorter than the other three, meaning it's not level without a shim underneath. Second problem is the clips you attach to the poles that hold the shelves can and will crack. One pair of these cracked as soon as I put it in place, rendering them un usable. Third problem is the hanging hooks were not included.

Once I finally got the rack put together and shimmed under the short leg, the entire contraption was wobbly and flimsy. There's absolutely no way I would put a microwave oven on this mess. I'm putting this in the barn to hold paper towels, lightweight plastic cups and coffee pods. That's all the weight I feel comfortable placing on the racks. It's just not safe for an actual appliance.

DIED after 90 days with hot motor and burned odor!!. ******Updated Review September 2018 Reduced to 1 Star!****

After barely 90 days of use, this fan has completely died. I have not abused it in any way at all, but today the motor got hot after running for 35 minutes on level 1 and emitted a smokey odor and stopped working entirely. I've used it almost every day for a few hours a day usually on level two, but never running 24 hours at a time and never on the highest setting. I've kept the fan clean and with plenty of air flow. It's disappointing and concerning simply because the heat and odor means something inside was trying to burn up and that could be a safety issue if it happens when you're not home!

~~~~~~Original review is below. ~~~~~
This is Texas and it's hot. Of course we have central air conditioning, but we also have multiple fans in the house and ceiling fans going 24/7 from April to November. We keep the ac at 76 degrees and the fans move the air enough that it actually feels cooler, so they are a must around here.

This one is about as basic as a fan can be without being a straight box fan. You have to assemble it - that took 8 minutes from start to finish and no tools needed. It has a nice wide turn radius for the oscillating setting and there's no rattling as it moves.

In a small room or down a straight hall, this fan puts out decent air flow that is easily felt on the medium power setting. However, in a big open room, you need to put it on full power to feel any difference more than five feet away from the fan. And at full speed, you can definitely hear that motor going. So for us, it will be a guest bedroom fan only.

Poor quality materials, shoddy construction and badly prepped. Falling apart. What an unpleasant experience and disappointment. This cabinet is not prepared properly to survive a cross country trip in a truck at all. It arrived beaten to a pulp and almost unusable for its intended purpose. There are two reasons for this. Poor quality of materials used in construction and zero consideration given to packing it. At this mid three figure price point, that is inexcusable

The back of the cabinet was completely off and all the screws were stripped, loose in the box. The inside of the back was splintered where the plywood had been damaged - plywood. Really? The front edge corners are all battered into broken bits with the enamel veneer peeling off. The front left door had the top hinge completely broken off and looking closely, the top hole was never actually drilled. Which means that the hinge was never fully attached at the factory to begin with! That door simply doesn't close and the inside rail is splintered and cracked anyway.

The grey finish is pretty and the size overall is good - it also could be a very nice looking cabinet in a dining room or study. There's enough room inside to repurpose it for any number of uses beyond liquor bottles. However, I would think twice about the (lack of) quality and care taken in making this piece and getting it to you.

Cheap materials, badly made, looks cheap and tacky, difficult to put together. This headboard arrived in a massive box with loads of padding and was very heavy. So we had high that it was indeed a luxurious piece of furniture made from "high quality" materials. Opening it and laying all the pieces out to put together was were our hopes were dashed and the cursing began. this is a two man job without question. And you need a mallet.

The main part of the headboard is in two large sections that attach in the center via a single dowel and then are braced on the top and bottom using six screws and two brace boards. Joining the two pieces together with the dowel requires two people and so much force, pushing and hammering with a soft mallet that we were sweating. Fine. It's in and done and there is a damage to one side now from the mallet where the cheap veneer dented and pealed back. See the photo. The bottom brace aligned and fit perfectly with almost no visible seam. The top brace...has a huge gap on both sides if you want the pre-drilled holes to line up. See the photo.

Pulling the padding and slip cover down over the assembled unit was amateur hour - the sides aren't smooth and the padding snagged and tore as it went down. It's not visible once you get the suede like slipcover in place, but none of it lies smoothly due to the bunching and snagging of the padding. This could be prevented entirely by making the padding case another quarter inch wider on both sides. Attaching this thing to the bed frame was another aggravation since the pre-drilled holes didn't match up to the standard queen size bed rails on the bed frame we already own. We had to rig it up and at this price point, that's beyond ridiculous.

Bottom line... Three star deduction for poor quality materials. Poor quality control on measurements at the point of construction. Further more the difficulty of assembling this headboard is overly complicated and poorly thought out. Honestly, this headboard could and should be shipped to customers completely assembled and ready to use - the size of the box it comes in would not need to change and the weight certainly would not change by pre-assembling the entire thing at the factory. At this price point I expected that! And most importantly, the final product looks cheap and tacky. It's fine for a little used guest bed, but by no means is this good enough for your master suite. See the photo. It's lumpy, uneven and the sand color is bland and looks like you grabbed a piece of random fabric at the hobby store. If this were priced in the under hundred dollar range it would be a 3 1/2 star rating, as it is...a two star is the best I feel it deserves.

Arrived factory sealed smelling of rotted meat and mildew. Three washes and smell is still there. I love a fuzzy, soft, cozy throw and so do my dogs. This one is soft and the grey blue color is very soft and pretty. However, this arrived with a horrific stench right out of the package. It's hard to define exactly - a cross between old, spoiled meat and wet dog fur and mildew. The smell is so strong that my husband noticed it down the hall as I was opening the box. I'm not joking.

I have washed this three times now with scented Gain detergent and hot water and it STILL STINKS. It came from the factory smelling like rotten meat and mold and that scent will not come out. I am throwing the entire thing away and running a full sanitize cycle on my washing machine now. Just avoid.

Cheaply made, poorly designed.. Ugh. I'm so tired of junk and I see this exact paper towel holder being sold under several "brands". This is not truly functional in a real kitchen. It glues on the wall - recipe for failure over time. The actual bar does not hold a full roll of paper towels, the space is too narrow. It just looks cheap to me. I've relegated this to the bathroom at the horse barn. When it falls apart out there, it won't be a problem.

Missing pieces, holes not drilled and no assembly instructions. I needed a small file cabinet for volunteer records and paperwork and I assumed that this one would suffice. It might if there were some manufacturing quality control. However, it arrived with missing pieces, no assembly instructions at all and parts that weren't finished. Some of the holes for screws were not even drilled out.  I tried to get it together several times and the pieces just don't align properly. I'll have to just buy a pre-assembled cabinet from a local store.

Poor safety features. Yeah...no. Pressure cookers are generally safer than the ones our grandparents used, but this isn't like the brand name units today.  This thing scares me and I refuse to use it again.  There is no cancel option in the settings  - you have to unplug it to reset if it's programmed incorrectly. Additionally,  it will start cooking without the insert piece in the pot. Frankly, I prefer my fancy rice cooker and old school crockpot to this. The rice in this was sticky and clumpy. If you must have a pressure cooker, invest in a major name brand from a legitimate manufacturer.

Cheap material, hard to assemble. I have the grey nightstand. It's very heavy and actually took two of us to bring the box inside. The color is very pretty blue toned grey. The assembly is ridiculously over complicated and difficult considering this is just a nightstand. And it's just not the best quality material either. There are definitely better options out there. We'll use it, but I sure won't buy another one.

Uncomfortable, hard, parts don't fit together properly. I gave it the dogs as a bed.. Ok, at this price point, you really should not have any expectations of anything beyond the bottom of the barrel in quality. That's exactly what you'll be getting by the way. Where do I start? The fabric - it's a linen type weave that's pretty stiff and harsh against any skin. You're not going to be snuggled up on this seat without a thick throw between you and the fabric. Then there's the lack of stuffing which makes sitting here like sitting on a layer of foam over a rock.

Putting it together is relatively simple until you get the part where you zipper the fold out cushions to the base. That zipper is a total failure. It doesn't work and I can't force it to work so my two fold out cushions are just acting as the seat. Even if they zipped together and folded out correctly, the entire set up is flimsy and seriously uncomfortable. I would pay for a hotel room for my guests before I ever considered making them sleep on this.

The only reason I'm giving this two stars is because I'm able to repurpose it as a big dog bed. Sort of a mini sofa just for my dogs. They aren't thrilled with it, but they are including it in the dog bed rotation.

Ok as a sofa throw, but not as soft as expected. Update and reduced to 2 stars. After two weeks the thing is unraveling at the seams. Loose threads everywhere now and it looks terrible.
************************************
I love the white, fluffy, sherpa side of this blanket. It weighs very little and is a great little sofa throw while reading. It is also very soft and warm. It's just the reverse side with the waffle pattern that I don't care for. The texture is rough to the touch and does not feel anything like the white side. It feels stiff and the opposite of cozy actually. I thought it might just be me, but my dogs don't want to snuggle on the waffle weave side either.

Holes don't align for correct assembly.. May I just say how much I absolutely detest all Allen wrenches projects?? This little table is very pretty and is exactly the correct dimensions for a tiny space in the master closet. Unfortunately, because the legs and bottom shelf require Allen wrench screws, it takes much longer to put together than it should.

This is further compounded by two legs with misaligned holes - the bolts literally cannot go into the top holes on either leg. So we had to find the drill and create new holes and sort of jimmy everything together. It worked, but the quality control is in need of improvement before these tables ever reach the customers.

Flimsy, weak and wobbly. I had hoped to use this for extra hand tools like drills, wrenches, hammers....the random detritus that collects in the garage. However, this thing is very flimsy and badly made. The shelves don't stay in place and when you do get them set and not falling down, they wobble. ------------
* Not fluffy. More like sticky.
* Despite a product listing on Amazon that is full of words, there is no advice on "how much" water per packet. They simply say add water. Even on the packet, all it says is add water. So if getting fluffy snow depends on the right mixture of water and powder... then good luck! It's trial and error.

DAY 2 UPDATE:
-------------------
* So, just as suspected, this won't feel like snow at all. Today, we purposely pour very little water to a packet and watch it fluff up. We continued to add water little by little, hoping there will be a stage where the snow will be both fluffy and sticky. Unfortunately, there is no such stage. Once there is enough water to make it sticky, the fluffiness is gone. So here are your options:

* Option 1: Less water equals fluffy snow, but you can't make a snowman or anything. It's just flaky or powdery, it does not take any form.
* Option 2: Keep adding water till it gets sticky. At this point, the fluffiness is gone. You'll be playing with clumpy goo, and your hands will always have gooey "snow" sticking to it. Real snow will flake off your hands clean. Not this gooey snow.

Lastly, it says this "snow" will dry out and return to powder form, and will be reusable. It's been several days, and my bucket of goo hasn't changed one bit. I think you would need to wait for eternity for it to return to powder form.

Tried EVERYTHING -- descaled (twice), disassembled and cleaned every part that could be disassembled, changed the filter twice, installed a NEW filter holder. Nothing worked. It's done.

That's it. No more Keurig machines. I'm not going to pay Keurig's premium prices for something that lasts only 1.5 yrs.

Currently looking at other brands that can handle k-cups. (Love my k-cups; just have to find a good machine, or one that's cheap enough so that when it fails, it's not such an angst-producing event.)

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
My older Keurig bit the dust recently -- the pump went out after 5 years of daily use -- and the cost to repair made getting a new machine a reasonable choice.

Looking around and reading the reviews, I settled on this K45 system. It's not a "fancy" as my old one but has enough of the features that I've grown to love after 5 yrs of use.

I've had it a few months now, so I've had a chance to put it through its paces. It's easy to operate: fill the reservoir with water, hit the "on" button, load a cup into the receptacle, and wait for the "cup" lights to blink. I've learned over the years that for me, the middle setting (~8-oz cup) works best and gives me the best flavor. After a brief pause, out comes freshly brewed coffee. I usually use a large mug, so I brew 2-3 "cups" to fill my mug, and the "brief pause" can stretch longer since the water has to heat. Watch the lights, and you'll see what's going on. Just don't expect coffee to be dispensed immediately after hitting the "cup" button (that always seems to throw visiting guests who are using a Keurig for the first time ... ).

It's not perfect -- I wish it had a slightly larger heated water capacity so it didn't have to pause as long between cups -- but that's really a small quibble.

Overall, this is a solid machine, working great so far. I'll update this review if I notice any problems.

Had problems with overflow. This kept overflowing from the top of the carafe, not because I put in too much water, but I believe, because the grinds kept getting past the filtration and stopped up the opening connection. My daughter wondered if it might be because I was putting the lid on too tightly for the coffee to pass through; however, if the lid is not locked down it simply won't fit beneath the filter. The first time it happened was my fault. I used a cone filter, rather than a large basket filter. I went out and bought the right kind, or at least what I think should be the right kind. The plastic basket is pretty large, and the paper filters do not reach to the top. But the problem continued to happen on occasion, and I could never figure out why. I decided to return it for a refund, although an exchange was offered. In fairness, I did purchase this from Amazon as a warehouse return or used, so maybe something was wrong. I could have tried another of the same, but I just ran out of patience. Even when it did brew correctly  -- as in coffee did not flow all over the pot and counter  -- I was really not that impressed with the taste. Given the price point and the specialty coffee endorsement,  I expected something more amazing. It is suppose to sprinkle the water over the grinds more evenly, but I could not taste the difference. I went back to my old coffee maker which has worked well and predictably over several years. I kind of think that the OXO brand is over rated and over priced, but perhaps, that's not a fair assessment. I could have tried a little harder on trouble shooting, and apparently, OXO will send replacement parts, but I'm tired and didn't want to work that hard. I just wanted something I could just take out of the box and make great coffee with that wasn't too complicated. This maker doesn't appear to be complicated, but it certainly has issues.

Mixed Feelings, Overall Satisfied for My Use. I have some mixed feelings about the NOXU White L Shaped Desk with Shelves. I assembled this myself, but for those that get overwhelmed easily with boxed furniture assembly, you may need a buddy to assist. I've assembled another desk that was also L-shaped of the same price range. In comparison, this one isn't as sturdy and the assembly was complicated. I've assembled many pieces of boxed furniture, and this isn't the worst piece to assemble, but much more complicated than it should be as there are no moving parts. Not all of the pieces were labeled, and some of the written instructions didn't match up to the diagrams. The instructions are in need of revision. When I was in doubt, I referenced the diagrams. Some of the bolt alignments that attach the frame to the desktop were misaligned. This isn't something I've observed in the desks I have assembled in the past. This took me about 30 - 40 minutes of assembly time using an electric screwdriver. I strongly suggest to avoid tightening all the bolts/screws completely until you have an entire section aligned for the best fit. Small tools are included, but I only used the wrench as I prefer my own screwdriver over the small one that was included. It's not something I would consider incredibly sturdy. There could be some engineering improvements to the frame at the point of the back corner assembly, which would make it much more sturdy. The corner section is the weakest point, and the section over the shelves is the strongest point. Two points of attachment for the foot rest would also lend to a more sturdy design. As it's designed, I do not consider the foot rest sturdy.

The desktop is thin as is the metal of the hollow tubes that make up the frame. On the upside, it's light-weight for the size. I'm using it in my hobby room where I do small crafting projects and sewing. This desk replaced two older mis-matched desks I was using before. It does make for an aesthetic improvement. For my purpose, it's a good fit for my space and works well enough. I was mostly attracted by the shape and white color that better coordinates with my shelving units. The shelves are handy to have, and do add some stability. The feet on the desk are adjustable, so with some fine-tuning, you should be able to make it level on most floors. The computer stand will only work well on a carpeted surface as it's a slide design (no wheels) and not attached to the desk. I had a couple pieces of the frame arrive warped, with no damage to the packaging. This is a quality control issue. It was still able to be assembled, but I have a tapered gap between one of the rectangle parts and the corner piece. It's not a deal-breaker, but looks a bit sloppy. I would not attempt to bend it back into the right shape without risking the integrity of a welded seam. There is also some paint that was scratched on the frame, not due to the packaging, another quality control issue. If I had not received this desk in exchange for a review, I would attempt to return it for another.

If it were not for the quality control issues, I would consider this a very fair value. However, based on my personal experience, I cannot strongly recommend this particular desk based on quality control and needed improvements to the frame engineering. On the same note, if this desk fits your ideal dimensions for your space, and you do not intend to use it for anything that would need to withstand a heavy weight, it is not anything I would strongly discourage. For the size, it is a budget-friendly desk, but keep in mind it's budget quality as well. I hope you find my personal experience helpful, and kindly will click the button below.

works well, easy to clean. howdy y'all,

strong, sturdy, [relatively] easy to assemble. howdy y'all,

first, if you want more shelves for this you _cannot_ get them in the "black anthracite" finish. shelves are only available in either black or silver.

this assembled pretty easily. i bought the casters for this kit and my _only_ complaint is that they used pressed-in leveler plugs. they SELL the posts with screw-in leveler plugs but do not use them for the starter kits.

for a clue on how to get the pressed-in plugs out, find a heavy item that will fit in the open end of the pole and drop it in. then do the shake-em-up-shuffle until the plug pops out. i used a 5/8" punch that a friend brought over.

a few bits of info ...
- if it aint obvious, the clips set on the inset rings so that the shelves do NOT align exactly at the inset rings.
- the space between wires on the 36x18 shelf is 5/8". so you likely won't need the plastic liner if your bits-n-pieces are bigger than that.
- if you aren't tall, you will pro'ly want to assemble the entire thing on its side. trying to reach up and align the poles with the holes in the shelf corners was a bit of work for me and i'm 6'1".
- they are pretty sturdy. i weigh 160 and stood on the bottom shelf to test it. no wobble at all.

to make things very clear - i'm buying another set of these and a pair of black shelves to split between the two sets.

rated a THREE since it does what i expected it to do and no more than that.

take care,
lee

But I had faith it was working as I could feel it heating up from putting my hand on it. About 25 min later I had usable rice! It was slightly firm in texture, like that weird microwave pouch rice. I think it's ok but you just have to think of what you want and if it's worth it. It wasn't too difficult to set the app up on my phone. I did that and set it all up and ran the vacuum. It did pretty decent and went back to it's base to charge. I ran it a few more times and it's ok but I hate the small dirt cup as it fills up way too fast when you have pets and are dealing with pet fur. Honestly because of this, after testing this a few times- I've parked it and have stuck to my cordless stick vacuum that's meant for pet hair. It maneuvers thru the house well and in a smaller house, I can push it thru pretty quickly. The roller brush on the stick vacuum actually lightly scrubs the dirt up off the floor and the wood floors feel so amazing after I run the push vacuum! I honestly am going to get rid of the Roomba and stick to my old vacuum personally.

I think if a person has pets and wants to use this- either plan on constantly emptying the dirt cup (which defeats the purpose of an automatic vacuum) or get one of those little Roomba dustbin machines they sell that cost an arm and a leg. The machine I guess sucks the dirt out of the bin and puts it in it's slightly larger bin. It gives you a little more time until you have to empty it. I just don't have more money to throw into this so I'm letting it go and calling it quits.

Other than the hair issues in my house and the small dirt cup- the vacuum does work decently. I just feel like for the price point, I'm not super impressed at all. It doesn't do THAT good of a job for what they charge. I think it's a toy for the lazy essentially. Now if you are disabled I could see using it but then again having to bend down and empty it non-stop, I can't see that many disabled people would be able to do that. I suppose if you had home health or family person willing to empty it daily, this absolutely could help a disabled person. Or someone with health problems limiting their ability to bend over (I have a bad back and it's hard for me to bend over and empty this) It's not a bad vacuum, Just not for me personally.

Great concept, poor execution. My mixer came with this shield, and it was one of the deciding factors between the Artisan and the Design model, as I thought it would be very helpful. Serious Design Flaw Prevents this Reviewer From Purchasing More Than One Set. I do like this drawer divider. It's sleek and modular design is perfect, albeit a tad on the expensive side. This design has a gummy sticky piece on one end that secures to the back of the drawer, but the front doesn't so the front of the unit floats about unless every space has the spacer pieces installed. I have expensive wood drawers, and am quite reticent about "glueing" a piece in the drawer. What will the long term damage be to the drawer? I'm keeping the one set I purchased, and have it installed, but will probably not buy any more.

Extremely disappointed.. For a pillow that retails for a little under $50, I am disappointed. I received this Stone & Beam pillow for an honest review. I didn’t mind the assembly (unwrap the pillow and stuff it in the cover), which is pretty simple, but the quality was lacking. The fabric (a mixture of linen and viscose) looks ok but seems thin and not durable at all. The design on the front, three wavy lines are cute but look a little unfinished or rough looking. I guess the whole pillow seems like something I would have made, kind of amateurish.  What I do like is the color (flax) or tan. It is neutral enough to match a variety of sofas, chairs or comforters. Colors like maroon or navy would make this pillow pop. In the past, I have tried Stone & Beam products and found them to be great, so I won’t let this “miss” turn me away from the brand. In conclusion, when I consider the price and quality, I give this pillow 3 stars.

Not the best but not the worse. Average.. These AmazonBasics queen sized sheets are decent. They aren’t fantastic, but they aren’t awful either. They are just standard, middle of the road, average sheets. Perhaps it was because of the vivid description that I was expecting more. They are described as “organic sateen”, so I expected them to be luxurious and soft. These are more of a mid-grade set of sheets.

What I do like about these sheets: (1) The color. The mossy/sage color is soothing and perfect no matter the time of year. I think they also pair well with a variety of comforter/duvet covers, colors. (2) They fit my bed well. They don’t ride up or come off the corner of the mattress during the middle of the night. And (3) they wash well. And even if you forget to remove them immediately from the dryer and they have a few wrinkles, you can use a warm iron to smooth them up.

What I am still not sure about or sold on: (1) The feel of them. While these sheets are comfortable, they aren’t super soft. With that being said, while they aren’t as luxurious as I thought from the description, they do provide a decent night’s sleep.

Kotton culture. Kotton white.. This sheet set by Kotton Culture are decent. They are 100% Egyptian Cotton, 600 thread count, stark white sheets with deep pockets. They fit my king size bed well. The only thing I noticed was that when I washed them, prior to placing them on my bed, they wrinkle a lot. I had to iron them before placing them on my bed. That was a little inconvenient. But otherwise, these sheets do make for a nice, peaceful sleep.

Pretty but not sure practical.. The Soma ceramic mug is pretty. I would even say eye catching. The body is two toned, soft blue (mint) and white, with a bamboo twist-off lid. I would suggest washing it by hand, although the body (not the lid) can be washed in the dishwasher. It can keep liquids hot or cold. While I think this mug is a nice gift for a tea or coffee lover, I would hesitate to give it 5 stars.  Why? (1) When full, this mug is heavy. (2) It is a little pricey ($30 for 12 ounces). (3) Taking care of this mug is tricky. Hand wash is recommended.

Offers some protection for your table but could have been cuter.. Look/Appearance: These DII gray, woven placemats are simple with a floral design in the center. They are round but would have been cuter if they had a nice border, which would have also made them a little larger. They are lightweight and stack well. *Note: One of mine was a little discolored. It wasn’t worth sending them back and since I usually set the table for 4, it wasn’t a big deal.
Cost: To me, these are a little expensive for what you get. These retail for around $25 ($4 each) on Amazon. You can find some cuter ones for that price.
Care: These are easy to care for. You just wipe them off with a damp cloth.
Overall, these are just ok. I would give them 3 stars.

Pricey.. I was a little worried when I received these two (2) puredown Goose Feather Down pillows. My son has several allergies and I selected these pillows to replace some of his older ones. So far he has not had any issues. I simply inserted them inside hypoallergenic pillow covers before slipping them into cases. He says these pillows are soft and comfortable, just not very full. They are on the thin side. But they are moldable and can be rolled/folded to accommodate your head. For the price (which are a little expensive) they could have been a little thicker/fuller. The cover on them is durable and well made. They fit easily inside standard pillowcases.

Basic.. I had hopes for this little wooden napkin holder by Woho. It is “U” shaped and stained a pretty brown. The wood is nothing special except it shows some grain/striations in the wood. It is very rugged looking. Does what it is supposed to do, just nothing extraordinary. Wish it had been a little larger.

Not as impressed as I had hoped.. The Quawreath is pretty, very Fall-ish/Harvest-y. Unfortunately, it is not as pretty as I hoped. The colors are pretty – yellow, red, green and orange - but interspersed with hydrangeas, dahlias and something similar to eucalyptus. This wreath looks better and more expensive in the picture. I do like that it comes with a hook, which makes it convenient for hanging. Initially, I wanted to place this on my front door, but after reading the care instructions carefully, it said to avoid direct sunlight and rain, so I will probably put it over my fireplace. And finally, it is expensive ($50) for what you get. And while I do like the sturdy box that it came in, does that make it a must have? Probably not.

Interesting design but flawed – too small.. I ordered these Cube Home Olivewood mat & coaster set with high expectations. You get four of each – 4 mats and 4 coasters. I like that they are unique looking – appearing to be a slice of wood/rings inside of a tree. These are lightweight. The back is covered with a cork material. I wipe my mats off with a clean, damp cloth and follow it with a (dry) paper towel. My biggest complaint is that these mats aren’t very large. My everyday dinner plates barely fit on them. Appetizer plates would probably work better. In conclusion, if these were larger, I think I would like them a lot better.

Does what it is supposed to do, just not sure how long it will last.. I needed a new toilet brush, so I ordered this one by Joybos. It does a decent job. It comes with two brushes, with firm (slightly spread) bristles, and a base to store it in. The base pops open and closed easily. It cleans the toilet well. However, I only give this set a 3. Why? Because I am not sure how durable it will be. It is made of plastic and seems at time to be a little flimsy. For now, it is opening and closing, but I am not sure that it will work that well in a few months.

Love the concept, just wish it could have been executed better.. I love Christmas. And not because of the gift giving, but the time spent with family and beautiful holiday decorations. I love the gorgeous trees, the wreaths, rows of garland, and the Christmas lights. With that in mind, I thought pre-lit garland (by Kvdukoa) would be a nice addition to my decorations. And it is kind of. Let me explain. What I liked: This garland comes decorated with red berries and miniature pine-cones. It is also pre-lit with tiny white lights. It is battery operated, so there are no cords or wires. It is long enough (9ft) so can be placed it on the fireplace mantel or along top of your front door. What I didn’t like or an unsure of: While decorated, it doesn’t have enough lights or decorations. It could have used a lot more of each. I ended up adding additional red berries, but it would have been nicer had it come with more. The pine-cones are small, so adding some more would have made it more festive. Another thing that I will add is that you should secure the garland wherever you place it. Initially I placed the garland on the mantel of our fireplace. But one day something made it fall, breaking the battery compartment. My husband was able to reassemble but had to tape it shut. Fortunately for me, it still works, but I learned a valuable lesson – you definitely need to secure it. With all that being said, this garland is pretty but needs more. I give it 3 stars.

Chicago has nothing on me.. Lately, I’ve accepted the challenge of making Chicago style deep dish pizza (Pandemic challenge). I have the method and recipe down (my son schooled me based on his experience working at a pizza place last summer), my only issue is what kind of pan to use that will give me the crust that I prefer.  I have used everything from glass pie pans to cast iron skillets. Both options get the job done, but I still wanted to try a traditional, deep dish pizza pan. So, when offered this one for an honest review, I couldn’t resist. It arrived quickly and was in great shape. It is stainless steel, large, huge even. It is big enough to make a personal pan pizza (thin crust), a deep dish one, or brownies. It is a nice size for my family of 4. I was surprised about how thin the pan was. It is super lightweight. It is thinner and lighter than some of my other stainless steel pans. It does distribute the heat and cooks evenly. I guess I just expected more. And finally, caring for this pan is pretty simple. It is dishwasher safe, but I don’t usually clean or place pans in my dishwasher. I hand wash them. This pan, while huge can be stored with your other pans. In conclusion, I think this pan is a nice option, I just think it could be a little thicker.

Useful for a nursery.. This is a pretty lattice hamper. If you have teenage boys, this might not be the best hamper for them. However, because of the size (small), I think it will definitely work in a nursery or playroom. It can hold small clothes (infant and toddlers) or toys. If you use it as a toy box, you can teach your child to “clean-up” while singing the “clean-up song”. This hamper collapses and has two handles, making it easy to move anywhere. It can fit in the laundry-room, corner or closet. And finally, this hamper is coated with something that makes it mold resistant and leak-proof.

Just sheer panels!. I think these sheer panel curtains by OVZME are useful and perfect in my son's room.  (1) They are basic sheers. (2) They provide protection from sunlight keeping the room cool. (3) There are 4 small panels versus 2 big ones. (4) I ordered them in beige, but they also cine in cream and white. And (5) They are inexpensive (under $20 on Amazon). I'd recommend them.

Gorgeous glassware with flaws.. These handblown, Mexican themed glasses are beautiful.
 They are colorful - glass sprinkled with confetti. The colors include: red, yellow, blue, white and green.
They are textured and hold about 10oz.  
The set has 6 glasses.
 Unfortunately, because these are handmade/handblown, there are some sharp, rough edges. Basically, there are some areas that just aren’t smooth. For example, on the bottom of all 6 glasses there is a round area that is open and has a sharp edges.

Now, the saving grace: These glasses can be used for a variety of things. Multiple uses. Not only can they be drinking glasses, but they can be used as votives, all you would need to do is add a candle. These would be some pretty pencil/pen holders. They can even be used as a toothbrush holder.

In summary: (1) Appearance - 5 stars. (2) Versatility - 5 stars. (3) Design and Execution - 2 stars.  Overall, 3 stars.

Old school meets new school!!. This butterfly chair reminds me of my youth - chairs my parent(s) had when I was young. It has a black iron frame and a leather seat. It might take a few minutes for you to assemble, between the lettered parts and instructions, but once you do you will have something that resembles the old school butterfly chair. To me, this chair isn’t really all that comfortable for someone my age and size (53 with bad knees), but for a young person (teens to early 20s), it will work. With that in mind, I plan to use it as an accent piece. It would also work in an apartment, office or entry-way. I also wouldn’t recommend this chair for someone who is really tall or heavy, they wouldn’t be comfortable, although we all know that leather gets more comfortable the more it is used or worn (i.e., the longer you sit in it). And finally, there is a slight odor to the leather, but airing it out for several weeks should do the trick.

Super cute lunchbox but pricey.. This Very Bradley lunchbox is super cute. It has black quilted/twill fabric with a silver zipper. There is a window on the side that you can put your business card in. The inside is lined/insulated. The only issue I have with this lunchbox is the price. On Amazon it runs about $39, which is expensive especially since there is no drink holder or special compartments. It literally can hold an average size lunch: salad, yogurt and piece of fruit OR sandwich, chips and a cookie. So besides being cute, this isn’t worth the money. 3 stars

Does what it is supposed to do.. The Fanhaq shoe rack is a little tiresome to assemble, but once it is, it serves its purpose. (Oddly enough, it even comes with white gloves to protect your hands from some black stuff that comes off the parts.) It is my opinion that it holds shoes without heels better than those with heels (this isn’t a deal breaker for me, but ladies beware). This is perfect for the garage where we keep shoes that we don’t use every day. Now my garage appears to be more organized. It will equally work in a closet or dorm room, really anywhere that it is needed. It is a decent quality, affordable and useful.

It's ok, not great.... So I just received this is the mail yesterday and was really excited, Jack White is my favorite artist regardless of what band he's with or solo and I've been a White Stripes fan for almost 10 years now. Now it doesnt say anywhere that it is like licensed merchandise or anything, but still was hoping for slightly better quality, theres just something a little "off" about the ink, like it's really shiny in spots, But I guess for the price I really cant complain too much.

Inconsistent results, but works OK.. I have zero previous experience with any other egg cookers. I got this for doing meal prep and trying to have healthier food on hand and ready. Overall I like it, but I do have some concerns. Nothing major since what I use it for, it doesn't really cause a huge problem. But if I were to buy another cooker, I would not purchase this one again.

So I get some really inconsistent results. I've used both eggs that are a few weeks old and super fresh. I've tried it on all settings, with 1-2 eggs in there or with a full plate. If I am not doing a hard cooked batch, they either bust out the top, through that little hole. Or they end up totally liquidy inside and under cooked. Fortunately, I like my eggs pretty hard and always use that setting. When I do it that way, they do cook entirely, but out of every 12 eggs or so, I will get 1-2 that come out of the top a ton and aren't really usable.

I'm not sure if this is unusual or not for an egg cooker. I reached out to the company and got no response back. But I've tried it several different ways, and don't end up with the same thing, so I think there is something off with the heating element or something.

Beware of Finish. Hi, had this for 6 months and has been used less than 10 times. Works great but the out side finish (red)  is delicate and is already scratched down to bare metal in spots, disappointing for the price.

Works Good Enough. Really, one can't expect much from such a simple concept. It either works, or it doesn't. I use large eggs with this, and it is sufficient. There is nothing to really brag about though.

Bought this cart as I have no automobile, and .... Bought this cart as I have no automobile, and rely on public buses. Otherwise does the job.
Cute shoe, size down. Shoes are off by a size, way too big.
