Makes bacon in shape of a bowl. First of all it takes a little experimenting to get the Perfect Bacon Bowl down. I still don't have it down to a science after making about 20 bacon bowls over the course of 3 days. (Rouse's had 3 lbs cheap generic brand bacon on sale for $4.99). This allowed me to come up with a few techniques.

I recommend spraying the bowls with a non-stick spray before laying down the first strip of bacon. Makes them much easier to remove from the bowl. Really, that's the only technique and it was already printed in the instructions.

Second, bacon from a microwave is not bacon. If you are using these bowls, cooking bacon in a microwave and complaining about it, the problem is not the bacon or the bowl -- it's you.

Finally, there's really not much going on with these bowls. Sure you can come up with a few recipes and get creative, but we're talking about bacon here. It's not going to last long once it is cooking and the scent is in the air. I found myself eating bacon shaped like a bowl 3 nights in a row, sharing lots with my dog for training purposes.

The case is lovely,  pillow is a rock. The outside is velvety and luxurious,  the "pillow" is hard as a rock.  It zips open and what I thought was going to be memory foam is unlike any memory foam i've come across.  Almost plastic feeling to it.  Would not recommend.

Such a big stand and a small receptacle. The ash/butt storage compartment is so small.  I thought you would be able to fill this with water to ensure fire safety, but it's such a small thing it's barely worth it.  You would have to empty and clean this thing weekly,  if not daily depending on usage.

Description doesn't warn you. Just had a plumber here.  He saw this sitting nearby and warned me, if I use this, it's going to blow out the wax seals. And you won't know it right away.  It will leak, the subfloor will rot and you won't know how bad the floor is likely until it's too late. You're better off getting a toilet snake. Returned after attempting to mount to the wall. It was very clearly not going to be stable against the wall with the enclosed hardware. Great concept it didn’t stand up. This was a great idea for college but it didn’t stand up so she would need a hamper as well.

Quality Is Low. You get what you pay for. The quality of these is very low. They are very thin wooden numbers that are very easily broken. The magnets are small and can pop off. Keep an eye on kids while they're using these since they will break and the kid could choke. They are bright and the kids enjoyed using them for a few times before they broke. Since they were so cheap, I don't feel disappointed in their breaking. But I likely won't buy more due to safety concerns.

Whose Clues?. This pillow case is apparently printed when you order it. It took FOREVER to get to us. (I didn't realize prior to ordering that it was shipping from China.) It arrived and it looks cheap. The fabric is cheap and it just looks like it is printed on. It does not open on the side, but rather has an envelope back. The back of the pillow case is solid white. My 2 year old loves it, though. (He loves Blue's Clues and it is rather difficult to find BC items since the show has been off air for so long.) Okay Futon. This is really easy to put together. The legs come in a secret zipper compartment underneath the cushion- so be sure to look there. I do like this futon. It does have a variety of seating options. It isn’t the most comfortable for sleeping, but definitely above normal futon grade. Really, the only thing I dislike about this futon is the fabric choice. It just shows dirt like crazy and is really hard to keep clean. Things tend to smear on it instead of wiping off. Pet hair is attracted to it. Crumbs are almost impossible to get out of the crevices. I would just think there would be something better to put on the surface of a futon. Something waterproof that isn’t so textured that is grabs onto everything.
The futon is high enough to put baskets underneath for storage, if you are so inclined. The arms go up in multiple levels. It is decently comfortable to sit on.

Not For Heavy Use. This is a really cheaply made CD case. It does the job, but it would be best for CDs you don’t need to be taking out very often. We are using it for our kids’ math curriculum discs and the daily wear on it really shows. It will have to be replaced very soon.

Pretty. These lights are cute. They look very pretty. The string is not long. It goes across the queen size headboard my daughter has. It takes two AA batteries that are not included. The battery pack looks pretty cheaply made, so I am trying to be careful to not break it. I wouldn't expect like super high quality for what I paid. They look awesome. They work. **Update- After one time hand washing this mug, the paint started chipping. I wasn't hard on it at all, but it chipped. Amazon did make it right, but I am not sure I would buy it now having known it would chip like that.**

Not Quite The Anticipated Quality. I would have expected better quality from Mikasa. The vase is nice and thick, like hand-blown glass. The color is more of a milk glass. The finish is just sloppy looking. There are small bubbles in the finish, not nice looking ones, but kind of frothy looking. The finish isn't perfect and smooth. I would expect some variation, but this just looks bad. I have much cheaper vases that look much nicer than this one. Mine is 10" tall, so there seems to be some minor variation on actual size. Also, the picture looks like the top is slanted and mine is completely flat/even.

Not Worth It. This ice tray does make pretty clean ice cubes. I find that they sometimes have small bubbles in them, but overall, they are generally pretty clear. The ice cubes are a bit difficult to remove from the tray. You put water into the silicone holder, which has a small hole at the bottom. Under the ice cube there is space for an entire other ice cube, which forms under the silicone tray. These two complete ice cubes are connected through the small hole in the silicone bottom. So, you’re pulling against a lot trying to pry the ice cube out. You can leave it out and let the cubes melt a little. Or you can use warm water to melt them a little to get them out. Neither method is particularly easy or quick. (And the under cube is completely useless and not intended to use.
Sometimes the silicone squares float up as I fill them up, making a less than cube ice cube. The entire tray is an enormous burden to have hanging out in your freezer. It feels like a cheap thin plastic over styrofoam. It takes up quite a bit of room to make 4 ice cubes.

Just Okay. This is a really large storage bin. It has canvas outside and that fabric paper type stuff inside. The Chevron stripes don't perfectly match up at the corners, but they do come close enough not to bother me. It works for its purpose. But there are 2 main things that bother me with this basket.
(1) The rose gold, while beautiful, is scuffed up. It doesn't look pristine and perfect. And if it did, I'm now aware it wouldn't look that way for long. The rose gold paint on the canvas just shows the imperfections really easily.
(2) The edging isn't up to quality for me. There are too many fraying or not quite sealed areas between the lining and the outer fabric. So, if you're really digging the print, they might still make you happy. But if you are on the fence, the quality issues might annoy you too much.

Cupcake Stands. These are just the weirdest.The marble look really does look like marble. But the bottom of the stand doesn’t look like marble. It looks cheaper, like plastic. It’s Gonna Get Hot. I really wanted to love this set. However, the “space saving” design causes some problems.
First, I really love the size of these. We have a large family and these pans seem up to the task of our family in terms of size. I do have bigger stock pots, but this one is big enough for some things.
Second, I really like the nonstick on these. It seems very durable and it actually works. I generally shy away from nonstick coated pans, but these don’t bother me much.
Now on to my issues with these. First, the space saving design doesn’t same much vertical space. I have gotten used to storing pans nestled together and then lids separate. This just has you pretty much stacking everything without much nesting. That creates vertical storage issues. The pans are also wider than my taller under counter cabinets are. I can fit them in the cabinet, but have to slide them through the cabinet door sideways. When you’re stacking this huge heavy pan stack, that itself is problematic and I end up having to take every single item out and placing them back in order from bottom to top. I also had to clear out this particular cabinet because I usually store my pans in a higher cabinet, but the height wouldn’t work in those.
My next issues are functional. The handles of these pans always get blazing hot. Like cooking with an iron skillet, you cannot touch the handles without an oven mitt. Even on the stove top, the handles heat up with the pot. Even the skillet handle. I got quite a few burns before learning to treat these like an iron skillet.
My final issue is the lids. They are made with the lid handles to the side instead of on top. This means the entire lid, including the handles, is always hot. There is no simple lifting of the lid to stir. You have to use a pot holder every single time. And because the handles are on the side for the “space saving” issues, it makes the lid awkward to hold when you’re just lifting it for a minute to stir. I cannot tell you how many times I’ve burned myself on these stupid lids.
So, in attempting to solve space issues in your cabinets, they have created pans that have entirely different problems. I had gotten my space issues handled, so the new problems are just frustrating for me.
These pans are really well made, great size, and great quality. I’m just not a fan, at all, of the space saving design aspects. I’d prefer the classic versions of these pans.

Fortunately, those tears were covered when we assembled the chair. However, it does show how weak the fabric is when you pull at it. I doubt the seat will last long. All it is going to take is one bedazzled bottom or something in a pocket to rip it open. And for people who actually use their furniture, this isn’t going to work well. Assembly was pretty easy. It comes in 4 pieces. (Back and back legs, seat, and 2 front legs.)

Mediocre. I have had beach towel like this before that were much, much cheaper. These have super cheap feeling terry cloth. It isn’t very wide. The colors are nice and saturated. But overall, this is a mediocre towel you could grab anywhere.

Low Quality Look To Graphics. The print on this cup isn’t the best quality. It is a little fuzzy, like it a low quality image that has been enlarged too far. The seam is practically invisible. The fell of the cup in the hand is nice. The kid dips downward, which makes drinking from it very much like there isn’t a lid. The edges are thick, so there is that. It is a cute cup. I just wish the graphics didn’t look so low quality. I don’t know if it was an intentional design decision or an accident, but either way, I’m not a fan of the end result.

Doesn’t Flow As Well. This is my second backflow incense holder. This one doesn’t seem to flow as well as my smaller one. It comes with a ton of backflow cones, unfortunately, they all just kind of smell like burning. Doesn’t have a nice smell. I typically prefer a Nag Champa type smell and these are just a generic cheap incensy smell. It is also a little bit difficult to get the cone onto the top and have the holes lineup perfectly. The mat under the bottom is like a round mouse pad, which confuses me a bit.

Really Soft. This throw is really soft, but it looks pretty sad. It gets all weird because the front and back layers aren't quilted or fused in any way. So, it ends up looking like a pile of random fabric. The ribbed side is also not quite right. It isn't ribbed enough to look like corduroy, but it is too ribbed to look normal. It is just such a weird look. The color is also pretty lackluster. Again, it is super soft and cozy-- it just doesn't look great to have sitting around. It came vacuum-packed and looked really bad when it arrived. Once I washed it, it fluffed up and looked better, though still a bit weird.

I Don’t Like It. The quality on this pillow is great. It feels nice and soft. The cover is comfortable. The strap is super silky and soft. The memory foam is not too dense, but not too soft. However, I just don’t like the shape or feel. I tried between my thighs, I didn’t like how that angled my legs. Tried between the knees— it just fit awkwardly. Tried between the ankles— super uncomfortable. I think I just don’t like have my hips and legs perfectly stacked while on my side. I tend to want one leg further forward than the other, or tipped slightly toward my stomach. You can’t vary your position much with this pillow. You can lay perfectly on your side with legs stacked evenly on top of one another. I just don’t sleep like that, so the pillow doesn’t work for me at all.

Work Okay. These are much smaller than I anticipated. I can fit one skinny TV remote and one tiny Roku remote in one pocket. It fits one Xfinity remote and one small sound bar remote in one pocket. If you’ve got a clunkier universal remote, it may not fit at all. It adheres to a surface with a sticker. The entire floral bit is adhesive on the back. It didn’t feel particularly strong, but it is staying put without a problem. Also, one of mine came with a tiny crack. I think this is useful, I just think the quality and size are a bit lacking.

Messy. This incense holder looks nice, but it is super messy. The ashes just fall all over the place. You can put multiple sticks in at a time. The top two flowers come off of the third flower, but they don’t connect. The top just sits onto the bottom. Again, they look nice but the mess and construction aren’t ideal.

Small. This coffee grinder is very small. It is okay for a single cup pour-over, but isn’t sized for hand grinding enough for a pot of coffee. I was surprised by that, because I typically use an electric grinder every morning for a pot of coffee. I was hoping to replace the electric one with a hand crank version. This is not that solution. It does work. And it looks really cool. But it is the size of a pepper grinder.

Painted Wood. This is my favorite style of incense holder. However, the paint on these makes them look really cheap. You can obviously tell the holes are haphazardly drilled. The wood version just looks a lot better in person. I like the size. I like the tray style. Just something about the painted wood just looks really cheap and not very nice.

Plastic. I got these in glass and loved them. They were the perfect food storage! I love the glass ones. These are not glass. The entire thing is plastic. I don't know why they put the silicone covers on plastic, that seems unnecessary. They look *exactly* like the glass version. But I'd rather not store my food in plastic.

Shorter Than It Seems. This chair support is much shorter in person than it seemed online. It does easily stretch around the chair. It does offer lumbar support, but it isn't the full-back support I expected.

Oddly Sized. This particular back flow incense holder is rather large. It has a large hole in the bottom. The size makes it so the incense really doesn't travel down the waterfall well. It kind of gets lost after the first fall and dissipates around the room. The large hole in the bottom (under the last fall) is just unsightly. I've had several back flow incense holders, and this is my least favorite one I've ever had. Also, why can't they make back flow cones that smell nice? They're always that super cheap big box store type of incense smell that just smells mostly like smoke.

Good. These are good storage bins. I like them, but I have some issues with them. First, they aren't the correct size to hold one normal box of cereal. Second, the lid can be a little difficult to get on and off properly. It just wants to be wonky. it did come with label stickers. Also, they don't fit stacked on my shelves. I know that is a personal pantry issue, but it is the reason they just aren't the best solution for me. I like them. They're pretty good. But they have issues.

The Press Isn't Great. In this set, two pieces are good. The silver bar and the silicone tube are excellent. The bar gets garlic and onion smells off your hands. Just wash you hands with the bar. The tube is great for peeling garlic. Pop a clove in, roll it on the counter, and then just pour the garlic out. It is also easy to clean. The press, well, I'm not a fan. The plastic just isn't strong enough to really press the garlic firmly. The cover also gets in the way. I'm not a fan of that part of the set.

Having Issues. First, mine came dented. I mean, it was inevitable in my busy household that it would eventually get dented, so I kind of took it in stride. But that wasn't a great start. The whole thing is large. But the trash side is smaller than my pervious can and the recycling side is even smaller. It does have holes in the inner plastic bins so bags glide in and out easily. But a completely full bag in this can is about half full when you pull it out. That is a little frustrating. Also, the bags don't sit very securely inside the inner plastic bin because  the bins are smaller than kitchen trash bags. They just don't sit very well. The foot lever also require quite a lot of force to open the lid. And the lid is ONLY openable by the foot lever. The lid closes flush to the can, so you cannot open it without using the foot lever. It can be propped open.

Not Great. We gave this a good couple months and it just never got more comfortable. I’m not sure if it would be better if it was thicker or what. It isn’t as hot as some memory foam mattresses, but it seems to add more pressure to the hips and shoulders than is really comfortable. I don’t hate it. But it certainly isn’t the most comfortable and won’t be staying.

Good Stools. These stools look great. They are nice and very sleek. The rising and lowering lever works very well. My only concern is that they don't seem very securely grounded. Perhaps I'm just not very used to using stools, but they seem to require a bit more balance than I expected. I also have a complaint, though: I have a pet-peeve with companies that use nice chrome metal for their product only to then use cheap, fake chrome plastic for some of the detailing. These stools disappointingly did just that. Ugh.

Looks Cool. This looks super cool. It is heavy. It looks expensive. But it is really poorly laid out and poorly made. The things in it just don't fit in that perfect "made for this" way. It also isn't everything you really want/need. It has only a few tools in it. For something this large, it should definitely be more complete. You could also use the container for ice. If you're looking for something decorative, this is likely perfect. If you're looking for something functional, keep looking.

Collapse. I love DII baskets, but these are just cheaper feeling than all my others. They are laminated cotton fabric, but the fabric is a tight weave, not a thick weave. They still work, they just don’t hold their shape very well at all. I find them constantly collapsing, even when they have things in them. I think the fabric is just too thin for this use. Or they needed an actual liner or something.

Wood Is Better. This is way too shallow to preserve soap properly. It works to keep the soap slime off your sink. However, wooden or bamboo holders do a much better job at really drying and preserving soap.

Okay. I'm not a gamer, I just spend a lot of time in my computer chair reading and writing and hoped this chair would be a comfortable chair for me. The arms are a little too short. (And I am not tall.) The foot rest feels very flimsy and cuts off at my ankles. (And I'm not tall.) The material is fine-- a little cheap looking, but comfortable and holds up well. I don't find this chair significantly better than a regular office chair, to be honest.
Interesting Incense. Amusing label. Interesting incense. It doesn’t burn like a typical incense stick. The tiny stick burns completely. It has an okay smell. Not long lasting at all.

Very Thin. I used this roll up mattress when we were at camp. The floor was cement, so this wasn't really the most comfortable. It was fine if you slept on your back or stomach. But if you're a side-sleeper (as I am) it is pretty miserable. I do find it more convenient than an air mattress (although it doesn't roll up to be very small). It was a decent size. On carpeted floor it is a little more comfortable, but definitely not something you're going to want to use for more than a night or two. A week on this was a bit brutal.

Okay, Not Wonderful. This Duvet Cover is super thin. It is like having white hotel sheets over your duvet. If you're using a comforter instead of a solid white duvet, know that this cover will be see through. With a solid white duvet, it is completely fine.
The peacock feathers are embroidered on, which I like. However, there are several skipped threads on the embroidery, making the feathers look a little messier than I think is intended. There were just several places where strings were hanging off.
The cover looks good. It has hidden buttons in the closure and the pillow covers are envelope back. It looks nice and crisp on the bed. It is 100% cotton, so it did need to be ironed before I put it on the bed. It is easily washable, which is a big plus. The colors are great and look beautiful.
It also does not fit like the picture. It barely covers the mattress, not the entire mattress and box springs like the ad shows.

Broken Elastic. I would have given this five stars if it had been sewn correctly. The first time I went to use one of the towels, the elastic popped off. I had to sew it back on. I also wish the "tail" that you twirl your hair in was a little deeper. I have long, thick hair and it is always spilling out of the tail of this towel. However, it absorbs water like crazy! And it doesn't frizz my hair. So, those are good things.

The light is not always on.... [[VIDEOID:dfe4772c732bf11aa61d84e5cff51cb5]] I like the vintage look of the clock, the size is just right and everything works fine. My only issues with it is that the light needs to be a pressed button and even then it's not light enough to light up the entire clock to truly read it correctly. So if you were hoping for a glowing clock at night, this is not it... and they put that in the description, I just happened to miss that detail.
The alarm seems like it's not lowed enough to wake you up at first but it goes from one level to a second, third and maybe a 4th of loud beeping. I personally just wanted a vintage clock that maybe glowed at night - or whenever you press the light on button. The light also works as a snooze button.
It's a good light, I would probably rather have spent about $11.99 for the functions I needed and what works compared to what the products mentions. It's not bad but it could use some improvements.
Works for flat surfaces. Not sticky enough to stay attached to lights placed by edges/ridges.
Not a towel to dry anything. Pretty but not very absorbent.
Very disappointed.. Not impressed at all had two seams and was not finished on the edge. Would never buy from this place again at $100.00 definitely not worth it. Very disappointed.

Works OK, but nothing spectacular. I ordered three different grinders for a test and this was the poorest performer of the bunch.  it works, but that's about it.  See my other reviews for the other two grinders.  There are definitely better performers at the same price or even cheaper.

It works, but it seems very thin and fragile. The good news is that it fits, but I'm not sure it will hold up to daily use.  We ordered an OEM replacement (more expensive but also more substantial) and are keeping this as a backup should the need arise

They work okay, but questionable origins and manufacturing. These are listed on Amazon  as being from the manufacturer HOOJO, but they are clearly marked VTOPMART on the bottom. Some of them have measurement markers on the side, some don't.  All in all, they seem to seal okay. It takes a while to get them lined up compared to other brands such as SISTEMA.  My main concern is that I question the true origin of this product, given the inconsistencies.  They are not specifically labeled as BPA free, but are marked as PP and code 5, which indicates BPA free polypropylene.  But - they are also marked as originating from VTOPMART....

Cannot run the filter manually and turn off the lights which are very bright.. Sleep mode is poorly designed, or perhaps mine is faulty.  I only have the option for the fan to be on the lowest setting and the light off.  I cannot turn off the lights independently of the fan speed.  So I have to use tape in order to run this at night, as the light is way too bright.

Bought as amazon warehouse deal. Product was quite a .... Bought as amazon warehouse deal. Product was quite a bit more damaged than what I was prepared for. We needed to use the shelf and did not want to take the time to return. My husband was able to bend back the pieces decently they will work at least.

Very thin. I purchased these to make Halloween bags for the kids. They worked but we’re very thin. (Like very low thread count and could see between the threads.) I didn’t have high expectations with the price, but was a little surprised by how thin. I will say they worked and no one said it fell apart.
Not very wide so make sure you know that when .... Not very wide so make sure you know that when you purchase. Takes longer to vacuum because it is so small.
it is okay item, the biggest complaint is the .... it is okay item, the biggest complaint is the 4 stand are so slippery, they should have put a rubber bumper under.
Okay but, not great!. Cheap and little. Maybe ok if you need to put in smaller location? The door on the hinge is half-working..not that great. Blinking tea light barely lights through it.

Not what you're expecting...not an insulated cup!!. These are reusable but, they are thin plastic and not worth the $ you pay...Wow! Starbucks should not put logo to the cup, without saying it's not meant for HOT drink. Should cost half of the cups you'd buy in the store...these also have a snap on lid, NOT the twist screw lid. Save money and buy cup that actually won't burn your hand with hot content inside...because, this one will. It's plastic sure, but like a thin plastic cup..and as guessed, when full of hot..plastic gets hot!!!

Beware of random label in mug!!!. Works fine, I did think it was plain silver. It has some random lame logo...?? They do a good job of keep that piece of labeling info. Tucked away in the description. (I say if it's true...just say!) It's good for the job if your just trying to get hot drink from A to B. If wanting something fun..pick something  fun on the outside, even if it costs a few more $.

Don’t be fooled by the size/amount..!!. These are absolutely perfect with the exception, and if you’re advertising them with the larger size rock- it can be a bit misleading at best. tbh, it would be SO helpful if seller showed what 50 of these look like in a glass cup, then 100, and so on…
It’s better to order the amount you need the first time and that usually isn’t done by a number quantity but rather a volume capacity! Something I find would make all the difference and save the buyer a lot of frustration.

Take notice of the photo included… I had filled this just over 1/2 way full and was hoping by adding these it would bring the volume to 3/4 full. Ha..!! Not even close- it would’ve taken five orders for sure- again, something that could’ve been avoided by sharing a visual of the volume these small stones would fill.

Otherwise, aside from being small like the size of a peanut out of it shell- they are a pretty color and at least add variety to a fun mix. Anyone interested be aware.. volume you receive from a single order is approximately 1/4-1/2 cup. Hoping this helps others not make the same mistake I did.. stay safe!

Love the concept… Just hard to use!. So, I wanted to love these so much!! How can you not have fun with a circular ice globe in your drink?! Problem is the container itself to create the ice globe is challenging at best!
This item splits through the middle must be exactly lined up together and when you fill with water.. it is hard not to have water leak out!!! Once you create the perfect seal, the other issue comes from this not aligning perfectly… So, getting a circular smooth sphere.. is nothing but, a challenge!

The price point was decent and almost too good to be true. If the product is hard to use then, it sort of renders useless!? This became more of a quest to create the perfect ice globe… Not that it matters on any important level. Just know, it is harder then it looks to create the perfect ice sphere!!

Removing the frozen ice was not difficult and expelling ice from case seemed rather easy. If any trouble- just a tad bit of warm water to outside.. let’s it come out with ease. I love what they’re trying to do in concept with this ice tray- it just misses the user friendly mark-
As for an on flavor of ice? Did not notice any… However, did not eat the ice but rather let it float in a drink. ** keep in mind the size of sphere to the cup- this could be a challenge to fit in some bar glasses If the opening to the lip is not wide enough.. our glasses fit these perfectly. These would be best use floating in a large punch bowl… However, can’t imagine trying to make enough to pull it off!

Not very sturdy- yuck sticks to brush!!. I was looking for a small durable dustpan and brush… This fits the size, just not sturdy and durable. It will do the trick. Keep in mind the bristles are plastic or acrylic and tend to stick to things such as hair or fuzzies that you try and sweep up. Basically, you have to hand remove some of the yuck from the bristles after you using! The lan itself needs to be more sturdy- but, it was cheap and get a decent set for the easy sweep messes!

Liked but, I did x4 of same color.. all black!. Ordered these for my son in high school… He’s into the necklace wearing theme! In the photo you can definitely see that there are four distinct colors. Brown, green, blue, burgundy.. unfortunately, the color I received were solid black x4 of them??!! Now, I would not mind a black color but because, I wanted the variety… This did not for fill the need we had.
The necklace itself hangs on a nice softer piece of leather cord, The knot to hold the pendant in place is a bit bulkier then, I expected. But, it is not a dealbreaker… Especially when being used by a teenage boy!
If, the quality control was there to make certain the variety pack held x4 different colors…this would have been much better. I removed a star for this issue- and a star for the bulky knotting. I’m not unhappy.. I just wish we could have gotten walk through photograph had shown.
The price point is very reasonable to receive four necklaces- and if the issues I had won’t cause you any concerns (ie. maybe these are gifts for different people and therefore, color is not as important?) then, you may be happily satisfied with the purchase. It is quite nice you can slip off and on without having to undo any type of clasp-

Nice in theory- not user friendly. Great in theory and wanted to help the environment.. But, this just doesn’t seem very feasible in reality. Feels like a prototype! The item itself comes in a small capsule which the straw telescopes in on itself… The cleaning brush is kept inside the collapsed straw as well. I do like the fact that this item can easily be contained on a lanyard or a keychain etc.. however, when fully assembled there are a few things that make it difficult to function and be satisfactory.
Each time one uses the collapsible straw-
you remove from case, take out cleaning brush and put cleaning brush inside capsule that stay closed up and reattaches to keychain or item of your choice until done using... and this is doable.

However, I am not certain how logical it is to store cleaning brush inside of straw? Yet, you want to house cleaning brush with you if using on the go… It will make clean up after use- so much easier. But, it seems like it’s not the most sanitary way to do this.. and sure, I understand the reasoning to keep size to a minimum, it just doesn’t feel sanitary!

Next, try as I might I can’t Rid of metallic/metal taste well using the straw… I did try some of the tricks offered online to rid the metallic aftertaste when using a canteen or, the likes… But, it didn’t seem to help? Maybe it’s mind over matter- or, planet over mind over matter??! Either way – this was not something I could get used to very easy.

Lastly, if you have ever used a large at straw for a milkshake? Be prepared for that type of opening with the straw.. it’s jumbo!! I realize the need for this with the telescoping closable feature but, this was the breaking point for me. Probably we’ve been spoiled in a world with plastic straws at an adequate size- I get it’s going to take a lot more tweaking and awareness to move away from the world with straws available at your leisure… BUT, this was not the end product I was hoping for- I believe there will be more revisions of the reusable straw in the future.. and they will trouble shoot these issues. So, I feel while people figure out the remedy for plastic straw consumption.. this is a middle step.. toward progress- not, perfection!

So, IF size of straw can be jumbo without bothering you AND metallic twang does not hinder your taste buds… AND you are not “germ afraid”’like myself – this may be something you’re interested in. As mentioned, the size and convenience of clipping this onto a keychain/backpack/wallet/lanyard is nice and let’s it be user ready when you need it..

If i could, I’d give this 3.5 stars and read why!!. To begin I’d like to get this 3.5 stars but, being that is not possible, I’ll include in a review as to why-

First of all, this arrives in a fabric carry tote bag that ties at the top.. this was quite unique and nice making things easy to travel/store. However, this would have been better if the tote bag zipped shut to secure it keeps clean while not in use. Although, most comforters arrive in plain plastic packaging- they offer a zipper to securely close that’s most beneficial! I wish the tote had a zipper...

It’s hard to hold anything against this comforter for being Light weight/thin/flat/crisp… If reading the description provided by the seller, they use light weight and crisp in their actual verbiage! So, being thin, shouldn’t/isn’t an issue- However, flat and lifeless is the best visual I could provide. Quilts by nature are not overly thick but, they do have some sense of some body to them.. I felt this lacked in that capacity- and when thinking of bedding.. that is something most expect and appreciate- A creature comfort feeling, something of substance that offers a warm an inviting feeling.. therefore, I deducted one star.

As for the color- we chose white. But, this feels to almost have a bit of a gray hue to the white, giving off the feeling of being old but, not in an heirloom quilt sort of way! It seems in trying to create a shabby chic/rustic look, the use of beige string trim was done. This doesn’t resemble as much shabby chic.. Only, more of a dinghy look. I realize, this may just be a with the white color.. But, when providing bedding in any space- be it a guestroom or otherwise, as the buyer I want to insure the confidence of nice/clean and inviting space to sleep- even though this may be all of the above… It’s important that the item look the part as well!! Therefore, if I could- I’d deduct .5 stars- simply because as mentioned- this may only be a problem or, feeling with the white color?!

Overall, I did appreciate the random lines and stitching- that does hit on the “shabby chic” look quite well. I would definitely recommend being certain of color choice when ordering and if one is wanting this to appear with a brand new “wow factor-“ it may not be suited for you, at least in certain colors. If, wanting to create a nostalgic or, a more heirloom type setting ie, in a cabin or antique room setting.. then, this may fit what you’re looking for!
I do hope the info. provided was helpful.. feel free to say so!

Beautiful ambience.. cute jars or amber volitive. The amber glass casts a beautiful glow in a room which looks stunning .. and it’s all powered by the flame of the votive glass… This set has a romantic and classic charm to it- its a perfect choice for a wedding, candlelit dinner or taking a bubble bath to a whole new level..!!

The 3 scents are pleasing and definitely can be enjoyed alone.. however, these complement each other nicely if lit altogether- there’s definitely a common thread allowing them to do so. I find the strongest throw is “Endless Summer..” however, it isn’t more then 5-7ft max.. being smaller in size this is to be expected. (see included pic’s to see size comparisons.) These are best used sitting closer to the user on a desk top, bathtub edge.. or in smaller spaces such as bathroom or office- if wanting to enjoy the aromatherapy at its strongest and not just the visual effects.

For a set of 3 at $13- this is a solid find.. each candle provides 5-7hr of continuous burn. These have beautiful aesthetic‘s that can step up in any occasion appropriately or, be gift worthy from start to finish these have all the attention to detail- including the hinged box provide to gift and/or store candles in.

Only issue experienced when using.. 2 of 3 candles had wick swallowed up by wax! It appears as if the heat dislodges the wick base as it burns low.. it wont be an issue if burned in x1 sitting. But, if planning to use over time- this may pose a problem.. it happened on both candles with 1/4 of the candle left. Something to consider with how you plan to burn. Hoping this info will help in your decision- stay safe!

Fun add-on to a special event.. but, has limitations!!. Makes for a fun night or celebratory event.. but, lacking quality in structure to last a long time. At the right price point- there are always special events where this type item can kick up the fun and be a hit.. New Year, SuperBowl, Mardi Gras, Frat Nite, 21st bday, Spring break, retirement, bachelor party and so on!

Personally, we purchased to help our daughter celebrate and induct her thru the right of passage to the 21yr club!! Amongst partygoers (most being college age) this was a hit. No! This did not perform as we had intended- as it had ability to hold and fill shot glasses equally at once- BUT, carrying by the handle was NOT an option.. Doing so would’ve been disastrous. this is not stable enough to lift and carry once filled, contrary to description provided. If you see yourself walking around passing out shots like a gracious host... Think again!!!

Hold onto the tiny plugs included.. since shots aren’t always taken in increments of 6.. these can plug line and cut off liquid.. these performed well without leakage.

Set up was simple and straight forward and overall footprint is small..(about size of dinner plate circumference-) Note: spinner option on top.. is just a fun accessory. It allows you to make up a fun twist on the dispersing of the shots.. but, of course it’s optional.
Shot glasses are done in varied color and are a bit smaller in width vs. height. (an odd shape for most shot glasses) Made of a cheap acrylic plastic.. IF, these didn’t come in a set you would probably think they were disposable. NOTE: this CANNOT accommodate a standard shot glass- so, careful when clipping into position.. there are no replacements- and part of issue with this not being strong and long lasting.

This can be a lot of fun for an event.. but, it has limitations in carrying ability and longevity. I hope this info can help your decision… Feel free to let me know!

Beautiful cover.. truthfully, it needs more inside!. A beautiful linen cover that’s surprisingly far softer than ever expected.. I love the outer edges are left raw and frayed- It gives this a real unique almost rustic or, shabby chić flare of character..

The quality craftsmanship is there with a traight, clean finished seams.. Zipper is actually located on the upper back side vs. hidden inside the end seam as usual. I mention in case this bothers anyone it’s in plain sight.. for myself, it was a non issue. Zipper mechanics are functional- easy open/close.. no loose/unfinished strings to tangle on the interior side. (a problem I’ve encountered with many other pillow covers!)

The compressed insert will take shape as its released from the air tight sleeve. My issues with this pillow come in the amount of fill one actually receives.. its simply not enough! After waiting 48hr for insert to reach its expected size/shape in expansion- there wasn’t even enough to fill up all the empty space inside the cover. Sold at a higher price.. I expect filling to be in a large/solid enough quantity.. especially at $51 price point!

Don’t get me wrong.. this is beautiful! When put together and set nicely on the couch it’s fine for visual aesthetic’s- it looks nice. Problem is, this insert easily flattens under any weight as the stuffing doesn’t stay firm but rather smashes into the “left over empty space..” all bc, the the insert isn’t met with a snug exterior shell- my plan to fix this is ordering a more robust insert.. Something that shouldn’t if paying $51.

Overall, a beautiful accent pillow- it just needs problem rectified with insert for the price. Hoping this info helps your decision.. stay safe everyone!

Building is from scratch!! Better for smaller shoes..!!. Wow! A bit intimidating when seeing the construction that must take place.. every section of PVC pipe comes in single sections and must be built one connector at a time!! Truly, a bit of a jigsaw puzzle so I recommend first spreading out and grouping all pieces into their matching counterparts. Next unroll one mesh “platform” at a time and insert pipe inside the mesh sleeves and cap with corners to create the physical platform- repeat for all 4 levels. Once you have shelf structure to work with.. it’s a lot more feasible to connect the layered tower. I’m assuming this is the reason for the lower price point.. The buyer does 100% of the construction- something to keep in mind when purchasing! If a PVC pipe tower is not in your wheelhouse.. another option maybe better.

Once assembled.. this has a lower height profile which helps keep it stable. This is definitely smaller in size and could be useful in tight or limited spaces. However, if using with adult size shoes…this more likely is to fit 6-8pair only (depending on the shoe.. some shelves may only fit 3 single shoes vs. 4…) I would definitely recommend this for children size shoes or, adults with smaller feet!

Overall, this is not for easiest purchase for convenience! It will take a bit of patience to assemble.. and once built it does have limited capacity. So, be certain it will fit your specific needs in its sizing and structure prior to ordering. Has both perks and quirks- be sure it fits your need!. A brushed nickel toilet bowl cleaner that hides the dirty ugly stuff in the bathroom- let’s face it, out of sight/out of mind is such a better option when it comes to toilet bowl cleaning! With a hinged flip top lid- this keeps the aesthetics in any bath or powder room looking far nicer then the alternative. However, the lid can be fickle which needs one to physically “click open” with their hand.. Uhh, yuck!!

As for the brush: Cleaning wand connects easily by the 2 ends with pre-made grooves that simply screw together to connect handle and brush. **Be sure to attach this tight!! I found while cleaning in a circular motion the brush can unscrew the two connective pieces.. Yuck again!! To avoid brush head falling off in the most inopportune moment- be sure connections are truly tightly fastened!!!

Bristles provide good scrubbing capacity- and although head doesn’t angle or bend.. it sort of shape-shifts to reach underneath the rim. Overall, a $15 solution for an “out of sight/mind” aesthetic for a bathroom.. it has a few quirks that could improve making it universal. As is- just be sure the length for toilet bowl won’t be a concern! Hoping info helps your decision- Be stay safe everyone.

Things like this I feel are not the buyers responsibility to waste their time to try and figure out… Not at the price you pay. Why 3 stars?? Bc I cant give it 2.5 and tbh, it is a nice sturdy option for a “first department” or game room. It isn’t an investment piece.. Single 36” wide size (NOT 80” queen size!) lower profile- NO built in pump!!. Listed as a queen this is actually just 36” across when the standard width is 80”.. So, not even close! Being far smaller its more in line with a twin. Be aware if needing for x2 peep-it may prove problematic!

Also note- the lower profile! Perks: it will take far less time to fill up and it will also fit into tighter spaces ie, back of camper or truck bed, inside of tent, etc.. if used for kiddos they aren’t rolling off to injury!l Quirks: may be difficult for older/compromised person to get up/down from just above floor level- something to keep in mind.

Online Ad itself states pump needed to fill along with instructions.. but, the box may be a bit confusing!? Not only does it list queen size, it also claims to have built in pump! FYI- NO PUMP IS BUILT IN..!! You need a pump to fill mattress.

Fill process approx. 5min. and prior to any weight in acclimated temp. mattress held air without leaking. *Dependent on temp. variances one should expect mat to expand/contract- ie, filled outdoors at nite while camping in Mtn’s mats tighter exterior will hold less air. The same mat moved into warm sun will relax and stretch in heat.. appearing to have lost air- when really outer material stretches creating more space.. and that extra space is what empty!! Whew- Science lesson at its finest! Body weight also causes mat to stretch.. keep in mind mat may need daily “top of dose” of air to maintain comfort/shape! Ideal for juvenile/teen sleep overs.. camping for x1 adult or x2 kiddos. Best for smaller needs vs. extended use. Hoping info helps clear up any unsure aspects- stay safe everyone!

Great gadget but the saddest nonstick pan on the planet. I have owned this Pizzazz for about 6 years I think. Goes back to before I started using Amazon, and I can't even remember where I bought it but it had to be brick & mortar.

I LOVED this thing. For frozen pizza, fantastic. But I have my own pizza recipe with my own homemade dough and that proved to be the downfall of pan #1. I think I made two frozen pizza and on the next pizza night, my own homemade. It was a long time ago, I think I smeared some olive oil on it with a paper towel (NO PAM, NEVER use PAM on any nonstick, I know that). The pizza crust ultimately was fuzed to the pan. It was very sad. I scraped it off with a plastic spatula and soaked it for hours. I didn't even have a dishwasher in that apartment so I certainly couldn't have abused it. It turned dark brown more places than not, almost like a shellac or varnish and I took pictures of it and wrote customer service at Presto. The lady was very nice and sent me a new pan.

Well, tossed a frozen pizza on that baby, it came off reasonably OK. Popped into the sink, and I never saw so much non stick coating float away in my life. It looked like a mosaic. I had not even taken a sponge to it.

So, for years my Pizzazz sadly sat in a cupboard. On occasion when it was too hot to fire up my real oven, I would cover the pans with foil and make my own or a frozen pizza. It was always fine. Really like the oven. Hate the pan.

I got the sadz for making pizza in summer and ordered a replacement pan from a vendor. Again, very careful. This one has survived two frozen pizzas and I am tempted to embark on the homemade variety. I am going to try and get pics uploaded of my two original pans and the new one. See how the new one fares. Again, I never use nonstick spray on nonstick pans. That is the kiss of death. And I don't every use this for anything besides pizza. I see in my Target store an "Ultra" pizza model and wonder what is ultra. The old one was fine. The pans are not worth the aluminum they are coating with whatever.

Received as a gift no previous to compare. I have never owned a bread machine so with nothing to compare it to am being neutral as possible.  Received this as a gift when lamenting to my mother that my arthritis is now so bad making even a little batch of pizza dough is too difficult.  Well I have made about a dozen loaves in this and three batches of pizza dough.  Also two batches of french bread in machine but turned out and baked in oven.  Most of the issues, first three, I have with it seem to be common to most average bread machines.  Too dark a crust, I always use light setting since I can always pop into my convection oven if necessary but can't undo a 1 inch hard crust around it.  The paddle hole on some breads can make it nearly impossible to slice nicely as the bread crumbles when you get near that. SMOKE often.  I haven't noticed any bad spills between pan and oven I didn't clean before it got to work but I still have smoking and can only assume it is from the flour that does get tossed up a bit. The cover can come off a bit too easily but I think if you have cabinets in the way of opening it completely you would see it useful.  Paddle got too loose on its spindle and did get thrown away inside a bad loaf.  This, after being loose enough to come loose in dense whole wheat dough and go kerboing around pan with the dough. I picked up replacement paddles and I put a thin slice of silicone oven liner in paddle hole to tighten it up a bit. Can also be difficult to clean around the spindle/gasket for paddle.  But overall I think bread machines are helpful appliances - just make do for folks that can't knead anymore whether it be time or physical constraints.  I am satisfied, in cooler weather now I may take more of it out to bake in oven rather than machine.

OK if you don't mind the clean up. Fed up awhile ago with George Foreman grills. Awful to clean and the best one I had the paint melted off the back of it and smoked and ran if I cooked for more than a few minutes, and well, that was the best one I had.

I replaced it with a very heavy Hamilton Beach grill with temp control, removable plates that were also non stick and dishwasher safe. It has served me for a couple of years but like with many of these double grills, the food always seemed more steamed than grilled. It was also monstrously heavy and though pretty compact, you had to be real careful the heavy plates were secured when you moved it.

I saw a grill similar to this one in a catalog and thought I would look into what was out there. I was torn between this and the more expensive Zojirushi. Really could not decide. I guess it was the cover that won me over. And that the grill plate was immersible. The cover does come in handy if you don't want to splatter the place up and you don't mind a little steaming going on. I don't find it causes as much steaming as two sided grills - the cover is loose so it doesn't steam up as much as it could. The grill marks are definitely better, probably because of the higher heat and reduced steaming. I was not sure I would like the little griddle part but it is nice. I can make little potato wedges pretty quickly on it, usually faster than the meat, have to watch that. Put a couple of slices of bacon on it another time.

I am still in a learning curve with timing but hoping to nail a london broil soon. I am notorious for killing london broils on anything but an outdoor grill and so far have had two flops. Both going by recipe time or booklet time. Some day. Maybe I will get that perfect medium rare and not gray throughout.

Then there is the cleaning. Oh. Well, I have not tried to put the grill surface in the dishwasher yet. I don't care to wreck nonstick in the DW. I would put my HB's grill plates in once in a while but didn't want to run down the nonstick. So I have been soaping up in a sink and letting the suds sit for a bit and scrubbing with a George Foreman grill sponge. It does an adequate job. But often have to use a grout type brush to get in between in the slats. It still does not come out perfectly clean but I can usually take a soapy dishcloth and get the last spots while it drips on the counter. I dry it and pop it in the stand. The water tray is another tricky deal. You definitely don't want to put too much water in there, very difficult to get it to the sink or a coffee can or wherever you are going to dump it. It is best to transport it in the plastic base as close as possible to where you will be dumping. I sometimes dump it in the DW if there is room. Otherwise, it is really not difficult to wash in the sink. The lid is similar though I often stick that in the DW if I need room in my drainboard for other things.

It did a nice job on burgers and steaks. And of course the potato wedges were a nice surprise. Pork chops were not good but I think it was really a case of bad tough pork chops to begin with. Chicken I overcooked, which like London broil I tend to be challenged by. It is nice, a little more work to clean so as not something I want to use everyday but I can use it once or twice a week without be traumatized by the clean up.

UPDATE: I have put it in the dishwasher and was pleasantly surprised. I mean I put the grilling grate in there. I have a tiny, cruddy little apt dishwasher and it just fit but I put the socket end toward the door so it would not get too soaked and I have got to say it came out nice. It also rusted on the bottom. Such is putting anything metal in the dishwasher. I would certainly not put this any more often in the dw than I did my Hamilton Beach grill grates. But when you have the room, don't have the time or patience to deal with it in the sink, yeah, it is what I would call dishwasher safe.

UPDATE - the second trip through DW will be its last. It didn't get it clean and there was a nasty grease film on everything else in the DW. Won't do it again. The coating seems more worn than ever I have used it 5 times and twice tried to use DW. Backing it down to three stars because cleanup is practically impossible from what I see/have experienced at this point

bearings went just under warranty - mfr replaced. I have been using the Norpro manual meat grinder for years now and was very satisfied with it. However, like all grinders it takes considerable time to clean. Since I could not do much of a quantity with my little Norpro I felt the ground meat output to clean up time ratio could stand some improving. So I looked for an inexpensive grinder that could do a larger quantity thereby making clean up time worthwhile.

This fits the bill. I knew going in it was not terribly powerful but I am not putting up mass quantities of ground beef or grinding up a deer or anything like that. It worked fine on a mix of chuck, sirloin and round. I did between 2-3 pounds which is about two weeks' worth for me. That would have been a good amount of grinding by hand.

Clean up is somewhat more complicated than the Norpro and this (and scant directions especially concerning "kubbe" sausage? attachments) are why I took off a star. Aluminum is lightweight and won't rust but it is a pain to clean when dealing with raw meat in that you cannot use a bleach solution on it. So it takes a lot of soaking/scrubbing in very hot soapy water. The mostly plastic Norpro can be cleaned with bleach ensuring that you are doing a good job sanitizing it. Of course grinder plate and blade needs to be hardened steel but I wouldn't mind a plastic hopper or chute.

Speaking of blade, whoever says this or any grinder won't grind at all almost certainly has the blade in the wrong way. It seems illogical when you have it facing against the grate but that is the proper way for any grinder to work.

UPDATE - the bearings (what it sounds like) have apparently gone after about 20 uses in 11 months. I have used this for 11 months as I said before, every 2-3 (lately more like 4) weeks. It is such a pain to clean (ALL grinders are) that I try to do a quantity of a couple pounds a time since I will be cleaning for at least an hour or two. I am NOT grinding Bambi's mommy. I am grinding cubed sirloin, round and chuck. Anyhow, after a session two weeks or so ago that went alright, today I cubed about 4 pounds of sirloin, chuck and round in preparation to grind. I assembled grinder and put some meat in hopper. IMMEDIATELY hear a horrible knocking sound and after a minute or two there was a smoky smell. I thought I had assembled something wrong so took it all apart with raw chunks of meat and put it back together, turned on the switch and same loud KNOCKING. OK, took off the whole hopper assembly and grinder, nothing but the motor and sure enough switch it on and the knocking and smoke. OK, it is the motor, probably bearings. This thing was NOT used heavily at all by my standards.

UPDATE: I first emailed the Mfrs customer service in China, after several days without a reply I went to Amazon as time was growing short on that mfr warranty. At first, they gave me the same Mfr email in China and even suggested I call them (kidding? No, I don't think they were) I don't speak Mandarin and was not going to spend on an intl call to find out if they have any customer service there that speak English. I then asked Amazon about contacting the vendor instead. Well Amazon sent an email to vendor with the order number and said customer doesn't know what to do with item. Huh? Excuse me, in this case the Amazon customer service was worse English than what I ultimately got in China. Well, I then sent my own email to Vendor explaining that I do know how to operate it and was for 11 months until it conked out. I waited two days without a reply and then picked up a better known model on "well known online auction site". Now here is the truth, no sooner did I complete my purchase there than there is an email from vendor (I believe also in China) saying they will check into it. Another day they say they contacted mfr and have decided to send me a new one. Another day and they ask me to verify mailing address, tells me it takes about 1 to 2 weeks fedex from China and they would get back to me with a tracking number. A week went by and I heard nothing until yesterday they email me to say that tracking says I wasn't home (apparently they sent it needing a signature). Ok, left a note for Fedex and now have two grinders. My replacement will probably go in the garage as a spare since the other I purchased is a more powerful, better rated one. But you never know. I have not tried it yet, have not tried even the one I purchased but I figure between the two of them I should be covered. Not the first time I have ended up with two of something just like this happened, it did with a convection oven also.

Moral of story is it pays to be persistent about warranty service/replacement if it doesn't cost too much to ship back or if they don't ask for the broken item. But it can take awhile. I would like to give them two and half stars since they did replace it but you can't give halves so will go with three. It did last nearly a year and for a cheap one that isn't bad, though again, it was not pushed hard or often at all.

Nice, But With Issues. UPDATE: The next paragraph has my original review. At the end (under UPDATE INFO), I compare the Mop Away to the original Jaadoo spin mop, but as a pre-summation, I believe that each has its advantages and disadvantages and I prefer the Mop Away's bucket design and performance.

This Mop Away Wet/Dry Mop could have gotten four to five stars from me if the mop head screwed on or snapped on easily, but it doesn't. Below, I examine the pros and cons, while I consider possible users who might benefit from this product. Before I continue, however, please know that there are two other units out there, including one by O Cedar, which might be better than the item that I'm presently reviewing, since the mop head appears to attach easier. A third manufacturer is Hurricane. All are made in China. You might also want to check the Korean made Jessy and the Smart Twin mop/buckets. They are fascinating to say the least and I suspect that any of these buckets, especially the Korean ones can double as portable small garment manual washing machines and wringers. The Hurricane and Jessy models offer mop heads that appear to snap on and off easily, since they connect at the circular base instead of at the end of the pole. The Hurricane, Smart Twin, and Jessy mops also spin while you're cleaning. The Jessy boasts a sturdy stainless steel pole. The O Cedar's triangular base allows you to reach into corners. Any of these mops are good for dusting by making the handle shorter.

Positives:
It arrived with three mops and a duster; very nice. The mop's pole assembly is easy. It comes in three parts that screw into each other, producing a nice tall, sturdy pole that offers 90 degree bending in opposite directions, making it possible to clean walls and windows with the mop, if you have the strength and dexterity to attach the mop to the pole.

I love the foot operated mechanism that twirls the basket and the mop. As the piston and gears spin out of sight and below the basket, the basket and mop head rotate, producing a centrifugal force that squeezes the water out of the mop. The ball design at the bottom of the pole allows the mop to spin while the pole remains steady in your hands.

The bucket is well weighted, so you don't need to worry about it tipping over while you operate the pedal.

Negatives:
Because of the foot operated mechanism, this bucket is understandably heavier and wider than an ordinary bucket. Its oblong design accommodates the mechanical parts. The added weight and design could be a problem for individuals like me who suffer from arthritis, but people with healthy joints and muscles will probably not have a problem with the bucket's weight and shape.

Another issue for people with arthritis or who may have balance issues is the height of the foot pedal. I would have preferred it a little lower. I operated the pedal with my back against the wall and believe it will also be easy to operate from a sitting position. So, if you're in a wheelchair and have functional limbs, you will probably be able to operate that pedal.

As I mentioned above, my pet peeve is with how hard it is to attach the mop head to the pole. Having small, arthritic and weak hands it's a major problem for me. However, a healthy young man offered to snap it in for me and I noticed that he too had trouble with it. After about four attempts, he managed to get the head to remain in place. The problem is due to the poor design at that contact point - there is no release/hold mechanism, but simply two square shaped pegs on either side of the pole that are supposed to fit into the square openings on the mop head. That thoughtless design has convinced me that the head will probably snap off repeatedly while the mop is on spin mode. I've learned that it doesn't pay to return certain things, so I freed myself of future headaches by getting rid of this spin mop/bucket combo. I can't see myself dealing with the problem every time I need to replace a dirty mop.

Yes, you can machine wash the mop and reuse it. However, machine washing such an item could clog household pipes, causing additional problems. So, to save yourself from that headache, I suggest you wash the mop in the bucket with a little bleach. Also, I recommend that you keep filled buckets away from small children and pets in order to prevent drowning and other hazards.

Now, I hope to have a look at the O Cedar competitor. It will be my third attempt at trying to recapture past memories with a good mop and bucket. I hope that the third time's the charm. Walmart is selling the O Cedar combo for $29.99; free home delivery with $45 qualifying orders.

UPDATE INFO: During further research, I decided to purchase the original Jaadoo spin mop and bucket instead of the O Cedar. The drawbacks for the Jaadoo are: the bucket isn't as steady or sturdy as the Mop Away; the wringer spin basket is too small for the mop; the bucket's spin mechanism jams while the Mop Away spun smoothly; without hesitation (however, I gave each a dry run; I didn't wet either mop in case that became a problem for my arthritic hands - I can't wring out most items by hand, if it came to that, and a full bucket increases its weight, not worth the trouble for a test). The Jaadoo's pole is 64", about 1/3 taller than the Mop Away, which I didn't measure before I got rid of it. I suspect that the added Jaadoo's pole length, attributed to perhaps an extra extension, might be a mistake, since the dealer (which was NOT an Amazon affiliate) sent me a unit that was obviously a reject, judging from the smudges on the bucket's handle and the pole's base, which also smelled of ammonia. It doesn't pay to return the item(s) to the Jaadoo dealer, since they want a 25% restocking fee and I have to pay for shipping. While Jaadoo's bucket comes with two spinners (one for washing the mop inside the bucket and the other for wringing), the bucket's flimsy design and the mops being too large for the wringer as well as the pedal/spinner's tendency to jam reduce the dual spinners' appeal. Unlike the Mop Away, the Jaadoo's mop heads snap on and off the pole easily. If I hadn't gotten rid of the Mop Away set, I would have had a functioning Mop Away bucket and two good Jaadoo mop heads and pole that would have wrung out nicely in the large and steady Mop Away bucket. I provide an honest review, but I obviously didn't make a good decision by dumping the Mop Away bucket the same day it arrived.

Finally, I filled the Jaadoo bucket to see if it could be used as a small garment washer/wringer. It failed that test too because the water immersed spinner is placed too high, in addition to the jamming problem, and the wringer needs a cover to retain a garment within the strainer. The bucket's combined oblong/rectangular design also makes it difficult to toss out the water. If you have a house wares/hardware store in your area, you might want to test a few of these buckets, mops, and poles side by side, but I found Sears' prices to be overinflated. You shouldn't pay more than $30 or $40 for any of these spin mops/bucket combos.

UPDATE - The O'Cedar bucket (Sept. 19, 2013):
At $29.99 (postage included at Walmart) the O'Cedar spin bucket was the least expensive. The others (mentioned above) were $40 and $70 (postage included). The positive about the O'Cedar bucket is that it's lighter and smaller than the others.

The negative is in the foot pedal. It allows the strainer to spin well, but its length is too short. It's probably good for people with small, thin feet. My feet aren't that big (6M-6 1/2M, depending on what I'm wearing). I operated the pedal with my slippers, which wasn't a good idea because the clearing between the pedal and the housing is narrow, and yes my big toe got pinched in the limited space. Another negative: the bucket's upper lip extends beyond that foot pedal, so as you stand above the bucket the pedal isn't easily visible for operation.

If I feel industrious enough, I could duct tape a metal or wooden lever to the pedal, thus extending its length and making it easier to operate. But, the longer a lever is, the higher it will be along the angle's trajectory. The solution to its height, curving the lever, would involve too much work.

Given the problem with the pedal, I didn't bother with the mop attachment because I doubt I'll be using this O'Cedar device.

OK Serving Bowl for COLD Foods. If you are shopping for dishes for the first time in a while you’ll notice a plethora of dishes made of Melamine. The prices are reasonable and the design choices plentiful. As a potter who understands the dangers dishes can pose due to the glazes used, I decided to dig into what Melamine is and whether I wanted to use it with my family.

So let’s start with what exactly is Melamine?

Melamine is an organic compound also called urea or carbamide, that is mixed with formaldehyde to form a polymer resin. Melamine can also be mixed with other inorganic compounds to become a flame retardant, a fertilizer and a plasticizer for concrete.

Melamine is commonly used to make strong hard plastic dinnerware but is made using formaldehyde and the safety of melamine dishes is controversial.

Any heat can cause these chemicals and resins to migrate into your food, so it’s wise to stay away from plastic and melamine tableware options as they aren’t exactly the safest dishes to use for health.

Melamine plates are not oven safe and the FDA advises against using melamine in microwave ovens. Melamine is made from melamine-formaldehyde resin, and the melamine can contaminate food at 160°F and above.

Pfaltzgraff?

I decided to do a bit more digging... Like many, I have been eating off Pfaltzgraff dishes my entire life. I have the dishes my mom had that I then inherited - they are Pfaltzgraff dishes that have been in daily use for 45+ years.

Pfaltzgraff had been produced in Pennsylvania since 1811 with the first factory opening in 1865. Pfaltzgraff was truly an American standard that many of us knew, grew up with and the name carries weight.

In 2005 the Pfaltzgraff Co. was sold to Lifetime Brands, Inc. It was at this time the vast majority of production moved from the US to Mexico and China. After doing quite a bit of digging, from what I can decipher, of course this information is not easily found, it appears the Melamine lines are produced in China.

So My Thoughts on this Melamine Serving Bowl...

There is no question that it’s plastic. This will be a personal preference to some degree but I think plastic serving dishes look cheap. Yeah the outside looks like marble - kind of. It is lightweight and Melamine is harder to break than ceramic - though it will break, especially if it’s cold.

After extensively researching Melamine dish safety I’m not comfortable with the potential risk of chemical leaching when temperatures are over 160°F or if foods are acidic. These dishes are definitely not microwave or oven safe. Something I always have to keep in mind is that while I would know not to microwave anything within this bowl that doesn’t mean my son or a guest would know that.

This bowl is one that I store in a different cabinet and use when we are going to a pot luck and I want to take banana pudding or the like. It works ok for that, it washes well and looks nice. Beyond that type of use I would not recommend it.

OK LED Smart Strip Light Set at a Reasonable Price. I have been using SmartHome products for more than 10 years, very close to when they started being produced and widely used. A few years later, I began testing, reviewing and writing about these products for several non biased comparison sites. Due to the experience within this particular area I have a broad base of knowledge within the Smart Lighting arena.

There are several considerations that need to be taken into account when choosing the appropriate Smart Light for a particular situation.

I have tested and written about literally dozens of LED strip lights over the last 10 years. I have tracked the advancements in the technology, understand the most likely areas of product failure and what separates the best LED strip lighting from the others.

In terms of light output, strip lights, of which this review focuses, is typically used for ambient or mood lighting rather than light to work or read by. Similar to the Hue Smart Strip Light, and frankly most major branded strip lights, this BIHRTC Light Strip can only produce one color at a time. In comparison, the LIFX Z Light Strip has 8 distinct controllable zones in every meter of light strip which allows for rainbow colors, animation effects and a full host of special effects.

The materials this BIHRTC Light Strip is constructed from are pretty standard in quality. The rubber covering the LED bulbs is thick yet very flexible. The 3M adhesive tape is standard on these smart light strips although people regularly have issues with them sticking.

The best advice I have as to getting any light strip to stay is to first thoroughly clean the surface the light is going to be attached upon. I first clean with a typical cleaning product such as a Lysol wipe, then thoroughly dry and then clean with an alcohol pad. Personally I don’t use the 3M double sided tape to hang the lights as it’s so prone to coming loose. I recommend the Gorilla Glue double sided tape which will be guaranteed to hold your lights where intended until you move them.

In comparison to other Smart LED Light strips this BIHRTC strip light is lower in lumen output to the Hue Smart Light Strip sets. While the colors are significantly less vibrant when compared to the Hue.

When comparing the duoco strip App (the actual name of the app used to control these lights) to the Phillips Hue App - the Phillips Hue app is much more robust and easier to use. When considering either of these two smart LED light strips to the LIFX Z, I have found the LIFX Z has the best colors, most versatility and best app - but it is also by far the most expensive.

In terms of the duoco strip App I had no issue connecting to the light via Bluetooth, due to it connecting via Bluetooth and not WiFi, range will be far more limited in terms of controlling, but this is rarely an issue. The app has plenty of pre programmed lighting modes, allows for syncing to music and custom colorization. Due to this being a product specific app I have yet to find a way to integrate it with my SmartThings hub.

A huge bonus to this BIHRTC LED Strip Light set that is rarely seen is the ability to control it with a connected control module. Consisting of only 3 buttons it allows the lights to be turned on, change colors and switch between modes. The set also comes with an IR remote that allows for greater control and, of course, the app which allows for even more.

This product, BIHRTC LED Strip Lights is decent quality - especially at this price point. The other sets I compared it with cost approximately 4-6 times as much - I chose those as they are the ones people are most familiar with.

In terms of value and functionality this is decent LED Strip Light Set that I recommend if you are not looking to integrate with other SmartHome products.

We’ve decided to use this as a travel blanket as it’s lightweight and portable - the clip on the storage bag easily attaches to our carry on case so it will be there when we need it.

Decent Clear Hangers for Lightweight Light Strands. These clear hangers will work perfectly if you want to hang fairy lights or even the smaller Christmas style light strands - though you will have to use more of them and likely need to use a nail to attach.

I have utilized these in multiple locations, some with more success than others. I have found these perform far better indoors rather than out and it is critical that the surface be prepped prior to adhering the clip. Should there be any dust or debris these will not bond properly.

Something that is important to note - these will damage interior walls. The glue used on these clips is not similar to what is used by Command Strips brand clips so when you remove these clips it is difficult to do so without damaging the wall beneath.

I have had great luck using these to hang decorations in odd locations where I could not use any other method and these have proven to be more effective than I anticipated. By utilizing 2 clips in succession they can support far more weight than a singular clip - this has come in handy for hanging a few odd Halloween decorations.

This is a great set to have on hand. Understand the potential issues and avoid them. These can be used in really effective ways.
