So just a warning to someone else shopping, the product is great but don’t forget to buy hooks!
It has a real nice look. The item is very nice looking easy to hold easy to drink from. But the bottom  cap Keeps falling out so it makes it unstable to set up a table.
Blurry. Love the print, but it is quite blurry and that is disappointing.
not high quality. These do not include the fine tooth saws needed for details
Nice Curtain. The curtain was exactly what I was expecting. It fits its purpose but it wasn't as pretty as I've hoped.

Small Fan. Although very pretty, this fan is very small. I just thought it was going to be a lot bigger because it wasn’t cheap. I bought it so I can use it every day at work, I didn’t buy it just for looks. I was disappointed when I got it.
Not comfy. Nice sofa for small apartment but comfort is not there. Cushion is so thin.
Poor quality. Item arrived with chipped paint on all corners. Worst, the drywall anchors are easily broken. They broke when I tried to install them following the instructions. Will be returning
Smaller than expected.. Too small. Quality is not the best.

Much smaller than the pic. Ok...weird..
The adhesion is ok..so far nothing has fell off..HOWEVER, the quality is not the greatest. Mirror finish is nice once you peel off protective covers. Extremely tedious to install . Super small, nothing like the pictrue at all. About the size of 2 8×10s depending on placement..cute, not elegant..just ok

Tiny table, more like large footstool. Table is much smaller than expected. Very small.. Wood is NAKED..you cannot wipe it, you will get splinters.  Very pretty though. One panel is already loose...not too heavy.  Easy assembly. All in all,  not worth the price,  although handmade, craftsmanship is sloppy.. I have to go buy sealer because you cannot place anything on naked wood..WEIRD!

Not Quality..... bound to mess up within time!. Clothespins take a lot of abuse. They endure the weather if left out, endure knocks to the ground, possible stepped on. Plus, clothespins take a lot of handling. I hang mostly sheets in the winter and other clothes, so I use a lot of clothespins. These are ok with the color, although color may not last long either in the weather and sun..... especially if left out on the line.

The bracket that holds the sticks together is where these go wrong. The clothespin bracket is easy to twist, therefore easy to break off. The price is conducive to the quality of clothespins.

Nice lightweight chairs! Don't work as great. Hard to push up or down. This barstool set is attractive, black and silver chrome. It is nice to be able to adjust it to the height you need. There is a foot rack that helps keep your feet in place. Also, there is a rubber ring at the bottom to prevent scratches on the floor. The seat is comfortable, soft, and cushioned well.

However, in testing the up and down level gadget, I had one issue. If you have this at the highest level and need to bring it down, and are not sitting on it........ lay your body on it to PUSH it down. Push hard!

I like that it is very lightweight....move it with one hand. That is an asset. However, if you are sitting on it, put your entire body on it. Do not set at the edge of the seat.....otherwise you will tip the chair. Please do not allow children to try to climb it, as they will tip if ..... if you know how childjren climb.

I am using this as a puzzle table. I have a table that adjusts and 360 degree turning radius. And this chair matches it perfectly. Plus, I am using the other one in my lower level for craft work.

ONE NEEDS A DRIVER'S LICENSE TO OPERATE THIS. ... SUCTION IS GOOD.. This vacuum has powerful suction. Very good. However, maneuvering it is rather cumbersome. As you move along, the front of the vacuum steers to the left or right, without any notice or intention to move it that way. It becomes rather heavy, and steering it takes a lot of control from your end.

I like that it uses no bag. However, in my home, the bag can become full rather soon. Especially with cat hair and just plain dirt. So, the container for the bag is at MAX level...... when it is half full. The brush attachment tends to not roll. Not sure what is going on there. And, as per usual with attachement release buttons, they are always hard to do.

As for the "floor sensor", I am not sure that plays an effective role. There appears to be no height adjustment on this, so that tends to be a problem going from floor to thin rug.

I wish companies would stop trying to create a magic vacuum. Just keep it simple and all is okay.

►► ►►EDIT ! COMPANY WAS CONTACTED AND WARRANTY WAS IN PLACE.. EDIT ►► ►► I have the base of the vacuum detach from the STEM. There are Two wires showing, RED and Black, and I cannot get it to reattach again! I contacted the company and the Repair was made!

Ever have to drag around a dead fat pig??? That's what this vacuum feels like, but so do almost all canister vacuums feel. It is not easy to manipulate canister vacuums, but if you must, drag this one around. It picked up so much crud..... I didn't even know I had that much. Of course part was cat hair, and the other part was the carpet fibers he scratched out.

Granted, the vacuum has all the neat things, attachments, lights, bells and whistles. But, one thing I do like is starting it from the handle! You don't have to keep going back to the dead pig.....ooops, the canister to turn it on. This is great.

And, another great thing to have is the Brush Cleaner! Well, I haven't seen a clean brush. I had to pry off strings and dirt from the brush. Who likes cleaning the brush??? Not Me! So this is an important feature, provided it works. I also like that you can adjust the levels Digitally.

I struggled with this, and have not mastered it. It is never easy using canister vacuum, but this one was more challenging than I expected. I guess if I was vacuuming the Taj Mahal, it might be easy, but a home, with hundred things in the way???

Ok, I did like the Brush attachment. I have wood slat blinds and I used the brush and I could see where I cleaned! However, it won't get it 100% clean, but does a good start.

If you like canister vacuums, this will do the work! If you do not like canister vacuums, try this one anyway..... It is a powerhorse! The BEAST!

Good, but Lettering is NOT Visible Much!. Update. CONTACTING THE COMPANY FOR RESPONSE.
Thank you for the company who responded to my review. All is good now!

I like this toaster, it is silver and goes with my black and silver decor in the kitchen. It doesn't take up much room, average two-slice toaster. Works efficiently. I did try at the beginning a once slice that didn't toast good on the other side. But, as a use it more, it did seem to work good, both sides.

What I don't like is the lettering. The company claims the lettering is easy to read. NO, it is not easy to read. And, when you have company coming and using the toaster. ....... they can't read the markings either. The font is too small and doesn't stand out against the silver color.

Other than that, I will monitor this closely.

Not worth the effort!. I think this is a case where the old fashioned way is better. Pull the pot out, fille it with water and time your eggs on the stove. There are too many devices for us these days. We do not need more that are not necessary. I would not try cooking a scrambled egg. I have boiled eggs and not with great consistency.

The device is lightweight.....too lightweight. So, this is more trouble than it is worth.

Cannot get "moisture" in the air. All I feel is the fan.. I'm not too keen over this digital readout evaporative humidifier. I have tried it several times, and for one thing, I usually get a moist air from an evaporative humidifier, but even on high, I could not feel anything but cool, dry air. I was not getting any indication that it was a moisture air.

OK.... EDIT. I ran it again for the 5th time and I do believe it did shut off automatically.

But my issue is that I believe a evaporative cooler should put out "some" moisture, and I am not getting it on this one.

Well..... it will warm your fingers!. This fan is lightweight, easy to use. However, the hot air is not sufficient. It is not strong. You can warm your fingers, but that is about it. Hubby wanted me to use this in my giant garage to work on my business in the winter. I told him...... this can't even warm the kitchen!

The cooling fan is the same..... Pass this!

Nice concept, attractive with easy off and on. Doesn't get hot enough.. This is actually a beautiful coffee warmer. I like the concept of an attractive piece, and by that I mean, it is discreet and looks good in the living room! I like the easy, off and on button in the front. Very easy access.

There is also an Auto off feature. It is 8 hours. It would be better if it shut off within 3 hours at the most. I don't like that it could sit in the ON function for 8 hours......too long.

And, third, it is only 20watts. That is not any better than most of the coffee warmers. I would prefer something that keeps the coffee .... at least a little hotter than normal coffee warmers.

Need to run the air condition below 60 degrees to get serious cool.. Well my confusion is in the "draining" of the thing. I never figured out how it drained, or if it needed to be drained. But, I put this in the larger living room, and it seemed to be cooling, but you need to have it at 60 degrees. Sixty degrees is cold in air condition talk, but for a room, it is not cooling.

I used it in the small bedroom also. And, I think that you have to run the air condition at 60 or lower to get it to remain cool. The hose is stiff and I placed it out the window. I will used it more next summer and see about the drain thing. I couldn't figure it out.

Not as absorbent as I would expect. This material is big, nice size, and great for those large pots and pans that need drying. It is also great to dry your larger platters.

However, I feel the absorbency does not react as well as it should for a drying towel. I believe that the material is just too flat, without any fiber to pick up the wetness. Material to absorb needs to have material that is not flat, but with more cloth fibers to sop up the wetness.

I love the bright green color. Easy to spot in the laundry crowd..

The good thing? There is a White small band that serves as a ring to HOOK the towel somewhere.

Can't see the use of the "grill  ridges". I can't see where this grill pan is beneficial for a grill-look.  It doesn't really do that look efficiently.  So,  if you use it as a regular breakfast egg pan,  the ridges get in the way.  It is big,  and nonstick, and functionable for use when no "grill-look" is needed.

UPDATE I had to trash the pitcher.. UPDATE~ UPDATE~ I used this pitcher faithfully, and didn't know when to change the filter, so I tried changing and could never get it back in. It was the blue filter and I tried and tried so I had to trash the pitcher.

I got this pitcher because my refrigerator needs water filter and those are expensive, plus they don't last too long. So, I do need to have filtered water and decided on this method. And, hopefully, the filters last long and are priced good.
This is a large pitcher, and I choose to have it on my counter where the coffee is. I drink from it all day, and use it for cooking and coffee. I don't need ice cold water, so I use it all day.

The one issue I have is that it DOES take a long time to fill up. And that must be because whatever you pour into it, takes time to go through the filter.

This is a nice, large plastic water pitcher. It is black on top of the clear plastic. Looks nice. I may get another one so I can keep one in the frigerator for hubby who likes cold water.

Heavy Duty yes, but don't try to overload it. These are very nice grocery bags. They open wide and the material seems durable. The bottom, however, is not meant for heavy packing. I take these and put all the bread and bagels in it. Or, cereal boxes. The base is not strong enough to support heavy cans. Nor should it support the gallon of milk.

The sides feel like lite cardboard, and that cardboard feel means it will not support much. So, use it sparingly if you use it for groceries!

The Toast Popper Upper doesn't Pop high enough!. I have not had a toaster that did not pop high enough. Well, I found one! The toaster is simple to use and using bagels quite often, you just need to adjust the temperature level FOR the bagel. It takes time to find out what works. I do have mini bagels too and those need an adjustment level also. The SLOTS are wide enough, no problem there. But, if you use small breads, like French Breads, the bread will not even reach the top ...... to pop. I have even turned the toaster upside down to release some toast!

The toaster is simple, knob adjustment and a bagel button. Different breads and bagels may take a different adjustment level, but keep experimenting to see what works best. So, my only serious fault right now is that the Popper doesn't Pop high enough. Grab the toast carefully!

With A Seat This Hard, Who Needs a Chair?. This modern looking chair LOOKS comfortable, but it is not. It appears as if the seat is soft, but I sat on this and practically bounced off, it was so hard. Plus, this is geared for a taller person, someone whose back will come right to the back of the chair.

If you are not tall, a pillow for your back would help. And, again, what is with the hard seat? The legs appear spindly, and I can't be sure they would support a few-hundred pound person.

The chair may be best for an office, but I will tell you, the seat will be the first thing someone notices. So, all around, this is not comfortable, whether you place it in your office, or your home office. I doubt anyone will want to sit in it for long.

◕◕ .. If you use this for the office, where you have customers/visitors, they might want out of the office quickly, if they have to sit on this chair. If you have someone to visit and need to get rid of them quickly, let them sit in this chair. I guarantee, they will leave quickly.
Toaster - Really ONLY ONE BAGEL AT A TIME!. Toaster - Really ONLY ONE BAGEL AT A TIME!  All else is really great.  But you can only toast bagels on the left side.  STUPID, STUPID.

Not very good. Not very good at all. I have tried 5 times to make it look like its so post to and it never come out right .

people must like sleeping in quicksand. Wow can't believe people enjoy sleeping on something so mushy. It appears to be a well made product but it is like soft sponge, no support whatsoever. No smell. Easy to Handle. Thank goodness because I returned it. Bought a firm cover at Wal-Mart for $16.00.

Great looking. Very small. Poor controls. Bought at Walmart for a few dollars more. Not big enough inside to make much of anything. Controls are inexact and hard to figure
Out. I am returning it.

The wrap around idea worked but there are other wrap arounds for half the price. I will be returning this.
Small. I have 5 crockpots and none of them fit in this bag.

Deceptive pictures.. I would love to give the pillow 5 stars but, I fell for the picture too and NOWHERE in the description or elsewhere could I find where it said how many pillows were included. I assumed for the price that there would be 2. Now I have 2 guests and one pillow. My fault, I usually read reviews. I would have known had I read them since the company failed to disclose this info. Good pillow though.

Towel Rack. This towel rack is lightweight and extremely easy to assemble.  I was able to do it without a few seconds.  I like that it holds several towels and fits over the doors in our apartment.  We live in a small apartment so being able to find alternative storage is great! What I do not like about it, however, is that, once installed, we are unable to close our door!  We live in an older building with the old wooden doors.  Once we installed the towel rack, we were unable to close the door all of the way.  Due to this, we have moved it to our bedroom door.  We live in an older apartment with thicker doors.  This may not be the case with every door though.  I also think it is a bit overpriced ($39.99).  I like the OXO brand and have many of their other products so I understand their items can be a bit pricey.  For a towel rack that doesn't allow us to close our door, I would expect it to be a little less expensive.

Manual ones are better.. This is great to use if you have the time and patience. Honestly, though, I've had a harder time using this than the manual openers. How? I can never get the position flush with the bottle, and it always scrapes to the side. The machine always sounds like it's going to run out of the juice, thought it doesn't for a while.

It's sleek and adds to the kitchen, but the manual one, though less "fancy" is better.

Spilled pepper everywhere.. I for the life of me could not figure out how to use this. While it comes with instructions, it doesn't actually show me how to use it. I ended up spilling a great deal of pepper on the counter, not even realizing I was doing so until about ten seconds in.

The finish is great, and the twist is okay with a little bit of resistance, but instructions would've been nice with how to actually use the device.
After I actually used it I had no issues with it leaking.

Basic wine rack. I like to drink the occasional bottle of wine. We have a specialty beer and wine shop down the street from our apartment so we have been known to stock up on wine from time to time. I attempted to place the bottles we had on hand in this wine rack and it proved to be rather difficult. It takes up a lot of counter space (this may just be me being picky!)
My husband made a good point that this particular wine rack did not tilt the wine bottles like other wine racks we had seen. We aren't wine experts, but this seemed like something to note. Although the price seems reasonable, this wine rack is nothing special - a basic wine rack for those who like to dabble in wine from time to time.

Chore to use.. The grinder comes in multiple pieces so that it's easy to clean. It's handheld, so it's small, so expect to grind a lot to get the right amount that you need. I have to grind for about five minutes to get a couple cups' worth of coffee. The handle slips easily when trying to turn it without coffee in it, but shockingly I found that it didn't sleep once when I ground the coffee.

Just be aware that you will have to exert a lot of energy to grind. I developed a technique where I turn both the handle and the container at the same time to get a few more rotations in.

Not what I expected. Between school lunches and baking, I have a ton of boxes that need organizing. For this reason, I was excited to receive this, but I was quickly disappointed upon using it.
It’s not very sturdy and does not hold the boxes in place. It is a nice idea/concept but needs some adjusting

Not for traveling.. These are for keeping office garments clean at home; they do *not* work well when traveling. Yes, they are light, but with that they have no sturdiness. One ripped easily when it stuck in my closet and I was trying to pull it from a metal hanger. I use these to store clothes long-term now.

They start excellent, but after a couple of washes they become difficult to clean.. I was super excited to get these. I just received a bottle of Tennessee whiskey and when I saw these glasses I knew they would be perfect to break open my bottle with. They're a little classier than the shot glasses and whiskey glasses I have, and they look great without liquid in them too.

When I opened them out of the box, I was a little surprised to find they were made of glass. They seemed--and still seem--a little thin and almost plastic-like in feel. I'm almost confident they're glass, but it's a very thin glass. I think it would've been better if the outside was solid; instead, it's just a thin, single wall around the glass and the bottom is completely open. It's cheaper for them to make, but difficult for us to clean. As we don't have a dishwasher and I wash all my dishes by hand, I have to use both the regular dish scrub and a bottle scrub to get in all the crevices.

But the thinness of the glass starts to rear its deformed head after a few uses. At first I thought it was me, but when my wife, who doesn't drink whiskey at all, mentioned that the glasses looked yellow I realized it just wasn't me. The glasses were staining and were not getting cleaner the more I cleaned them. They look great when there's liquid in them, but on the cupboard they don't look attractive. The outside would've been better if it was solid glass rather than a thin wall, methinks.

It's a shame because I think the design is really neat and I they work mostly great. The rim, I think, could be a bit thinner as sometimes the liquid has too much space to travel on top of the glass before it reaches the inside of my mouth, so sometimes the liquid unintentionally slips over the edge of my lips.

Great construction, but very narrow width.. The bottle itself is very sleek and smooth. I've used it a few times so far and it has held up my drinks nicely while having a nice plastic filter that prevents the liquid from spill out too much when drinking.
The top is pretty easy to screw on and off, though I wish they didn't etch that logo and text on it. Seems gaudy.

The only thing is that it's ridiculously narrow. Even our bottle brush has a hard time fitting fully inside it, and none of our spoons are thin enough to go in and mix ingredients.

Great machinery, but the etching and width really drive it down a bit.

Did not last. I loved the idea of being able to store extra blankets during the warmer months. This storage bag held two lightweight blankets. However, the bag was not very durable and did not last. I would recommend investing a more durable option.

Good, but weak lid.. Works wonderfully in our CR-V between a booster seat and a toddler's car seat. Our daughters store coloring activities, snacks, winter wear, and toys. The lid is pretty flimsy and doesn't stay put. I think it should be rigid, maybe incorporating plastic into the structure.

Feels cheap, stains easily, but hasn't broken yet.. The glass this is made from is very thin and feels fragile. I'm honestly surprised I haven't cracked or chipped it in the year I've been using it. It also stains easily, as it has blackened especially so in the spout.
The metal is thin, but doesn't feel as cheap. I'm still able to make my tea without it spilling or becoming too hot, so I guess I'll continue to use until it's no longer functional.

Overall great, but can create a disaster.. Definitely the best cups of coffee I've had from a home machine. When it works, it works well. However, I've created huge disasters from this thing, and it's due to the filter container. If it's not completely in its place, the brewer won't pour the water and coffee into the pot, instead, it will overflow out the container and outside the pot, creating the worst coffee messes I've ever had. There is a little point under the container that must be positioned correctly on the pot; if not, then the water will not go in. But instead of having a shut-off mechanism, the coffee maker instead will pour the water and coffee outside the pot. This is a huge flaw that I ran into twice. Considering I'm the owner, I can't imagine if a guest decided to make a cup o' joe.

These towels shed!!. I would not recommend these towels. They were great the first few days we used them. As soon as we washed them in the washing machine - GAME OVER. They are cheaply made - they constantly shed link on your skin. Note to self: do not use these to dry your hands right before putting your contacts in! Lesson learned. I would not recommend purchasing these - they are other towels in a similar price point that do not shed.

Works well enough, but thin and the zipper is light.. I don't expect to have this travel bag for that long. It's good enough to take to and from work, but not for heavy travel. There is no area for shoes or accessories, so keep that in mind. Great for short travels, however.

Purposeful but not high-quality.. After about a month of use one of them started to tear away at the top; part of the clear plastic started to remove itself from teh black fabric. We keep these under the bed with very minimal movement against them; the bed is high enough so that it doesn't touch the storage bags at all. We have hardwood floors, and the ottoman against the bed and the bed itslef has metal legs; I don't think these are the culprits, but I'm not sure why else the plastic would start to tear away.
We use them to store seasonal sheets and they're fine for that; the plastic tearing itslef away doesn't prevent me from using them. The tear is only a few inches long, and there's only one (so far).

Nice machine; most versatile of the ones I've used, but still leaves watery coffee.. After visiting a friend with a Keurig we caved and got one for ourselves. The coffee was convenient, and we've used plenty of Keurig machines in the past, so we had a substantial idea as to what we were getting. We chose this model as it seemed to cater both to individual cups and larger brews, and had a large water reservoir.

I spent about a good week messing around with all the different settings to finally land on the ideal settings for me--but it still isn't "perfect." As a Dunkin aficionado, I prefer black coffee with a bit of flavor swirls, and sometimes a bit of sugar depending on my mood. I found that, with this Keurig, it's best to make a smaller cup so I get that concentrated taste, and add flavored syrup and a bit of water to get it close to how I like. However, no matter what, the Keurig always leave the coffee watery, and that's not with the fact that I add just a smidge after the fact. I can never get that concentrated taste I like, and by the second cup I always toss the rest out after I finish half of it.

I also like to point out that Keurig doesn't make it easy to recycle these things. I knew of the environmental factor before purchasing, but as I had no reason to look up actual recycling services until after purchase I was shocked to find out they don't make it easy for consumers. I have to send it to third parties to get that done.

I do like the versatility and convenience. Visitors can easily make a cup of tea, hot chocolate, coffee, or cappucino in less than a minute. For that alone, Keurigs are well worth it. But as for everyday use I find it better to get some Dunkin from the local shop.

Has one (large?) flaw.. We got this to use on our daughter's upper bunk. While the cable is a bit short for our liking (it barely reaches to the other end of the lower bunk), we were able to make do. The one big flaw for us is that, because this fan is used on the upper bunk, the fan doesn't stay in a lower position. One slight touch or movement of the fan or cable and the fan immediately toggles upward. You have to be very gentle to keep it blowing downward.
We get that, because of the footprint of this fan, this is mean to blow upward. However, it would be beneficial for a fan of varying heights to be able to stay at each height without moving unintentionally.

Could use stronger lower back support.. Out of the past four office chairs I've used, this is definitely the best, but it still isn't perfect.
When I got the huge box at my front door, I was excited to get it assembled; my old chair had been losing the left arm, which had broken off some time ago but was kept in place by some duct tape. Assembling this chair was extremely easy, and it was set in my office in no more than ten minutes.

While this chair has more gizmos and levers than any previous chair I've owned (with the exception of a headrest, however), there is one huge flaw for me: the seat cushion doesn't recline as far backward as I'd like. The seat angles forward quite a bit, but it's almost flat when I recline it all the way backward. Also, the whole chair itself doesn't lower as much as I'd prefer, though it's got quite the height at its highest. I'm 5'8" if that matters.

The levers on the bottom right are very easy to reach. They put icons on them for ease of use, but I sometimes still find them confusing to interpret and have to maneuver them all to find the one for which I'm looking. For instance, to adjust the seat forward, there's a lever that has an image of a person sitting on the chair, with the chair highlighted in white. There are green lines to show what the lever does (green lines in front and in back of the chair, indicating it moves the back forward and backward), but there's green crossing into other areas of the chair which the lever does not control. It would've been best to just leave green and omit the rest, this way I would know that the lever controls that specific function.

The four levers, (three on the right and one on the left) control height, angle of the seat, seat glide, and the angle of the back.

Now, the back of the chair provides great support, though I wish it could lower just ever so slightly. Still, it's great, but I have noticed that over time it has loosened, so who knows how much longer it'll last at a tight angle.

All in all, this chair could be better. The fact that it doesn't angle more forward or provide a little lower adjustment make it slightly less comfortable for shorter people. At least it is for me. Otherwise, it's the better of the four office chairs I've owned and used.

Marble for sure, but porous.. This marble feels unpolished and porous. There's even a hairline crack in one of the stands I received, though no broken parts. Even one of the rubber pads on the bottom was peeling off, but it's been stuck on ever since I placed it back.

They are heavy and support my books just fine.

Not so easy to install, but so far is holding up.. We have plaster walls in our building, but I figured it wasn't too far removed from the drywall you're supposed to use this shelf with. Unfortunately, the first time I tried to hang it the hooks would not go through the wall, so I had to use a hammer. It wound up tearing against the wall by the time I was ready to hang up the shelf.

But that was a month ago, and so far the shelf is holding up (literally). I have one picture frame on it and an Amazon Dot, but nothing else.

Sleek and handsome, but heat dissiptation is a bit weak.. Maybe I'm just used to the space heaters that blow out heat to the point that it burns my skin if I'm too close, but this heater is a bit weak for my experience. It's not bad; we tried it in a medium-sized living room and it struggled to warm the room unless it was on the highest setting. Unsure whether that's intended, but it was unexpected.

Out of the box, it just needs either the wheels or the wall mount installed. We opted for the wheels since we'll be using this in different rooms. There's a small screen on the front with all the buttons you need: strength, child lock, temperature, and timer. The screen turns off after 3 minutes of non-activity; I prefer there be a feature that keeps it on since I like looking at the temperature. As for temperature, it goes by 5-temperature increments; for example, there's 70 and 75, but no way to make it 71-74. There are also a timer and child-lock features, so no worrying about leaving this on accidentally. There's a main power switch to the side that needs to be flipped before the heater can be used. The heater also comes with a remote that has all the same buttons.

It's definitely a nice-looking heater that's light, thin, and portable, but I wish the heat strength were stronger.

Our Dyson is a bit old, and right now these two have the same sucking power. That's not a good thing; this Bissell has a hard time sucking finer particles, like fur and litter. Our cat is shedding at the moment, and we still see fur after vacuuming. Our cat also likes to kick litter out of his box, and this vacuum can't suck all of it. It mostly spreads the litter around, so I end up using a dust bin.

But for general use it works great. It has the hard-floor and carpet settings, which seem to work effectively for its size.

Prints are a bit fuzzy.. Decent prints that hang well. We use Command strips to hang these and they stay on fine. There doesn't seem to be any warping or other uneven framing.

The prints themselves aren't sharp, however. I can notice pixelation on the edges of text.

Good but no way to turn off alarm.. Very accurate and a great replacement. We can't do without thermometers.

Because the thermometer didn't arrive with instructions, I had to figure out on my own how to shut it off: setting the minimum temp at a very high level. Robust, useful, but lacks one major feature I'd like.. While I've had ADHD all my life and had pretty noticeable symptoms, I was diagnosed with it only last year. Following that came lots of professional, life-changing help and advice. One of those was using a TIME TIMER to manage my time; it's been a daily routine since then. I use it at work and at home. I saw this offering for a watch version and thought, "Now I can take it with me on the go!"

There are three mods of the watch: regular watch, TIMER mode, and stopwatch. Of course, the TIME TIMER mode is the one I planned to use most. I like that there's a 60-minute option and one for longer sessions. You can save presets for each timer, but--and this is the big omission I'd like--you can save only one. Sure, the normal TIME TIMERS can't save presets, but the watch is different. I use the pomodoro technique where I assign 25-30 minutes for a task, then take a 5-minute break (this review is being written during one of those breaks), then reset. I use the 60-minute timer to save the 25-minute setting, but there's no option to save an additional preset. On my watch, you can save only one for both the 60-minute mode and the longer timer, not each. It's not a huge pain to set a 5-minute timer, but, considering how easy the normal TIMER is to use as well as the watch being able to save at least one preset, I'm not sure why there isn't an option to save more than one preset. It's so expensive for such a simple watch, too. It feels sturdy and that it can take a beating, but $85 MSRP? That's a bit much.

The clock is cool because it uses the timer display for the analog clock. I like that it vibrates too, so I can use it during quiet study sessions.

A Tale of Three Pillows…. Works Well as Simple Dehydrator; Slower, Less Versatile Than More Expensive Competing Product. [[VIDEOID:moTYGPGLRDB4O4]]This bargain-priced (about $24) OSTER FPSTDH0101 ELECTRIC FOOD DEHYDRATOR works well as a dehydrator, but the more expensive (about $60) [[ASIN:B0090WOCN0 Nesco FD-75A 700-Watt Food Dehydrator]] works faster, is easier to clean, has adjustable temperature settings, and accommodates more trays. See the accompanying video slide show for my side-by-side comparison of these two dehydrators. (I purchased the Nesco Pro model from Amazon, and received the Oster model through Amazon Vine.)

SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCES: The Oster and Nesco models have two very significant differences. First, the Oster electrical drying unit is bottom-mounted, while the Nesco electrical drying unit is top-mounted. The bottom-mounted drying unit is a real disadvantage, because fruit, vegetable, and meat juices invariably drip into the base from the drying trays above. Since the electrical base cannot be immersed in water, the base must always be cleaned carefully by hand. This isn't difficult, but it's much harder to remove juices from the base than from the trays. In contrast, the top-mounted Nesco drying unit stays clean throughout the drying process. At most, it requires a quick wipe with a moist cloth or paper towel. The bottom tray of the Nesco model is even easier to clean than the trays.

Second, the Oster drying unit is equipped with an on/off switch, while the Nesco drying unit is equipped with an adjustable temperature-setting dial. In this respect, the Nesco model is far superior to the Oster model, because the Oster model with the simple on/of switch has only one drying temperature. With the Nesco model, you can start your food drying at a higher temperature, and dial it down after a few hours to the "normal" 135-140 degrees, to speed up the drying times. You can also adjust the temperature from 95 degrees to 160 degrees, to accommodate foods needing lower (e.g., herbs) or higher (e.g., jerky) temperatures to dry optimally. A disadvantage of the Nesco model is that it lacks an on/off switch, and can only be stopped by unplugging the whole unit.

SIZE AND CAPACITY: The Oster and Nesco dehydrators are almost exactly the same size, and take up the same amount of countertop space. However, the Oster has only four (4) trays, and doesn't appear to be expandable. (The instruction booklet makes no mention of the availability of expansion trays.) My photos show the Nesco model with 4 trays, but the basic Nesco Pro model has five (5) trays, and is expandable to 12-14 trays.

With only 4 trays, the Oster dehydrator's capacity is limited to the equivalent of what you see in the photos: 1/2 cup blueberries, 1/2 apple, 1 pear, 2 extra-large bell peppers (1/2 pepper in green, red, orange, yellow). With the Nesco model, you can dry more food at one time, by using more trays (and maybe use a bit less electricity). With 9 trays, the Nesco model will dry 9 extra-large peaches.

TRAYS: The Oster and Nesco trays are also nearly identical in size. The Oster trays are made of a flexible plastic-netting material, the Nesco trays are made of a hard plastic more like Bakelite. The Oster trays are dishwasher-safe; the Nesco trays can be washed in the dishwasher if you remove them before the start of the drying cycle.

However, the trays for both the Oster and Nesco models are quite easy to clean without even using a dishwasher. Just soak the trays for a couple of minutes in hot, soapy water; then use a soft dish brush to remove any sticky bits. Because of the differing "hole patterns", the Oster trays pick up a few more bits than the Nesco trays, but the difference is negligible. All the trays fit in a large kitchen sink.

FOOD PREPARATION: Fruits and vegetables should be cored and seeded, and cut into 1/4-inch slices. Food with edible skins (apples, pears) can be peeled or not. Fruits that turn brown if left exposed to the air can be tossed with orange juice, pineapple juice, or a product like Fruit Fresh to prevent this during drying. (I used Fruit Fresh in my test.) The easiest way to slice the food for drying is to put it through a food processor, using the widest possible slicing blade. This goes very quickly, and gives you uniform slices that will dry uniformly. The food processor cleanup is easy.

DRYING TIME: In my test, I halved a cup of blueberries (blanched first in boiling water), an apple, two pears, and four different-colored bell peppers; then I arranged them in similar tray patterns and stacked the trays in the same order. After 4-1/2 hours at 138 degrees, the Nesco model had dried everything except the blueberries to flexible-leather consistency; after 6 hours, the Oster model (at an unknown temperature) had accomplished the same thing.

The instruction booklet for the Oster model suggested 12-18 hours for the fruits and 14-18 hours for bell peppers; the instruction booklet for the Nesco model suggested 4-10 hours for apples, 6-16 hours for pears, and 5-12 hours for bell peppers. Obviously, both the Oster and Nesco units dried the food in less time. In my experience, foods usually dry in less time, so I always check back after 3 hours.

With both the Oster and Nesco models, you will need to remove some food or rearrange it on the trays, or rearrange the food trays themselves, before the full drying time is up. Even the most uniformly-sliced food will dry at slightly different rates because of air circulation patterns inside the stacks of trays.

After 9 hours, both the Oster and Nesco models were still working on the blueberries. Perhaps I didn't blanch the berries properly to break the skins. Some of the berries had dried and achieved raisin-like status, but most had a lot of liquid left inside. I decided it wasn't worth the cost of electricity to continue drying the blueberries, and abandoned the test there. If anything, the Oster was ahead of the Nesco after 9 hours.

CONCLUSION: If you're serious about drying food--making trail mix, preserving summer's bounty, drying herbs, making jerky, or stocking an emergency pantry--you will want a full-featured dehydrator like the Nesco Pro model. The Nesco Pro comes with 5 trays, and with clean-a-screen and fruit roll sheets (2 of each). These sheets are used, respectively, for drying herbs (to prevent the dried bits from falling through the holes in the trays) and for drying fruit purees. Nesco also sells a "jerky gun" as an extra food dehydrator accessory for making uniform strips of jerky from ground meat. (The jerky gun can be used with any food dehydrator.)

If you're not so sure about your commitment to drying food, then you may want to start with this 4-tray Oster model; or with Nesco's bargain-priced (about $31) 4-tray [[ASIN:B003I4F7AS Nesco American Harvest FD-37 400 Watt Food Dehydrator]], which has a top-mounted drying fan, is expandable to 7 trays, and can use the Nesco clean-a-screen and fruit roll sheets. Because of the single temperature setting and the bottom-mounted drying unit, I rate this OSTER 4-TRAY ELECTRICAL FOOD DEHYDRATOR at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).

Great Receptacle, Not-So-Great Egg Separator. Because I regularly make meringue pies and home-made ice cream, I separate a lot of eggs. What I love about this WILTON BETTER BAKING EGG SEPARATOR is the 10-egg-white receptacle that stands firmly on your kitchen countertop--and the snug fit of the egg separator atop the receptacle. What I don't love about it is the design of the egg separator itself.

The egg separator design is fairly standard. There is a central round section for the yolk, with cutouts on both sides that allow the white to slip through. But the central yolk section is not very deep, and is not large enough to allow the yolk to move around. This means that if the white doesn't immediately drop through completely--and you have to gently rotate the yolk to finish the egg-separation process--you are at risk of breaking the yolk and contaminating the whites already in the receptacle. This is especially true if you are working with older eggs that have been in your refrigerator for a while.

Because of the less-than-optimal design, I rate this Wilton Egg Separator at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale). A couple of egg separators that I like better are the plain, bargain-priced [[ASIN:B0079G2EQ6 Mini Egg Yolk Separator]], and the excellent [[ASIN:B00A2KD8NY OXO Good Grips 3-in-1 Egg Separator]] that hooks onto bowls of all sizes.

Inexpensive Alternative to Custom Table Pad Protects Against Spills. This BENSON MILLS DELUXE VINYL TABLE PAD can easily be cut with scissors to fit any table that is smaller than the 52" x 90" dimensions given on the package. Placed between a finished wooden tabletop and a tablecloth, it provides an extra layer of protection from spills--particularly those horrible rings caused by water and wine glasses.

This table pad is made of thin white vinyl that is backed by a thin layer of flannel. It's no beauty--you will always want to cover it with a tablecloth. It should reasonably protect a tabletop from hot dishes, because it doesn't catch fire immediately when a lighted match is placed directly on the vinyl surface. However, the lighted match, if left there, does melt the vinyl and burn a hole, so the table pad won't protect against cigarette burns.

The flannel backing is a good idea, because it prevents the vinyl from getting permanently stuck to the finished (varnished) tabletop. However, the flannel backing also causes the protective pad to slide around on the tabletop. A tablecloth will help hold the pad in place, but a thin table pad like this one lacks the weight it needs to stay firmly in position.

This 52" x 90" table pad (about $20 on Amazon) is an inexpensive alternative to a custom table pad, and offers good protection against ordinary spills. However, because I wouldn't want to rely on it to protect a tabletop that I really cared a lot about, I rate it at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).

Well-Made, Works Well, But Not Best Available Corn Stripper Tool. If it weren't so fiddly to use, I would really love this RSVP SHUCK DELUXE CORN STRIPPER. The product's clear plastic outer tube is both its best and its worst feature. The best, because the tube catches all of the stripped corn kernels, and is easy to empty. The worst, because the tube must be opened and closed for every single ear of corn; each ear of corn must be carefully positioned inside the tube; and the yellow cap at the bottom of the tube has screw threads that run in the "wrong" direction. (To unscrew something, the mantra is "righty tightey, lefty loosey"--but this tube opens when turned right, and closes when turned left. Probably it's designed this way so it won't unscrew when the corer is twisted.)

The stainless steel "corer" is sharp, and it cuts the kernels off the cob with very little downward pushing effort. However, it misses all the kernels at the narrow end of the ear. The gadget is a little confusing at first, but simple to use once you understand how it works. You cut the kernels off by twisting the scalloped yellow part that's attached to the stainless steel corer; then you use the knobbed yellow part to push the stripped cob out of the corer. It's easiest if you take the knobbed part out before you strip the corn kernels off the cob. All of the corn stripper parts are sturdy, and they are all dishwasher safe.

This RSVP Corn Stripper is slightly more efficient than my [[ASIN:B000V78JGO OXO Good Grips Corn Stripper]], which has to be emptied several times for each ear of corn, and is a bit awkward to take apart and reassemble each time. However, my favorite tool for this job is the [[ASIN:B006GDRD9G Zyliss Corn Stripper]], which strips an entire ear of corn completely with 4 or 5 quick downward strokes (when you hold an ear of corn over a bowl or plate, you don't need either a tube (RSVP) or a container (OXO) to catch the stripped kernels).

Because it's fiddly and not the best available tool for the job, I rate this well-made product at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).

Excellent All-Purpose Kitchen Timer With Independent Memory Function. EDITED August 11, 2012:
After about 4 months of use, the part of the display that shows the second number for the minutes went partially blank. ORIGINAL REVIEW:
