A slider on the side makes it simple to switch between the three main functions: (1) an accurate 24-hour digital clock, (2) a count-up timer (stopwatch), and (3) a count-down timer (food timer). The display shows time in hours, minutes, and seconds-- the maximum time is 23 hours, 59 minutes, 59 seconds. The timer is powered by a single flat, round LR44 battery (included).

The timer's best feature is the independent memory function that will recall your most frequently used time setting. I keep the memory set at 20 minutes--the time it takes to freeze homemade ice cream--but the memory can be easily erased and reset to something different whenever you like. You do NOT have to set the timer and allow it to run to completion to invoke the memory function (a requirement with many other kitchen timers). Instead, the memory is set independently, by using the regular Hr.-Min.-Sec. buttons and then hitting the Memory button. The timer has a built-in stand, plus a fairly strong magnet that you can use to attach the device to any convenient metal surface.

I rate this timer at 5 stars ("I love it" on the official Amazon scale). The only negative thing I have to say about it, is that it is quite small. At 2" high by 2-5/8" wide, it is slightly smaller than a credit card. Because my household has two cooks, I use this timer alongside another excellent timer, the [[ASIN:B004PYA3B8 Robic Three Memory Timer]], which is limited to 99 minutes but which remembers three frequently used time settings.

Excellent Knives Are Included With Costly Magnetic Stand. The Renaissance-series knives in this expensive MERCER CULINARY M21940 RENAISSANCE BOARD MAGNETIC KNIFE SET (6-Piece, 11 3/8" x 9", Stainless Steel) are of superior quality. However, you’re paying a LOT for the weighty (more than 8 lbs.!) acacia-wood magnetic stand in this knife set (about $222 on Amazon for knives and stand). If it's good knives you want, consider this similar [[ASIN:B00MRU46DS Renaissance Wood and Glass Block Set]] (about $155 on Amazon). The difference in the sets are (1) the knife stands, and (2) a filet knife in the expensive set instead of the utility knife in the cheaper set.

Is the magnetic stand worth the extra cost? I don’t think so. The stand is a counter-space hog that is wider than a knife block. It also requires space above the acacia wood rectangle for removing the knives, because they don’t pull off all that easily when pulled straight forward. (Note that the cheaper set also requires vertical space for knife removal.)

A magnetic stand may be a good storage solution for these Renaissance-series knives, because they should be hand-washed and dried. The manufacturer’s website states: “Cutlery should never be washed in a dishwasher: the intense heat and radical temperature changes may cause the handle to deteriorate; the blade edges will become dull through rubbing against each other; and caustic soap will cause staining and pitting of the blade.”

However, the set does NOT include a sharpening steel (which the magnetic stand probably doesn't support). The set is shipped as (1) an 8-lb. magnetic stand in a box (some assembly required), and (2) five separate knives in retail hanging-display clamshell packaging.

The Renaissance-series knives are Mercer’s most expensive knives for non-professional cooks. They’re comparable to Wusthof Classic knives.

Pretty Dinner Plate, But With Flaws on Back. In my home, this pretty MARCHESA SHADES OF BLUE DINNER PLATE (by Lenox) will see duty as a cookie/cake plate. The scalloped edges, accented with gold, make it perfect for presenting desserts and treats. The product page photo is very accurate as to the color, which is baby blue with a hint of teal. The plate is ironstone, so it weighs more than porcelain, but it's thin, and not particularly heavy (unlike some stoneware).

However, I was surprised to find three very conspicuous flaws in the glaze on the back of the dinner plate (left side, right side, bottom center), because this plate is not cheap (about $26 on Amazon). These surely are caused by contact with a rack during the firing of the glaze. I don't know whether it's normal to find such flaws in dinnerware in this price range, but I was disappointed.

Dinnerware Is 'Twixt and 'Tween Casual and Formal Table Settings. This MIKASA ITALIAN COUNTRYSIDE 4-PIECE PLACE SETTING is high in quality, but it's rather thick and heavy for porcelain. Of course, this is a "countryside" pattern, so Mikasa may have intended for it to resemble the humble stoneware more than the elegant porcelain.

(Note: In one place, the Amazon product page description says "crafted from stoneware"; in another place it says "made from quality porcelain". However, the retail box and the actual dinnerware pieces all say "porcelain". My everyday dishes are Heath stoneware seconds, and these feel different, so I'm guessing porcelain.)

The all-white pattern is a raised design formed from vertical bars beneath a narrow scrollwork band that goes all around the edge of each piece. The edges of the design are NOT crisp and cleanly stamped into the porcelain; and my personal preference in this style of dinnerware pattern is for crisp lines. Again, Mikasa may have intended this effect to suggest a rougher, "countryside" appearance.

Nevertheless, this dinnerware is kind of 'twixt and 'tween casual (everyday) and formal (guest) dinnerware. The all-white, raised design is basically elegant; the heavy porcelain emulating stoneware is basically casual. It doesn't really feel right in either setting--the formal design is just "too much" for use in everyday dinnerware; the weight and lack of crisp patterning make it "inelegant" for formal dinnerware.

This line of Mikasa porcelain is microwave safe and dishwasher safe, which is nice. The bowl is large and deep, good for soup or cereal; the cup has a pleasing upright mug shape that doesn't require a saucer; the dinner plate and salad/dessert plate are generously sized. However, because this Mikasa "Italian Countryside" has a split personality, and doesn't seem quite right either for casual or formal table settings, I rate it at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).

2" Openings Lack Gripper Coating; Poor Choice for Tightly Packed Closet. This INTERDESIGN REMY SCARF HANGER CLOSET ORGANIZER (No Snag) will hold scarves, and any other long and narrow clothing items that can be threaded through the holes. It's definitely a "no snag" organizer, because the openings are surrounded by smooth plastic. The openings are NOT coated with rubberized material (to lightly grip the items and prevent slipping off as the organizer is moved along the closet rod).

To mininize sliding off, the items should be added carefully with the midpoints at the organizer holes (so that the weight of each item is balanced on both sides). When the organizer is fully loaded, the items overlap, so it's easy to pull off more than one item at a time.

The openings are 2" across--wider items will need to be folded lengthwise. This type of organizer doesn't work well in a tightly packed closet, because the items hung on it will take up space on both sides. Also, you need some extra space to add and remove items.

Because of the lack of gripper material, I rate this scarf hanger at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).

Useful Markings--But Uneven Stamping Spoils Cutting Board's Looks. Because I have a small kitchen with limited countertop work space, and cook for only two people, I prefer small cutting boards like this FRED CHEESE DEGREES BAMBOO CUTTING BOARD. The markings on it are actually quite helpful for when I want to cut things (not just cheese) into uniform wedges, cubes, or chunks.

However, I doubt that the markings will remain visible for long. The markings are cut or burned quite shallowly into the bamboo board, as if incised by a hot metal stamping device (akin to a child's woodburner). Also, the markings on my board are not as consistently precise as those on the board in the product page photo.

I will try to preserve the markings for as long as possible by always using the plain, unmarked side of the cutting board when I don't need the markings. This cutting board is NOT dishwasher safe--it's hand washable only, not to be left submerged in water, and should be oiled regularly to prevent drying out.

My small (6" x 8"), plain, dishwasher-safe Epicurean cutting board (about $11 on Amazon), will definitely remain my favorite, but this larger (7" x 8"), fancier, pricier (about $25 on Amazon) cutting board is useful, too. If the markings were stamped precisely, I would love it, and would recommend it as a gift for almost any cook. Unfortunately, the markings are NOT precise, so it's not very good looking. I rate it at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).

Oversized, Thick-and-Thin Bath Towel With Interesting Grid Pattern. This OTTOMANSON PURE COTTON COLLECTION LUXURY BATH TOWEL (27" L x 55" W; Lavender) is a pleasing shade of lavender; is a very big, oversized bath towel; and has an interesting grid pattern formed by raised terry cloth loops on a plain woven cotton base fabric.

However, it is a very thin towel, made of “Turkish cotton dobby terry cloth”, that doesn’t have a luxury feel at all. It seems very expensive (about $18 on Amazon) for what it is. I much prefer thick bath towels with terry loops all over—towels that resemble the pile on a thick carpet (see, e.g., [[ASIN:B00GQP0Z9E Utopia Bath Towel Set]]).

Beautiful Cookware That Requires Special Care to Keep Its Looks. This ALL-CLAD MC2 PROFESSIONAL MASTER CHEF 7-PIECE COOKWARE SET is drop-dead gorgeous. It is meticulously designed, machined, and hand-finished. However, it's a poor choice for me, because (1) my kitchen has a ceramic-top electric range, (2) it's heavier than my all-stainless-steel cookware, and (3) it requires hand-washing and a lot of extra care to keep it looking beautiful.

In general, aluminum cookware is the most energy-efficient, which is why "stainless steel" cookware usually has an aluminum core. Aluminum cookware is also lightweight. However, cookware made entirely from aluminum poses some toxic risk in regular use, because minute amounts of aluminum can leach into food during cooking (particularly into acidic foods like tomatoes).

This All-Clad cookware has a stainless steel interior that won't react with food. Thus it's completely safe for all cooking. It cooks efficiently, because it has an all-aluminum core plus an all-aluminum brushed exterior. However, it isn't particularly lightweight. The 9-inch All-Clad frying pan from this set weighs 1 lb. 9.9 oz., while my 9-inch Cuisinart stainless steel frying pan with aluminum-core bottom weighs 1 lb. 6.6 oz.

My ceramic-top electric range is not friendly to aluminum cookware, because aluminum has a fairly low melting point. The manual for the electric range suggests using extra caution when cooking with aluminum cookware, because aluminum can leave scuff marks on the cooktop, and because a pan allowed to boil dry can melt, fuse with the cooktop, and severely damage the cooktop. Of course it's fine to use this All-Clad cookware on a ceramic-top stove, but the cook needs to exercise particular care (1) to never turn the heat on under an empty pan, and (2) to follow the All-Clad recommendation and always use low or medium heat, except when boiling water. (The recommendation to use low or medium heat is NOT just for ceramic-top ranges, because high heat can warp any cookware.)

However, the main reason that I'm disappointed with this All-Clad cookware is that it requires so much extra care to maintain its stunning appearance. The All-Clad instructions include the following cautions: (1) to avoid the formation of white dots or pits in the cookware, bring water to a boil or wait for foods to begin cooking before adding salt; (2) to prevent water spotting, rinse in hot water and dry immediately; and (3) to prevent discoloration, avoid overheating (produces brown or blue spots), remove food films before reheating, and avoid high-iron-content water. In addition, for ordinary cleaning, the stainless steel interior should be cleaned with a paste of fine powder cleanser, washed in hot soapy water, and dried immediately. (You musn't use oven cleaners, oven cleansers, or chlorine bleach.) The aluminum MC2 exterior should be cleaned with commercial aluminum cleaner, and rinsed in lukewarm water.

In short, this cookware is "not recommended for dishwasher use". Because this All-Clad cookware is beautiful, but requires pampering to stay that way, I rate it at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).

Cute Mini Trash Can; Limited Usefulness. This MIND READER DESKTOP MINI TRASH CAN (Silver) is a cute little swing-lid trash can, made of lightweight stainless steel. The price (currently $11.99 on Amazon) seems a little high, because there are ripples on the edges of the lid (as seen in the product page photos if you zoom in).

As a trash receptacle, this will hold only seven (7) used K-cups. If filled full of K-cups, it is hard to empty. It strikes me as useful for collecting makeup waste like used cotton balls, but I use a small powder-room wastebasket for this kind of thing. I am a loss for how to use this on my office desk, because I have a medium-sized trash can underneath the desk. Maybe kids would have fun with it in their room?

If you need a mini trash can, you could do worse. However, I don’t think this item is very practical or useful.

Budget-Priced “Full/Queen” Comforter Doesn't Really Fit Queen Bed. This SWEET HOME COLLECTION MICROFIBER DOWN ALTERNATIVE COMFORTER SET WITH PILLOW SHAMS (Full/Queen, Reversible Burgundy/Black) is a nice budget-priced (about $33 on Amazon) everyday comforter. It's a 100% microfiber “down alternative” comforter. That means no feathers, so it's good for those with asthma or allergies. The microfiber fabric looks and feels like ordinary cotton.

The comforter just covers the top of my Queen bed lengthwise; on each side there is a 6-inch overhang. The comforter comes nowhere near reaching to the floor at the foot and sides, as shown in the product page photo. I haven't washed my comforter yet, so I don't know whether it will shrink, or whether the microfiber fill will shift, when the comforter is machine washed for the first time.

The pillow shams are Queen-sized pillowslips made from the same fabric as the comforter. One side of the pillowslip is dark red (burgundy), one side is black. The stitching is kind of coarse, with some hanging threads. The colors in the product page photo are accurate.

This "Full/Queen" comforter is sized to go underneath a Queen bedspread (for warmth), not to serve as a decorative bed topper.

Not-So-Powerful Pedestal Fan Works Well in Smaller Rooms. This HONEYWELL ADVANCED QUIETSET WHOLE ROOM PEDESTAL FAN (with Noise Reduction Technology, 16”) has a standard-size, fairly large fan (16”). It isn’t all that powerful, so it’s right for a small bedroom or office where you want to circulate air without blowing your papers around or creating a strong draft.

The remote control is a nice feature to have with a pedestal fan, which is usually located across the room from wherever you are. If you plug the fan into a WEMO switch (or other brand of smart switch), you can also use Amazon Alexa to turn the fan on and off.

With a pedestal fan, you don’t need to use precious desk, countertop, or tabletop space to hold the fan--it has its own stand. You can place it anywhere in the room, as long as the cord (or the cord with an extension cord) can reach an electrical outlet. Also, a pedestal fan moves the air in the top half of the room, where it does the most good.

However, in recent years I’ve become a fan of the Vornado whole room air circulators (see, e.g., [[ASIN:B00TX79BK6 Vornado Vintage Jr. air circulator]]). You can put one of those in the corner of a room, aim it toward the opposite ceiling corner, and the air will be turned over throughout the room.

Set of Beautiful Designer Kitchen Tools. This KITCHENAID 7-PIECE KITCHEN TOOL SET (KT455MLER; Red) has all the basic tools (slotted turner, basting spoon, slotted spoon, short turner, ladle, silicone tipped tongs, manual can opener), but does NOT include a rack to hang them on. My set arrived in frustration-free packaging (a plain brown corrugated cardboard box, NOT a retail box); and this is something to consider if you’re giving this set as a gift.

These beautiful designer tools are made of heavy-gauge stainless steel, and the red handles will perfectly match your red Kitchenaid stand mixer and/or your other red Kitchenaid appliances. They are functional tools (with hanging loops), but they seem more at home hanging decoratively on the walls of your Kitchenaid kitchen, than being held in your hands as you cook everyday meals.

As working tools, I prefer the ones with nonstick nylon or silicone turners, spoons, etc. Among these types of tools, my favorite brands are Sabatier (e.g., [[ASIN:B01FM0JEHW Sabatier slotted turner]]), and OXO (e.g., [[ASIN:B003L0OOVW OXO nylon ladle]]).

Wonder Woman Design Placemat Isn’t So Easy to Clean. This BUMKINS DC COMICS SILICON COLORING PLACEMAT (WONDER WOMAN), which is recommended for ages 3 and up, seems rather adult for a 3-year-old. However, it surely doesn’t hurt to introduce little girls early to female superheroes, because there aren’t a whole lot of them.

The box says that the 100% silicone placemat is easy to clean with soap and water, but that’s a bit misleading. The full care instructions read as follows: “Wash before first use. Wash after coloring, before placing food on mat. Some food items may cause staining. For best results, clean immediately after use. Wash with warm soapy water or in the dishwasher. Dishwasher safe on top rack only (up to 350 degrees F.). Do not use abrasive products for cleaning. Keep away from sharpobjects. Store in a cool dry place.”

Heavy Weighted Blanket Doesn’t Work as Throw. This TRU LITE BEDDING TRU BLANKET (Weighted; Happiness Embroidery; 60"x 80"; 15 lbs, Gray) is pretty, but it does NOT work as a throw. It’s far too heavy to wrangle around for snuggling up inside it. Fifteen pounds may not sound like much, but it’s a lot to deal with in a blanket that’s large enough to cover a regular double bed.

In my opinion, the weighting is a gimmick. It is true that when you’re underneath this blanket, you feel very warm and protected. However, you can get the same effect from several layers of bedding (combining blankets, comforter, heavy bedspread, etc.).

I can’t imagine this being acceptable to a couple sharing a bed, unless one person is an incorrigible “bedclothes hog”. The weight is the problem--it restricts bed mobility. For that reason, this blanket is a terrible choice for an elderly or disabled person. It makes it very difficult to turn over and change positions at night.

The blanket is quite well made, with the word “Happiness” embroidered on the underside of the silky “slipcover” for the weighted, quilted interior blanket portion. The appearance of the slipcover is a bit misleading--the textured polka dots are part of the weave of the fabric, and do NOT have anything to do with the weighting. (For some reason, I thought that the dots indicated little round weights.)

If you’re young, healthy, and strong, and dislike extra layers of bedclothes, then you’ll probably love this blanket for its “swaddling” effect. If you’re elderly or disabled, you probably won’t be able to use this blanket at all.

Fragile Beauty Conducts Heat Well. This COPCO FLIGHT ENAMEL ON STEEL TEA KETTLE (5197724; 2.4-Quart, White) is beautiful, with a graceful modern design. It’s enameled both inside (black) and outside (white). It conducts heat well—on my ceramic-top stove, it took only a few minutes to heat half a kettle of water. It has an urgent, piercing (but NOT annoying) steam whistle that tells you the water is boiling.

Unfortunately, it is fragile. Mine was dropped, and the black handle snapped off cleanly where it joined the silver top of the kettle. The kettle is now useless. (I could glue the handle back on, but I don’t trust even superglue to hold the entire weight of a tea kettle filled with 2.4 quarts of boiling water.)

This model has one other negative feature—the maximum fill line is marked with a sticker on the front of the tea kettle, but not with anything you can easily see when you’re filling the kettle. Even if you set the kettle down (so that the water surface is level), It’s difficult to follow the instruction to “ensure water level is below Max Fill line or at least ¼” below the bottom of the inside spout opening”.

“Plain Vanilla” Electric Alarm Clock Has Battery Backup System. Old habits die hard, so I like to have an electric alarm clock--one with an easy-to-set alarm--on my bedside table. Ths AMAZONBASICS DIGITAL ALARM CLOCK (with Large 1.4-Inch Display) satisfies that need. However, it seems expensive (about $18 on Amazon) for what it is--a simple electric alarm clock with a single beeper alarm.

The alarm clock does have one nice “extra” feature. It has a battery backup system that keeps the clock going during a power outage so that your alarm still wakes you up on time. The backup system requires a 9V battery (NOT included).

For a couple of dollars more (about $20 on Amazon), you can get an [[ASIN:B07DQYFCXM AmazonBasics Digital Clock Radio (FM only)]]. This alarm clock has two separate alarms, a battery backup system, an FM radio, and a USB charging port. The built-in radio speaker is pretty bad, but you can use the beeper alarm option instead. I think that the clock radio with two alarms is a better choice than this “plain vanilla” digital alarm clock.

High-Quality Travel Pillow Is Difficult to Bag. This HAOBAIMEI TRAVEL NECK PILLOW (Memory Foam, Grey) is a high-quality, well-made travel pillow that can be positioned in myriad ways to support your head/neck comfortably in all kinds of seating. However, it’s bulky--about the size of a small loaf of bread when bagged. The bagged pillow is also an awkward shape (and a little heavy) to carry everywhere you go.

The memory foam provides solid support. However, the pillow is much more difficult to bag than the product video suggests. Bagging requires hand strength and sitting down so you can force the folded pillow into the bag.

A bonus thin sleep mask is included, but it isn’t very effective in blocking out light. It’s just a flat piece of padded black satin fabric.

Heavy, Edged-in-Gold Rose Is Oddly Weighted. This ICREER 24K DIPPED GOLD ROSE WITH STAND (Pink) is advertised as a giftable “dipped” rose. What it is, is a home decor piece. A fresh long-stemmed rose is encased in plastic and then edged with gold. But the stem is so straight, it looks and feels like a gold-colored metal rod. The overall impression is that the rose is manufactured.

I don’t care for this “forever” rose at all. Although you can see the veins of the original rose petals through the plastic, the piece is very artificial-looking, and it’s very heavy. Something about the weighting, with the heavy bud atop the rod-like stem, makes me want to swing it and hit something with it. (No kidding. This happens every time that I pick it up.) As a gift, I would far rather receive a single fresh rose than one of these “dipped gold” roses.

The rose comes in a nice, plastic-foam-lined, presentation box. A fancy gift tag is also included.

Before you buy, you should consider where you might want to display this rose. It’s a decorative piece that is an awkward height, and that is easily knocked over. (The plastic stand adds even more height.) Also, you should shop around for the best Amazon price. “Gold-plated” roses with closed buds like this one seem to cost a little more than the ones with open flowers assembled from plastic-coated, gold-edged petals.

Manufactured Home Decor Piece Made From Real Rose Petals. This CAVEBEAR 01 24K GOLD LONG STEM ROSE (Real, Fresh, Dipped, Plated; Red) is advertised misleadingly as a “real fresh” rose, or as a “gold-plated” rose. What it is, is a manufactured home decor piece. Fresh roses are taken apart, their petals (and stems, I think) are coated in plastic and edged in gold, and then the encased plastic pieces are reassembled into a product that more or less looks like a rose.

I don’t care for this “forever” rose at all. Although you can see the veins of the original rose petals through the plastic, the piece is very heavy, and looks more artificial than a plastic rose. As a gift, I would far rather receive a single fresh rose than one of these “dipped, fresh, gold-plated” roses.

Before you buy, you should consider where you might want to display this rose. It’s a decorative piece that is an awkward height, and that is easily knocked over. (The plastic stand adds even more height.) Also, you should shop around for the best Amazon price. Gold-plated roses with opened flowers like this one seem to cost a little less than the ones with tightly closed buds.

Expensive Specialized Crevice Tool. This BLACK & DECKER HHVJ320BMF26 SMARTECH CORDLESS 2.0Ah LITHIUM HAND VACUUM is a terrific crevice tool, but the price (about $122 on Amazon) blows me away. There are features that I love--the lighted display that shows how much charge is left; the built-in crevice tool extension--but the usefulness of this "hand vacuum" is severely limited by the 2-inch-wide nozzle. The battery holds enough charge to vacuum a flight of carpeted stairs on the high-speed "power boost" setting (impressive!), but it takes a zillion passes to do stairs in 2-inch-wide strips.

The suction is okay on the low-speed setting, and very good on the high-speed setting. It takes 5 hours for a full charge, so you'll probably want to store it in the plugged-in charger (wall-mounting hardware is included) to keep it topped off, as the manual recommends. The charger light turns off when charging is complete, but removing the device from the charger for even a few moments will cause the charger to restart for a few minutes.

The crevice tool extension makes this ideal for cleaning my stairway, which has a stair lift installed. (The support posts for the stair-lift track not only collect dust, but are hard to clean around.) However, the release button for the extension is stiff, so that it's often difficult to push the extension back into the nozzle for storage. The crevice tool extension is great for cleaning crevices in overstuffed furniture. The nozzle without the extension does a good job of dusting a smooth rubber floor mat.

The hand vacuum is fairly easy to clean. The big cyclonic element in the handle releases easily, and the whole thing pulls out sideways. Dust, dirt, and larger particles collect around the plastic filter module, and are easily dumped into a trash container. However, thick dust accumulates quickly on the cloth filter inside the plastic filter--and it clings, so the "dust bunnies" must be pulled off by hand. (This isn't good if you have allergies or asthma.) Filter reassembly is simple, and the filters are washable.

This is a vacuum for dry materials only. After washing, the filters need to be completely dry before you operate the vacuum. The cyclonic element is not particularly capacious, so I can't see this device as indispensable for ordinary kitchen cleanups like cereal, flour, or dry pet food spills. It is lightweight, and well-balanced for hand vacuuming.

As good as this device is for cleaning crevices in upholstered furniture and for cleaning carpeted steps, it is expensive for such a specialized tool. Also, it requires storage space and an electrical outlet to keep it charged and always available for ready use. For these reasons, I rate it at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).

Faint Lavender Scent, Pretty Lavender Color--Good for Home Decor, Not Aromatherapy. These DII Z02076 HIGHLY SCENTED TEALIGHT CANDLES (36 Tealights, 1.5x0.63, Lavender Blossom) smell like lavender when you open the package, but they produce only the faintest of lavender scents when they’re burning. It’s disappointing not to get the expected lavender fragrance (which I love).

However, the tealights do burn for a long, long time, and they’re colored a pretty pale lavender. Thus they’re nice for home or party decor, if not for aromatherapy.

A Throw That You Can't Curl Up In. This oversized SUNBEAM ARCTIC PLUSH HEATED THROW (Dusty Blue, TSA8TS-X590-13A00) is really just a small electric blanket with a thick plush cover. The large size means it will cover an adult napping on a couch. However, you can't really curl up in it, because (1) you can feel the wires, and (2) the instructions say NOT to use it bunched up.

The throw provides a lot of warmth, even on the "low" setting. The control is simple to use--you just press the center on/off button to cycle through the settings. The throw turns off automatically after three hours.

The placement of the control makes this throw awkward to use. The control is located partway between the plug at one end of the throw and the plug that goes into the wall socket. To keep the control within reach, you need to keep the entire throw fairly close to the wall socket. (This also keeps you from curling up in it.) The generous size of the throw (which should be a terrific feature) actually makes it hard to get everything lined up just right.

I don't care for the plush cover, which looks kind of cheap. The throw isn't something that I would particularly want to display on a couch or overstuffed chair, even though the dusty blue color is nice.

WARNING NOTE: You should NOT use this throw with a recliner chair, mechanical bed, or any other motorized furniture (because of the danger of catching the electrical cord in the moving parts).

Because this excellent small electric blanket doesn't work well as a throw, I rate it at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).

Nice Apron, But Upside-Down-Printed “Cheat Sheet” Has Limited Usefulness. This DII “MEASURE UP” CHEF’S PRINTED APRON (28” x 35”) would be a lot more fun if the upside-down-printed “Cheat Sheet” had a better selection of reference information. Why would you want to know the F. and C. equivalents for oven temperatures? Or the pinch, dash, and smidge amounts in teaspoons?

Also, the charts that are moderately useful aren’t presented well. For example, the equivalents for liquids are hard to read, because the larger amounts (e.g., 2 cups) are shown at the bottom of the cup graphic, rather than at the top (as if the graphic cup were filled with liquid). The vegetable cooking times chart is fairly useful, except that it doesn’t mention the quantity of vegetables being cooked.

Otherwise, the adult-sized apron is exactly what I needed for cooking with my new Instant Pot. (The IP tends to spatter oil during sauteing.) The bib covers my front completely, as long as I adjust the bib height by pulling on the black ties after putting the apron on over my head. The body of the apron, with the pockets, wraps around my sides and covers the rest of my clothing.

The apron includes a hanging loop. You need this because the ties and the loop that goes over your head are actually one long piece of black material that is threaded through casings on the sides of the apron. Once you get the head loop adjusted correctly for your size, you don’t want to hang the apron by the head loop.

The apron is washable, and I’m sure that the printed “Cheat Sheet” will wash out eventually. (My apron hasn’t been washed, so I don’t know how long the print will last.) However, the apron will still be functional long after the print is gone.

Oil-Filled Space Heater Has Desirable Safety Features, Odd Snap-On Feet. Space heaters of all kinds make me nervous, and this NEWAIR PORTABLE INDOOR SMALL ELECTRIC HEATER (NIH040WH00) (with Silent, Energy Efficient Operation, White) is no exception. It has desirable safety features--automatic shutoff function, tipover kill switch--but it has snap-on feet that leave me wondering about its stability.

If an oil-filled heater tips over or leaks, it can cause a fire. Oil-filled heaters stay warm for some time after they are turned off (which adds to their energy efficiency), but it also means they can set fire to combustible items (e.g., fabrics) that contact them even after they are turned off. Generally, combustible items should be kept at least 3 feet away from any oil-filled heater, even if the heater’s surface remains cool.

Given the safety issues surrounding oil-filled heaters, I’m NOT comfortable using this one (or any other model). I was interested in this model because of the slim panel design and small size, but it was a mistake for me to order it.

Noisy Air Purifier Requires Expensive Replacement Filters. In my bedroom, this MOLEKULE MINI AIR PURIFIER (with PECO Purification Technology, White) doesn’t seem to be as effective as my [[ASIN:B01LCX9QWG GermGuardian Air Purifier]] at clearing particulate matter from the air. The Molekule is supposed to destroy (not simply kill) germs, which is why I purchased it (from the manufacturer’s web site). However, there is no way to verify this germ-destroying claim.

My [[ASIN:B07JF53NRK Temtop indoor air quality monitor]] shows about the same readings for particulate matter, volatile organic compounds, and air quality, regardless of which air purifier (Molekule Mini or GermGuardian) that I use. The GermGuardian does come with a UV light for killing germs, and the light does seem to make a difference in how clean the air feels. (Again, there’s no way to verify the manufacturer’s germ-killing claim). The GG UV light requires replacement from time to time, but not as frequently as the manufacturer suggests.

The Molekule Mini is more expensive than the GermGuardian, and much noisier. I find that the Level 3 fan setting (out of 5) is the highest “always on” fan setting that is reasonable, and even this setting makes it hard for a nearby Amazon Echo device to hear the wake word.

The Molekule Mini requires expensive replacement filters every 6 months. The GermGuardian also requires replacement filters, but they’re less expensive, and the GG is pretty forgiving if you don’t replace the filters right away.

The Molekule Mini is kind of heavy, and has a surprisingly large footprint on my bedside table. Unlike the GermGuardian, the Mini lacks a display that shows the particulate matter count, and it doesn’t have an Auto setting that makes the fan speed up automatically if extra pollutants are present in the air. (There is a new, more expensive model of the Molekule Mini that does have some kind of particulate matter display.)

Overall, I was extremely disappointed with the Molekule Mini. After using it for 6 months, I decided to take it out of service. It doesn’t improve the air quality in my bedroom (over what I get with the GermGuardian); it’s too noisy; and the filters are too expensive.

Fits Under Kitchen Cabinets, But Releases Steam While Brewing. This HAMILTON BEACH 12 CUP COMPACT PROGRAMMABLE COFFEE MAKER (Black with Stainless Steel Accents (46200)) really is compact--it fits under my kitchen cabinets with room to spare. However, it’s a good idea to pull it out from under the kitchen cabinets when you’re actually brewing coffee, because steam escapes from the top--especially if the coffee maker is in need of cleaning.

It makes good coffee, so I’m happy enough with it. I don’t use the programming feature--which other reviewers say will fail after a few months because steam gets into the display--so the coffee maker suits my needs. I truly hated a fancy Ninja coffee maker that was too tall to fit under my kitchen cabinets, because it hogged so much counter space.

The best coffeemaker that I’ve ever owned is this [[ASIN:B0844DSDBH Hamilton Beach Frontfill Deluxe Coffee Maker]], which fits under my kitchen cabinets, does NOT release steam while coffee is brewing, and is extremely easy to fill. If you can find one of these, it’s the one you should buy.

Other reviewers have complained about the inability to get replacement carafes for the Hamilton Beach coffee makers. This is true of virtually any brand of coffee maker. If you need a replacement carafe, you should ONLY buy a carafe that says it fits the particular brand and model number. The carafe lids on different models of the same brand have slightly different dome heights or configurations, so that the carafes are NOT interchangeable from model to model.

I’m okay with the carafe thing, as long as the coffee maker isn’t very expensive to begin with. It makes sense to simply buy a new coffee maker if you break the carafe, because the inexpensive models only last 2-3 years anyway.

Sturdy “Y” Peeler; Blade Not Particularly Sharp. This FARBERWARE PROFESSIONAL VEGETABLE PEELER (“Y” Peeler, Black) works just like any other “Y” vegetable peeler. Because it is advertised as a “professional” kitchen tool, I expected the blade to be very sharp. However, the blade isn’t any sharper than the blade on my other less fancy “Y” peelers.

The peeler handle is big and heavy. No doubt the peeler is extra sturdy, but I don’t like the way that it feels in my hand. This was a big disappointment, because I’m generally a huge fan of Farberware products.

Budget-Priced, But Not Recommended for Reduced-Salt Bread. This OSTER BREAD MAKER WITH EXPRESSBAKE (1.5 or 2 Pound Capacity) is budget-priced (about $112 on Amazon). It makes a nice vertical loaf of bread, IF you weigh your bread flour and follow the included recipes exactly.

However, baking a loaf strictly according to the recipes is difficult, because the recipes do NOT include the flour weight. This is true even though the booklet advises you to weigh your bread flour! The recipes call for cups of flour, so you will need to do the weight math. Your bread flour packaging should tell you how many cups there are to a pound (for example, Gold Medal white and whole wheat bead flours have 3⅓ cups to a pound, which works out to 408 grams in the 3 cups required for Basic bread).

If you need to adjust your ingredients (for example, if you need to reduce the salt for a no-salt-added diet), your first loaves will collapse badly in the middle while baking. I had to make a dozen experimental loaves to find the specific combination of 1 tsp. salt, flour, and water that would produce the 30% whole wheat flour loaf shown in my photo.

When I followed the included recipe for basic raisin bread exactly (1½ tsp. salt), the loaf was beautiful–but it was inedible for someone who has been on a no-salt-added diet for some time. It tasted incredibly salty.

Bread machine recipes found by Googling say that salt can usually be reduced by one-half, with no adverse results. This was true with my old Regal bread machine, and is true with my more expensive [[ASIN:B0044WWC7E Panasonic SD-RD250 Bread Maker]] (about $260 on Amazon). With the Oster machine, reducing the salt requires a lot of experimentation.

I like the Panasonic machine a lot. It makes a horizontal loaf, and it is flexible regarding the amounts of salt and other ingredients that I want to play around with. However, a number of reviewers have stated that the Panasonic machine quits after a few months. I haven’t been using my Panasonic machine (purchased to replace this Oster machine) for long enough to know whether it will offer more than a few months of service.

There are differences in the way that the Oster and Panasonic machines make Basic bread. The included recipes for the two machines are quite similar, but the kneading and overall times are different. The Oster machine begins kneading as soon as you press “Start”, and takes a total of 3 hours for a Basic loaf. The Panasonic machine leaves the ingredients to “rest” for up to 2 hours before kneading begins, and takes a total of 4 hours for a Basic loaf. Both bake the loaves for about an hour.

Both machines have settings for French bread, dough, etc. (check the product page descriptions for the exact types of things that the machine is intended to make). Both machines also have “express bake” settings that will bake a loaf faster than the normal 3 or 4 hours.

Handy Little Egg Cooker Makes Good Poached Eggs. This CHEFMAN ELECTRIC EGG COOKER (Makes 6 Eggs; Midnight Blue) has a small countertop footprint, and cooks eggs quickly. It has an audible alarm that tells you when your eggs are done (omelet, poached, hard-, medium-, or soft-boiled).

The cooker poaches 1 or 2 eggs at a time. My first poached eggs came out too soft (undercooked whites), but I fixed this by adding more cooking water than the instructions called for in the second batch. The poached eggs are almost as good as the ones I make in hot water on the stovetop, and they’re a lot less trouble.

The cooker makes up to 6 hard-cooked eggs at a time. Mine came out as expected, but one egg cracked open during cooking. (I think that it had a hairline crack before I started.) This meant a bit of extra cleanup, but it wasn’t a disaster.

Probably I will continue to use my Instant Pot for cooking hard-boiled eggs, because the Chefman doesn’t cook Large eggs quite as thoroughly as I like. (I hard-cook older eggs in batches, and then store them for several days in the refrigerator.) The Chefman is easier and faster than the Instant Pot, if the hard-boiled eggs will be eaten right away.

For optimal results, it might be best to use Medium eggs. However, Large eggs cook adequately, especially if you add a little more water to increase the cooking time. (Just be sure NOT to overfill the base.)

The parts of the Chefman egg cooker are top-shelf dishwasher safe (except, of course, for the base).

Light Potting Soil, Suitable for Succulents. This ORGANIC POTTING SOIL (Fast Draining Cactus and Succulent Soil Mix; 4 Quarts) is advertised as a “professional growing mix”, and I’m not qualified to challenge that statement. I do know that cacti and succulents grow better in lightweight or sandy soil that is designed to drain quickly and provide the correct Ph balance. This potting soil seems perfectly fine for my succulents. (I'm not sure whether you need to add additional fertilizer, once your plants are rooted.)

However, the potting soil is very expensive (about $10 on Amazon for a 4-quart package). Think about the volume of 1-gallon milk jug. That is approximately the amount of soil you receive in 4 dry quarts. This amount will allow you to plant a lot of little succulents in 3” starter pots or cells. However, it will fill only a couple of 6” houseplant pots.

If you need cactus/succulent potting mix on a regular basis, you can save money by purchasing it in 8-quart or larger bags (e.g., [[ASIN:B08DHDLRYN Hoffman cactus and succulent potting soil]]). Also, local nurseries generally carry potting soil for many specialized uses (e.g., cacti, palms, African violets, orchids), and their prices are usually lower than those of online sellers.

Saves 1½” of Storage Space, But Is Hard to Open. This RAPID BRANDS MICROWAVE SPLATTER COVER (Vented; Dishwasher Safe; BPA-Free) measures 1¼” when collapsed, and 2¾” when fully opened. Thus it can save 1½” of storage space, but it is difficult to open and close. Unfolding it takes two hands, and a fair amount of force.

The splatter cover unfolds to the same height as[[ASIN:B00LQCB6I6 this non-collapsible splatter cover]] that I’ve been using. I much prefer the non-collapsible cover, which works exactly the same as the collapsible one.

The non-collapsible cover is easier to use, and easier to clean than this one. The non-collapsible cover is made of a single piece of flexible plastic, so that it lacks the food-collecting crevices of this cover.

Well-Made 10 Lb. Blanket Makes It Hard to Move at Night. This SERTA ZEN REST WEIGHTED ADULT BLANKET (twin-size, 48 in by 72 in, 10 lbs, Navy) is my second weighted blanket–and it proves that even a 10-lb. blanket is too heavy for me. It makes it too hard to turn and move naturally during the night.

I love the concept of weighted blankets, because I have a thick, furry, heavy throw that always makes me feel protected and “safe”. Its only drawback is its size (50 in by 60 in), which is short for optimal use on a bed at night. I will go back to using this as my weighted blanket.

The Serta blanket is well-made of polyester and glass beads. It is noiseless. The care label says “spot clean only”.

Holds Many Utensils, But Dominates Kitchen Countertop. This MONARCH ABODE HAND HAMMERED KITCHEN UTENSIL HOLDER CROCK (Large, Nickel) is very large indeed--about the size of a champagne bucket. The upside is that it holds a lot of kitchen utensils; the downside is that it dominates your kitchen countertop.

To my eye, the utensil holder is cheap looking. In the product page photo, the crock looks quite attractive because it appears to be smaller than it actually is. In reality, the decorative hand-hammered “dots” (each about the size of your little finger tip) don’t appear as decoration, but as big depressions that are arranged in uneven rows. The gray matte interior is unattractive.

I don’t think that this item is dishwasher safe. A trip through the dishwasher will probably ruin the exterior finish. My photo shows the utensil crock with a pineapple corer to give you an idea of the size.

Incredible Nonstick Surface Makes Cooked Food Hard to Remove. These two COOKING LIGHT ALLURE PREMIER CERAMIC NON-STICK COATING SKILLETS (8 inch and 9.5 inch Skillet Set, Stay Cool Handle, Easy Clean, Red) are gorgeous. The outer finish is a deep red lacquer.

The skillets have a nonstick surface that is incredible. Unfortunately, the nonstick surface is so good, it’s hard to remove your food (e.g., fried eggs). The cooked food just slides across the skillet surface as you try to get a spatula or turner under it.

Also, the skillets don’t conduct heat very well. They take a long time to warm up. The instructions say that for best results you should preheat the skillets for 2-3 minutes on low heat. That is good advice to follow.

The “stay cool” handles heat up somewhat. The handles have red silicon wrapped around them, but you can feel the heat through the silicon. Usually you won’t need a hotpad, though.

The two skillets come in convenient sizes. The smaller skillet is 8” across; the larger skillet is 9.5” across. The skillets are “hand wash only”, but they’re easy to clean because of the ultra-slick ceramic surface.

Panel With One-Way Design Is Too Large for Front Door. I love this DII HAPPY HALLOWEEN LACE SPIDER WEB WINDOW OR DOOR PANEL DECORATION (1 Panel, 38" x 84"), but it's far too wide and long to hang on my front door. It's also too long to hang on the curtain rod over my sliding patio doors. Be sure to measure the area where you plan to install this!

I think that the panel will work as a table runner for a large table (over a solid-color tablecloth). However, the design woven into the lace is a one-way design, with "Happy Halloween" at the top left, and a flying ghost at the lower right. Because of the design, I can't think of any way to partially fold (or cut down) this panel to make it fit onto a small table or standard door.

I haven't washed my panel, but I doubt that it will shrink the many inches required (both vertically and horizontally) to make it fit my front door. This panel is probably too delicate to hang outdoors, exposed to the elements, on the side of my house. The care instructions say: "Machine wash cold on gentle cycle, use mild detergent, wash dark colors separately, do not bleach, tumble dry on low setting, press with warm iron as needed."

Because this charming Halloween panel is too large to use as a door decoration on a standard-sized door, I rate it at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).

UPDATE: After washing in warm water, the panel shrank, but not enough to fit my front door. It's still 3" too wide, and 8" too long. I guess that the panel would work to decorate an open doorway, if the extra length is folded down at the top or up at the bottom.

Beautiful But Heavy 12” Skillet Needs Lots of Storage Space. This CALPHALON PREMIER SPACE SAVING NONSTICK 5QT SAUTE PAN WITH COVER is a beautiful nonstick cookware item. It’s a capacious 12” skillet (12½” across the top, with 2½” sides) made of heavyweight hard anodized aluminum. The two handles are stainless steel, which stays cool when you’re cooking on a stovetop (gas, electric, glass top). The hard nonstick surface is okay with metal utensils.

The space-saving claim is somewhat exaggerated, because it refers to the skillet’s ability to stack VERTICALLY with other cookware (with the same 12” diameter) from the “Calphalon Premier Space Saving” series. In fact, this very large and heavy 12” skillet consumes a lot of horizontal storage space, because it measures 23½” from the handle on the left to the tip of the long (primary) handle on the right. The skillet is almost two feet wide! If your plan is to buy several 12” diameter pieces from the series and stack them, don’t forget to calculate the total stack height to make sure it will fit in your storage area.

The tempered glass cover is flat (for vertical-space-saving stacking) rather than domed like most glass skillet lids (which may or may not store upside down in their skillets). The flat glass cover takes a little getting used to, if you’re accustomed to domed covers, and it is NOT vented. The glass cover has its own long stainless steel handle, which adds to the substantial total weight of the skillet plus cover.

The skillet is oven safe to 450 degrees Fahrenheit. (My kitchen has a rule against using long-handled cookware in the oven. I take it out of the oven with a hotpad, set it down somewhere, and burn myself every time by forgetting that the normally cool handle is still oven-hot.) The skillet is quite heavy when empty; I need to use two hands to handle it safely when it is filled with food or covered with the lid.

The skillet is dishwasher safe. However, the dark gray exterior may bleach out to a streaky lighter gray if you wash it regularly in a dishwasher—this is what happened with my Classic Calphalon anodized aluminum cookware. If you have a glass or ceramic cooktop, be sure NOT to preheat the skillet on high heat, or to heat it empty.

EdgeKeeper Sheath Makes Carbon Steel Knife Special. It’s the “EdgeKeeper” sheath that makes this FARBERWARE 5252819 EDGEKEEPER BUTCHER KNIFE (7-Inch, Black) special. The sheath sharpens the blade every time that you insert or withdraw the knife, so there’s no need to mess with a sharpening steel to keep a good edge on the knife.

The knife itself is made of carbon steel, and has a hard plastic handle. It’s a decent knife, reasonably well balanced, and comfortable to hold. The edge is sharp, thanks to the EdgeKeeper sheath. However, the knife doesn't hold the edge well as you use it, so you need the sharpening sheath.

The knife is strictly hand-washable (use warm, soapy water). Wipe the blade dry immediately after washing, before replacing the knife in the sheath.

Scrub Brush With Adjustable Long Handle, Stiff Plastic Bristles. This OXO GOOD GRIPS EXTENDABLE TILE & TUB BRUSH is basically just a scrub brush on a stick. The brush is high quality, but it only "pivots" up and down (instead of swiveling in all directions like a Swiffer mop). This limited pivot action makes the brush far less useful than I'd expected for scrubbing certain hard-to-reach tile areas alongside and behind the toilet in my condo's powder room. It takes some acrobatics to aim the rounded parts of the brush into the corners and oddly shaped areas.

Also, the brush has very stiff plastic (or maybe nylon) bristles that don't absorb water or floor-cleaning liquids at all. When I used my brush on the tile powder-room floor, it scrubbed the tile, but I still had to finish up with a mop and some extra hands-and-knees "detailing". At the end of the job, the brush needed cleaning, because it had picked up dirt bits.

The extendable handle adjusts to many different lengths. It took me a little while to figure out that you must twist the handle rods--not the colored plastic band that encircles one of the telescoping rods--in order to adjust the length.

Probably this brush works fairly well for tub and shower wall cleaning (using a powdered cleanser and rinsing with bath or shower water). However, it seems kind of expensive (about $15) for a nonabsorbent scrub brush with a handle. I rate it at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).

Lacks Automatic Air Quality Monitor Included in “Smart” Model. I ordered this GERMGUARDIAN AC4825 22" 3-IN-1 FULL ROOM AIR PURIFIER (HEPA Filter, UVC Sanitizer) for my home office because the fancier “smart” model (see [[ASIN:B01LCX9QWG Wi-Fi 4-in-1 GermGuardian]]) has performed so beautifully in my home. I have three of the “smart” air purifiers, in constant operation for more than a year, and none have presented any problems. They clean the air (odors and allergens), and the automatic air quality monitor (not included in this model) speeds up the fans when I cook something that smokes.

The wi-fi feature isn’t terribly useful, so I chose this 3-in-1 model for the additional room with the home office, not realizing that the air quality monitor was omitted (along with the wi-fi capability). The air quality monitor is a feature that matters to me, so this 3-in-1 model isn’t suitable to my needs.

KITCHEN CABINET. This product was pretty damaged when we received it; we were reimbursed approx 40% and I am working on 'the looks' of it; also, the glass for the top doirs was missing and the drawer slides were missing; I ordered drawer slides from Amazon to replace the missing slides.

Whitmore Chrome Shelf. I purchased this to put under our kitchen sink to create a vertical storage space. I like the adjustability of the product and once assembled is very sturdy. Unfortunately, though I measured THREE times, height, width and depth of cabinets, I didn't take into account the plumbing. The vertical post on the rear right won't go under the pipes without compromising the top shelf. It's in the garage now, with stain and rags and other stuff, so it isn't a complete loss, but now I have to find another product that will accomplish what this was purchased for. This kitchen cabinet is so wide that the pull out drawers plan we originally hoped would work, wasn't an option.

Advent wreath with candle cups. it's much smaller than I imagined, but as I wanted to carry it back and forth to a religious education class I teach, the small size and the built in candle cups were ideal.  Placed it on our coffee table between classes and 'dressed it up' a bit with pink and purple ribbons.  Worked very well for my class and will reuse it year after year.

It's soaking in hot water in my kitchen sink to soften up the plastic lid in hopes I can get the lid off for use it tomorrow. I like the handle and it fits perfectly on my kitchen drawer shelf. It's Anchor Hocking so I'm assuming it will be very durable and satisfying to use eventually.

NOT SOFT AT ALL.. I usually read all of the reviews and it seemed many people found this to be comfortable. It hasn't worsened by back pain, but it hasn't eased it either. Still looking for the ideal desk chair cushion that I can sit on for extended periods of time at my desk. Still haven't found it.  I'll use it in my sunporch on hard wood chairs, but not what I needed at this time.

1200 thread count sheets. I knew I must have missed something in the listing when the product came. I had tried to sort for 'cotton sheets full' and this product popped up. While they may have 1200 thread count, the thread used isn't cotton. They were very stiff to put on the bed, so I ran them through the washer/dryer to see if that softened them up. It did remove sizing, but they still have a grainy feel to them and are not nearly as soft as percale cotton. I originally purchased these for my teen daughters bed with the idea that if they were soft and comfortable, I'd get a larger size for our master bedroom. My daughter likes them well enough, but I won't purchase the second set as I prefer
cotton percale. The percale is pricey, but in view of how long they last and the sleeping comfort they provide, the cost is worth it to me. No I would NOT purchase these again.

Easy, Attractive, DOES NOT MUTE GLARE. I have french doors leading to my yard from my home office. The morning glare is harsh and prevents me from clearly viewing my desktop computer. Previously I've hung curtains to mute the glare but wanted to update the room since I'm doing basically a 'whole home' makeover.  I like this window cling material and it was truly VERY easy to put up. Today is the first 'morning glare' since I installed it yesterday afternoon. While still attractive and colorful, this product does NOTHING to reduce the glare. I ended up hanging up the curtains again. I won't remove the film since it does provide a level of privacy, but it didn't work as I had hoped.

Well woven light blue rug. It's rolled around a heavy cardboard tubing but it still won't lay flat. I really DON'T like the prominent black features since I ordered a light blue with pink rug for a master bedroom. I put it on a 3 season room now since it won't work for my master.

VERY SMALL BLANKET. I bought this for my bed for my medium size terrier to cuddle with and to protect my bedding from hair, dust, dog dander etc. Way to small, so I put it in her doggie bed in the living room rather than waste time returning it. BUY SOMETHING ELSE if you need a larger blanket.

I loved the blue and white 'china' style travel mug.. This is a very attractive travel mug but is EXTREMELY HEAVY especially when full of hot coffee. it keeps the coffee nice and hot, almost too hot to drink for an hour or so. This would be great for a long FreeWaY commute, but not a good option for just errands around town. I bought a 'green' refabricated one from Starbucks that says "Sip sensibly" for the errand trips.

Cute but thin. This is a very cute blanket, and nice and soft. However, it is much thinner than I thought it would be. If you run cold in the winter this probably isn’t the throw for you. I expected it to be at least twice the thickness it is.

Hot in the Summer. These are okay if don't have a cat that sleeps with you or if you use them during cooler weather, but I discovered that they pick very easily and they're really hot during summer temperatures.

So-So. This is a mice looking container, but it doesn't hold a lot and the sides fall down very easily. For small things that you want to be able to move out of the way it's a good idea, otherwise not very functional.
It’s okay. The color isn’t as vibrant as I would have preferred, and there are three random white spots on it. It’s okay. Not something I’d personally recommend to a friend.
The sleeves. the sleeves are made of verry thin plastic and they are difficult to put CD's in

This is not as pretty or sturdy as the picture shows. I was disappointed with this clock.  Its made out of a plastic and you have to physically push on it to get the different colors.  If you want it for a kids room , it would do ok.

The toaster is great, BUT the really LOUD beeping doesn't belong in .... The toaster is great, BUT the really LOUD beeping doesn't belong in my kitchen! It TOO LOUD! What genius thought of this I wonder.
BUYERS beware how loud this thing is before you buy, especially if you value sleep.

It broke easily. After 2 months, it stopped working.

Meh..... I would spend the extra money & get a better made item. This one is cheap & not very sturdy.
Meh.... Meh... Only small onions fit in the case. Hard to open. Not thrilled. Cute but that is about it.
Meh. I returned these. They look good in the photo & are good quality but in reality did not work for what I needed - would be better to be used in a drawer not free standing.

Not worth the money.. [[VIDEOID:e7b388138bb200ae9f310cf74a0f855f]] Silverware portion of this rack is HORRIBLE - doesn’t fit right & it is too big for the space it is to slide into & the hook is plastic & near impossible to open up. Already has stress marks on the unit.

what's the point?. This was a dumb buy for the price as it offers nothing extra special for its stated purpose.  It's just a piece of plastic with indents and one of those unnecessary products that sound good at the time.  Takes up too much counter space for me and I could just as easily turn my chemex upside-down on a dishtowel or in the dish drain.  I suppose it will make it marginally less likely the glass will break and allows air to circulate but I thought the material would be special.  It's not.  So. average.

Nice bowls. Pretty bowls.  Well made.  But the pouring design is lacking.. This is a pretty set, nice color, well made and very useable as bowls., However, the handle is too awkward to use for lifting and pouring, particularly given the weight of the bowls.  I hefted an empty one and mimicked pouring and it's not convenient.  Unlike a regular handle, it takes two hands to grasp and pour.  If the contents were hot, it would particularly be a problem.  The spout is broad and shallow.  I withhold judgment but as a person who has cooked and baked for over fifty years, I'm expecting it won't pour as precisely as I'd like.  I wanted these to be both pretty and practical.  I don't really need more bowls.  I wanted very effective, easy to manage pouring function.

Ok for purpose. Just didn't like "in Person". I found I did not like the pattern or the feel of the cloth of this shower curtain but I think that's personal taste.  I'd buy a more substantial cloth instead.  But it works fine.  Just not my taste.  In person, the colors and design didn't work for me either.  Not "elegant" enough.

Very Cute but cannot use washer or dryer to clean. I would expect a hand towel, even a cute cat novelty hand towel to be machine wash and dry.  Particularly since I want to get germs out of it.  This one must be hand washed in lukewarm water and dried in the shade.  It only gets three stars because it is cute.  Knowing the care instructions I will not acquire more.
Umm.... be careful with it?. It sucked good but fell over alot bc of crap design. Then it broke. Not happy.

Do not buy if you have a dog.. Nowhere near as full as shown in the picture but not terrible. My kids are okay with it but I dont use it because I'm too old to and broken for minimal support. Dogs love and will destroy and cause a giant mess.
Don't waste your money; appear cheap and not as pictured on website. Very expensive,. Did not appear as advertised

Small, hard to clean. The set has been fun to use, but they are smaller than expected. Unless I smooth oil or flour first, the baked pies stick to the cups, making them very hard to clean. I did not end up using them as much as expected.
Not for tall plants. Very pretty and I like the look. However, it is not good for semi tall or thick plants.

THIS SLICER IS MADE IN CHINA....

possible water/germ/food entry at point of handle & plastic overlay. KitchenAid makes a good ice cream scoop. I have this in the color, Pistachio.

It is a metal scoop with a plastic overlay on the handle. I was perplexed by those mentioning

1. water possibly getting into handle
2. plastic pulls away from handle.

I went in for a closer look and sure enough, these things happen. I placed the scoop in a mason jar filled with water, waiting 20 minutes and checked. I would not have noticed this before since I never let my scoops sit in water, and I don't put them through the dishwasher (in the past, doing so seemed to make them get pit marks, especially if it was an aluminum variety). So I hand wash...It's ice cream.. I just rinse and dry and then back in the drawer it goes. I may use it 10 times a year, and that's if I don't use a spoon to dig out ice cream. Anyway, I took scoop out from water, dried it, and shook it. I thought I could hear something. So then proceeded to pull on the handle to try to separate metal from plastic, and sure enough a couple drops of water came out.

As for plastic overlay pulling away from the metal, that does happen but only if you are looking to do so. I took it a step further and twisted and pulled to see how far I could go with it. No damage. I doubt it will ever fall part. However, the fact that it can be manipulated means that it is a pressure seal. It is likely why it is "possible" for water to get in. It isn't going to happen by just rinsing it. I bet I never ever experience that outside of this contrived experiment due to the way I handle my scoop. BUT if you are inclined to run it through the dishwasher or let it sit in the sink with water, then your experience may vary. No one should need to even be concerned with that, so I can't rate fully based on that.

It does get really good rating across several "best of" articles. OXO seems to win out, but this is considered a good one. I think it is a good one. I like the feel of the handle. It feels just a tiny bit heavier than my older Farberware one. It definitely cuts through hard ice cream. The slightly wider, thicker grips gives me a better grip. I do wonder if the handle may be too smooth for some people.

As a rarely used item, I will have this a long time. As a rarely used item I am more liberal with what is acceptable, particularly since it is just a means to grab some ice cream. However, I'm a little grossed out at the possibility of water or other gunk possibly building up where the handle and plastic overlay meet. It takes two hands to demonstrate it, so I would need assistance to take a picture. I don't know if it is a design flaw, over sight, or somehow intentional (the extra gives allows more pressure to be place into handle to scoop extra hard ice cream)?

I do love KitchenAid, and I normally highly recommend their wares. But this item of this design style does not impress me like everything else.

Again- great feel, good grip, cuts into hard ice cream, typical scoop shape, attractive

BUT, that spot where steel meets plastic.. Nope.

3 stars.

decent bags for light duty use, all 100 02 absorbers are packed together, inc labels. 3-4 stars for the bags. 2 for the absorbers if only based on how they are packaged (all together).

Bags are of nice size and thickness, with gussets for standing. Though not as thick and robust as some bags I have. These would be (for me) for short term storage. Think snacks and such that can benefit from "mylar" storage, but maybe not for super long term storage, unless storing these in a container for long storage (think of food grade buckets filled with mylar bags filled with food). You do you though.

I normally dont buy these kits for the oxygen absorbers. For that, I prefer to buy a very trusted brand, since it is all about the 02 absorbers in terms of effectiveness. Cant risk it, and I dont really have a way to test it in a manner that I would/could comfortably do (seal some food, come back a year later and see if it molded, or went bad in another way). But I do appreciate the inclusion of O2 absorbers, and here again I will use them for stuff that I am not concerned about for long term storage. More is better, so feel free to use extra in your bags. So, maybe a batch of cookies I made, or storing some chips, powders, etc.

Yet, I still factor the 02 absorbers into my rating. I consider them "good enough" if they are individually packaged, and pretty much useless if all stored together. Once open, they have all been exposed to air. I'm fine with a handful being in one vac sealed packet, but not all 100. And so, if you buy this for using the whole kit, then plan to use up the 02 absorbers quickly as well. I suppose some can be used, then just tightly packaged the unused ones back up.. but I'm not chancing it.

I wish companies would say if the absorbers are all packed together (unwrapped) or packed together but also individually wrapped. I come across both scenarios and this is the former. Figured I would mention it in case you are looking for that info too (the pic they include doesnt quite clarify).

Overall, the kit is "OK". Which is 3 stars, and means just that-- it is OK. Not great, not bad. Has pros and cons. Will be up to you to decide. I just have my preferences, and it wasnt something I could totally detect from their description or pics alone.

Does what it's supposed to, just be careful.. I purchased this 1-gallon water distiller for producing water for my carnivorous plants (they are sensitive to contaminants.) It produces distilled water as it should, but I have a few gripes.
First, and most importantly, the unit's design is two pieces. A top containing the fan lifts off, and the bottom contains the water chamber and heating elements. The top piece has its own plug which must be plugged into the base. Then, the base has its own plug, which is removable and plugs into the outlet.
If you are not careful, there is a *serious* risk of electrocution and/or damaging the unit due to this design. The plug on the base of the unit is pretty much guaranteed to be exposed to water dripping down the sides when you remove the lid to add more water. I highly recommend covering the back side of the unit with a dry towel when you remove the top. Water that has evaporated in the machine will still be present in the top and will drip all over the place.
Additionally, when you go to fill up the tank, ensure you don't allow any water to drip over the side of the base. (The water tank is not removable from the base, you have to tote the whole thing to the sink or bring a pitcher of water to the machine.)
Despite the flaws in its design and a lingering suspicion that cleaning this thing will be difficult, I would still recommend it for those who need distilled water on demand. It saves you so much trouble buying and lugging it from the store. Just use caution!

Not Really What It is Advertised As, but a decent quality frying pan. There is a lot of hype about these red copper pans being non-stick and scratch resistant.  Don't believe it.  I have cured the pan a couple of times, according to instructions and while it helps a little, for a while, to prevent sticking, food still sticks and sometimes sticks badly, especially eggs.  In TV commercials they show the eggs sliding around the pan freely.  Maybe if you keep moving the eggs around that would work, but wouldn't it with any pan?  The scratch resistance is hype too, as my pan scratched after just a few uses, although they are minor scratches and don't seem to impact the cooking much.  (I didn't use metal implements either.)  On the plus side, the pan does heat evenly and appears to be able to take high temperatures without warping.  I have been using mine for months and no visible warping.  The pan cleans up without too much scrubbing, even with stuck on food.  The stay cool handle works, sort of.  It stays pretty cool on the part you would normally grab, but don't reach too close to where it hooks on the pan, as it gets hotter, the closer you get to the pan.  You might not burn yourself, but you wouldn't want to hold on for very long.  Also after you cure the pan in the oven, the handle will be too hot to grab, so you have to use a holder and let it cool down.  I wouldn't buy another one of these, as it is only slightly better than an average pan.

Good Suction; Nice not to deal with a cord; power head is heavy. I haven't used this for very long, but I like to review things based on first impressions, as often they seem the most accurate.  First of all, this is easy to assemble; together in 5 minutes with no tools needed; just snap the sections together.  One thing that I didn't like right away is that the two included attachments don't have on-board storage.  Apparently Shark sells an overpriced accessory to hold the attachments.  For the high price of this vacuum, they should include this.  The second thing I noticed right away is the vacuum cannot stand upright without collapsing and folding down the handle (but that is easy to do).  I gave it a quick cleaning run around in several rooms in the house and it seems to have strong pickup capability and actually almost drives itself, so it moves along smoothly and rapidly.  Simple switch to go from hard floors to carpet and back again.  The biggest issue that I would have with this vacuum is that the power head (which also doubles as a hand vacuum, which is easily detachable), is quite heavy.  You have to hold most of that weight of the power head while using the machine, as the angle that it has to be held at in order to clean puts most of the weight on your arm.  If you are young and strong, maybe not a big issue, but if you were doing a whole house, your arm might hurt after using it for more than a few minutes.  If you can't lift much weight, then this is not the vacuum for you, but the total weight is not bad; it is lighter than a typical vacuum.  The collapsing handle is a nice feature for getting under furniture, so I should be able to clean some places that haven't been in a long time.  Not having to deal with a cord is a huge plus and the two rechargeable batteries that you can swap are also great.  The batteries seem strong, but I haven't run the vacuum long enough to know if they last as long as claimed.  They do take a while to charge.  The battery packs are easy to swap in and out and have indicator lights showing charge progress and how much charge is left; they are well designed.  I should give this more than a 3-star rating, but having to hold the weight of the power head/hand vac while using the machine could be a real problem if using it for an extended period of time.  The dust cup is small too, so will no doubt fill up fast, but they couldn't really make it any larger without adding more weight and bulk.  Overall it is a well designed vacuum, but I know if I let my house cleaning crew use it, they will break it fast, as they will forget that you can't stand it upright without folding down the handle; they already broke one vacuum that way.

Well Designed, Light, Convenient, not the best on heavily soiled carpets. I have mixed feelings about this carpet cleaner.  I am spoiled by having used a Rug Doctor, which really does an excellent job.  My old Rug Doctor is on its last legs, so thought I would give this cleaner a try.  I had bought a Bissell carpet cleaner several years ago, but ended up returning it as it didn't work that well.  Thought I would try again as I assumed that improvements had been made over the years.  It does seem like it is a better machine than the one from several years ago and it really seemed to get a lot of dirt out of the carpet and pulled out a lot of lint too.  I would classify it as an adequate cleaner if your carpets are not heavily soiled.  It didn't work as well as my Rug Doctor to get out ground in dirt, but when you consider that it is 1/2 to a 1/3 of the price of a Rug Doctor, it does a lot for the price.  I like the idea that the tank you fill will hot water comes out and you can take it to the sink and leave the machine plugged in and not have to move it.  With my Rug Doctor, every time I need to fill the water, I have to unplug it and take the whole machine to the sink, dump the dirty water and fill it with clean water from a pitcher.  With the Bissell, you just run the water directly from the faucet into the tank.  The power cord is a reasonable length.  It's long enough so you don't have to move the machine too often, but short enough not to get in the way.  The machine is light and easy to manuveur. Rug Doctor uses one backwards pass to clean.  The Bissell uses one forward and one backward pass dispensing cleaning solution and then a foward and backward pass to vacuum up the water.  It's 4 passes instead of one, but the machine is not that heavy so it's not a big deal to make the 4 passes.  I liked the hand attachment that you use with the built-in hose; it worked very well.  The machine noise is about normal for a carpet cleaner, approximately like a vacuum cleaner.  Very easy to assemble the machine; just a few screws.  So what's wrong with this machine?  On heavily soiled carpets, it seemed to leave a lot of streaks and put out too much soapy mixture.  It's possible I used too much cleaning solution as the small included bottle said double strength, but I used the included measuring cup, so I assumed it was the right amount.  I also had a hard time figuring out how the built-in hose was supposed to wrap around; there is no picture or diagram.  My sister figured it out right away how to do it, so chalk that up to my being a dummy.  The biggest issue I had with this machine is that when you turn it off and start to move it, it drips a lot of water out and can spot up the carpet; then you have to run it again over the spots and they don't come out easily.  I also noticed that the restricted area that sucks up the water is narrow enough that lint accumulates and requires cleaning just about after each use.  This is a decent machine for the money and I would give it a solid 3 stars; maybe 3 1/2.  If you don't have a lot of very dirty carpet, this might be perfect for you.  It beats paying double or triple the price for a more heavy duty machine, unless you need the heavier duty cleaning power.  If you clean your carpet regularly, this should do the job just fine.  If you have a lot of dirt and have pets, this might not quite do the job, unless you use it often.
