I would recommend the product they are quality but make sure you know what you are ordering and it’s use.
Nice but picture is as vivid in person. Nice but picture is as vivid in person. Think I’ll go for acrylic next time for a glossy & cleaner picture

Not good for burgers. Works well for small, thick tortillas.. I originally bought this to make burger patties but this makes them paper thin. I use it for making sopas...kind of like a thick corn tortilla.

Good size press. I liked the size of the empanada press. However I thought that if I put it down on the door I could cut it but when I pressed down to cut the dough it also cut it down the middle with the bottom seam. I’m also afraid to push too hard because it is plastic and I’m afraid to break the handles off.

Very thin for the price. The quality of the product is great, but whomever takes photographs for their sales team does a good job because this is thin and flat.. no where near as thick as the picture looks. Im not returning it.. was sleeping on the floor after my air mattress went flat.. but they should really double the thickness of the padding they use.

It came with a nice matching cover and storage bag.. its fairly nice... just for the price it's a bit too flat to make it worth the cost. It's like laying on an over sized yoga mat.

Editing to add that after sleeping on it a few nights it's rather comfortable

Width a little short. For some reason the cubical walls in my office are extremely wide, like four inches or more. :/  This item works with that configuration, but it is too narrow, looks a bit off when installed, and a lot of times the hook comes off when I remove my coat.  No problem to just put it back on, but I would have preferred something that fit better.  It does work, however, and I've had many of my office mates ask me about where I purchased it. :)

We use a lot of these. We have been using this little timer for about three years now.
To be clear, we've used MANY of this STYLE of time over the last few years.

These are from the Dollar Store, and do what they are supposed to do for about a year.
The displays, even when brand new are not very easy to read, and you have to tip them
back and forth until you get just the right angle to actually view it. (Even then, I sometimes
cross my fingers that I read it right!)

They are easy to set. Because of the difficulty I have in reading them, I just count the minutes
while pushing the minute button!

If you are doing several batches, like when you bake cookies or muffins, you have to push
the Min and Sec buttons at the same time. Just push the start button to get it going.

The timer makes a beeping sound when it goes off. The beep gets weaker with time, so within a
couple months of regular use, you'll have to really listen for it carefully.
The magnets are useful - they have a magnet on the back, so we stick them to the vent hood
over the oven.

I'd like to find a reliable wind-up time, but haven't found a decent one yet that got good reviews.
So until then, we'll keep buying these 3 or 4 at a time from the local dollar store, and enjoy
them while they last. They come in three colors - black, blue or red.

Keep on shopping - okay for a buffet table, but that's it!. This one has a ways to go before it is useful.
I bought it because our family loves deviled eggs and I make them almost weekly in the warmer weather.
I wanted a way to store more deviled eggs, as the container I had only held 12 halves. Not enough! The fact that each tray held 18 halves was really a great thing, so I thought. I also wanted something that wouldn't take up a lot of refrigerator room, and thought this might slide in on top of other items in the fridge.

The item came with the two trays and lids shrink-wrapped together. There are little clamps on the egg portion of the tray that hook to the lid portion. Not well, but they hook. There is NOTHING remotely sturdy about this set. You cannot pick it up by the handle. If you think you can quickly grab an egg and pop the lid back on, think again - it is not quick and you will probably need both hands.

The tray itself holds the eggs very well. Almost too well - the indentations are deep, and we found ourselves using a fork to get the eggs back out. No big deal, but something you should know about these. They would work very well for a buffet table (that is at your home, and you did not have to transport them in these trays anywhere). Some others have said they put ice in the upside down lid and put the tray on the ice. I could see that being helpful in a picnic situation.

Bottom line is that they do not fasten well enough in any way. I would not trust them for transporting eggs. I would not trust lifting them out of the refrigerator. I would not even trust them to keep the eggs fresh, because the seal is not tight on the top/bottom. It basically sits on top of the gg tray, and you use the little latches to pretend to hook the top to the bottom. Meh at best. I would have returned these, but as mentioned, I can see these working well for a buffet or self-serve party situation. That's ALL they would be good for, in my opinion. Just too flimsy for anything else.
I have already purchased a different set via Amazon that is perfect for our needs and airtight too.
So, if you have a lot of home dinner parties or family dinners, this will work on the food table.
If you don't and might want to drive to somewhere and bring your deviled eggs with you, please get a different container.

Curves are not angled properly for the majority of ornaments or for larger ones. This is a beautiful ornament stand. BUT...the only way it can actually hold an ornament is if the ornament itself has a very SHORT hanger. In other words, all the beautiful ornaments with fabric ribbons and such won't work. I tried four different ornaments, and every one of them hung way too low and touched the bottom curve of the stand. If I cut the ribbon shorter, it would not ever be able to be hung on a tree, to be able to alternate decorations.

It needs to have the top where it curls over be extended/uncurled one turn. We experimented with ours, figuring since it wasn't working anyway, the worst we could do would be to break it. Either way, we weren't able to hang ornaments on it. So my husband started tweaking the curves and coils with tools. We managed to uncurl the top enough to raise it up, which helped a little bit, but not enough. We also played with the curve in the middle, having to UNcurl it some to get a little more height. Once that was done, the ornaments still faced sideways, due to the placement of the top curl. So yet again, we played with that, and turned the top curl 90 degrees out, which finally allowed a regular ornament to be put on there without touching any of the stand or facing the back of the stand.

So, over all, it is a sturdy stand, and the bottom curl is beautiful. Note that it has a fairly large "footprint", and will take up some room. But the design is a little flawed in reality, with the curves' angles needing to be revamped to make it useful. You'll note in the photo that the ornament they display is actually very small, and does not have a drop-down hanger of any kind - it is a very short little hanger too. Most ornaments that you would display won't be like that. This would be great for small ornaments, but the larger ones that you might hang on your tree just won't work.

Buyer beware on tray quantity. Well, my feelings on this are mixed, but not because of the tray itself.
The tray seems to be a nice quality. I bought them to make fat bombs for Paleo. I think they will be perfect for that use.

What ticks me off was how deceptive this listing was. It has since been changed, but the photo clearly shows TWO trays, and when I bought it, gave the drop-down choice of mixed colors or all green or all blue. I chose mixed. But when I received the order, I only got ONE tray!! Very irritating, since I could have purchased just one tray for $2.00 less from a different seller.

So, nice tray that will be useful for coconut oil recipes, but was a very deceptive listing. (Again, this has since changed to say one tray, but too late for me.)

Adorable decorations that don't ship very well.. I wanted to buy these because they were just funny, in my opinion.
You don't have to be into gore to enjoy it.
It can be for Halloween or for baking/cooking decorated cupcakes for your favorite chef.

I would have enjoyed them even more, had they arrived whole. Instead, half of ours were broken and cracked.
I haven't tried to glue them back together with syrup or something yet, because I haven't opened the package yet.
Disappointing.
Better if you buy these in the store, where you can see the condition before you purchase them.

Base is great, arms fragile. This is a great looking ornament - and who doesn't like a shiny Dalek - but purchased this five times now (one for me, two for my adult kids who are Who fans as well). Out of those purchases, two orders were cancelled without explanation, and the other three arrived with parts broken off.

So, we love these, but there's a problem with either the packaging or the product. But he looks good on the shelf anyway.

Really cheap fleece, not soft at all.. This would catch the eye of any Doctor Who fan. That's why we ordered one... love the moon being so prominate in the design.

BUT... know up front that this is not a cozy, soft fleece throw. It is a slightly rough, CHEAP fleece fabric that has been zig-zag stitched around the edges. Cheap, cheap, cheap.
The $4 fleece throws you find every winter in a country-wide discount chain are softer and nicer. Truly sad. The only saving grace is the design. Not a cuddly throw for sure.

This would be much better to hang on a wall as decoration than to use as a throw. :-(

Majority of reviews are for a different product.. Just a heads-up that nearly all the reviews for this meat grinder are for an air fryer, not even the same product.
Proceed at your own risk.

THIN, cheap, but soft. It's okay.. Good and bad on this one.

The bad:
The backing is VERY thin fabric. Think the tops of dollar store Christmas stockings. Very thin, but has a tiny nap on it. I took a picture with a dollar store flat flashlight showing through TWO layers.
Also, it is not attached anywhere but the outer seams. You'd expect a few seams through the middle areas so it doesn't shift, but nope. This is just two pieces of fabric sewn together on the outer edges. That's it.

The good:
The furry part (the "top") is very soft and has a great feel to it. Again, a lightweight fabric, but it has a longer nap and makes for a nice throw.

They sent me the wrong color, but I was okay with the one sent, so not returning it. I actually got it as an extra blanket for our cats, but it is nice enough for an extra chair or loveseat throw too.

I'd buy it again if the price is right.

Too heavy, too rough, unappealing. Well, this is one of those items you will either hate or love - unlikely you will be on the fence.

The colors are lovely and neutral enough to use in almost any decor. However, this is NOT one of those super soft throws. This one is very heavy, a little awkward, and I found the texture very unappealing. Mine also came with a big ol' snag in it already.

If you've ever used those cotton basic blankets, like hospitals often use, you'll have a good idea of how this feels, except hospital blankets are softer.

The plaid is nice, the colors are good. But the texture and weight is a real turn-off to me. I can't recommend this one.

You get what you pay for. Cheapie holder, just okay grinders. I recently got some different peppercorns and needed some new grinders. So I decided to try this set.

The grinders themselves are pretty small. The grinder mechanism does not look super sturdy, so I hope it surprises me.

But the worst part is the holder. Either I received a corroded holder, or these have a really bad finish on them. It feels like there is salt on a lot of it, but there isn't - it is the bad finish. I tried cleaning it, in case something got on it at the warehouse. Nope - just a bad finish. Maybe some day I will sand it down (yes, so rough that it needs sanding) and just paint it. But I am not using the holder as is.

Pretty but also pretty cheap. I actually love Christmas socks, and used to collect them, decorating our whole house with them. So of course, I was drawn both to them being socks and them having sparkly gold stars on them.

First off, the red fabric is like a cheap, low-pile chenille. The gold stars are stamped on, and have a little bit of a holographic glitter on them. There is no inner liner. The back of the fabric feels like felt.

Then the cuff... it is white, and made of a slightly-longer-pile fabric. The cuff is lined with what feels like white felt. There is a generously-long red ribbon hanger sewn to the inside.

Now let's talk about construction. These have some decent fabrics - it is a shame they put them together so cheaply. The cuff is sewn on pretty badly. As in, you cannot fold the cuff over, and it is smaller than the sock, leaving a weird seam on the side.

So, these are cute enough, but the quality certainly is not there. If I was serious about using these at my house, I'd probably replace the cuff entirely with a faux fur.

These are ok. Depends on what you plan to put in them. I mis-read the description on these bags. I thought they were heat-sealing bags. Nope, just zipper type.

I had to play with one for a while to see how they actually opened. With the zip area and a hanging cutout, I thought these might open from the back. They don't - the zip part is the only thing that is sealed - the bags are completely open at the top above the zipper.

I wouldn't put anything expensive in there, that's for sure. I would not buy again.

Did someone need to store their 45's?. Really? Really??

I could hardly believe how small this rack really is. I took some photos with a basic advertising pen in the photo as a size comparison.

When I looked at the rack, I told my daughter it looked like someone is trying to repurpose a warehouse full of old racks that held old 45 records! I had the same kind of rack 40 years ago.

It seems pretty sturdy, but with its size, I won't be using for cookie sheets as I had planned. Maybe baking racks or lids instead.

Smaller than expected, but okay. The largest one was smaller than I had expected. (Yes, the measurements are in this listing, but were not available on the listing from which I purchased these.) However, these should work fine for why I wanted them - to cut shapes from biscuits and sandwiches.

I have to say, the ones we received were not a beautiful, shiny silver like the ones in the photo. Ours are dull, and almost look unfinished. One had a crooked seam.
I am sure they will work out okay. I was just disappointed that they were not the shiny finish in the product photo.

Very heavy bowls, hard to maneuver for me. These are very nicely made pink bowls that are large enough to hold a good amount of soup or chili.
The pink swirl is very pretty as well.

For some reason, I expected these bowls to be much lighter than they are!

I don't have a lot of hand strength due to arthritis, and I find these bowls very awkward to use and wash up. Not because of the finish, but because of the sheer weight of each bowl.

They are good looking and have a nice finish, but I don't see myself using these very often. They are just too heavy and awkward for my hands.

Think decorative tarp, more than a tablecloth. This is a cute plastic tablecloth.
The background is red, with colorful winter designs all over. These make good table protectors for spills or sticky things.

The tablecloth itself has no flannel backing, so I would be cautious about the finish of any wooden table you use it on. This is basically a heavy tarp with a holiday print instead of standard blue.

Ok, but flat, not a globe shape, and very heavy. When I saw this one, I thought it was going to be a round ornament. It even says "globe" in its own description.
It is not.

The ornament is a flat disc.
The Santa/reindeer are molded shape, like a pour mold. The ornament is surprisingly heavy for what it is. It comes with an attached red ribbon for hanging. You'll need a larger tree, because the weight would topple a little or tabletop sized tree. You could always hang this from a standalone ornament hanger as well.

Overall, not what I thought it would be, but it's cute enough.

It's okay. Very short handle, spoon area small. You can always use another slotted spoon if you cook very much.

This one is smaller than any slotted spoon I have previously owned. It appears as though the mfg took a small plastic slotted spoon and dipped it in a silicone bath. There is a hole at the end of the handle for hanging.

It won't scratch pans, which is a good thing. But the spoon is just too short to be of much use at the stove. Perhaps it will be more useful as a tabletop serving spoon.

Heavy, sturdy, but what are all the symbols around the edges. This is the largest, most industrial apple corer I have ever seen! It is very heavy.
This could have been on a knight's table, ready to eviscerate any random food that happened to be served.

What bothers me greatly about this is that there are unidentified symbols all the way around this corer. It is divided into 12 sections, so I thought perhaps they went with a zodiac theme. But if yes, then who's? It doesn't match English symbols or Chinese symbols. What did I just let into my home?

There are gold symbols around the heavy, scored handles. Are they supposed to be lotus flowers? Who knows.

I find it disturbing to have unidentified symbolism all over this item, and not a peep from the manufacturer about it. It was not visible from the page from which I ordered this - it just looked like a black apple corer. I want to know what these symbols are, and what they stand for.

Died after about 6 uses.. [[VIDEOID:3771fa2415bbef1a5f9d2b062c9ae074]] I loved this when I first got it. It did a pretty decent job of vacuuming and sealing. I used it maybe every other month to seal up spices or meats. It isn't large and a quart bag is the biggest size you can use on this one.
BUT - just got it back out to seal several pounds of wild rice. It vacuums out the air just fine, but the heating strip no longer works!! So here I sit with a freshly opened five-pound bag of wild rice and cannot sral it up. I also had a stack of mylar bags I had planned to heat seal as well.
Nope. Dead in the water. One year later, with using it approximately six times.
Of course, it is well past the return date.

Get something better if you are serious about food storage. This one can't cut it.

Disappointing. Too heavy to be useful. [[VIDEOID:6298e434137e626718c3d15e3c8b1301]] These don't look as good as I had hoped. We have a couple other magnetic tiebacks and really like them. I like bling, so thought these would be great. Not so much.

The sparkle part looks ok, although the plastic gems are sometimes not glued in the exact spot. But, these are constructed differently in a way that I do not care for. I made a short video to show folks how they fasten, and the cording on these.

The cords are not cords like on all my other tie-backs; these are metal and stretchy, like a 1970's necklace. Maybe they found a warehouse with old necklace cording amd wanted to use it up. But it adds nothing, and makes the tieback heavier.

The backs are flat and cheap plastic. It is harder to match up the magnet on these than it is for the others.

Overall, these get a "C" in my gradebook. Nice try, but too many design flaws to be really useful.

Brightly colored, a little small. Simple, plain can coozies that quietly do their jobs.
I am not sure how they fit regular 12 ounce cans, as I don't have any my photo is with a "mini" can, which is 7.5 ounces. The minis come right to the top of the cozy.
These would be perfect for around a pool to keep cans colder.

Pass on this one. Plastic handle is too slick. Everyone can use bench scrapers. They are handy tools to scoop up chopped veggies or greens from the board to your bowl. Of course, they work well for dividing up dough or scraping scraps up.

The blade is plenty sharp and is sturdy. BUT...what I don't like is the handle. It is only plastic, and once your hands are wet or goopy, good luck holding on to it any more.

For that reason, I cannot recommend this scraper. It is too hard to hold on to.

VERY thin. Good for quick mixes, but not heavy batters. [[VIDEOID:b1c39e9c3ed9b4477fb806459f2b707a]] It is hard to have too many mixing bowls. We don't have a dishwasher where we currently live, so I am always looking for something that will fit in our small sink and be easy to wash.

This is a set of four nested mixing bowls. In theory, they take up less room that way. Each bowl has a small handle to help keep a grip on it, and a silicone-type ring on the bottom to help the bowl not move around on your chosen surface. I really like the shades of blue as well.

Now that I have used them a while, I did notice both good and not-so-good on these. The ring is good and does help them to not slip around, but it falls off pretty easily on most of the bowls. I wish it popped into place instead of just going around the ridge.

These are VERY thin bowls. They bend very easily. If you have something heavy in them, you will need both hands to pick it up and not dump the contents. I made a cream cheese dip and almost dropped it all on the floor when I just picked it up by that side handle. These should definitely be thicker. I did a muffin batter in the largest bowl, and it bent all the time. A little frustrating.

Overall, these are fine for a spare bowl, or whipping up eggs to be scrambled. But they do not handle stiffer or heavier foods well. The plastic never feels truly clean either. I only use Dawn dishwashing soap. Even with a steel wool pad and Dawn, they still feel "greasy" to the touch. Maybe a dishwasher would take care of that, but without one, I can't answer if that would help.

So they are okay, but just okay. I will stick to my stainless steel bowls for most things, and leave these to the tinier jobs.

Not nearly as big as they sound. I guess I need to adjust my mental expectations on this one. When I read "half gallon", I mentally see half of a gallon of milk.

These are not nearly that large. They are more like a large container of a dry spice. They will work just fine for some things, but not for what I had planned to use them for. Very lightweight.

So, don't think physical half gallon if you are thinking about buying these...think more along the lines of liquid measurement, 64 ounces. That's my best guess on what they were thinking.

Only one of them held the seal. Well, I really tried to like these. We live in a pretty tiny place, so saving space wherever we can is a must.

I always shrink-bag our winter blankets and coats each spring. We did 3 bags of blankets and one of coats. Only ONE bag out of four kept its airtight seal longer than a month. One didn't even make it two weeks.

Very disappointing, and I cannot recommend these bags.

Ok, but would not buy again.. These fit in our air fryer all right (basket-style Cosori), but for some reason, none of us like using them very much. We very much prefer to put a foil sheet in the bottom below the basket.

Maybe they will win me over some day. But for now, they are just annoying. I would not repurchase these.

Big, but lacking quality control. At our house, it is hard to have too many gnomes, or too many pumpkin decorations. This item covers both.

The pumpkin is an odd knit fabric. The black face parts are glued on rather oddly. I was trying to get the "nose" off, because it looks VERY odd, but could not do it.

The gnome itself is also cute, but lacking quality. Ours needs me to sit down with a glue gun and do some major cosmetic surgery. Lots of loose ribbon, fabric and such. One arm is hanging loose with just a dot of glue on it. Still cute, just lacking quality consistency.

I'll like it better after I do some work on it, but it is a cute decoration.

Ok. A little thin, not very large. These racks reminded me a great deal of the old racks I used to have to kerp my 45 records. Yep, I really dated myself on that one. These look to be coated in a silver-toned paint of some type. They did also paint the metal end tips, which is nice - it makes them a little less sharp.

But, that is what these racks looked like - recycled record racks. They don't seem big enough to really hold up cookie sheets properly, but would probably hold baking racks without problems.

Works ok, but it is too small. The idea behind this mat is good - it is absorbant and good to put your freshly washed dishes on.

The mat quality is nice. We tried it out, as we don't have a dishwasher. Our kitchen is very small and we have very little counter space. I thought the mat might be great.

Well, it could be, if it was a lot larger. Even with our very small counter space, this mat is too small! It won't hold a lot of dishes or pans.
If it is just one person who doesn't like to cook, this might be great. The water absorbing part did work well. But there just isn't enough room for our use. I went back to what I was using before, a large bath towel to sit everything in.

Good idea, but only covers a little space, so mostly good for singles.

Cute, but impractical. These are very cute! You get a good color assortment, so you can use them nearly anywhere.

But, we rent, so we are very limited on where or how we can use these. I have not tried one on a painted surface yet, as I don't want to peel paint off the wall.

The main downside to me, is that it really only holds one cord at a time. The one I currently have on my nightstand holds 5 cords...the little hands, just one.

So, very cute, but impractical.

If I didn't know these were Corelle, I would have never guessed it.. I love Corelle. I own odd plates from my mom, and two of my own sets. So I thought these would be good to try.

I have to say that these are different from any of my other Corelle ware.
The color is nice, and the quality is still there. But they feel different.

These are VERY heavy when compared to my other Corelle plates. I really don't know why, or if this is a different lines, or what the deal might be. To me, they are awkwardly heavy. I thought maybe they did a stoneware line, because that's what they feel like. But the box says they are still glass.

I don't plan on adding them to our daily use dishes. Too heavy for comfortable handling.

These are not very soft.. These fit our king sized pillows without any problems. But...despite being washed several times, these are just not soft. They almost have a rough texture. Maybe we got a bad set - I don't know.
But, these have been relegated to the back of the closet, for desperation use. I don't recommend these.
Three Stars. it is quiet. I thought it was oscillating. That is not the manufacturers fault though.

Soft Design, Dries Quickly! Mediocre Padding 🛀🏽. I do love the soft air mesh material of this bath pillow, and the zigzag pattern is relaxing to look at! The suction cups seem to exhibit reliable adherence, and the pillow does easily hang up by the attached plastic hook for necessary airing out post-bath. Even if the pillow gets completely submerged in water during use, it still seems to dry fairly quickly. It did arrive to me folded in half, but I suspect it was easier to ship it that way. I will say that the padding feels less than substantial, so it doesn’t provide an optimally cushiony bath experience, but it never promised to be a premium item to begin with. There are definitely squishier tub pillows on the market, but this ergonomically shaped one still provides a certain level of appreciable comfort.

At the time this review was posted, this product had a list price of $14.88 on the product page. I do believe that price was already showing reflection of a recent decrease, and that value seems reasonably appropriate for this item and what it can offer.

Cheap, save space, but thin plastic. Returned. I like how you can stack them to save space. However, I returned it because of the cheap plastic.

Three stars because they are good for once a while baking session, but not for me as I intend to use it daily.
Was not a set of four. While the bucket seems nice and like it will last, we did not receive a set of four as advertised. I wouldn't pay this price for one storage box.

These are not "stickers". I like the table runner and mantle scarf a lot. They're actually cuter in person than pictured. But I feel the term "stickers" to describe 113 out of the 115 pieces is misleading. These are vinyl window clings. They will not stick to most walls, as shown in the fourth picture. They're thin, dollar store window vinyl clings.

Not easy to clean, does not come apart. I liked the compact style of the cutter, with the nice roller handle. The cover was a bit odd, rolling over to close the device. However, the problem came when trying to clean it. I have had these small circular cutters before, and they all came apart for cleaning. This does not, and when you are trying to clean off the food, it rotates and just pushes it back INTO the cutter. I am not sure how you are supposed to get this completely cleaned. I put it in the dishwasher, but there is no way to disassemble and manually clean it. I would look for one that comes apart better

Stiff and wrinkly. While the headline is telling, it doesn't convey just how wrinkly this bottom sheet comes out of the dryer. Maybe it's just the dark gray color and the shadows (meaning maybe wrinkles in lighter colors sheets aren't as noticeable), but the wrinkles are terrible looking to me. And I'm a messy person by nature, so I don't usually care about such things. I really don't.
I also found the sheet to be not smooth and rather stiff. I washed and dried in a heated dryer a couple hoping that would help loosing the threads a little, but it really hasn't. I can't say I'd recommend this one knowing Amazon has better options available.
Hope this review was helpful

Ceramic dish came chipped and is "fake" grounded. Overall, this wall warmer works well. It gets warm enough to give a nice throw in my bathroom. It looks very pretty too. But I had to deducted two stars. First, the ceramic dish that holds the melted wax came chipped in two places. Had I used my hard earned cash to make this purchase, I would have been disappointed. Second, I deducted another star because the electric plug in is not technically grounded. It has the traditional American two prongs on top, and that fits into my wall plug fine. But the third prong (the bottom one of the triangle), is a plastic rod. Since plastic does NOT conduct electricity, it defeats the purpose of why this became a standard plug in feature here decades ago.
Hope this review was helpful.

Ours came damaged. Overall, this is nice and looked like the item pictured. But I had to give it a lesser rating because the fluffy white material inside the hood of ours came damaged. It appeared to be melted in a couple of different places. It was really weird. Had I purchased this outright, I would have returned this; so I can not recommend it.
Also, this blanket hoodie smelled slightly of mildew. A faint scent like that usually will go away with the first washing, so I normally don't think it is a big deal. But thought I should mention it because I could see someone purchasing this as a gift.

Very small. This towel is so small, it feels more like a large face washcloth. It is made from soft thread and I like the third layer. That was unique. But goodness, there is an unusably high amount of care instructions for a towel. Not to mention, the price. I would have felt ripped off had I paid full price. I wouldn't purchase this again, so I can't recommend it.

It's heavy and big!!!. I have a ten year old clothes steamer that still sells today on Amazon for half the price; and I think it works just as good. Actually maybe better simply because I can only get one shirt done before needing to refill this CHI steamer; where as I can get two shirts done with my old unit. Nor did the CHI save me any time. It simply doesn't work any better on my husband's dress work shirts than our old steamer.
And as I mentioned before, this unit is large and quite heavy (especially once filled with water). So I wouldn't be packing it for him on his business trips. The only thing that I did like about this steamer is that it has a very long cord, that didn't get tangled up easily. And of course it is sturdy and it looks pretty. My bottom line: I am usually a huge fan of CHI products, but I think you'd be paying a high mark-up for the CHI name if you purchased this one.

Doesn't get warm enough. I order the blue with pink/red swirls. Mine doesn't even get warm enough to completely melt all wax. Half the dish will have a melted pool a wax, but the other half will barely be melted. So needleless to say, this warmer doesn't throw a scent well. I've tried it with several different brands too (both commercial and independent brands)

Looks inexpensive. This container is bigger in person than it looks in the photos (pictured next to a 11-year-old boy, for reference). It's sturdier than I expected as well. But the construction isn't the best quality. The fabric was sewn in wrinkled and some areas and not pulled tight in others. Some areas the fabric is an even connected because the sewing machine ran out of thread, and whomever was stitching just kept going. The fabric is thin and I expect it would rip pretty easily too. I wouldn't repurchase this container, so I can't recommend it.

My son said no. By the third night we had to take it off, since it was waking my son up all night long. It was just too loud and crunchy sounding (even with -two- white nose apps running in the back ground). He is such a light sleeper though, so solid sleeps my not care one bit. On a positive note, it was easy to get on and off. And stayed in place while we tried it out.

Industrial machine washing is probably required. One of the tiniest details I missed in the description, was the manufacture says they do not recommend washing this blanket in your washing machine at home. Washing this blanket in an industrial machine is most likely required. And I didn't think to confirmed until after the blanket is here, but our front loading machine has a weight limit of 18lbs. I personally am not interested in wasting my time and money at a laundry mat every time my cat pukes on bed. No matter how comfortable this is, a twenty pound blanket is to work for us.

Cheaply made. Ours arrived broken and warped, so it forced me to inspect these extra closely. I found these medallions are made from some pretty cheap and lightweight materials. Plywood might be too nice of a description. The center white material feels almost like a molded cardboard or thick paperboard.
Not all of the holes were punched all the way through on ours either. The outside circle frame (made from inexpensive looking pine wood), also arrived chipped. This trio might look neat from a distance, but up close they look and feel incredibly inexpensive. I should be able to fix them enough to make them hangable, but I shouldn't have too.
I don't usually comment about an item's price, because a "good deal" is subjective. But had I paid the $75 these were listed for at the time of this review, they would have been returned. So even though they are eye-catching and pretty, I can't whole heartedly recommend them.

Still reaching for my parchment paper.. I haven’t had the high heat issues like others have mentioned but I do think these are difficult to clean. They never feel/look clean. Always greasy feeling. Maybe silpat brand is the same, I don’t know. Bottom line, these keep me reaching for my parchment paper.
Just Okay. The box was pretty mangled upon delivery, the product is a cheap tv product which we expected but we had random items in the box that didn’t go with it, pretty odd.

I was told these could replace swedish dishcloths. They definitely can NOT do such.

I don't see these making it through even a single wash.

Not so great zippers. These are nice and thick pillow covers. Unfortunately The zipper is cheap and hard to work. The seams started tearing out of the zipper before I could even get the pillows in and zipped.
Not expensive. Kind of cheaply made , but bought many as trophies for a dog show.

Great For Thin Garments. These are great for shirts and blouses but not so good for suits and coats. They are just not wide enough, at only 2 inches. The sleeves are being crushed in. I think they should have made them 3" for suits and coats.

Overpriced and Flawed. Way overpriced, and flawed design. First of all, for the amount they are charging, they should include drywall anchors with the screws. Secondly, for this amount of money we should not have to provide and then apply velcro to keep the shelf from sliding off the two rods. This is unacceptable.

Without the velcro, the shelf is flimsy, loose, and often hard to keep flush against the wall.

Poor design. Poor implementation. Overpriced. I do not recommend this as is.
Very Disappointed. Poor quality, which you can see if you use a magnifying glass. Discolored fork on the first day out of the box.

Clean & Convenient (Bags Beat Bins For Sure!). First, I think Oreck deserves a lot of very high praise for being the first to make one of these types of cordless vacuums that have a bag (which they call a Pod, of course). I hate the collection bin-type of vacuums because I do not like the mess and dust inside the collection bins.

At the occasional $399 discounted-by-Oreck price, I give this Oreck Pod Vacuum 5 stars because it is a bagged cordless, which means no mess and dirt and dust inside a collection bin you constantly see and frequently have to clean. When this vacuum is sold at its full retail $569 price, I will deduct 1 star because I feel it's too expensive at that high price.

I also deduct 1 star because this vac cannot be used with the a/c cord plugged in. If the battery power is depleted (or if in the future the battery no longer can hold a charge), the vacuum becomes absolutely useless. It would have been really nice if we had the option of running the vac with the power cord plugged in just as a backup.

One more negative: The soft bristle brush easily sheds its bristles--and the bristles easily become deformed--by just running the brush lightly over bed sheets or a soft blanket, etc. (And you might want to use this cordless vac on those types of things to vacuum up hair, etc. I have received multiple replacement brushes from Oreck just in case the one I received was an anomaly, but they all do the same shedding thing as mentioned, and quite badly.

This cordless vacuum is lightweight, and it has good suction. It is convenient to use on stairs, and on bathroom and kitchen floors. On low or no pile carpets it also works well. On medium to high pile carpets it is not as easy to push and pull, but it works well.

If you dislike dirty vacuum collection bins and if the price is in your budget, this Oreck Pod Cordless Vacuum is certainly worth considering...and assuming you do not get a defective one, you'll probably be happy you purchased it.

Only Slows the Movement. Sadly, while it helps to slow down the chair cushion's movement, it doesn't eliminate the movement. If you want complete elimination of the cushion sliding forward, this product is not the one to buy.

Not Really Crystal Clear & It Smells. I will start with the negatives. Multiple times the seller uses the words "crystal clear" ... and there is a picture which shows a crystal clear shower curtain. The curtain I received isn't even close to being "crystal" clear. You can see out, so it's clear...just not crystal clear, and it certainly doesn't match the photos at all.

The curtain also fogs up easily, slightly diminishing its clarity while using.

And the final negative: Its odor. The bad odor is pretty strong at first, even after washing it per the instructions. And even after a few days, the odor is still there when you get real close.

The positives: It is thick and heavy, which is very nice. The weights at the bottom, added to the fact the curtain itself is heavy being 12 gauge, are effective at keeping any billowing to a tiny minimum. This is the curtain to buy if you really don't want billowing. Also, the price is perfect, in my opinion.

So, if this company could make the same thickness and heavy-weight curtain in a version that is both truly as crystal clear as in the photo and did not smell, not only would I buy it, I'd also pay more money for it. Hopefully the seller will remove the misleading photos that show a truly crystal clear curtain, and remove the words stating that the curtain is crystal clear.

Too Much Power If Used in Smaller Glasses or Cups. Battery Compartment is Tight.. If you are going to use this in an 8-ounce or 10-ounce glass or cup, don't bother. This mixer is too powerful. The liquid will splatter out.

If you're going to use this in a taller glass or cup where you do not fill up high, the mixer's power will mix the liquid fast and well.

Unfortunately, because this mixer doesn't have power settings, if you want to mix smaller ounces of liquid, you need to be using a much taller glass or cup.

Someone else has already mentioned the battery compartment here at Amazon. It really is very tight. I had a difficult time inserting the batteries.

Shrinks Too Much. The width of the flat sheet shrinks a lot, even after just the first wash. I washed using cold water, gentle cycle, and in a very large mesh laundry bag designed to use when washing sheets in the washing machine. I put it in the dryer on very low heat, and did not over-dry, and removed immediately.

The sheets are soft and not too thick. Perhaps if they made the sheet larger and then pre-shrink it, that might be better.

The Grip Needs to Be Tighter. The gripping action needs to be tighter. This gadget is easy to open and close, attach and detach. And it seems to hold the pan, but it wobbles due to the grip not being tight enough. It doesn't inspire confidence that the grip will hold.

Too Narrow. The width from left to right where the bag attaches is only 7 inches. It's really too narrow. You cannot put in a full size paper or plastic dinner plate into the bag straight in left to right. (If you turn the plate as you're starting at the top of the bag you can get it into the bag, of course.)

If you do not mind the narrow size, and if it holds up (some have reported their have not held up), this bag holder will work well for you.
Three Stars. Too thin

Wish it was more sturdy for the price. I bought this for my son’s Birthday. I did pack it to capacity, but with one hit the string broke and it fell to the ground. Kind of disappointing for the cost. It looked just like the picture and easy to stuff. Wish the string was more sturdy.
I wanted more suction. This is not a good vacuum for this.. Not enough suction power.  I use it for light vacuuming because I can't use my bigger one. Disappointed.
Design Flaw. Beautiful cake plate. Gave it a three star because there is a flaw in the plate. The defect is very visible, but I needed for the holidays and could not send back.
A few burst. Mostly they worked okay, but a few of them burst so I was afraid to give out for Halloween, which is why I bought them.

Is not a cooling pillow because it says gel.. It is not a pillow to be used for a cooling pillow.  It is okay as pillows go but not overly comfortable.  If sending pillows back wasn’t so difficult,  I would send them back.

Oh, that noise!. I really want to like this cookware. It's reasonably attractive... for grey hard anodized aluminum cookware. The handles are quite comfortable and also have a hidden hanging ring built into them. The pot walls are decently thick; not so heavy they're hard to use and not so thin then bend and dent easily. The pan bottoms are extra thick so heat distribution is better. The glass lids fit well and the silicone handle allows burn free handling. The whole set is oven safe to 400°. Nothing sticks when cooking and they clean up easily.

With all that being said I hate the noise my utensils make when going across the 'Circulon' bottom of the cookware. It's not that food sticks to it, as I somewhat feared might happen when I first saw the interior of the pans, I've both fried and scrambled eggs in the frying and saute pans without any sticking. It's the 'Zippp..zippp...zippp' noise of every spoon, whisk and spatula going across the ribbed bottom of the pans. It sets my teeth on edge like fingernails on a blackboard.

I'm on the fence about this cookware. It performs well, cleans up easily, except for the handle rivet heads on the inside of the pans which aren't non-stick, goes from stove-top to oven readily but that noise... it really annoys me and makes my cooking experience less enjoyable.

Pillow Too Thick For Me. I read the product listing where it said this item was three inches thick but it turned out to be much thicker at least four inches, possibly more. This was too much material under my neck. I also tried using it to raise my ankle off the bed and it was a bit better at that task but still a bit too thick. The pillow is reasonably soft. Soft enough that you don't feel the rod inside that helps the pillow hold whatever shape you flex it into. If this were thinner I'd gladly use it every day but it causes too much extension/flex of my neck.
This just didn't work for me.

A Litle Pricy. Doesn't stay well on an 11" mattress and wrinkles pretty easily.  Sheets are reasonably soft and comfortable. Price could be better for the quality. Color is nice and true to what was advertised.

A Disappointment. We've only used the yellow mold for making ice cubes. We don't make chocolates and haven't yet tried it with Jello.
As an ice cube tray this is a bit of a disappointment. The cubes are rather small and melt away rapidly. They are cute and do look like Lego blocks but they just don't last long enough to be worth the effort. We also found removing the ice cubes from the mold to be somewhat difficult.

Please note; I received this item in exchange for my review.

Decent Grinder, Hard on the Hands. I like this grinder, it produces a perfect grind for my French press. However if you want a super fine grind for espresso you're not likely to get it. You change the grind by tightening the top knob that also holds the handle on. This means each time you refill the whole bean container you're going to have to guess how tight you had it beforehand. It's a little aggravating because there's no set grind levels. Your grind will be different every time.

I'm disabled and have some serious nerve damage in my hands as well as arthritis trouble just about everywhere. Today, the third time I used this grinder, I wanted to make two large mugs of coffee. I had to open and put whole beans in the grinder three times. Unscrew the small and somewhat hard to remove knob. Remove the cap and handle then fill the cylinder with beans then put it all back together to spend several minutes grinding away. After I was done with my third cycle I was pretty sore but I did get a couple great cups of coffee for my efforts.

In the end it works okay, again for a grind great for a French press, which I think is the best way to make coffee. It can give you the sense of accomplishment to hand grind your own beans and it is a bit more gentle on the beans. But it's a lot of effort in the morning. Me? I'll used up the bag of whole beans I bought to test this with and then I think I'm going back to buying fresh ground coffee.
I received this item in exchange for my review.

Pretty But Not That Useful. Heavy knife. Looks light and cheap but the blade has some serious heft to it. The white background, green handle and sheath along with multicolored wording (Celebrate!) and balloons make it fairly attractive. But looks are secondary to performance. This will cut cake. Then again so will dental floss (unflavored is best), and my near razor sharp pocket knife that's not serrated. It's cutting other, more difficult things that separates the wheat from the chaff so to speak. The blade cuts cardboard fairly well.i tried it on two different types of rolls; a heavy white bread hoagie roll and a pack of King's Hawaiian sweet rolls. Even though the product is described as designed to prevents food from sticking or tearing while cutting I found it dragging less than halfway through both types of rolls and the heavier hoagie rolls were somewhat crushed while the lighter and softer Hawaiian rolls cut cleanly though there was definite drag cutting both rolls.
The knife comes with a well fitting cover/sheath that has holes which amusingly line up with the balloons on the blade. There's also an opening that runs most of the length of the cover. My guess is for easy drainage.
This knife is BIG I'm having a hard time finding a place to keep it. There is a hold at the tip of cover I may have to hang it on the wall or inside a cabinet.
To be honest I bought a somewhat shorter and sharper serrated knife at the Dollar Store it fits in a drawer and cuts better. This knife? Cute for birthdays and other celebrations but really not much else. A lot of space for something that won't get used much.

Not Great, Not Horrible. We've washed these three times to Try and soften them up some but they're still rather rough. Now, that's bad for drying your hands. That's a little uncomfortable. But for wiping down the stove, counter top or sink the roughness comes in handy. I think with use and more washing they'll soften up even more. They're okay, a decent size for the kitchen, absorbent. Just a little rough.y

Looks Nothing Like The Pictures. I wanted to love this. I really did. I collect skulls, they're all over the house. I saw the pictures in the product listing and just had to have it, plus it was on sale, then it arrived. Whoever photographed this did an amazing job of making thin, cheap, extremely fragile, plastic that is a pale comparison to the product listing's images. The gold doesn't shine the green doesn't look like jade. It looks like something you could pick up for a couple bucks at a bargain store. . . and likely in a year or so that's where these will be found. They couldn't even include an ornament hook which can be had for less than half a cent each. Hallmark used to sell a quality product across the board. Very disappointed in this item. Three stars only because I really like skulls. It really deserves two.

Firm & Thick, Not Very Soft. Firm density, soft. . . That sort of contradicts itself. Is if firm or is it soft? It came vacuum packed, first time I've ever seen something that wasn't memory foam packed thst way. The pillow continues to get thicker and firmer. At first when it was thinner and softer I thought I could use it for a head pillow but as it thickened and firmed up it just wasn't compatible with my adjustable bed. I would raise the head of the bed and this pillow would force my head uncomfortably forward. But I do  use a pillow under each arm for comfort and this replaces an older pillow that was getting a bit flat. If you sleep flat on a bed and like a firm pillow that's not really all that soft this ma be the one for you.

Mixed Results, Moderately Impressive. Unless your mirrors are spotless and you're really just wiping off steam. . . and even if it's just steam for that matter you're going to need a few paper towels or an old terrycloth towel around to clean up the drips and wipe of the blade and mirror as you go.
What I've found, because my car lacks a rear wiper and has a spoiler the combined shapes coat the rear window with dust and water drops faster than you can believe. Also requiring an old towel I've found keeping this inside the garage to wipe off the back, side and side-view mirrors quickly after being out in the rain or with a spray or three of glass cleaner if it'd been dusty a far handier tool than in the bathroom.
I think this works far better on the car than the bathroom mirrors where it did a fair, if somewhat messy job.

Not Impressed. First and foremost a towel has to dry, dishes, hands, the counter. These are pretty lousy at any of those things. Even when there's a spill of water on the countertop I find I have to press these towels, they were washed twice before using, into the spill otherwise it would just push the water around the counter. My hands never feel dry no matter how long I try. They're cute, the design is attractively retro but I'm going to have to replace them because they're not much good at being a towel.

These Are Pretty. If they didn't include so many huge marbles and put it four or more mid-small size it would be so much nicer. The large marbles are SO much bigger than the rest they just seem out of place. Colors and shades are nice. We have them in a dish surrounding a large candle.

Does The Job (edited). Heater warms up quick, heat output is rather impressive and warms my 12-foot x 12-foot bedroom in just a few minutes. There was a brief smell as it initially started up but that was even shorter than I expected. The timer and remote, which is fairly basic, work fine. Setting a temperature allows the heater to turn on and off over time maintaining the room temperature. I like that a unit at this price point has a removable and washable filter. I gave it four stars because we can't award half stars, this is really more a three and a half star item because of the. . .
Cons -
The display is on the top, the unit uses the same beep tone for everything. So you can't see temperature or any changes you make to the system. I wake up in the middle of the night, it's chilly and I want the room warmer so I grab the remote, there's a couple beeps and. . . I have NO idea if I've changed the fan, temperature, turned the swing mode on. You need to get up and look at top of the unit to see what's what.
The temperature only changes in five (5) degree increments. Why? I like specific comfort levels and it's really hard, for me at least, to be comfortable at 75° when I want it to be 72° and 60° is too chilly when I would prefer 63°. It may be nit picky but I see no reason in 2020 for a heater to only operate at five degree intervals.
I have no idea what the swing feature does. The unit doesn't pivot and it only has one exhaust vent so. . . what's it do? The instruction book doesn't say.
(here's the edit) Found another con, this is enough to drop the rating to three stars. I don't like my room hot, warm is more than enough. I'm quite happy to have the temp set to 60° or if it's a bit damp and raw 65°. Turn the unit off, as an example, when you're going out and don't want to leave a heater running when you aren't home and it defaults to 70° when you turn it back on! That just. . . annoying! Who makes these arbitrary decisions and why? This is dumb. Especially since the manual says it starts up with the previously used settings. It does not. (end edit)
The unit operates either vertically or horizontally so there's no tip-over protection.

If You Gotta. . .. First I read the instructions  which said 'install 4 AA batteries, then aim the product at the can and hit the button, and you can simply watch as it opens' I tried this and the can opener sat there aimed at the can making whirring noises. Nothing happened. Next I actually tried putting the opener on the can and it took some finagling but in the end it opened the can easier than the manual crank opener I have. Smaller Than Expected. I love three tined forks and especially the smaller salad forks we've had in the family for decades. I got these, black being my favorite color, and while I'm going to use them they did turn out to be quite smaller than I expected and are kind of silly but still well made and durable.

Kinda Large. This is SO huge. . . the mug is hard to hold especially at the top. It's leakproof which I liked but the top does dislodge easily so even if it doesn't spill when it tips over use care grabbing for it or you could pop the lid free. Something that screwed into place would be more secure. The paint appears durable and doesn't scratch easily. Capacity is enormous. Your coffee will be cold long before you can finish it. Well, maybe.

A Candle in a Plastic Cup. It smells good, not overpowering but does 'scent up' an area in a short time. Very relaxing and calming. Have only burned it a few times but it does appear that it will last quite a while. But it's ugly. Its a yellowy amber jar with a white plastic lid. It looks like a face cream jar. And it's plastic! A candle in plastic, why? I don't get the design and I'm being real careful not to melt the lid or container but I do like the scent.

A Little Disappointed. You get a Friends branded Central Perk travel mug which stays capped fairly well though a sharp knock can pop the cap lose. You also get a single packet of cappuccino latte mix. Just enough to make six ounces of coffee. That's it. A travel mug with a logo from a popular TV show and a single small cup of coffee. Granted it was tasty coffee but they could have included a couple packets of mix and maybe something else related to the show; keyring, lanyard, something to make this worth the price. The mug will get reused, the packaging went to a landfill and the 6 ounces of coffee were barely enough to give us both a taste. Somewhat disappointed in this.

It's a Flask. Easy to fill with the included funnel. Easy to drink out of. The flask is reasonably attractive though it feels like it will scratch easily. One thing I didn't like is the top doesn't have a tether. If you were out at night or camping the black colored cap will disappear if you drop it. Nothing really special here. Does it's job.

Okay Quality. The box is a reasonable size; 6" x 4" x 2.75". The opening, a slider panel in the bottom which I had a very hard time opening. Granted you may only open this once or twice in your lifetime it still requires some effort to open a thin, fragile, door.
The carving is delicate and attractive and the wood is nice but the carving poorly done in places with cuts that extend into places they shouldn't. It's just a lack of attention to detail. It depends on how you feel about your loved one. This box is pretty but imperfect. That might matter to you.

Very Thick Pillow. No matter how I shaped this pillow it was always too thick to be comfortable in my bed. I like a very thin pillow. The one I have is 20+ years old and flat as a pancake. All these pillows today are crazy thick and put a lot of painful pressure on my neck. I didn't enjoy using this pillow.

Very Adjustable. I like an incredibly thin pillow and they're almost impossible to come by these days, everything is incredibly thick and uncomfortable. With this shredded foam pillow you can remove literally as much material as you want. It comes with a bag of additional fill to actually add more fill to the pillow. I took out more fill than they sent to add and I came up with an incredibly thin and soft pillow. . . the only problem is it's all loose fill which makes the pillow wrap around your head and my ears get hot. This is okay in the winter, even nice but in the summer, wow it's hot. Still, this is the thinnest new pillow I've found in years.

Unimpressive. Meh. I just wasn't impressed with this pasta cooker. It doesn't save that much time and when you're done you have a plastic container full of nearly boiling water that's malleable. I was much more worried about spilling hot water from this plastic container than when using my heavy duty aluminum cookware on the stove. Used it twice and went back to the stovetop to cook pasta.

Pretty But Cheap Quality. This is a pretty stone, from a distance. Up close the flaws stand out badly. Cracks in the base and sides, chips on the edges, uneven grinding. There's even a plug in one of the flat areas (clearly visible in my photos). I don't mind this for my decorations but I'd be embarrassed to give this as a gift to someone.

Fun Collection of Stickers. I would have preferred more skulls and serious artwork but there was a wide selection good enough for just about everyone. Quality is good, adhesive sticks well, stock is nicely thick, colors are vibrant.

Not Very Useful For Me. Just wasn't for me. I'm sure there's people this could help but I need to keep my heels off the bed and this was so narrow it left my knees in the air arching backwards which was extremely painful. I tried for five days to break it in as a head pillow. I do like my pillows narrow but it was hard and I'm guessing older style memory foam because it held the heat like crazy and being half round it wasn't possible to flip this to 'the cool side' and have it still be comfortable. This was unusable for me. Three stars because it may be useful to others and the company handled the refund flawlessly. I do like people who back their products 100%.

Works, Pretty Well. Wasn't crazy about the color but had gotten tired of thin coozies not keeping the beverages cold. This easily doubles the time you have before your drink starts to warm up when wrapped with a piece of foam. Will probably get a can of engine enamel paint and do this up more in my style.

Messy, NOT Biodegradable. I had a pack of poppers a while back. They were biodegradable rice paper. Shot them into the yard, it rained, the mess dissolved. Poof, gone. I didn't pay attention and we took these out into the yard, they were VERY hard to activate which being disabled I found to be a rather annoying but at least it keeps kids from setting them off. My issue is they're full of shards of what appears to be Mylar wrapping paper and it's EVERYWHERE. And being disabled I'm stuck with it. Maybe I can convince my lawn guy to clean it up. These things should always have biodegradable contents. BTW, use caution setting these off indoors. They're nearly as loud as my 9mm. We set one off under the edge of my porch roof and the report was enough to make my ears ring for several hours. These are not toys.

More Decorative Than Anything. I really wanted to like these. All my pans are nonstick I can't use metal in them and the plastic stuff I keep getting is flimsy and useless. I hoped these wood utensils would be just what I needed.
Unfortunately these are more for display and decorations than even casual let alone serious cooking. They remind me of kids toys. Overly thick edges dulled points so no one gets hurt. With a sheet between myself and the blanket the scratchy feeling is somewhat mitigated. Being 100% cotton the blanket breathes well so I find myself sweating less than under a heavy quilted comforter. Not truly happy with this but for now it does the job.

Smaller Than Expected. I needed to use a shower curtain to close off a hallway for privacy needs. I had a rod but it was too long for the hall so I found this. The pictures gave nothing for scale. The length was in the range I needed and the price was right so I ordered it. The rod is seriously thin. Thin Sheets. Great, absolutely great for summer in Florida. Not so great for fall and worse in winter. These are thin. Thin enough to read through and I bought the black. They're very soft and feel nice against the skin. They seem to wrinkle very little. I had heavier jersey sheets the past few years which are the reverse of these. They were way too warm in the summer. These solve that problem. Overall I'm pleased with the purchase.

What's It Doing?. Is it? Isn't it? I ran this continuously for a month in my 11' x 12' bedroom. I've checked the filter a couple times and it appears to be nearly as clean as the day I got the purifier. I made sure to close the door quickly, spent 12+ hours at a time in the room and to be completely honest I haven't detected any difference in the air quality/feel of the room with this running and without.
Construction seems decent, it's sturdy and things snap in and out with satisfying solid sounds. Moving this I found next to impossible, the handle is shallow and slopes at the wrong angle to get a good grip. There's also nothing inside the hole to grab onto, it's just a rectangular hole in the back. I'm disabled and almost dropped it twice just moving it to the back of the house. There's a UV light inside to kill mold and bacteria. I know the technology works, the local hospital has them in every room and our A/C vendor keeps trying to sell us one. When you turn on the UV light a half ring across the face of the unit lights up BRIGHT blue. You can't dim the light and there's no built in cover. You're not going to want to run the UV light when you're trying to sleep. In the past I've slept with lights on in the room (usually hospitals) and I can't stand this on when I'm trying to sleep. Speaking of sleep. You won't want to run this on anything but low if you're using this in a bedroom. Medium and high move a LOT of air (be sure to keep away from drapes) and make a LOT of noise. On the subject of noise. In the course of the month I've been testing this unit the fan, on low, has gotten almost twice as loud as it was when I first plugged it in. I've vacuumed the filter and checked the visible parts of the unit over and it seems fine so the fan's just gotten noisier which I find exceptionally annoying as I have very sensitive hearing.
In the end? I don't know what if anything this is doing beyond running air through the device. I don't feel healthier. The air doesn't feel healthier. My eyes and sinuses bother me exactly as much as they did before this got here. I haven't seen or felt any benefit from this room air purifier.

Very basic; construction feels cheap. I have several brands of kitchen scales that I use daily as I frequently test cookbooks from the UK that require metric conversions. This was my first Taylor scale, and I have to say that as an experienced baker, I was let down by the fact that you are limited to Imperial and grams (no liquid measurements with this scale, so forget about measuring in fl. oz. or ml). The max weight is 11 pounds. There are only two buttons and it is very simple to operate. The glass top is easy to wipe clean and has a hefty feel, but the plastic base is extremely lightweight and feels cheap.The plastic door to access the batteries feels cheaply made. I do like the look of the glass top, and this has a small footprint on the counter. Also, the fact that it takes two AAA batteries (vs. button-cell batteries like my thin-line digital scale) makes it easier to find / replace batteries (my thin digital scale requires unscrewing the battery compartment door to replace the batteries).

Verdict: This is fine for those looking for an entry-level scale, particularly for those weighing portions, or for weighing small letters, etc., but more experienced bakers and those who frequently cook using metric will want a scale that offers more versatility.

Good concept, but needs work (would have been four stars if lid snapped onto colander!). I own numerous OXO gadgets, many of which I wouldn't cook without. When I had the chance to review the 3-Piece Berry Bowl and Colander Set, I was excited. The 1.5-qt bowl has a nonslip bottom and all three parts are dishwasher safe. I used it to wash and presoak mung beans and fresh blackberries. For the mung beans, I stored them in the fridge overnight, and ran into the major design flaw: the lid is designed to snap onto the bowl, but only if the colander isn't inside. I had my mung beans sitting in the colander (in water) and the lid continually fell off when I would move it in the fridge. Likewise, if you have already rinsed fresh berries, you will want to store them in the colander to keep them from sitting in moisture. Also, my lid didn't fit the bowl; to make it snap on required a lot of contortion and hand strength, making it unfriendly for those with arthritis (which OXO products are marketed to). It was also extremely difficult to pry off once the lid was on the bowl. The bowl itself is smooth with no handles, so you'll find it hard to hang onto the slippery bowl and pry off the lid at the same time.

By making the lid so it doesn't fit the colander (the colander has handles that extend beyond the edge of the bowl to keep it from falling in), OXO has really decreased the potential utility of the design. Also, the OXO website states "The 3-Piece Berry Bowl & Colander Set is the perfect size for rinsing berries, quinoa, beans and more;" I agree that it is great for rinsing berries and beans, but rinsing quinoa would be a nightmare, as the holes in the colander are far too large to rinse quinoa without most of it ending up in the water (or down the drain).

If OXO would fix the lid design so that it would snap securly onto the colander, this would be a four-star product. Also, with the colander inserted, the storage is very small (even without the colander, it is too small to be used as an effective mixing bowl unless you're beating an egg or two).

Good, but has some design shortcomings.... My faithful [[ASIN:B0009VELTQ Cuisinart CBK-200 2-Pound Convection Automatic Breadmaker]] finally died after years of faithful service, so I was happy to be offered the Black and Decker B6000C Deluxe Bread Maker. I used my Cuisinart regularly to make yeast bread (white and whole wheat), sweet bread (on the dough setting), and jam. Because I am more familiar with the Cuisinart, I will use it as the basis for comparison here.

As I unboxed the B&D, I was surprised by how light the unit is (the Cuisinart had a metal body and lid). The unit is larger due to the shape of the pan and the fact that it bakes 3-pound loaves, but it does not have handles like the Cuisinart, which makes it difficult to move or put it away for storage. I was also a little dismayed to see that the large, heavy lid relies on a very small plastic hinge, which seems like it will crack / break sooner rather than later (the lid also tends to wobble a little when closed). The metal pan seems a bit thin, but I liked the fact that the two paddles are straight rather than curved like the Cuisinart. The B&D also seemed to do a better job at kneading due to the two paddles, but you'll still want to stop and scrape down the sides of the pan using a nonstick tool.

After getting the bread maker set up (I had to move it because the unit is tall and narrow and I could not open the lid fully because it kept hitting the underside of my cabinets), I used the included recipe to make a 3-pound loaf of herbed garlic French bread on the French cycle (setting 3). As other reviewers have mentioned, the LCD readout is a touch on the faint side, and may be difficult to read (my old Cuisinart did not have that problem and was easy to read from several feet away). I found I had to add extra liquid to the recipe, as the dough was far too dry at first and didn't come together, but the resulting loaf was moist and fluffy. I also liked the way the bread baked in the B&D; my Cuisinart tended to overbake everything, even on the "light" crust setting.

Here is one area where the Cuisinart excelled over the B&D manual: the Cuisinart bread machine includes dozens of recipes for each of the machine's settings, with ingredients scaled for 1, 1.5 and 2-pound loaves. The B&D manual only has ONE sample recipe for each setting, and the ingredients are automatically scaled for the largest 3-pound loaf size. Also, the Cuisinart listed the exact length of each step in the cycle for all of the settings; there are no times listed for the B&D. This can be problematic if you want to remove the paddles before the bread enters the baking cycle; the Cuisinart would beep before the final rise, but the B&D does not. Because there are no times listed in the manual, it takes a bit of guesswork (the LCD does underline which step of the baking process you are on).

Overall, I would still recommend the [[ASIN:B0009VELTQ Cuisinart CBK-200 2-Pound Convection Automatic Breadmaker]] for the many included recipes, variations, nutritional info, and design features, especially for new bakers. The B&D does turn out a decent loaf of bread, but the lack of included recipes (and scaled ingredients for smaller loaves), and more crucially the lack of knead and rise times, can make this less than user-friendly.

I am fairly new to the world of slow cooking; I purchased my first-ever slow cooker, a [[ASIN:B005GZ2OBW Hamilton Beach Stovetop Slow Cooker - Black/silver (6 Quart)]], about a year ago and have been slow cooking several times a week ever since (I have several slow cooker cookbooks that I rely on constantly, including [[ASIN:054700303X The Italian Slow Cooker]], [[ASIN:0547744455 The Mediterranean Slow Cooker]], and [[ASIN:1936493578 Slow Cooker Revolution Volume 2]]). I use my slow cooker regularly to make all manner of desserts (cakes, cheesecakes, bread puddings), soups, and entrees. This All-Clad slow cooker was the first All-Clad appliance that I have used (I also own several made-in-the-USA All-Clad pans that I use regularly and swear by).

First and foremost, I am not thrilled that it is made in China. It's obvious that the quality control isn't up to the same standards as their US-made cookware; the heavy ceramic insert has numerous tiny bubbles / holes, is rough on the bottom where the insert is not glazed, and the lid does not fit the insert snugly (nor is there a latch / locking mechanism or hole for a thermometer/temperature probe). The unit LOOKS impressive on the counter, although it is absolutely massive (it weighs close to 20 pounds with the insert in).

On to setting the cooking mode and time: you are limited to 2-8(?) hours on high or 4-20 hours on low, at which point the slow cooker will automatically switch to warm mode. This is first unit I've had with a programmable timer, but I did like the solid feel of the buttons. The cooking time limits seemed kind of arbitrary; it seemed strange that I could only program the unit on high for a maximum of eight hours, but up to 20 hours on low.

I used the All-Clad slow cooker to make several dishes, including a Greek shrimp and tomato dish. I went according to the time in the recipe so as not to keep removing the lid (it recommended cooking the shrimp 10 minutes on high; they were VERY overcooked, whereas in my Hamilton Beach, I had to cook them for a few extra minutes).

Naturally, I was apprehensive after reading the hundreds of one-star reviews about the ceramic insert cracking and breaking, or the electronics would suddenly stop working. I have not experienced either of these yet, but I was very careful to hand-wash the insert (even though the manual claims that both the insert and lid are dishwasher-safe, I'm not chancing it). During cooking on high, I did notice several very loud popping sounds coming from the insert that were audible from two rooms away; I was sure that the insert would be cracked, but could find no hairline cracks after washing and drying the insert (I waited until the insert was completely cool before washing). I have a feeling based on so many others' experiences that the insert will be the first thing to fail; luckily there is a one-year warranty, which I registered for immediately, and I plan to continue using this as my primary slow cooker.

Bottom line: it does what a slow cooker is supposed to do, but for this price, I expect a solid, flawless appliance that will stand up to several years of frequent use/abuse, an insert that does not crack, and responsive customer service.

The good:
+ I liked that there is a rubber seal / gasket that the ceramic insert rests on; as it is so heavy, it makes moving the slow cooker (and removing the insert) much more manageable.
+ It does come with a (small) collection of starter recipes, including Asian Beef Stew, Mahogany Glazed Pork Loin, Peach Melba Bread Pudding, Chicken with Mushrooms in White Wine Sauce, and Tunisian Spiced Turkey Breas with Root Vegetables.

The bad:
- Even on low, the temperature seems to run hot
- Finishing on the ceramic insert; small imperfections in the ceramic insert that can lead to cracking
- If/when the insert cracks (and it seems to happen quite frequently based on reviews), expect to spend a good $75 on a replacement if your unit is no longer under warranty

Good build, but not sure of the aim of this design. The KORVOS Cutting Board is made of good bamboo material and soft silicone footing for drying. It has stainless steel on one side and bamboo on the other. It also has a notch for hanging. It has a good build quality and has a nice weight.

The bamboo side has a liquid channel, but it doesn't go around the entire board. I suppose with this board being only 15x11, that may be enough.

As far as the stainless side, I'm uncertain when or why I would choose to use it. Metal on metal contact always gives me the willies and no matter how well it's built, there will always be a gap that liquid can get trapped in. So if cutting meat on the stainless side, blood can get trapped in the gap and allow bacteria to propagate. That would be the worst-case-scenario. In a milder case, water being trapped between the metal and bamboo would still encourage mold growth.

One should always use separate cutting boards for meat and vegetables. I ended up using this board for veggies and only on the bamboo side.

I suppose it does make a good presentation platter. You can choose to present your food on the bamboo or have a nice stainless surface to show it off.

PROS:
