- Assembly is easy; just attach the hardware (one clip and one arm) for the hose and the brush and you are set.

- It comes with a small bottle of 2x Little Green for Compacts solution.

- The solution has a nice, yet subtle fresh scent.

- The solution tank is easy to fill and the dirty water tank is easy to rinse out. Be careful when inserting the solution tank back into the unit because when I turned the tank over, I held the tank a little too tight which caused the solution to start squirting out. Once I changed my hold to be more subtle and on the upper part of the tank, this squirting ceased.

- The built in heater took only 25 seconds to heat up as opposed to the 30 seconds mentioned in the manual. I also found that the water does come out "warmer" than the other cleaners I have.

- A two-in-one crevice tool is supplied which can be converted with the flip of a switch from a small tiny brush to just a crevice tool that I assume can be used to soak up a puddle of water (although the manual does not say).

- The cord is relatively long for a compact unit which I measured to be around 20 feet; that's about 19-1/2 feet of useable extension. (See the CONS with regard to the cord, which is why I could not use this in my auto.)

- The unit has a quick-release cord wrap which enabled me to unravel the cord easily.

- The solution is easy to dispense and is dispensed out in a fan pattern over the stain. The further away from the surface of the carpet you hold your brush while dispensing the solution the larger the area it covers.

- Although the unit does not pick up as much water as my Spotbot does, I still felt that it picked up enough.

- I thought it spot cleaned my house carpet as well as any of my other cleaners. For my type stains, which are usually cat vomit, that means it lightened the stain. As a result, I suspect it would be great on upholstery and auto interiors such as floor mats, seats, etc. (although I wouldn't use it on the headliner--that's the material on the underside of the roof).

- I was able to clean my removable car floor mat by bringing it into my house for cleaning. It was black in spots and it came out almost spotless although I did use a lot of elbow grease when working the brush over the mat. In fact the dirty water was pitch black when I was done.

- The crevice tool (with the tiny brush) and the small brush that comes with the unit means that this is mostly for spot cleaning; however, with enough back and forth over the affected area, you could clean as much as you wanted.
- Customer service is available Mon to Fri 8 am -10 pm and Saturday 9 a.m. to 8 p.m. Eastern Time.

- I called them twice around 9 p.m. Eastern Time to clarify the WARNINGs in the manual and both reps gave me the same answer which you'll read about in the CONS.

- The unit comes with a 1-year limited warranty.

CONS:

- Only those who have a garage or access to a grounded power outlet within about 17 feet of their car would be able to use this. I said 17 feet because you do need some slack to get into the car even though the hose will extend some. I was unable to clean my car with this because the power cord was not long enough to reach and using an extension cord might cause a severe electrical shock or (as the reps on the phone told me) blow out the circuit breakers in my house. I made sure to call Bissell twice and ask if I could use a cord rated higher than the unit and they said no. I did not ask if this could be used with a jumpstart or other battery pack with an AC connection, although that might be an option, but I would caution you to check first. I live on the 2nd floor and my boyfriend does too, so neither one of us could use this in the car because the WARNING in the manual reads:

WARNING: Do not use an extension cord with the product. The use of an extension cord may result in a severe electrical shock, particularly if the extension cord does not have an electrical rating higher than that of the product, OR if the extension cord does not have a three-prong grounding plug and if the extension cord is not plugged into a circuit box with a ground fault circuit interrupter. Safety precautions such as keeping all connections off the ground and dry will not eliminate the danger.

- I do not like that I can only use the Bissell 2x Little Green for Compacts formula in this unit. This means I cannot use any other Bissell cleaning products in this unit and I called customer service to verify this. The WARNING in the manual reads:

WARNING: Use only BISSELL Little Green formula in your cleaner. Use of cleaning formulas which contain lemon or pine oil may damage this appliance and void the warranty. Chemical spot cleaners or solvent-based soil removers also should not be used. These products may react with the plastic materials used in your cleaner, causing cracking or pitting.

- The user instructions are not so good. For instance, nowhere does it mention that both the built in heater and the unit has to be in the on position to heat up the water; although that is intuitive. Also, the manual should say you should vacuum first before using. I already know this but not everyone would.

- A bit of water stays behind in the channel below the dirty water tank and in the tough stain tool which is expected; however, be careful if moving this around or transporting to another location because if the unit tilts the dirty water that remains in the channel might spill out.

In summary, I selected this product so that I could clean the attached carpet in my auto and the cloth seats in my boyfriend's auto, but was unable to do that due to the extension cord restriction. However, I still feel this is a satisfactory carpet cleaner / shampooer that can be used to spot clean carpet or upholstery in my home or the removable dirty floor mats that I can bring in from the car. As long as one has access to an outlet close to their car, based on the results in my home and on my removable vehicle floor mats I have no doubt this would work on cloth car seats and the non-removable auto carpet. I do wish I could use another Bissell cleaning solution (such as the pet solution) besides the one that came with the unit; but that did not take away from the cleaning power; it just takes away from the options. In essence this unit has only one cleaning option, the Bissell 2x Little Green for Compacts formula.

I feel this unit was 2.5 stars because of the limited options and rounded up to give it 3 stars. If the first two CONS were addressed, then I probably would have rated this four stars as it does clean as well as the three other units (including the Hoover) that I listed in my introduction. Nevertheless, as a potential buyer, only you can try to determine based on the the various posted reviews if this unit is right for you.

Tea brewer for use only with teas that brew in boiling water. Before I tell you about my experience with this teamaker, I feel it is important to elaborate on brewing tea in general.

There are two factors besides the quality of tea that make a good cup of tea. One is the brewing temperature and the other is the steeping time (how long it sits in the hot or warm water). Although temperatures will vary by person and by website and source being read, below is the general temperature guideline for each type of tea. I listed the teas in brewing temperature order from boiling to tepid. Black teas seem to be used more pervasively in the US and Britain, so I suspect this teamaker is geared to that market.

Rooibos (not a true tea; a tisane) - 212F (boiling)

Pu-erh - 212F (boiling)

Black - 205 - 212F (can vary but usually brewed at boiling temperature)

Herbal (not a true tea; a tisane)- 205 - 212F (can vary but usually brewed at boiling temperature)

Oolong - 195 - 212F (I usually brew this at 195F and less than boiling is typical for most tastes)

Green - 175 - 190F (I usually brew this type tea between 175 and 180F)

Yellow - 180 - 190F (I've never brewed this tea but my references show this is the appropriate temperature)

White - 140 - 160F (I usually brew at 185F)

In addition to the above temperatures, the steeping time is a personal preference. I usually steep black teas (or other high-temp teas) for 4-5 minutes and the more delicate white and green teas from 2-3 minutes. I have never steeped tea longer than 6 minutes so the 16 minute steeping time available on this teamaker is overkill but is still a nice option for those who want it.

Therefore, since this tea brewer does not have a temperature setting, I consider this appliance only useful for brewing black, pu-erh, rooibos, and most herbal teas or tisanes which are normally brewed at boiling temperatures or close to it. I suppose oolong tea could be successfully brewed with this pot by reducing the steeping time to offset the damaging effects of the boiling temperature but it is not something I would try with my expensive oolong tea. Personally, I drink mostly green and some black teas but also have a couple of white and oolong teas and a pu-erh blend. This means I can only brew my black and pu-erh blend tea in this teamaker because the water is too hot for the other teas based on my tastes. If I were to brew my green tea in this teamaker it would taste very, very bitter.

I have listed the other PROS and CONS below.

PROS

- My peach black tea, when brewed in this pot, tasted very good as it should have when brewed correctly.

- The unit is sexy with an hourglass figure and the glass carafe is cute.

- Carafe holds one liter of tea which is slightly less than 34 ounces (1 quart equals about 4 mugs of tea at 8 ounces each mug or about 6 cups if using a small teacup).

- Steeping time is adjustable between 2 to 16 minutes.

- Automatic keep warm function is enabled for one hour after tea is brewed.

- Stainless steel steeping container holds loose leaf tea without seepage of leaves.

- Indicator lights change between red and green depending on cycle and the unit clicks (rather loudly) each time the cycle changes.

- Tea bags, loose leaf tea or any blend of teas can be used.

CONS

- During my first use on the initial cleaning cycle, the water would not dispense from the brewing chamber into the carafe. The brewing chamber and carafe were seated correctly and snapped into place. Also, removing the chamber and re-inserting it several times didn't work, which is why I had to dump the water and start over. Had I been brewing tea, I would have had to pour my tea from the hot brewing chamber into the carafe myself. As a result of this failure, I had to dump the water out and try again. I jiggled the little spring loaded plastic pieces in the center of the unit. These pieces are similar to the plastic hinge you find on a coffee pot that moves into place when you remove the pot during the brew cycle. I then tried the initial cleaning cycle again and this time it worked. Later I was able to brew a successful pot of tea; I am hoping my first cleaning cycle attempt will be my only failed experience.

- There is NO ADJUSTABLE TEMPERATURE setting.

- Instruction book does not provide a troubleshooting section for the unit.

- Instruction book provides only half the story with regard to how to brew tea because it never mentions brewing temperature is critical. Instead it implies varying the steeping time is what brews a good cup of tea. Also, the book does not tell you the size of the measuring scoop. I use 1 teaspoon of loose leaf tea per 6-8 ounces of water. The scoop provided with this teamaker is 1 tablespoon (meaning 3 teaspoons).

- Although this is not a CON for me, the carafe, brewing chamber, steeper and accessories should be lightly washed by hand.

- The indicator light turns green when tea is ready as it is being dispensed into the carafe. It would be better if the light turns green once all the tea has made it from the brewing chamber to the carafe instead.

- The water is slightly painstaking to dispense into the tank. When opening the tank lid there is only a small rim that will hold water; if the water is poured too fast into the rim, there is not enough time for it to dispense into the tank. Instead a slow steady pour is necessary to prevent any water seepage. You must also wait until all the water drains into the tank before you close the lid.

- The unit is very large at 15 inches tall and just barely fits under my counter.

- Although the carafe is made of glass, the brewing chamber pot is plastic. I would have preferred glass here as well.

- Funnel provided looks like an apple corer with a center cover for the hole. To me this funnel is too much. The reason it is provided is to cover the hole in the steeping basket but the "spokes" in the funnel make it difficult to pour in loose tea without spillage onto the "spokes," meaning the funnel has to be cleaned or wiped every time.

- This teamaker is not worth more than $30 to me simply because I drink a lot of green tea and that should not be brewed with boiling water.

- There is a lot to wash on this teamaker after the tea is brewed including the tea infuser basket, brew chamber and lid, carafe and lid, funnel, and measuring spoon. The center island separator (shelf separating top unit from bottom) should be wiped down as well.

- This teamaker has no timer features; so you cannot wake up to fresh brewed tea if you wanted it.

The current price of $59.09 is way too expensive for this teamaker especially since it does not have a wake-up timer that will produce freshly brewed tea in the morning.

In my opinion, for the real tea connoisseur it is worth paying five times the current price and buying the [[ASIN:B003LNOPSG Breville BTM800XL One-Touch Tea Maker]] which has all the needed features and more to brew any kind of tea; I know because I own one. For anyone who just brews the teas that require boiling water only for themselves, I see it as overkill to purchase this pot. The only reason I purchased my Breville was to brew the more delicate teas and also because it really is a nifty appliance and quite a conversation piece.

Of course, if you entertain and want to set it and forget it when brewing tea, then this might be for you. Also, if you personally just prefer something that keeps several cups of tea warm and has a built in steeping timer, then this is an acceptable but expensive option; however, be prepared for a lot of cleanup as the tea infuser basket, brew chamber and lid, carafe and lid, funnel, measuring spoon, and center piece of the unit all have to be washed or wiped down after the tea is consumed.

From my perspective, this teamaker is just acceptable especially since I'm more of green tea fan, do not entertain, and only drink 1-2 cups of tea a day. If this teamaker had a programmable timer that could be set to wake up to a fresh pot of tea in the morning, I would have given it 4 stars even though I myself wouldn't use that feature. I feel all the decent coffee pots in this price range have that feature so there's no reason this teamaker shouldn't be similar. Nevertheless, as long as it works as designed, it does brew a good cup of black tea.

I will update this post if I encounter any more failures with the brewing chamber not releasing the tea into the carafe.

September 19, 2012 UPDATE - I've made more than 8 pots of tea with this unit and it still has not failed as it did the first time so I consider my first time problem a fluke. I will only update this review again if the problem resurfaces. On another note, my boyfriend saw this teamaker and also feels (as I do) that it is an aesthetically beautiful machine.

November 21, 2012 UPDATE - This tea maker is going strong and is still a pleasure to brew black tea in. However, today I just purchased another [[ASIN:B003LNOPSG Breville BTM800XL One-Touch Tea Maker]] for myself for Christmas after having my first one for over two years. I just had to have a backup tea maker for my green and other "non-black" teas. Since the price is now $200 ($199.99) during the holidays; anyone considering the purchase of this Nesco might also want to consider the Breville if they are brewing teas that do not brew in boiling water. However, if you only brew black and other teas that take boiling water, then this Nesco is your best buy.

A good kitchen scale with an 11-pound capacity; weighs in both kg and ounces/pounds; surface looks used however. I own a [[ASIN:B00009K3SI Soehnle Triple Digital Food Scale]] that has an 11-pound capacity but can measure in grams which I purchased in October 2005 and it is still going strong 11 years later. Obviously for measuring very light items(like grams of tea) I needed to purchase [[ASIN:B002SC3LLS American Weigh Scales AWS 1KG Digital Pocket Scale, 1000 x 0.1g]] because it wouldn't register on this scale.

This KitchenAid also has an 11-pound (5 kg) capacity. It measures in kilograms (which is 1,000 larger than grams) and ounces/pounds. It won't measure tiny teaspoons of tea leaves but I find it to be almost as good as my Soehnle when I compared it side-by-side. The tare function works as well as my Soehnle also.

The scale measures 7-1/2 inches by 8-1/2 inches. It comes with one-year replacement warranty. The scale takes one 9V battery which IS NOT included. It turns on easily and the display is bright and incredibly easy to read.

There are two things I don't like. First, my unit arrived discolored. Apparently the plastic packaging it comes in "melts" onto the scale surface and leaves a clear zebra-looking border around the entire scale that makes it look worn and used. The second thing I don't like is that the scale turns on easily. This means if I lay something on the exact spot of the LED that powers it on and off, it will power on.

Other than this, this scale is competitively priced and appears to be as good as others on the market. Of course only time will tell if this will last. I will update my review if this scale fails.

Nice tablecloth but not as rich colored as I had hoped. This is a nice tablecloth and festive for Christmas. However, I was hoping for richer color combinations, particularly in the red and greens. I would have also liked more design on top and not just the center element. I did order a size too long but I rather have it longer than shorter. Although it is machine washable on cold in the gentle cycle and can be tumbled dried on low and then ironed lightly, I do not wash my tablecloths. I cover them with a plastic topper instead because I feel washing them ruins them.

Overall, this is festive but more subdued in its color combinations and the table-top edges lack detail with the exception of the center design. The outer rim of the tablecloth is well designed, however, but that is not easily seen.

Good ice cream maker but difficult to assemble and disassemble. Several years ago my boyfriend purchased a [[ASIN:B0006ONQOC Cuisinart ICE-30BC Pure Indulgence 2-Quart Automatic Frozen Yogurt, Sorbet, and Ice Cream Maker]]. I was so impressed with it that I immediately went out and bought two of them. I wound up giving the extra one I purchased to a friend who also loves it. Therefore, when this T-fal came up for review, I wanted to see how it compared to my Cuisinart.

After using this machine a couple of times, I would have rated this T-fal 3-1/2 to 4 stars had I not already owned the Cuisinart. However, because I am use to such an exceptional ice cream maker, I find this one just okay, so that is why it gets a plain three star-rating from me.

PROS

- It makes one quart of good ice cream (my Cuisinart makes two quarts)

- I made both the strawberry ice cream and the lemon sorbet. The ice cream was good. The lemon sorbet came out excellent; although I was surprised the recipe did not call for heating the egg white. (My Cuisinart recipe uses water instead of egg white.)

- I consider the currently listed price of $34.99 reasonable and it's less than half the price of the Cuisinart I purchased.

- This machine is quieter than my Cuisinart.

CONS

- The ice cream recipes are not exceptional. Although my strawberry ice cream came out good, it was not as creamy or sweet as the recipe that came with my Cuisinart and it tasted icy or more like sorbet. The recipes that came with my Cuisinart are outstanding and a bit more flavorful and probably more calories too. For instance, the T-fal strawberry ice cream recipe calls for strawberries, powdered sugar, lemon, and heavy cream. My Cuisinart recipe also includes adding whole milk and vanilla extract and it uses regular sugar instead of powdered and calls for about ¼ more sugar than the T-fal recipe. I did not mark it down for this because this has nothing to do with the ice cream maker itself and recipe books can always be purchased.

- The chute on the cover is a little too small so it is not as easy to pour in the ingredients without messing up the top.

- Assembling and disassembling the unit is "sticky" and tricky. I had trouble removing the freezer bowl from the base because there is no grip when pulling straight up. Even lining up the top and locking that in place was cumbersome; although after several tries I have that down well. The paddle also requires a good push to get it into the motor but now seats easily.

- The instructions for cleaning are not adequate. There are actually 6 parts to this ice cream maker (as opposed to the 5 parts shown in the instructions). My Cuisinart only has 4 parts. In order to clean everything but the motor, I had to dissemble all parts. Getting the bowl out of the base is the most difficult. However, I had to dissemble the lid after making ice cream because the ice cream got stuck in the crevices of the top. I did not have to do this after the sorbet. The lid coms apart easily as long as I flexed it when I pulled it away from the nubs holding it in place.

- In my opinion, the bowl takes up an odd amount of space in my freezer compared to my Cuisinart. My Cuisinart 2-QT bowl is totally cylindrical and measures 7-3/4 inches wide by 6-3/4 inches tall. This T-fal 1-QT bowl is flared at the top and measures 5-1/2 inches wide at the very bottom to about 9-1/2 wide at the top due to the handles. It also measures 6-1/2 inches tall.

No matter what machine one chooses, making ice cream is messy and requires prior preparation because of the cooking instructions and the fact that time is needed in the freezer for the ice cream to harden. Also making ice cream usually costs more than buying the pre-made product. The joy I get from making my own home-made product, however, far outweighs these caveats.

In summary, although I cannot attest to the longevity of this machine, I think this is a decent ice cream maker for making small quantities of ice cream. Had I not owned a Cuisinart, I would have been more pleased with this machine. However, the cumbersome assembly and disassembly is the main reason it is a three star machine to me.

PS For those who are interested, I pasted a link to my Cuisinart review in the comments section of this evaluation.

Outrageously overpriced but necessary too for measuring the head space from the top of a jar when canning. I purchased this for $8.20 plus tax on Amazon and even though it was cheaper than the current price of $9.89, I still feel this is outrageously expensive. I had to purchase it here because I could not find it at Walmart or Home Goods or anywhere else.

This plastic "wand" could not be more than five cents to produce. Nevertheless, it works to measure the head space needed from the top of the jar when canning and for that it is indispensable. I can also use it to remove the air bubbles in a jar but that can be done with a chopstick as well.

Overkill for making iced coffee and a large machine; but better if making iced tea also. Besides this [[ASIN:B00CEHZZ4I Mr. Coffee BVMC-LV1 Mr. Coffee BVMC-LV1 Iced Cafe Iced Coffee Maker, 1, Black]], I also own three other Mr. Coffee speciality brewers and they are

[[ASIN:B005BG7MK4 Mr. Coffee BVMC-EL1 Cafe Latte]]
[[ASIN:B002FWMF8G Mr. Coffee BVMC-FM1 20-Ounce Frappe Maker]]
[[ASIN:B007K9OIMU Mr. Coffee BVMC-ECMP1000 Café Barista Espresso Maker]]

Unlike this machine, these three other brewers are excellent single or dual-purpose machines. However, I think this single purpose iced coffee maker is overkill because I can brew coffee in a regular coffeemaker and just add ice to get the same results.

Below are the PROS and CONs from my perspective:

PROS

- This brews nice ice coffee.

- A regular-sized pitcher is provided that I feel can be used as any other pitcher when not in use on this machine.

- The iced coffee is easy to make. Just fill the pitcher to the desired water level, pour it in the reservoir, insert the brew basket with a paper filter filled with the desired coffee grounds, swing the shower head over the basket, insert the pitcher filled with ice cubes to the desired level, plug in and turn the unit on.

- The unit comes with a recipe guide for making eight kinds of flavored iced coffees, one chai tea latte, and a recipe for cafe mocha popsicles.

CONS

- The unit is rather large. It is 12-1/2 inches tall; 10 inches wide, and about 12 inches in depth from front to back when the pitcher is stored in the sideways position or 14-1/2" in depth when in operating mode.

- The pitcher is not dishwasher safe. This is not a CON for me but may be for some people.

- Paper coffee filters (8-12 cup size) need to be purchased separately. It would have been nice had a small supply of about 5 filters come with the unit.

- When using decaf, the instructions say not to exceed 9 tablespoons of coffee and to set brew strength to the least amount (all the way to the left). I really do not understand why that is as it is not explained in the instruction booklet. To me that means less coffee can be made since when brewing 2 quarts, 12 level tablespoons of coffee grounds are suggested just don't use 12 if it's decaf coffee.

- The brew cylce takes a bit long (about 5 minutes) and water continues to drain into the pitcher even after the brewing sounds stop. Therefore, one must pay attention to ensure all the liquid has drained before removing the pitcher.

- As I removed the brewer basket with the spent grinds in it, the tiny bit of water that remained in the brewer basket resulted in coffee dripping down the unit as the basket is removed. This required extra cleanup.

Due to the CONS and the fact that I can make the same good iced coffee (minus the extra recipes, of course) using a regular brewer by combining ice with already brewed coffee, I consider this unit overkill. Nevetheless this is another specialty unit from Mr. Coffee that might satisfy a coffee fanatic who desires everything coffee related!

PS The links to my other Mr. Coffee machines is in the comments section of this review for those who are interested.

UPDATE July 18, 2013 - I've been using this machine to make iced tea and prefer to use it for that. So far I made about 10 quarts of iced tea over the past several weeks. As long as the tea is one that is brewed with boiling water, it actually makes iced tea quicker than I can make it myself. The reason is that it is only a one-step process with this machine. The regular way I would have to boil a pot of water, then steep the tea for 4 or 5 minutes and then pour the brew over ice. With this machine, I can use tea bags directly in the brew basket of the machine or a coffee filter for loose tea. For those who are both coffee and tea drinkers, this machine can serve two purposes.

Nice everyday pan but food sticks to it even when oil is used and it requires a lot of elbow grease to clean. I purchased this at a Pampered Chef party. I love the look and design of this crock. Coffee brewer for both hot coffee and cold coffee drinks and smoothies with one major design flaw. I am pleasantly surprised by this machine except for one major design flaw I outline in the CONS section below. It brews a great cup of coffee and also has a not-so-strong blender that brews coffee drinks and fruit smoothies.

I made a cup of coffee for my boyfriend and a classic coffee frappe, using the recipe in the booklet, for both me and him. My boyfriend and I loved the results. I especially loved the frappe. Below are the pros and cons that I found with this machine.

PROS
- Setup is easy

- Brewing a cup of coffee is simple--just add a tablespoon of coffee for each cup of water to the brew basket (a paper filter is needed), and fill the "thermos mug" with water, pour that in the unit, put the mug under the brew basket, and power on the unit. Note that the mug holds about 1-1/2 cups so that would be about a tablespoon and a half depending on taste preferences.

- Brewing a cold drink is also simple. The steps above are repeated but about 6 tablespoons of coffee (depending on the recipe) and less water is used. For the classic coffee frappe only 1 cup of water is used during the brew cycle. Add the brewed coffee and other ingredients to the blender, pulse a few times, then blend on high until done and a wonderful frappe is created.

- The instructions are well written and 10 recipes are included which includes 4 non-coffee recipes such as strawberry banana and pineapple peach smoothies.

- All parts are easily washed; even though the blender blade does not come out.

- The blender holds 32 ounces of liquid and the measurements are marked on the plastic.

- The "thermos mug" is very nice, has a good grip, and the lip on the cover makes it easy to drink from.

- After the brew cycle is done, only a few beads of water are left behind in the reservoir. Many other coffee makers I've tried leave behind a tablespoon or more.

- The spigot the water flows through sits behind a tab that holds it in place. This is excellent because it raises and lowers automatically each time the lid is open and shut.

CONS

- The classic coffee frappe called for 6 tablespoons of coffee to only one cup of water. As a result, when the brew cycle was done, not all the grinds were wet. Therefore, in my opinion the amount of water was not enough to saturate and brew such a large amount of coffee. I think if the spigot on the brewer was a bit larger or more water was used, this would be resolved. This is the biggest design flaw in my opinion and the main reason I brought this down to 3 stars. I've also reduced the coffee grinds and that still didn't help.

- The unit does feel like it's made of cheap plastic; but then again it is rare that products on the market today do not feel this way.

- Only crescent-shaped ice cubes (typically ones made by a refrigerator ice receptacle) should be used in the blender. I used the square ice cubes from an ice cube tray and the ice did not break down as easily.

- I was unable to use both the hot and cold cycle at the same time. What I mean by this is that while the unit was brewing, I decided to turn on the blender to see what would happen. Immediately the brewing cycle turned off. I had to stop the blender and turn the brewing cycle back on to finish the coffee brew cycle. I did not see any warning in the manual not to operate both sides. However, based on my tests, only one side can be used at the same time.

- No coffee filters were provided with the unit. The unit takes a cupcake style filter that looks like it's a size 4. I suppose a size 2 can be used as well. I only had a size 4 cone filter on hand so I flattened it and used that as a temporary solution. It would have been nice if Hamilton Beach had included at least a 5-filter sample pack with each unit.

Amazon's currently listed price is $69.99 for this machine. Personally, that is a bit steep. I think a good price for this unit is between $30 and $40; however, price is subjective based on how much such a unit is worth to the buyer.

In summary, I would have been very impressed with this java blend coffee brewer had it not had that design flaw. I do, however, love its versatility and the fact that a cup of coffee can be directly brewed into a "thermos mug" for immediate travel and it blends delicious cold drinks as well.

Good for bare floors and outdoor carpets; not good for pet hair or those with pile carpets. I wanted a canister vacuum as a backup to an old Kenmore canister vacuum I own. After trying this vacuum, I feel my old Kenmore Progressive 360 Swivel TrueHEPA is far superior (even though it's breaking apart).

Below are the PROS and CONS of this Dyson:

PROS

Installation was easy and the pictures provided in the manual were easy to understand for dis-assembly of certain parts (like the canister).

The cord is sufficiently long. I measured it twice and it is around 21-1/2 to 22 feet.

The maneuverability of the vacuum is great and so is the turning radius.

When vacuuming floors, the beater bar (brush bar) can be turned off by toggling the button on the handle.

The cord is retractable with the press of a button.

The canister is extremely easy to release and empty and hair didn't get caught in the cylinder like other bagless vacuums I have tried. Even though this is not a HEPA vacuum, I did not sneeze like I usually do when emptying other bagless vacuums.

Once the canister is removed from the base, the filter is easy to remove by lifting straight up and out. It is also easy to re-seat the canister to the base.

The tool caddy fits securely around the extension arm and the two tools sit snugly in that holder even while vacuuming. The tools are also easy to use. The crevice tool has a retractable brush; so it's a 2-in-1 tool. There's also what I would call the narrow floor tool. I did not see a name for it in the book.

The vacuum has great suction. Because the suction is so great, even with the release valve that reduces suction, I still had to use the brush tool provided to vacuum a pet bed successfully because the beater bar wanted to suck in the entire bed.

The beater bar turns easily and is small enough to fit between the legs of some of my furniture which is very nice.

The vacuum moves easily along bare floors and works great for that.

The vacuum is relatively quiet compared to some other vacuums I've used before.

The wand extends with the push of a button. I found it comfortable to vacuum when the wand was fully extended. I'm 5 feet 5 inches so I would suspect someone over 6 feet might feel the extension is not long enough; although for me it was perfect and I could have even collapsed it a bit.

The filter is washable. Dyson recommends it be washed with cold water on a monthly basis. It must be left to dry 24 hours before the next use.

The orange color is very nice and with the purplish blue trim of the filter and silver gray color of the base and hoses, it is an attractive vacuum.

A 5-year warranty is provided for parts and labor

CONS

Dyson recommends the filter be washed with cold water on a monthly basis and it must be left to air dry 24 hours before the next use. I believe the washing recommendations should be based on use. For instance, saying the filter should be washed after 2-3 hours of continuous or non-continuous use is better than a flat schedule because perhaps a user only vacuums once a month or once every two months.

The power button is located on the canister and not on the handle. This is a negative for me because I had to keep bending down and walking over to the canister to shut the unit on and off whenever I needed.

The biggest negative for me is that the beater bar gets clogged easily with hair and I found it almost impossible to remove the bar as shown. Using a tool like a screwdriver (or even a letter opener handle) damaged the plastic dome covering the beater bar. They did not say with what to remove the cover. I have four long-haired cats and I had to clean the beater bar at least once before I finished vacuuming because it kept getting tangled with all the hair that was picked up. Even though you couldn't see the hair on the carpet, the Dyson was exceptional in pulling whatever hair there was from the carpet. I don't have this problem with my Kenmore because the beater bar bristles are tiny and don't seem to hold onto the hair like this vacuum does. From now on I will clean the bar by pulling the hair out instead of removing the entire bar as recommended. It was also difficult to lock the bar in place simply because the plastic cover did not provide any turning leverage. This was the only part of the vacuum that I found difficult to lock and unlock.

The other big negative was that I have somewhat low-pile carpet, yet the suction was so great it was hard to move the vacuum over the carpet unless I opened the "suction trigger release" on the handle to reduce the airflow. I found that I had to use this release continuously. However, I did not have to use it on the outdoor carpet on my balcony which is low pile carpet that is almost like a bare floor.

The other negative was the comment in the manual that says "fine dirt such as flour should only be vacuumed in small quantities." That means I cannot use carpet powder with this vacuum. I like to put down carpet powder to give my house a flowery smell. The powder I put down adds up to almost an entire box worth for my condo. However, with this vacuum I really should not do that because it would clog the filter.

In summary, this Dyson has some great qualities such as good maneuverability, easy and light to carry, great on bare floors, and good suction. However, I feel that for those with pets or carpet in their house (unless it's outdoor carpet), would not find this vacuum a good buy. I also feel at the current price of $399, it is too expensive because of the CONS even though I'm impressed with its great qualities. In fact, I really would love this vacuum if I did not have carpet. Depending on the a person's circumstances I can see some loving this vacuum, other's liking it, most seeing it as okay, and some might even hate it. Based on the PROS and CONS above, it's just okay for my purposes.

UPDATE May 25, 2014 - I felt that my boyfriend would love this vacuum because he has a no pile carpet in one room and wood floors in the rest of his apartment. Since it's also compact and has excellent maneuverability (features I love), he would love that too. Today, I had him try this vacuum at his place and he LOVES it and rates it 5 stars just as I expected. Therefore, if I had the same situation in my house, I would have rated this 5 stars as well. Since it does not work for my purposes, I rated it 3 stars. This vacuum is for those who either don't mind releasing the airflow through the handle pull or for those who don't have pile carpet and want it mostly for hard wood or bare floors.

Beautiful towels that lack absorbency; wooden spoon is the only useful item. The two towels are gorgeous in my opinion. The one towel is a rich red plaid and the other is white with a beautiful red pompom fringe and ‘TIS THE SEASON TO BE JOYFUL written on the front. They are decorative for the holidays. However, they are not absorbent so I cannot use them for anything but a decoration. The water just runs off them similar to the way water beads and runs off a windshield that has Rain-X on it. I couldn't dry my dishes or my hands with these towels.

They can be washed in cold water and should be ironed after they are hung dry—unless one doesn’t mind the wrinkles. They should not be dry cleaned, bleached, or tumble dried.

After washing them and hanging them dry, they still were not absorbent. Both towels also shrunk about two inches.

In summary, I rated this set 3 stars because the towels only work as a decoration for me. The only useful item is the spoon. If the towels were absorbent, I would have rated this set 5 stars. It does, however, get 5 stars as a decorative linen.

PS I put a link to the textile “washing” symbols in the comments section of this review since the care instructions on the towels are in symbols only.

Very cushioning and non-slip mat that displays every footprint and barely bounces back. This mat is large at 20” wide x 40” long. It has a non-slip bottom, is easy to clean, is very comfortable to stand on, and has a nice weave design. I would have given this 5 stars if it were not for the fact that it holds all my footprints and barely springs back even after a couple of hours (see before use and after use pictures).  The indentations from use are very unattractive. Nevertheless, if one can get past the visible depressions, this definitely cushions the floor in a kitchen work area.

A "no-frills" tea maker for brewing different teas at various temperatures but it is not comparable to the Breville One-Touch. I love everything tea and have purchased many brewing apparatuses. My favorite is the [[ASIN:B003LNOPSG Breville BTM800XL One-Touch Tea Maker]]. I love that tea maker so much that I purchased two of them at a cost of $500 because I cannot stand to be without a good tea brewer. (For those who are interested, I attached a link to my Breville review.)

This tea maker is a knock-off on that one. It is comparable in looks but in functionality it unfortunately falls a little short of my expectations.

PROS

- This tea maker is a very sleek looking unit.

- The infuser basket does not "leak" tea leaves due to the very fine mesh screening.

- The cord wraps into the base and has three slots from which to anchor it when unraveled. (NOTE: The cord is short at about 27 inches from exposed end to tip but that is typical of most appliances like this.)

- It is relatively easy to make tea or boil water with the push of a button as long as only the default steeping times are being used. There are buttons to boil water and for different type teas like white, green, black, etc.

- The unit comes with a tiny recipe pamphlet for different tea drinks.

CONS

- The white and green buttons should really be switched in my opinion. White tea is normally brewed at a lower temperature than green tea. Instead the green tea button brews at a lower temperature than white on this machine. I attached a link to a brewing chart in the comments section of this review.

- The process of steeping the tea is not as unattended as I would like because once the water heats up and the kettle beeps, it's time to add the tea basket. Then the basket must be removed after steeping has finished to avoid over steeping the tea.

- The basket is narrow and long which causes two issues. First, when using a tea that unfurls (like Pomegranate Oolong from Harney and Sons or Jasmine pearls), the leaves tend to expand upward, leaving part of the leaves unsteeped which results in an uneven brew. Second, removing the leaves from the long infuser basket and cleaning it out is a bit more difficult than with a wider basket that is not so long.

- If I want to have the tea kept warm, I have to remember to set the keep warm function by pressing the tea button again after the brew is done but there's no way to tell that I've already set it. If I forget, the tea gets cold.

- Although it is possible to set custom steeping times, those times are not remembered once the unit is turned off. Also, the particular tea button originally chosen to heat the water has to be pressed once more to start the steeping process and then again and again for each minute increase in time. It is easy to lose count if distracted as there is no LED showing what was requested.

- This tea maker cannot be pre-programmed to start brewing at a certain time, meaning there is no Auto Start Option.

- The carafe lid is hard to dry due to the deep channel in the lid.

This is not a CON for me, but the carafe cannot be submerged in water. This is typical of any tea maker with a heating element attached. I just rinse the carafe or am very careful when washing its interior.

In summary, this tea maker is a "no-frills option" for those who want to brew different teas at various temperatures. It will suit that purpose just fine, especially if the tea is not left to sit in the water for an extended period of time. One can get use to its quirks and the fact that buttons have to be pressed multiple times without any indication of what's been done or any memory of the setting. I do not like that the white and green tea buttons are sort of atypical in the sense that green tea is usually brewed at a higher temperature than white; with this tea maker they have the temperatures reversed. Personally, my favorite is the [[ASIN:B003LNOPSG Breville BTM800XL One-Touch Tea Maker]] and nothing I have ever tried has even comes close to topping that unit. Nevertheless, this Mr. Coffee is acceptable.

Double boiler for VERY SMALL jobs but leaves an air space between my smallest pot rim and the boiler. I sometimes use a small double boiler to melt chocolate, sugar (for caramel), or butter. Previously I use to use a small yet heavy Pyrex bowl over one of my pots. What I like about his one is that it is light, has two pour spouts, and a long handle that stays cool to the touch. It makes it easier for me to carry and pour out the contents. It's also very sturdy and the handle stays cool to the touch.

The only reason I rated this 3 stars is because I am unable to find a pot that fits this with a tight seal. Normally a double boiler requires that a tight seal be made between the water and the boiler; however, on every single pot I tried there is a 1/4" to 1/2" gap between the rim of the pot and this double boiler making it take longer for me to melt butter, sugar, and chocolate. If I could find a pot that this snugly fits the rim of, I would have rated this 5 stars.

UPDATE - I purchased the [[ASIN:B003L0ZNVW Calphalon Tri-Ply Stainless Steel 1-Quart Open Sauce Pan]] from Home Goods for $19.99 plus tax. This double boiler comes close to creating a snug fit with this pot. I've tried many other pots and have taken some back and this is the best fit I can find. There's still about 1/8th" of space around the rim so it's not a tight seal. See attached picture.

I found the pictorial instructions easy to follow. It took me 40 minutes in total to unpack the bookcase and put it together. There are 9 pieces for the bookcase with 17 screws and 17 caps to cover the screw holes. One screw and one cap are left over as only 16 are needed. I found the pictorial instructions easy to follow. Note that there are two other tiny pieces of wood in the box which is part of the packaging material only. At first I thought it was some trim but it is not and that gets thrown out.

The package this arrived in was falling apart because it comes in a very small box and Amazon put it in a larger box causing the unit to slide around and push out the lid of the larger box. Other than this the boxes were not damaged.

The unit is made of particle board which is typical of cheap shelving like this. One of my shelf edges was damaged and it was not from the packaging (see first picture). When I did the installation, I made sure to flip the damaged shelf in such a way so that it is in the back of the unit (see the right side of the first shelf from the top in the second picture). The third picture shows the fully assembled shelf.

I only had to use a Phillips screwdriver for assembly and I used the top of the screwdriver handle to "hammer" in the screw caps because I was unable to seat them with my thumbs.

In summary, this is a cheap alternative for a bookcase and is not something that will last a lifetime of heavy use. It requires assembly. I have assembled a lot of my furniture over the past 30 years so I found it easy. However, I still had to review the specific instructions to determine which were the top and bottom panels and which way the divots should face. If I wanted a shelf that was longer lasting and looked more high-end, then this is not one I would buy. However, for a temporary solution or low budget needs, this works and is competitively priced for what it is

Very small butter-knife-sized spatula good for tiny jobs; the inability to remove the packaging label is a BIG NEGATIVE. This flexible icing and cake decorating spatula is tiny like a butter knife. It is flexible and does a perfect job for very, very small tasks like icing a cupcake, buttering bread, putting cream cheese on a roll, spreading jelly, etc.

There are several things I do not like about this listed in order of its worst features:

The first picture shows the knife in the package. The top label is not affixed to the plastic packaging; instead it is stuck onto the knife as you can see from the second picture.

2 - I would not really call this a spatula. This is so small that the surface area is only good for small icing jobs. In summary, unless one is looking for a butter-knife-like tool, there are better options elsewhere. However, for small jobs this works as designed and might be worth the purchase. If they corrected their packaging, I would have given this 3.5 to 4 stars.

I am a steamer fanatic who mostly cooks everything with steam. This is my 12th steamer and is somewhat disappointing.. [[VIDEOID:d686991dc4eaf4730ba34a52dbe64089]] I have been steaming most of my meals for over 25 years. In those 25 years, I owned or previously owned 11 steamers. This is my 12th steamer and is somewhat disappointing due to its unusual design and noise.

WHAT is in the BOX
In addition to the instruction manual and one-year limited product warranty pamphlet, this comes in nine parts as follows:
- Power cord
- Two steaming baskets with lid (four items)
- Steaming grate
- Drip tray
- Base unit
- Top lid

FEATURES
- There are two independent steaming controls with ability to synchronize finish or ability to run as a combined steam zone.
- The rapid start feature supposedly reaches max steaming power in less than 30 seconds; however, I did not see steam come out of the vent covers until I was 14 minutes into a 25-minute cycle
- There are two steaming levels (high and low), a keep warm only feature (for 45 minutes), a steaming only feature, or a keep warm (for 15 minutes) after steaming feature.
- It has a descaling option (which I have not tested yet) based on water hardness level, which the user has to test before first use. The water hardness test strip was not included with my unit as specified. I contacted Breville and they said they would send me one. However, it has been a week and they still have not sent it out. I decided to leave the level set to five so that I could use the steamer now.
- Everything but the base and drip tray are metal.
- The unit is easy to operate once one gets the hang of it.

LIKES in order of importance to me
- I love the option of using only the steaming tray because there is more surface area for cooking large items like filets of fish.
- I can split the steamer into two zones with or without a synchronized finish or cook on one side in split-zone mode.
- I can fill the reservoir from the outside as is typical of most but not all steamers.
- There is 45-minute keep warm feature to keep food warm. This is the "keep warm only" feature and can be used to keep food warm that was cooked elsewhere.
- There are no plastic parts exposed to the food. The plastic drip tray sits underneath the steaming tray and sits below the metal steaming basket.
- A full reservoir provides enough steam for at least 45 minutes of steaming.
- Cord has a finger hole for easy removal from socket.
- It beeps when done.
- There are descaling instructions inside the lid.
- The footprint is large and oval, yet sleek looking. It reminds me of a railroad car.

DISLIKES in order of importance to me
- This unit cooks unevenly. During a combined steam, the right side does not steam as well as the left.
- The steamer takes a long time to get up to a good heat level during a cold start (which is most of the time).
- Two steamer baskets are required to make a dozen hard boiled eggs because the main tray does not have egg indentations. This is a MAJOR oversight in my opinion. This means there is more clean-up required (due to being required to use the steamer baskets) and fewer eggs can be hard boiled. If they used an offset method, most likely they could have gotten 18 to 24 egg indentations on the main tray. Each steamer basket has only six indentations per basket.
- Max water level causes water to overflow onto counter. When filling the reservoir to the max level prior to adding the drip tray, it will cause the insertion of the drip tray to displace the water in the tank and overflow on the counter. It is best to fill the tank through the spout; however, avoid filling it to the max level because it overflows. I found the water must always be slightly below the max level. I would have liked a deeper reservoir so that I can fill it to the max fill line; either that or change the max fill line level indicator.
- Operational noise is annoying as it sounds like the unit is grunting.
- The drip tray fills up quickly when steaming some items like potatoes or chicken. Just the act of steaming causes condensation and water to build up. This is typical, so I would have liked a little deeper drip tray. In addition, it is a bit difficult to unseat the tray, so be careful when emptying its hot liquid.
- There are so many moving parts to wash or at least dry (depending on whether food has come in contact with the trays).
- Steam comes out of both sides of the vent cover even when cooking in one of the two split zones and not the other.
- The steamer is heavy.
- No rice bowl is included, although I can use any microwave safe dish.

In summary, I am a bit disappointed in this steamer and give it 2.6 stars (round up to 3 stars). My main disappointment is that it cooks unevenly and takes about 14 minutes to reach peak steam level from a cold start. The right side never steams as well as the left whether in combined or split zone. I dislike how water easily spills onto the counter due to the shallow reservoir and the misleading max fill line. The lack of egg indentations in the steam tray is also a negative for me. The steamer does offer the versatility of cooking two meals at once. Also, plastic is not exposed to the food. However, even if this steamer were fully functional and better designed, it is still overkill for most people. Most people want to cook one item like rice or vegetables. There is just so much to wash and I wash everything by hand. If this steamer did not have the first six negatives, then I would have loved it as a third-place choice for my purpose even though it is smaller than my Richard Simmons three-meal steamer I listed below. In its current functional condition, this steamer is priced too high. If it were better designed, then I would consider the current $165 price reasonable.

Attached are pictures of the steamer on maximum water level and the water almost reaching the spout. Once the drip tray is put in place, the water flows out onto the counter (notice water to top of spout). In the picture where I have two bowls, I was using the split steam zone to cook rolled oatmeal on the left and oat groats on the right. Since the steamer does not cook as well on the right side even though all the settings were correct, I actually had to cook it twice. In the pictures where you see just the steaming tray and potatoes or garlic, I was using the combined zone. Also attached is a video that demonstrates the Breville's noisy “grunts” during use.

Good as a desk clock but not for travel or as an alarm clock. In my opinion, this clock is only good as a desk clock and is really not suited as an alarm clock or a travel alarm clock because:

- It is a little larger than typical travel alarm clocks.
- The buttons are on the bottom and will be pressed automatically in the luggage causing the batteries to go dead. There should be something covering them.
- It is awkward to operate.
- One has to turn off the alarm on the bottom of the clock and when half asleep, that button is impossible to see.

FEATURES
- Battery operated (3 AAA batteries NOT included)
- Dual alarm feature (weekdays and weekends or set the same time for both)
- Seven-color selectable back-lit display (red, purple, blue, teal, green, yellow, white/clear)
- Graduated waking feature for alarm with both beeping and lights (initial alarm is one beep, then two, etc.; it cycles through the lights)
- Snooze feature from 5 to 60 minutes
- It has a date feature and 12-hour or 24-hour clock options.

I love the back-lit colors (although they only show when the alarm is on or when the feet or center top is squeezed). I also like the fact that this tells the time and shows the date but I do not like the other features. I was able to set mine to purple but the colors do not stay if the alarm is used. It cycles through all the colors when the alarm goes off and then will stay on the color it cycled to when the alarm was shut off. Setting up this alarm clock was cumbersome. I definitely needed the instructions. What I noticed is that the feet on the clock need to be depressed to engage the snooze alarm. I was unable to get this to work the first time because I had it on a carpeted stair. Therefore, it must be on a hard surface. The fact that I have to locate the snooze button when I am half asleep drove me crazy. I have trouble seeing without my glasses, so that is annoying. Overall, this is a good desk clock only.

Knife feels good in the my hands but I do not like the thick cutting edge. This knife has a good grip and feels weighty in the hand. It cuts okay. To me, I feel the cutting edge could be thinner and sharper.

According to the insert, this comes with a lifetime limited warranty. It is also dishwasher safe; however, I prefer to hand wash.

In summary, this is not my favorite paring knife in this price range. I own a Kuhn Rikon paring knife in blue like this [[ASIN:B00168EAPQ one]] that I like much better than this.

Looks and feels impressive but is not great for cooking with liquid ingredients such as eggs or pancakes. The Amazon title says this pan is small but that is not true. It is very large (11.25 inches) as you can see from the picture and extends beyond my large burner. I need a lot of room on the sides to prevent the handle from hanging over the stove.

I love the teal color and how wonderful the pan feels. It also appears to be very well made. It is sturdy but not overly heavy. The ridges on the inside are higher than I expected. As a result, this is best for frying bacon, making paninis, etc. with a [[ASIN:B005TGY0ME bacon press]] (not included).

OTHER LIKES
- It comes with a lifetime warranty.
- It oven safe up to 500 degrees Fahrenheit.

I used this to make scrambled eggs and because the ridges are large, the result was uneven and difficult as egg got stuck in the ridges. I own a [[ASIN:B01N5G52NJ Circulon 10868 11" Ultimum Forged Aluminum Nonstick Square Grill Pan, Large, Black]] that has ridges but the ridges are small and it works well with eggs and pancakes. This pan, on the other hand, is not as easy to work with when there are liquid ingredients.

CAVEATES
- It has a PTFE (Polytetrafluoroethylene) coating which is dangerous to birds and perhaps dangerous to food.
- This is NOT dishwasher safe.
- Due to the porcelain enamel exterior, there is the risk of this pan fusing to a ceramic or glass cooktop if overheated.
- The handle can get hot with extended cooking.

In summary, my first impressions of this pan were that this is awesome but once I put it to use and read the cardboard instructions, I am not so impressed. It works but there are better solutions available in my opinion.

Smoothies stay fresh but ice cannot be blended into the recipe & every ingredient has to be bite-sized before blending. After having tried this, I am actually disappointed I ordered this because it is not as versatile as my old blender or my [[ASIN:B00NGV3X2W Nutri Ninja Auto-iQ Blender]].

WHAT's IN THE BOX
- Main blender unit
- Blending jar with lid
- Vacuum storage jar with lid
- Two extra vacuum plugs

Each lid is 3 pieces (the filter, vacuum plug, and the lid housing). The blending jar is supposed to have a detachable blade but I was unable to remove it. Since it is sharp, I just used a brush inside the unit to clean.

LIKES
- The vacuum seal - removes the oxygen from the jars to keep ingredients at least color fresh which supposedly tastes fresher.
- Due to less air there is a reduction of foam on top and the blend is smoother.
- There's a cord wrap underneath the unit.
- The storage jar allows me to keep things fresh (after it's vacuum sealed) if not consuming immediately.
- The auto button allows me to set and forget with vacuuming and blending combined.
- There's an option to pulse if more blending is needed.
- There's an option to manually blend.
- The unit will not work unless blending jar is locked in position; in fact a continous beep occurs.
- The unit has non-skid suction feet but it did not adhere on my counter top glass but it did adhere to my counter without the glass.
- Register online and you'll get a 2-year warranty (doubled from 1 year)
- A tiny bare-bones recipe booklet is included.

DISLIKES
- The unit is too large (at 18 inches tall) for under counter storage (see picture).
- All ingredients have to be cut into small pieces.
- Ice (or anything hard) cannot be used in the blender.
- I was not able to remove the 6-blade assembly from the blending jar. This might not be an issue for some but it was for me. However, I do not care as I use a bottle brush to clean out the blade area with the unit intact.
- The blender cannot be run continuously for more than 3 minutes; motor burnout is likely to occur.
- Ingredients over 104 degrees should not be put in the blending jar, which means soup ingredients have to cool down first.
- The recipe booklet sometimes left me with questions, such as adding pre-soaked cashews to a recipe without saying how long they have to be pre-soaked (Page 36). Yet a few pages later it says almonds have to be soaked for 8 hours for another recipe.
- I have to be careful not to lift the unit by the top because the shape of it makes me want to do this. Also, the top of the main unit does not flip over enough. It keeps wanting to close on itself. Therefore, I have to hold the top while I am trying to insert and lock the blender into place.

Note that everything has to be added all at once starting with liquid ingredients first. There's no option to add ingredients as it blends because that would break the vacuum seal.

Since I did not have the ingredients for the recipes on hand, I did blend some strawberries with milk and the color was rich and the drink was smooth without all the foam a non-vacuum blender. It also tasted great. Nevertheless, because I could not add ice to the blend, it was warm even though the ingredients came out of the refrigerator. Adding ice cubes to the blending ingredients just doesn't have the same mouth feel and refreshing taste. This and the fact that I have to cut up the ingredients into small pieces are my main dislikes. I am also disappointed that I need to hold the top cover as I am locking the blending jar into place as it requires a bit of coordination.

Very nice candle with a very sweet tropical citrus fragrance when burned. This has a nice citrus fragrance and is very attractive. Once burned, however, the tropical blend is a bit sweet, so it gave me a slight headache. If it burned as it smells when it is not burning, I would have rated this 4 stars.

On another note, mine arrived with a slightly bent container as you can see in the lower right-hand corner and I suspect that was because it was shipped in a padded envelope.

The rug is a bit thin and small but it is fluffy and my cat loves it; it does shet. I got this for my cat to lay on (as you can see in the picture). It is very small. The measurements are of the longest width and the longest length (such as from the top of the head to the tip of the toe). It is very soft on the underside. There was no label on my rug. I assume it can be machine washed and hung dry. I already have another rug very similar (but a bit thicker) that I wash periodically. However, this does shed a bit where my other rugs like this do not.

I was loving this GoBottle thermos until I discovered it leaked. At first I was super impressed with this thermos because of its features and large 64 ounce (1.89 liter) size.

FEATURES

- The small spout is for pouring but I see no reason one cannot drink from that spout. The lid unscrews partly and flips back.

- When the full black section is unscrewed, it exposes a wide mouth thermos that makes it easy to clean and fill.

- The interior is made with 18/8 stainless steel, so there was no off-putting taste.

- It says it keeps drinks hot for 12 hours. I tested this with almost boiling water and after 12 hours the water was still hot to the touch. After 13 hours it started to become warm.

- I love how the exterior of the GoBottle stayed cool even with boiling water inside.

- Although the instructions do not say this, the full black section can be used as a cup. Just unscrew and turn upside down and pour some of the contents into it. The liquid did not leak out from the cup as long as the tiny lid is screwed on tight. Note that it is difficult to hold the large round base with one arm during the pour.

- It is BPA-free.

- It claims it keeps items cold for 48 hours, although I did not test that because I use this for hot items.

- It comes with a 10-year limited warranty.

WARNINGS

- This should be hand washed with mild soap, although they say the lid is dishwasher safe in the top rack. I hand wash everything even though I have a dishwasher, so this warning does not concern me.

- Do not use bleach.

- Fully dry before storing.

- Do not use in the microwave or freezer.

PROBLEMS

This would have gotten five stars except that it is not airtight and not leakproof. When I turned it upside down, the liquid started seeping out. I then tightened the black top as hard as I could, but I still had a few drops that seeped out of the bottom of the base (that is where the black top meets the body of the bottle). I tried this several times and I feel that since the top is plastic, it will eventually break and the seal will become looser or "stretch." This is the only reason I am rating this 3 stars. As long as one keeps this upright, it is fine, but should the bottle turn on its side or upside down, there will definitely be some seepage.

Not as spacious as my usual bag but I like that it cinches tight. This review is for the unbleached bags. I usually purchase these [[ASIN:B0773DJ8Q3 300 PCS Disposable Tea Filter Bags]] but decided to try these unbleached ones. The first picture shows how small and thin these are compared to my white ones.

My major like is that the string cinches the bag very tight and it stays closed unlike my white filter bag. However, since this is small, it is harder to insert one teaspoon of tea into the opening. It is amazing that the filter does not disintegrate in hot water. Also, I am shocked by how thin these are. A 300 pack of these filters take up one third the space of my white filters. I almost thought they did not send me what I ordered. However, the thinness is a plus for me for storage.

Overall, I like these. I do not know yet whether I will order these again over the white ones as there are pros and cons to both. For instance, the white filters I order never stay shut. I will decide when I need to place another order.

UPDATE October 23, 2019 - I have decided to lower my rating of these bags from 4 to 3 stars after using them for several months. These are smaller than the [[ASIN:B0773DJ8Q3 300 PCS Disposable Tea Filter Bags]] I am use to and they are easier to rip unless handled gently. I will only order these in a pinch and prefer the other bags instead.

Extremely functional but at this price, the tray should be flawless & without scratches. Come tax time my cost for this tray will wind up being less than the $50 advertised price. Had I paid the full $50, I would have been extremely disappointed. I am only somewhat disappointed since I paid less and I have no plans of gifting this.

The tray I received arrived with missing lacquer around the edges and scratches and other imperfections on the side. Although, this is noticeable, it does not take away from the serviceability of this piece. It remains highly functional, sturdy, and a great way to carry food items, coffee, tea, etc. to a porch, in bed, or wherever needed. A friend of mine uses a tray like this on her upholstered ottoman to serve tea on and protect her furniture.

Most of the finish on this tray is stunningly glossy. As can be seen from the first photo, you can see my reflection in the tray. Nevertheless, I expect the finish to be flawless. In its current state, the imperfections and scratches take away from its beauty and make it not giftable. This was packaged extremely well, so the issue stems from the manufacturing process. The $50 price combined with the lack of flawless finish is the reason I took off two stars; in every other way it is perfect.

This is an excellent spoon rest in EVERY WAY but ONE; the pesky label took me over 2 hrs to remove. This spoon rest is sturdy, has a non-skid surface that keeps it from sliding on the counter (photo 2), and holds many items. The third picture shows it holding two tea infuser baskets which is great for when I want to not drain the steeped tea leaf water on my counter. The fourth photo shows it holding an almost 3-inch spatula. The last photo shows a 4-inch one. This cannot successfully accommodate anything wider than 3.75 inches.

The one bothersome point that had me removing not one but two stars was the label that was affixed to the entire top surface of the tray. I tried lightly removing it with a razor. Then I tried to lift the corners with the tip of a knife. I had to be careful because I did not want to scratch the surface. I do not have any long fingernails, so I could not try that. I then had to soak it for a FULL TWO HOURS in Dawn Platinum dish detergent before I could even try to use my fingernail nubs to just barely lift one edge. Even when I did that, I had trouble pulling up the label because, it is so strongly affixed to the spoon rest. I had to use all my strength in my hands to finally remove the label. Total time it took was TWO and a HALF HOURS. The only positive is that it was a clean pull with no adhesive left behind.

A label that does not easily remove from a product is a deal breaker for me even if it is not for others. Therefore, this gets 3 stars for that reason. The product itself, once the label is removed, is 5 stars.

Good for small steaming jobs but not the quality I would expect had I purchased this at the list price. I'm a steamer fanatic and selected this because I'm crazy about steamers. In fact, I've owned 10 steamers in total. Since 2 broke, I now own 8 steamers with the receipt of this one.

This is a tiny steamer that works well for small steaming jobs. The broccoli I steamed came out beautiful. I filled the pot to the halfway point with boiling water, set the steamer basket on top with the broccoli, and covered the steamer basket. Once the water came to a boil (about 9 minutes in), I steamed the broccoli for 8 minutes until it was softened but still firm and a rich green color. However, despite my successful results, to me this steamer is just okay for the below reasons.

PROS

- It's great for steaming a small quantity of vegetables.

- It has a small footprint of 6-1/2 inches at the widest point on the bottom. However, if you include the handles, it's 11 inches wide by 11 inches tall.

- The red gradient color is attractive.

- The stainless steel basket feels sturdy (see comment in CON section).

- The steamer basket is 3-3/4 inches deep.

- The handles are comfortable and stay cool.

- The pot and lid can be used without the steamer basket and the lid fit securely on top.

CONS

- The steamer basket is really too small for family-sized steaming jobs where large quantities of items need to be steamed. The basket is not wide enough to steam a whole unbroken ear of corn. Corn would have to be broken in half and steamed vertically to get the most out of the space.

- The pot feels cheap. Although, the pot can be used as a regular cooking pot with lid without the steamer insert, I do not feel it will wear well.

- After steaming my broccoli, the steamer basket became convex. I had to push the bottom of the steamer basket back in place so that it would sit flat on my counter. However, to me this particular behavior of the basket is unimportant as most of the time the steamer basket sits on top of the pot, so I don't care if it's a bit wobbly.

- I put 3 quarts of water in the pot and the water was even with the top, so figure on getting no more than 2 or 2-1/2 quarts of cooking liquid in this pot for cooking purposes.
.
- I think the current price of $50.97 is a bit too expensive for this steamer. The maximum I would pay is half that.

- The pot is not dishwasher safe because it has a porcelain enamel-exterior. I don't care about this but others might be concerned.

- Although the packaging says this unit is safe for ceramic or glass stovetops, the product insert specifically states that they recommend the use of flat-bottomed stainless steel or hard-anodized exterior cookware on ceramic/glass cooktops because overheating porcelain enameled cookware or letting it boil dry can result in the fusing of the cookware to the stove requiring replacement of the stovetop.

Facts about the steamer as stated on the product packaging:
- The handles are oven safe to 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
- The 3-quart pot has a non-stick interior and a hard enamel exterior.
- The steamer basket is stainless steel.
- The pan and steamer insert are made in Thailand; the lid is made in China.
- The entire unit has a lifetime limited warranty.
- The entire unit is suitable for glass/ceramic (see comment in CONS section), gas, and electric stoves

In summary, I think this steamer is good for small cooking or steaming jobs. It's a cute little steamer that has a relatively small but tall footprint. However, based on the cons above and the fact that I do not believe the quality of the pot is as good as it could be, I'm rating this as just okay.

For those who are interested, below is a list of MY STEAMERS - PAST and PRESENT
