Shows lint easily; very thin throw good for a light covering but is not super warm; holds static. This very thin blanket comes packaged in a zippered plastic bag (mine was a ripped zippered plastic bag) with a piece of gold ribbon. I suspect the ribbon is to use for gift giving. To me that piece is unnecessary (see last photo).

This throw is generously sized and covers two thirds of the top of my king-sized bed as can be seen in the photos. Immediately, lint, fuzz, and cat hair started to show on the deep blue blanket. It is worse when the air in my house is dry as the blanket becomes full of static and hairs tend to stick to it. However, that is to be expected. This throw is very thin and is good to use when a light covering is needed but it is not super warm. I tend to LOVE SUPER PLUSH blankets and throws and this one is not that. Nevertheless, my three cats love this and Stephen immediately claimed his space.

I think the current price of $17.99 is competitive and acceptable for what one gets. However, although I love the softness and intense blue color, I would have preferred something thicker. My absolute favorite thick throw is the [[ASIN:B07J6GBTBW Life Comfort Throw in the Brown Quartz color]].

Note that the tag says this is machine washable on gentle cycle and to tumble dry this on low.

Shrinks items by about 50% but makes them longer; supplied pump is useless. These bags DO NOT reduce volume by 80% as is claimed. Yes they do shrink the puffiness of a comforter and the comforter I put in the extra large bag shrunk by about 50% but it spread out longer to almost of the full size of the jumbo plastic bag.

WHAT'S PROVIDED (photo 1)
- 5 jumbo storage bags (about 35" x 47" or 90 x 120 CM)
- 5 large storage bags (about 28" x 39" or 70 x 100 CM)
- 1 hand pump

I inserted the comforter (photo 2) into the jumbo bag up to the fill line (photo 3). I then had a difficult time trying to seal the bag. It seals just like a regular sandwich bag and I kept having to re-seat the channels. I finally got it to seal. I then tried one vacuum hose to vacuum the bag. That did not work probably because the hose opening was angled. I then tried the hand pump. That is completely useless. Next I tried another vacuum hose and that worked. It flattened into what you see in photos 4 and 5. What it did was spread the item flat in the bag and comforter became hard and long. So far it has held the seal.

These bags appear to be strong, which is a plus compared to some others I tried. One king-sized down comforter fit in the jumbo bag up to the fill line and reduced the height by about 50% but did extend out the length a bit. The length extension is typical of any bags of this type. Overall, these appear to be good bags. However, their claims of reducing volume by 80% are over exaggerated and the supplied pump is completely useless.

Horse image is stunning but blanket is as thin as tissue paper. Note that this review is for the horse (mare and foal) blanket labeled Pattern 8 on the Amazon site.

My boyfriend ordered this for me on Amazon as a gift because he knows I just love horses. The image is absolutely stunning. I love how regal and gorgeous the mare and foal look. However, the blanket itself is super thin like tissue paper. Although it is soft, I would call it more of a wall hanging than a blanket as it is incredibly thin.

The image gets 5 stars but it is 1 star as a blanket--hence the 3-star rating. The current price of $29.99 is definitely $10 too much for what this is simply because it is so incredibly thin. It is best used as a summer blanket or when one wants something that feels like a sheet covering them.

Basic queen coverlet that screams beach house but too $$$; also cat approved. This is a queen-sized quilt but I ordered it to cover the top of my king-sized bed. It is made in China of 100% cotton with 100% polyester filling per the label. It can be machined washed on cold and tumble dried on low but I did not wash mine yet. There is a warning not to dry clean this.

As can be seen from the attached photos, it generously covers the top of my king-sized bed even though it is a queen size. It comes with two standard pillow shams.

The quality is okay. To me the material feels more like linen and a bit scratchy or cheap feeling. It is thin and definitely for summer. It feels like there is one layer of thin cotton batting stitched into the cloth. I do not feel it will last through many washings. I would have rated this four stars for this reason but I lowered my rating to three stars due to the exorbitant price of $107.27. I personally would not pay more than $45 for this because, even though it is nice, the quality is not great, in my opinion. It reminds me of a discount store find and those "bed-in-a-bag-type" products.

UPDATE August 16, 2019 - I washed the comforter and it washed and dried well but did come out slightly wrinkled.

Vacuum sealing w/o a machine BUT it takes a lot of stamina to remove the air & it’s not perfect. I have mixed feelings about this vacuum sealing option. On one hand I wish I had known about this before I purchased my Foodsaver Vacuum Sealer, but on the other hand, I am glad I have that machine even though it is quirky.

For the current price of $25.29, the following items are included in the box:
- 1 hand pump
- 10 extra large vacuum bags (11.8" x 13.4")
- 10 large vacuum bags (10.2" x 13.4")
- 10 medium vacuum bags (10.2" x 11")
- 4 sous vide holding clips (used to clip the bag to the side of the sous vide)
- 2 bag sealing clips (the white clips used to seal the zipper)

The only instructions are on the box. I inserted the food into the bag and pressed out most of the air by hand. I then used the white sealing clip to seal the zipper. I had to try this three times before I was successful. What I found is that it is best to place the bag flush with the counter and then press down hard on the white sealing clip as one slides it across the bag top.

Once the bag was sealed, I placed the pump over the "hole" to suck out the air. I also had trouble with this. I had to push down hard on the pump to create a suction with the "hole" in the bag that is not really a hole. Then it took immense effort to pump the pump up and down. I felt like I was inflating a bicycle tire manually. I really had trouble with the effort this took.

Once I was done, I removed the pump, clipped the bag to the sous vide, and started the cooking process. The bag floated a little bit after awhile. This means that air does seep back into the bag. However, I have had this with my machined sealed items as well. Lucky the clips keep the food submerged.

Cleaning out the bag is not easy. I know I had a hard time because I was unable to clean out the corners even when turning the bag inside out. I wound up throwing it out. I am skeptical of re-using them because they cannot be fully cleaned; especially with fish, meat, or something marinated. The Amazon site says each bag can be re-used more than 10 times; I seriously doubt that nor would I count on that. I would consider one use to be typical. For me, it has been one use only.

In summary, this is one option to try if a machine vacuum sealer is not available. I do think this is a viable option for those who use a sous vide intermittently. However, if someone uses a sous vide regularly, I would not recommend this due to the difficulty and price of replacement bags -- since washing them out is difficult to impossible.

Well-made baking cups but too small, too few, and too expensive. These baking cups are well made. However, they are SUPER small (like a 1/4 or 1/3 cup size) and that is their biggest drawback besides the exorbitant $24.99 price and only getting three cups when six are really needed to be useful.

I ordered these for my 6 QT Ninja Foodi. These are good both for that appliance and the Instant Pot. Since these are so small, they "get lost" in the Foodi as it looks like I am baking nothing. I used these to experiment with making popovers in my Foodi on the bake cycle. Although the results looked like miniature turkeys (last photo), they came out well. However, they did stick to the sides even though I greased the cups and it was a lot of work to clean. Nevertheless, the cups came out new after scrubbing them.

These little "baking dishes" are also perfect for steaming flan and any other cup appropriate dessert like cupcakes.

Unfortunately, I am dissapointed that they are so small. I need about six of these little guys to make a worthwhile amount of food or dessert.  Each cup comes with a silicone cover that has an air hole to let steam escape.

These come with a limited lifetime warranty free from defects and workmanship.

In summary, these are good but small. Additional cups are needed to be useful. Uncoupling these from the packaging was extremely difficult as the cups stuck together. I store them separately with lids on to avoid this situation in storage. My rating of three stars is due to the high price and small size and quantity of cups that one gets for that price.

Cheaply designed mirror with one brightness setting. This mirror feels cheap. It has a cheap plastic base that looks and feels like a frisbee. There is a plastic post that connects the mirror to the base. I was unable to get that to seat all the way into the mirror itself. The base seated fine and locked in place, but I felt like I was going to break the mirror by trying to get it seated on top so I quit trying since it remained sturdy as is even if the base's name tag did not center correctly with the mirror.

It has to be charged for several hours first. The charging port is on the back of the mirror next to the power button. It comes with a charging cable but not the A/C adapter. However, most people have wall adapters for micro USB cables, so this is not a problem. It also comes with one small round 10X mangifying mirror that can be affixed to the front of the larger mirror via the suction cups.

To power on the mirror, just turn the button on in the back after it is fully charged. That button can remain on. I just press the on/off circular power switch at the bottom of the mirror and the light turns on and off with a touch. There is only one brightness level but it is suitable for tweezing or applying make-up. The mirror head also tilts for better visibility.

Since the base is concave, bobby pins and other small accessories or change can be put in this tray without falling all over the place.

For the current price of $19.98 for the pink mirror, it is okay and functional. Personally, I do not expect this to last, especially since I cannot seem to get the connecting rod fully seated into the top of the mirror as can be seen in the photo where I am charging it.

Excellent strainer but only half the functionality works as designed. I ordered this strainer thinking it was 5 inches around because I was looking for a very small strainer. However, by 5 inches it means across the top at the widest point. Therefore, this is larger than I expected but that is my mistake.

The strainer itself is wonderful. I can wash rice, millet, couscous, etc. without loosing the grains through the mesh. It is also good for washing berries, grapes, etc. However, what I do not like is that only half of this strainer's functionality works. What I mean by this is that there is a "hook" on top that goes over a bowl for hands-free operation. This only works if there is already food in the stranger which negates the purpose of that feature.  When I go to strain something, the strainer starts out empty. If I hook this over a bowl, it immediately tips out of the bowl and onto its handle because the handle is too heavy. This is a negative for me and half the functionality of this strainer is non-existent as a result.

As long as one does not want that "over-the-bowl" feature, then this strainer is great but the cost is too high just to use for straining without the functionality of that feature.

A limited lifetime warranty is included.

Operates exactly like a spatula spoon; I wish handle was silicone. This operates more like a spatula with a little bit of the spoon characteristics. I like the concept and the fact that the silicone is heat resistant up to 500 degrees Fahrenheit. Supposedly it is dishwasher safe but I prefer to wash this by hand.

I definitely like how this flips food easier than a spoon and is a good tool for stirring, scraping bits along the bottom of a pot, etc.  It is not great for scooping, however. My biggest negative is that the handle is not comfortable in my hand for any length of time. I wish the handle were silicone instead of plastic as that would provide a more comfortable and better grip instead of allowing my hand to slip off periodically.

Boy is “she” pretty; “she” works like any coffee press I tried; use coarse grind; holds 4 cups not 8. I tried several coffee presses previously and have another one that I purchased at a local store for half the price. This press works no differently. The only difference is this one is prettier due to the red metal casing.

I use this for tea but it is designed for either coffee or tea. If using coffee, make sure to use a coarse grind as a fine grind will clog the mesh filter. When using tea, also make sure the leaves are not so small that one would consider them tea dust.

After washing this out, I removed the cover, added my tea (enough for four 8 ounce cups), poured boling water into the carafe, inserted the plunger and pushed down slowly. I waited the requisite four minutes for it to steep and then enjoyed my brew. I had a few miniscule leaves escape but not much and they remained on the bottom. I got two full mugs of tea from this. This fits four cups of water up to the base of the top red rim.

There are two things I do not like about this product. First, when drying the glass with a towel, the carafe moves around easily in its frame. I had to keep turning it so the spout pointed opposite the handle. My other press does not move around so easily in the frame. Second, at the current price of $39.99, this costs twice as much as a comparable no-name press.

In summary, "she" is beautiful but "she" is also expensive and "her" frame is loosely seated around the carafe. Also, this does not hold eight cups as the Amazon site says; it holds four cups (32 ounces) of water. Otherwise, this brews a nice cup of tea (or coffee) as long as one does not use a fine grind or fine leaf.

Very attractive but small lunch tote; feels cheap but is functional. This lunch tote is definitely very attractive with its colorful leaf design. However, it feels cheap yet it is functional.

To me this is small. It is just enough for a day's lunch and a couple of small ice packs. In my photos, I show the two glass jars and two ice packs I was able to get into this tote. There's still room for a small package of nuts in addition to these pieces.  If I put any more than this in this bag, I probably would not be able to close the zippers. It keeps my items cold for about three hours and cool for a few more.

The current price of $13.99 is about $2 more than I would expect to pay for a bag of this quality.

It’s a thermos that calls itself a food jar with a great folding spoon; instructiions are poor. I am almost sorry I purchased this based on the other five-star reviews. First of all, this appears to be like any other thermos. The poorly-written instructions say this is a food jar with the ability to "cook" food inside. However, anything that is hard to cook, needs to be cooked first before putting into this "jar."

This unit comes in four parts that includes the base reservoir, the interior sealing lid with a foldable stainless steel spoon, and the top lid that can double as a soup cup. It also comes with an insulated carry bag and poorly written instructions such as "How to smoldering the food."

I pre-heated the thermos with boiling water as instructed and waited 10 minutes. I them dumped the water and put in my grains and added the necessary boiling water. I then sealed both caps, put it in the insulated bag, and by morning I had softened grains in cool water. I had to heat them to cook them.

Now it does say hard cooking grains should be cooked on the stove first but I chose to do it last. Even though the grains softened, I took issue with the fact that I had cool water by the morning. If this is insulated, I would have expected the water to be at least warm and it was not. Perhaps it cooled faster because I did not fill the water to the tippy top. Therefore, I did a test with a full container of boiling water. After nine hours the water was warm and by morning it was cool again, although not as cool as it was when I did not fill it to the top. Therefore, it keeps things hot for about four hours, warm for about eight, and cooler after that.

The best thing about this is the spoon. The spoon does need to be about one inch longer to easily get to the bottom of the thermos, but it still is a nice touch.

For those that care, this cannot be put in the dishwasher.

In summary, I can use this as a thermos for short stints but I will not be "cooking" with this. It certainly can be used to soften beans and grains before cooking if desired. It is perfect for storing loose leaf tea which is what I use some small thermoses for because they are airtight and keep out the light that destroys tea. This thermos would also have been better if it had a handle around the side. It is a little wide and somewhat hard for me to wrap my hand around the girth. If one is filling this to the brim with liquid, then it will stay warm to hot longer.

I am very disappointed with this steamer; design is poor-- it has too many parts – 2.5 stars. I am a steamer fanatic who mostly cooks everything with steam; this is my 15th steamer! Unfortunately, this is not even worth the money I have to lay out for this, in my opinion.

I have been steaming most of my meals for about 30 years. In those 30 years, I owned or previously owned 14 steamers. This is my 15th steamer and it is a whopping disappointment. I put this through the paces and it is one of my least favorite steamers. Yes it works, but it is cumbersome and bulky and has too many moving parts.

WHAT is in the BOX - In addition to the instruction manual, this comes in 11 parts as follows:

- Base unit
- Heater cap (also known as steam guard)
- Three (3) steam tray bottoms
- Three (3) steaming basket "rims" (upper, middle, and lower or what I call small, medium, and large)
- Top lid
- Rice bowl
- Drip Tray

FEATURES
- The steaming controls are LED and it comes with preset times for eggs, rice, fish, chicken/meat, and vegetables. I do not need this but newbies might like it.

- There is a keep-warm function (it is unclear for how long) and a timer function that allows steaming to be delayed anywhere from 1 minute to 12 hours and 59 minutes. I tested both the timer and keep-warm feature and they work well.

- The baskets are an opaque plastic and each basket is two loose pieces.

- The steamer has boil-dry protection so that it turns off if the reservoir is out of water.

LIKES
- The steamer cooks almost equally with all three baskets simultaneously. I usually put the food that gets done the quickest (the most delicate foods like fish) on top away from the intensity of the steam. The uppermost basket does not cook as fast but this is expected.

- It can steam a lot of food since it has three vertical levels.

- I can steam 18 eggs at one time--six in each basket. When I steam eggs, I want them to steam the same. I tested this and the eggs steamed in the top basket were less cooked than those in the bottom basket. However, this is to be expected. Note that I leave the uncooked eggs on the counter for about one hour before steaming so that they do not break during cooking.

- The keep-warm and delay-start features are nice to have.

- When in operation, the steamer is relatively quiet until the food is ready; that is when the beeps sound.

- A full reservoir provides enough steam for at least 60 minutes of steaming which is very generous; most steamers only last 45 minutes on full.

- Descaling is easy just like it is for all the other steamers I own. This steamer will develop mineral build up on the heating element. All that has to be done is to fill the reservoir with equal parts vinegar and water and heat on high for twenty minutes. I actually use almost 100% vinegar in most of my steamers. I have not used this long enough yet to implement descaling.

DISLIKES
- The opaqueness of the baskets makes it difficult to see how the food is doing during steaming.

- Each basket comes in two pieces. It is also easy to have the bottom slip out if not seated correctly. In addition, the top has to be placed on the uppermost basket just right or that will slip off too.

- The LED is awkward in the sense that the on/off button has to be pressed more than once to start the steaming process. I kept thinking the steaming would start and then the unit would turn off. The only way I could tell I got it right was when the two dots (:) blinked.

- There are way too many moving parts. The design of the baskets is very poor. They come apart like a springform pan without the spring.

- The unit with the baskets is also big and bulky and does not collapse into a small enough footprint for storage.

- There is no reservoir refill hole on the outside of the steamer. If I were serial steaming various foods, I would run out of water and would have to handle a hot steamer to refill or wait until it cools. When there is an outside hole for the reservoir, I can use a teapot or something with a spout to refill the steamer during operation or between operations without getting burned. Since the reservoir holds about 60 minutes of water, this issue will not affect me much as I rarely do more than two steaming sessions that go beyond one hour.

- Although this does not affect me at all, beware that the steamer is tall when in use. In addition, the cord is short as is expected of any appliance such as this.

In summary, I am utterly disappointed in this steamer. Although it works, it is cumbersome to use, too bulky, and has too many pieces. The design is not well-thought out. My main disappointment is that each basket is two pieces (a flat removable bottom and a plastic ring for the sided), which makes absolutely no sense to me.

This steamer will fail soon as I have had it almost six years and they usually do not last more than that before it burns out. This steamer also appears to be discontinued which is why a once $30 steamer is now being sold for almost $275.

- Three [[ASIN:B000JJMER4 Richard Simmons EST7 Steam-Heat Electronic Food Steamers]] which I absolutely love. These are very large steamers and are larger than the Breville. They have three steaming chambers and are good for steaming full meals (protein, starch, and vegetable) that FINISH at the same time by counting down in reverse. This remains my other GOTO steamer. This is the type of steamer that is not for everyone and which is why it was discontinued due to lack of customer interest. Because I love it so much, I purchased three as I cannot bear to be without one even though I do not use it daily.

I use this to dispense hand soap and it does that well but these are identical cheap plastic bottles. I have been wanting some tall skinny soap dispensers that fit between my faucet handles in the bathroom. These are perfect for that. I use both of them for hand soap and not shampoo or cream rinse.

The bottles are a very cheap white plastic with a metallic silver rim on top. Both bottles look exactly the same, so there is no way to tell them apart. If I were using this to dispense shampoo and conditioner, I would have trouble knowing which bottle had what solution because the bottles are absolutely identical. I did not see any difference between the two.

Each bottle comes with a clear plastic cap that can be snapped on to prevent the pump from working. In some of my photos the caps are removed as this is the way it should remain during operation. I leave the caps off all the time because I do not want to fiddle with removing them each time I need to wash my hands. In fact the plastic caps are the sturdiest parts of this entire set. In addition, the pump mechanism works very well and feels solid.

The current price of $8.54 ($8.99 minus 5% off) is competitive for this set. Just remember that the bottles are a cheap plastic but when they are in service, it is impossible to tell by looking at them from a distance unless someone squeezes the sides.

Beautiful personal size baking dishes but they chip easily. These are beautiful rectangular personal-sized dishes. I got them to fit in my steamer and toaster oven and they work perfectly for that. However, they chip easily. In fact, mine arrived pre-chipped and it was packaged perfectly. I am very disappointed by that.

The current price of $23.74 ($24.99 minus 5% off) is expensive for this set, especially when they chip. Other than this, they are beautiful and giftable and perfect for one-person meals.

Nice nesting heart containers but not as high quality as I expected. I ordered these containers to store various teas in very small quantities. There are 12 hearts in total with 4 each of 2 ounces, 4 each of 4 ounces, and 4 each of 6.5 ounces. I like that the hearts nest like Russian nesting dolls when the two larger sizes are empty (see photo). What I do not like about these hearts is the clear window. It is made of a plastic that feels like it will easily crack or break. Once that happens these become useless.

If I were using these as one-time only disposable containers, then it would not matter. For instance, these are great for making heart-shaped candles to be given away as gifts, to store candies for party favors, to store tea that is to be sold, as jewelry boxes with the addition of some cotton or felt inserts, etc. However, for permanent storage, they are more on the disposable side. Note the interior surface of some of the containers are a bit marred (scratched up) but that typically does not matter unless one plans to have the interior on display.

Difficult & awkward to use; needs strength. I have a Rosle 8-wedge apple slicer since 2010 and absolutely love it. It is by far the best slicer I ever tried. However, I wanted one that had 16 slices so that I did not have to cut down the 8 wedges in half for when I make cinnamon baked apples. I had a 16-wedge one previously but did not like it and it didn't cut well. Based on my research, this one was recommended. Unfortunately, I'm disappointed. It is just okay.

The slicer has a cover that is attached permanently via a hinge. This makes it awkward to use because that piece is slightly in the way during use. Second, it takes a lot of strength to push this through the apple--even when I put it in my deep sink and press down hard from above. Third, after I flip the cover over to finish pushing this all the way through, when it snaps in place, it still doesn't go all the way through around the entire apple (see my photo where skin and pieces are left behind). I had to be careful and use a knife to remove the debris left behind.

Yes this does make 16 slices, so I'll keep it even though I am not impressed. Had I tried this before buying, I would have never bought it.

The current price of $13.99 plus tax ($14.92 in my case), is competitively priced for this.

Dispensers tip over easily and top is impossible to wash; otherwise it works as designed. This set comes with two dispensers, a funnel, and a rack for the dispensers. I do like the small footprint of this. However, the triangular design causes the dispensers to tip over easily when they are out of the rack. I almost tipped them over three times. The design also makes the container difficult to wash except with a tiny bottle brush. The top is impossible to wash in my opinion and I do not like that. I personally would like to be able to wash everything periodically.

The top screws on via one turn, which I also do not like because it is never tight. Nevertheless, nothing leaked out, so the set is functional and works as designed. The top has a great flow as well and opens automatically as the oil or vinegar is dispensed. Despite its functionality, after having tried this, it works and is stylish but is not designed sturdy enough for my tastes.

The current price of $17.95 ($18.89 minus 5%) is competitive for this ensemble.

Nice lettering but the string ruins the look. I really like the lettering on this set (see photo). However, the string provided ruins the look. There are holes in the tops of the letters that need to be punched out and through which this string is passed. The letter H, T, Y, etc. have two holes, etc. However, I feel it would have been best if a gold string-like ribbon were provided instead of this thread as it cheapens the look.

The current price of $7.19 ($7.99 minus 10%) is a bit pricey, especially since only the letters are wonderful.

Nice stickers for sealing my envelopes but no colors are vibrant. These hearts are just okay. Their colors are not vibrant. In fact, the silver and gold are dull.   Also, removing the hearts from the paper is a delicate process. I actually ripped one because I pulled it off too fast.

Overall, these work to add to the seal of any envelopes I am mailing out. I really would not use them for much else due to their lackluster look. 

The current price of $9.99 comes to almost $.2 cents per heart which is too much for this style.

Medium functional plastic pump bottles for shampoo/conditioner/body wash, etc.. There are three medium-sized (i.e. 16 ounce) black lightweight empty plastic bottles in this set. They are labeled for use for shampoo, conditioner, and body wash. There are also three labels provided in case one wanted to re-purpose these for sanitizer, dish soap, or hand soap. If used for something else other than what is on the extra labels or on the bottles, then the label will obviously not be true to what is inside.

The pump mechanism works very well and feels solid. When filling this, it is important that the soap not come above the top rim because the insertion of the pump causes the soap to spill out over the top. It is possible to re-engage the lock on the pump when empty. I would not want to do that with liquid inside.

These work as designed. There are two negatives I see. First, since these are not clear plastic, the soap level CANNOT be viewed through the plastic. Second, these bottles look elegant but because they have the logo "Pr3mium Conc3pt" as a label on the bottle, it is easy to mistake this as a brand of the product inside. I personally would have preferred that label be left off.

The current price of $17.97 is outrageously overpriced for this. I feel a price of $2 per bottle (total of $6 for the set) would be reasonable for these empty and lightweight plastic bottles.

Nice set; no heat rating on utensils; handles too thick for slots; FORC label is upside down on mat. This set comes with a mat that has an embedded spoon rest and slots for holding five utensils. There are also four utensils included--one regular and one slotted spoon with silicone tips and wooden handles and two spatulas (one small and one large). The spatulas will not really fit well on the spoon rest, especially if both are in use simultaneously.  The handles of the wooden spoons are a bit too thick to fit in the slots on the mat. Also, there is no heat rating written anywhere for the utensils; therefore, I have no idea if they will melt at certain temperatures. This is a big negative to me. I wrote them over a week ago to find out the heat rating but have not heard back yet.

Second, the placement of the FORC label on the mat is upside down in the upper right corner--see PHOTO. This is sort of a non-issue but it is a detail that should be corrected.

The mat has a small lip around the edge that will keep water or liquids from running over the sides, which is great.

I love the neutral gray color of this mat and its versatility. It is certainly very functional. It does come with a 12-month warranty and the label says this is 100% BPA free.

I have no idea how much this will be priced at but anything more than $12 in its current state would be overpriced in my opinion. They are selling similar sets at around $7 such as Amazon product ID #B08P7KD5XW, which is another one of their sets. If this set had handles that fit in the slots on the mat, had a label that was not upside down, had a heat rating of 450 degrees or higher, and had two different sized spatulas,  then this would have received 5 stars from me.

Nice fragrance; has a multitude of uses to freshen up an area…I think????. There are five air fresheners in this set or perhaps they are "insect repeliennt" if one reads the PIG LATIN on the box (see photo).

More of a novelty item. I purchased this thinking the base detaches from the strainer so that I could hang it inside a cup with loose tea leaves on top (sort of like an open diffuser). Unfortunately, the strainer only swivels on the base and does not detach. The box comes with absolutely no instructions so I had no idea how this was supposed to be used.

However, after searching around on the web, I found that this was really designed for when you brew loose tea in a teapot. You are supposed to swing the mesh strainer away from its base and position it over your teacup then pour your tea. The strainer will catch any loose leaves exiting the spout of the teapot. When you are done pouring your cup of tea, just swing the strainer over the drip bowl to catch any dripping liquid.

Unfortunately, this is too cumbersome to use. Also, you can only use it to pour one cup of tea because once the drip tray catches any liquid, the next time you swing out the basket the drip tray is perpendicular to the cup causing the liquid to spill out. In my search for the instructions on this gadget, I also found that everyone (not only on Amazon) rated this item five stars. I'm very surprised by this especially since the liquid spills out if you use it more than once before draining or washing the drip tray after each pour.

On the positive side it can be used to temporarily store a used teabag.

In summary, it is a nice novelty item / conversation piece. I purchased two and will definitely not purchase more. If you are looking for a great tea strainer, try [[ASIN:B002Q710ZY The Empress Tea Strainer]] instead (I purchased six of these and couldn't be happier).

Fits on all of my pots; works well sometimes; other times it's not so good; size wrong - 2.5 stars. First off, the size listed is incorrect. In summary, I am not pleased with this because the design is such that the pasta can go above the strainer.

Nice print but unfinished trim and double the price of Home Goods & TJX bags. I'm actually sorry I ordered these. These are the EXACT same size as the $.99 cent colorful plastic Home Goods and TJX bags that are sold in those stores and there is more variety there. The only difference between these bags and the store brand is that these are more than double the price, the trim is unkempt and extends at various lengths beyond the bags, and there is no logo on these bags (the only positive beside the print). 

These are tall, large, and moderately wide and will fit the same amount as the typical Home Goods bags. The paw print design is nice. However, I do not like the feel of the thin handles nor the trim extensions on the edges (see photo). The handles are a thin plastic and not cloth, so they cut into my hands. The cloth handles on the Home Goods/TJX bags are more comfortable to hold and last longer.

At the current price of $13.99, this comes to $2.33 per bag. At this price I could have purchased 14 bags at Home Goods instead of the 6 here. I expected these to be better quality and a little bit wider.

Pretty tray with glued on image and legs that might crack. This is not exactly as I expected. It is a wooden tray in a beautiful aqua color. However, the image is a decal that is just pasted on the top. I guess I just thought it would be stamped on in paint and then shellacked over but that is not the case. Also, the legs open up but I hear them cracking as I open and close them. I can see them establishing a crack in the wood over time. However, this tray can be used without the legs. It is pretty from a distance, but up close I am not as pleased. However, for the current price of $26.99, one gets what they pay for. I like this but not enough to recommend it or buy another one.

Griddle is perfect for making pancakes, omelettes, & crepes; this one heats just slightly unevenly. This is my third crepe maker. In March 2011, I purchased [[ASIN:B001EZCJL8 Cucina Pro Non-Stick 12" Crepe Maker]] on Amazon for $44.42. Then a year or two ago I ordered my favorite crepe maker -- the [[ASIN:B07822Z42M Proctor Silex 38400 Electric 13" Crepe Maker / Griddle]] (no longer available) -- because the Cucino Pro felt too small and seemed more like 10" instead of 12".

Nevertheless, once I discovered I could make omelettes on these, I wanted another one so that I have the option of having two going at the same time.

This Chefman 12" is large enough and comparable in size to my Proctor Silex. It comes with one SMALL wooden crepe spatula and one wooden batter spreader. The tools are not so great but they are good enough. I personally am unable to make any crepe, omelette, etc. without using two crepe spatulas simultaneously.

I decided to make a 4-egg omelette on this griddle. I lightly greased the surface with coconut oil, then turned the dial up to max as recommended. Once the green light came on, I turned the dial to about medium and poured my omelette mix out. After about one minute the egg was partially cooked (photo 1). When it cooked some more, I added my stuffings. I then folded over the sides and corners and let it cook some more. Once I had a neat package, I used two wooden crepe spatulas (one of which was mine) to flip it. The entire process took less than seven minutes. The last picture shows it plated.

This Chefman is good enough for the price. However, there are two things I do not like. First, the unit does not cook evenly. If you look at my photos, the upper right-hand corner is a bit uncooked compared to the lower left-hand corner. The issue is rather minor but it is obvious to me. My counter is level so it is the griddle itself. Second, the dial feels very flimsy and cheap. I feel it will break after lots of use.

One the positive side, it gets the job done. The tools are a starter set only and likely new ones will have to be purchased after a short time. The unit is low profile so it takes up less space when stacking in a cabinet.

Memory Foam in Pieces Pillow; nice pillow; lovely pillowcases. I ordered the small square pillow. It comes with one extra pillowcase besides the one that is on the pillow. The pillowcases are quilted and relativelhy soft and thick. I do like the ear hole as it helps a little when resting on my left side. I particularly love this when resting the back of my head in the hole of the pillow. It is actually very comfortable.

The disappointment came when I opened the pillowcase. The entire pillow is composed of hundreds of memory foam pieces left over from the manufacturing process. It is contained via a thin mesh type cloth similar to what food store reusable shopping bags are made of. This means that if it rips, memory foam will be all over the interior pillowcase and the pillowcase cannot be changed. In addition, about 14 years ago I paid over $80 for two pillows that I thought were solid memory foam and wound up throwing them out after several weeks because the composition shifted making the pillows useless.

I am not saying this will happen with this pillow. However, be aware that this is NOT a solid memory foam pillow. It is made of memory foam pieces.

Despite this, I still like this pillow. Only time will tell if it will last. The current price of $38.89 is on the high side for this considering it is made of what I consider "memory foam waste."

Beautiful presentation; gorgeous cup; verse in broken English & slightly imperfect. This is a gorgeous cat cup, saucer, and spoon set. The presentation is outstanding. It feels like quality. Unfortunately, there are some imperfections and the verse is not in good English.

This comes with a gift bag, a gift card, and a "Thank You" sticker to close the gift card. It also comes in an attractive well-padded box.

POSITIVES
- Presentation

- Sturdy china

- Very attractive

NEGATIVES
- My saucer has gold dots in spots; a cast off from the rim trim (see photo).

- Also my saucer has several faint gold smears on the edge (see photo).

- The verse on the plate is in broken English and says "One day I waked up and found myself surrounded by cats with curious faces, I called that feeling: happiness."  It should say woke up and there should either be a period or semicolon between "faces and I" and there should be no colon after the word feeling.

- The gift bag and card say "specially for you" which is okay as a sort of slang but I would have said "especially for you" instead.

In summary, this is beautiful at first glance and for that I give it 3 stars. However, for this to be giftable, the verse needs to be corrected to say:

"One day I woke up and found myself surrounded by cats with curious faces. I called that feeling happiness."

[[VIDEOID:b4a2b5e2989ba187c937e4a1108f84f2]] Coffee scales are best used by coffee connoisseurs who want to produce a perfect brew every time by balancing the time, flow rate, coffee weight, and finish weight of a brew. Not all coffee weighs the same tablespoon by tablespoon, which is why it is important to use a scale. With regard to coffee, I do not have such a discerning palate that I would be able to tell the difference between slight variations in a brew.
Nevertheless, the Timemore Black Mirror scales are often compared to other more expensive ($100 to $150 more) scales on the market. For those who do not want to break the bank on a coffee scale yet get most of the features, then the Timemore Black Mirror Basic Pro (this one) is an option.

I personally feel this is best for making pour over coffee although people have been known to use this with a coffee machine if it fits under the brew pot.

I tried this for several weeks and the most disappointing feature is that the flow rate disappears immediately after I stop pouring. Unless I can remember the rate, I would have liked it to stay on the screen. I watched many coffee scale videos and noticed the flow rate remains visible for about 5-10 seconds, so I do not know if this is defective or a work as designed.

Nevertheless, after having tried this, I feel using a scale with all these features is too much of a hassle. It also makes brewing coffee cumbersome to me. I find the beep annoying and dislike the disappearance of the flow rate. I do love the automatic mode and have not gotten the hang of the manual mode. I also do not like that the controls are difficult to remember if the sticker does not remain on the machine. The instructions are lackluster to me also. I do love that this unit is rechargeable, so that is a big plus. The current price of $54 ($69 minus 15) is competitively priced for this and this certainly offers some of the more advanced features of more expensive scales (except for Bluetooth and apps). To me, I do not need this.

Stylish iron; runs hotter than expected; wish it were cordless. I own a cordless Hamilton Beach iron that is over 26 years old. It is simple to operate and I love it. I expected this CHI iron to blow me away compared to my old one and to some extent it does but not totally.

I ironed a cotton shirt (see before and after photos in the last two pictures). What I discovered is that the temperature runs hotter than expected as the shirt material was adhering to the bottom of the iron. Therefore, when I put it on cotton, which is what the shirt is, it was too hot. The iron became "sticky" and it was difficult to move even though I used the spray and steam buttons to dampen the cloth. I even tried certain sections not damp but it was still "sticky." Instead I had to lower the temperature to wool in order to continue pressing the shirt.

Also, during ironing, the cord kept getting in the way even though it swivels. However, this is typical of any iron with an attached cord.

When I was done ironing, I had to get the debris left behind from ironing the cotton shirt off the faceplate. That came off easily by ironing over a damp 100% cotton cloth. I also had to clean the iron using the self-clean button. That did not work so well in the sense that water still remained in the iron after self-cleaning was done even after I rocked the iron back and forth over the sink while pressing the button. Instead I had to turn the iron over to drain out the remaining water.

PROS
- This iron is very stylish; it's almost like functional art (see photos).
- The cord swivels and has a Velcro tie for wrapping it up when done.
- The steam and spray buttons work very well.
- The iron is easy to fill with water.
- It heats up rapidly.
- Fabric selection is easily set.
- It is exceptionally easy to clean the soleplate.

CONS:
- The iron runs hotter than typical for the fabric selected. At least that is what I noticed with the cotton.
- The cord gets in the way of what is being ironed; however, that is typical of any corded iron not just this one.
- The self clean button does not steam out all the water as instructions seem to indicate.

In general, this is a nice iron that is almost a work of art. It heats up rapidly and cools down pretty quickly too. It irons well but the cord gets in the way of ironing. Also, the fabric temperature setting runs hotter than expected and self-clean does not release all the water. Nevertheless, it irons well as long as one lowers the temperature. Cleaning the soleplate is a breeze.
