Also, it is not as cushiony as I expected as I have other Chenille Bath Rugs that are much more plush. In addition, since this has a thin non-slip backing, this will not last many washes.

I consider this a budget-quality bathroom rug. Had I been able to sample this before I ordered it, I would never have selected it as it is not the quality I prefer.

Nevertheless, it is functional and does absorb some water when exiting the shower.

The current price of $14.99 is on the high side of competitively priced for this quality.

Alternative comforter – YES but definitely not goose down; very soft. I was going to give this at least 4.5 stars because it is so soft, fluffy, comfortable, and vibrant. However, the Amazon site is very misleading as it says it is goose down, then in the next sentence it says it is alternative. This comforter has box squares stitched to keep the "cotton" in place. It feels like airy cotton inside the comforter. I personally love the way it looks, although I expected a better match with my purple bedroom. This "wine" color is really a fuchsia or hot pink than wine and the reverse side is a light pink. I like using this without a duvet. However, if I wanted to cover it, there are loops in all four corners and in the center to hold it in place inside a duvet.

It is lightweight and warm enough. I have not washed this yet and will not do that until after I used it for several months. I am unsure how this will hold up in the wash. I suspect the cotton in the squares will bunch up and have to be smooth out or may remain lumpy. It should be washed in cold water and hung to dry. It is made in India of 100% microfibre.

Overall, I really love the comfort of this comforter and one of my three cats would not get off the bed once I put this down--so it is cat approved as well.

May not be space saving & weight of clothes may break rod; assembly required. There are six colorful "space-saving" hangers in this package. Each one requires a slight assembly of the hook onto the hanging structure. Once installed, the hook can be slid around the hanger to either sit horizontally like a regular hanger or vertically.

For me, these are not space saving at all. Instead it drops the level of the clothing down to my next rod level, interfering with the bottom of my closet. In addition, there is now a bulk of clothes that hangs down a little further away from the closet rod. Even if it were space saving, the weight of the extra clothes may bring down the rod. There are nine holes on the hanger, which means there is room for nine garments, so each hanger gets very heavy.

Therefore, I would consider these more like closet organizers that do not save space but enable one to hang the clothes neater in the closet. After having tried these, I know they do not work for me.

The current price of $16.99 brings this to $2.83 per plastic hanger.

A pocket scale designed more for jewelry; 9 weight measurements. [[VIDEOID:8088e7459c5eafb1cbd100e5665e391f]] This is the type of scale I use to weigh tea leaves. This is really a jewelry scale (gemstones and precious metals) that can be used for coffee or tea or food; although it is a bit small for food.

It comes with two AAA batteries and two plastic trays that act as both covers and a tray for using the tare feature. Also included is a lousy instruction sheet that doubles as an eye test since the writing is so small.

There are nine weighing units available as listed below. Note that the instruction sheet is useless and I had to do an Internet search to understand these weights.

gn = grain (based upon the mass of a single seed of cereal)
oz - ounces
ozt - troy ounces used for buying and selling precious metals
dwt = pennyweight from denarius weight (measures unit of mass)
ct = carat (for gemstones)
lb = pound
tl = tael, a unit of weight used in east Asia approximately equal to 1.3 ounce
ml = milliliter (for liquids)
g - grams

The PCS key is apparently a counting function but I have no clue how to use it. It tries to explain that but I could not get it to work.

The accuracy of this scale is a bit off but it is still functional and within a reasonable range of difference from my other scales. The current price of this scale is not listed but most scales like this range between $10 and $15.

Beautiful, but disappointed in sz difference. To begin with, these baskets are beautiful! The size difference is not going to work for me, the photos look like they’re the same size, but one is considerably smaller. I should have checked the specs, but I didn’t think I needed to!
Ok at best. Smaller than the pic.  made it look. No real support.  Ok if you're a Smaller person.

While this is a great idea and definitely does its job. While this is a great idea and definitely does its job, its poorly constructed. The light strip kept coming undone and falling which lead to wires breaking away from battery pack. If your SUPER careful ITS AWESOME!!
Missing items. Missing labels and marker
To heavy. To heavy for me.  If I bought another I would get 10 lb or less.

Lightweight, Very, Very Lightweight. This is about what you would expect for the money. It is very lightweight in contruction and in vacuum power. This would be OK for someone in a small apartment with no kids, pets or real people living there. The cord is pretty short. The thing that holds the attachments is poorly placed. All in all I wouldn't recommend it and it isn't going to make me forget about my 20 year old Eureka.
Flimsy Handle. Kind of flimsy plastic handle. It would work on soft things, but scraping natural peanut butter out of a jar is a challenge.

Not Working For Me. We get a lot of minimally processed fish and there are often lots of bones to be removed. I thought these would help, but it is very hard to get a grip on the bones without just breaking them off at the flesh. Well made, just don't work for me.

Almost Too Small To Be Functional. I've just spent the morning starting the annual garage clean put and reorganization. I have a floor to ceiling pegboard on one wall and it was in desperate need of straightening out. I got these shelves thinking that they would be useful in some way.

First the pros:

Made in the USA (imagine that)
Easy packaging
Easily Installed

The Cons:

Almost too small to be useful in any way. I suppose if you purchased a bunch of them and lined them up together they may be a little more effective. If you are just starting out as a new homeowner and have a few little screws and tools to keep track of this would be OK for you. If you, like me have been a homeowner for 35 plus years than this isn't even a drop in the bucket.

The shelf part of the trio is really too narrow to put much on.

The divided part is great and I think it would be better to just have 3 of those than 1 of each.

The shelf with the holes for screwdrivers didn't work at all for my tools. They didn't stay in place neatly. I did manage to use those slots for a bunch of spade drill bits which display in nicely.

All in all depending on the kind of organizing you need to do, it might be better to get one of those pegboard units with the little drawers instead.

Hard to Regulate Temperature. I got this oven to bake polymer clay on the recommendation of several different clay guilds. It is difficult to regulate the temperature which is a problem with any kind of "toaster" type oven. For the cost of this I thought it would control better.

If someone were going to use this as an oven, I would be very cautious sitting this on a counter. The top of the device gets VERY hot when in use and a napkin or something like that inadvertently laid on the top could ignite.

Plenty of room for baking clay or whatever, just needs to be better regulated heatwise.

Doesn't Cut Well. I just used this for the first time today. As some other folks said, it really doesn't cut the ravioli very well, which makes getting them out a bit of a problem. I would have been able to give this 4 stars instead of three, if it worked better.

The Perfect Chairs For a Small Area. I got these chairs for the bar in my new kitchen. They were exactly what I saw in my mind. The quality is about what you've come to expect from China for this amount of money. I expect they may last about a year with daily use. Assembly was easily accomplished with one person. They are attractive but a bit wobbly because I think  one of the bases was a little out of round. Overall a very cheaply made product, but it will suffice since there really aren't any other options.
Overpriced But Useful. These are great, the 3 stars are because all of these Command products are overpriced for what they are.

Poor Construction. I am not at all impressed with this set of peelers. They are cheaply made. They are sharp, but the handles are so crappy that you can only cut soft veggies with them. Worked good on squash and cucumbers, but fell apart on a small new potato. I would not recommend these to a friend.

Charging Issues. I've been waiting awhile to review this in hopes that my issue would resolve itself. It hasn't. I love this vacuum except for the fact that sometimes it doesn't charge correctly. I have a small house with 98% hard surface floors and I use this everyday at about the same time to clean up cat litter sprinkles and other light debris. Some days I can do the whole house, no problems. Then randomly I will get one room done and it will stop and need to be charged.  Kind of a bummer. I had a Bissel Bolt Pet, that was terrific until it finally died after years of use. Never had a charging problem with that and it cost half as much.

Sort Of "Useful". Since we are over run with squash right now I decided to try this noodle thing that everyone is talking about. I looked a t bunch of these spiral gadgets and decided, based on reviews, that I'd try this one.

Pros:
Works well doing zucchini and turning it into noodles
The blade storage is handy.

Cons:

Kind of bulky. Takes up a chunk of cabinet space.
No little "tabs" as stated on the box to help you disengage the suction cups. This sucker stuck to my granite countertop and wouldn't let lose.
The instructions are OK, but keep the box because that's the only place the blades are described by function

The quality is about what you would expect for the price. I expect it to last about as long as my fascination with veggie noodles.

Nonstick But That's About It. I'm always looking for an upgrade in kitchen equipment. This isn't one of them. I saw this and mistakenly thought it was like the ones you use in hotels. Not even close. Poorly constructed of the finest plastics China has to offer. It heats up faster than my old iron, but the product produced isn't anywhere near the caliber we are used to. The waffles come out easily, but even at the highest setting they are gummy and not crispy. My old Proctor Silex model takes a while to do a waffle, but they come out as light and airy and crispy as a feather. Besides, this thing takes a ton of space to store!

Uninspiring Product. A bit disappointed with this product. The quality is mediocre at best. This only fits over a standard interior door. Will not fit a metal door. The finish is kind of fragile. I actually managed to scratch it up removing it from the packaging. I think it says this is a satin finish, but it is not like any other "satin" finish I've seen. Kind of cloudy over the metal. Don't expect this to hold very much weight besides some light clothes or jackets. Might be good for a bathroom at best.
Just OK. Been replacing my original gaskets with these for several weeks now. They are OK, not as thick as others I have had.
Large Is Relative. These are nice liners, but were not large enough for my purposes. Did not fit a large muffin pan.

Disappointing To Say The Least. I would like to give this 1 star for not working and 5 stars for product quality. I have a large heavy duty stainless Blanco sink in my new kitchen. These would be very handy if only they stuck to the metal. They stick to my stainless dish drainer, but not to the sink. Not being aware that this should be " installed" prior to the sink being set, I thought it might work. Unfortunately I am not enough of a contortionist to crawl in the cabinet, stand on my head and try to line up my trifocals so I can "install" the included magnetic tape that might work.
The quality of the product is first rate. Heavy and well made. If you are building or remodeling and getting ready to set a sink, than give this a try. It could be probably work after market if you have a plumber or someone nimble enough to get in under there and place the tape.
Not Easy To Use. Still got my cake stuck even in this kind of pan.

Difficult To Clean After Use. I used this to cook some bacon this morning. I usually just do this on parchment paper in the oven. I used this instead. I was OK, but just. The worst part was trying to get it cleaned up afterwards. I used everything in my arsenal and it was a real bear to get into all the grooves and crevices. This seemed like a valid concept, but I'm not real pleased.

OK For Light Use. Once again another disappointing appliance. I already have a T-Fal fryer that is awesome. I got this one for those times when you want some more fryer space when entertaining. I knew right out of the box that it wasn't as nice as the one I have. Not nearly as heavy. Could be due to the fact that this one doesn't have an oil reservoir and has to be drained into the bottle after use. Nice digital controls that are really not necessary. If you are frying and setting a time that's not a good thing. Best to always be paying attention to what is in the fryer. I make a lot of potato chips. The directions in the book for this machine say to cook them for 17 minutes. Really!? Talk about burnt to a crisp.

The plug to this is magnetic, like my other one, but this plug won't stay in at all. Barely makes connection and the slightest bump makes it fall out. Not as deep as I was expecting and doesn't hold as much oil either.

The little door that opens in the front to drain the oil is cheap.

It cleans up easily, but I will only be using it on rare occasions. Bottom line, get a T-fal. Better machine.

Bad Glaze. I rather thought that this being Lennox and made here in the USA that it would be a better quality. I have done ceramic work for most of my life and this piece is very obviously over glazed. So much so that the decal work is fuzzy and not very distinct. The leaf pattern is almost non existent. Nice enough to use as a watering can I suppose. Overall I'm not that excited about it.

Not Absorbent. Gorgeous springy colors. 100% cotton. They are nice and absorbent. The stitching seems solid even though they are made in India. For my taste they are a little on the small size. They are a little smaller than the size of a standard washcloth. With shrinkage, they are kind of small. Otherwise a great addition to any cooks kitchen.

UPDATE: I have changed my review from 5 to 3 stars. After washing and using these for several weeks, they are NOT absorbent at all and are pretty, but useless for washing dishes. 100% cotton should be better than this, so I am skeptical that they truly are cotton and not some blend.

Heavy and Unbalanced. I really wanted to like this but there are quite a few design issues that prevent me from giving this more than 3 stars.

Likes:
Assembles easily
Dirt cup empties well. No filter in the middle to get everything hung up on.
OK suction out of the box. But most of these kinds of vacs are good for about 6 months before they start to decline in that regard.

Dislikes:
Very heavy and poorly balanced. I have a one level house and by the time I had gone around one room getting the dust bunnies, my shoulder was aching. This thing is very lightweight from the floor attachment upwards. The motor is disproportionately heavy causing a continual struggle to keep the vacuum grounded to the floor. When held at a comfortable angle, the motor practically lifts the floor attachment off the floor. I cannot honestly see doing anything over your head with this.

In that same vein, I put the stair attachment on to go over some furniture. Awful balance. It is a constant struggle to hold this without it trying to turn over in your hand.

The battery when fully charged barely lasted for the 15 minutes it took to go from one end of my house on one level and 3 pieces of furniture before the indicator was showing low.

This will be relegated to a back up vacuum when my Hoover of a similar style dies.

Kind of Low End Quality. A bit disappointed in this product. I have had other items from this manufacturer that were to notch. This is sort of yard sale quality. It is not long enough or deep enough to be of any benefit in my cabinets. I suppose if you have smaller spaces it would be great. It just isn't wide enough front to back and you lose space because of that. Easy to adjust for the height, but doesn't seem sturdy enough to me to hold much weight. Hard plastic shelf that seems very susceptible to cracking. All in all I would not purchase this.

No Waffle Plates. Let me first say I am a real hard case when it comes to kitchen gadgets. They have to really WOW me to get a good review. I was hoping that this would be a WOW considering the cost. More of a EH.. Let's start with the good.

It's a good size. I have an older version of this that the plates don't come out of. Have used it for years and love it. This is probably twice as big and easier to clean.
It's heavy and seems pretty well made.
The plates are very heavy and well made compared to other grills like this that I have reviewed. They also have their own heating elements built in so that there is a better heat distribution.

The cons:
No waffle plates with this model. I was so hoping to get rid of a waffle iron and use this. That was not clear in the ordering information I had. I see it on the regular product page way down at the bottom. Easy to overlook.

The sear function is very brief. Have your meat ready to go and don't dally or you will miss it and it can not be restarted for 30 minutes.

My machine has an area of chipped and blistered paint right out the box along the edge where the plates sit. Not sure how long that will hold out under heat stress.

Getting the lid to hold position for the broil feature is a tricky balancing act.

The plates are removable, but they are also kind of tricky to get in and out. You have to wiggle around to get them to seat.

Very short cord which is difficult to reach an outlet with.

Sticky residue on the hinges and some of the moving parts that was awful to get off before first use.

Personally I wouldn't spend the money for this. It is disappointing in a lot of ways.

Very Disappointing. I really wanted and needed a pepper grinder and I still need one. This little gadget only holds a very little bit of peppercorns. It will be fine for table use only as you have to work very hard to get a little bit of pepper out. As for spices, I have no idea what they thought is going to go into this small diameter tube as far as spices go. You might be able to force some fennel seed in there, but certainly not much else. Very disappointing.

Quality Machine With Instruction Manual Issues. Plastic Taste. I am impressed with most aspects of this product.

Pros:
Appears to be well made and well put together
Fairly small footprint for an office or studio space. Pretty self contained.
Can be connected by non plumbing personnel but having some experience helps.
Hot water in a flash
Great tasting cold water no bottles involved.
So far no leaking issues.

Cons:
Basically the instructions are kind of goofy. Missing steps and things not mentioned. The pictures could definitely be a little bigger and show all the steps involved, not just some of them. There seem to be some steps missing and I can see people having problems with connections and things not working because of it.

There needs to be more complete information about the features of the machine and what to expect when you turn it on etc. My self cleaning light is on and I can't figure out if it should be or not. Nothing on the website or the manual. Really incomplete.

It would be nice if there was some way to tidy up the connections and tubing that hangs all over the back of this.

This bills itself as a "countertop" model, but there are no instructions for how you would make this work on a counter as far as making the connections, etc. If I wanted to use this in say a kitchen, I would imagine you would have to drill a hole through the counter for the water line. That would not be nice if you have granite counters.

This will work quite well in my art studio, providing me with good drinking water no bottles involved, and the ability to make hot drinks as well.

UPDATE: Changing my review to 3 stars instead of 4. After using this for several days and following all the instructions, the cold water from this tastes like plastic unless you waste a bunch running it out. According to the instructions you should run a quart of water through in the beginning. I did this. But every morning after the machine has set overnight the first bit tastes like plastic. I have a well, so my water tastes great to start with.

Overpriced Item. My first thought when I opened the box was that this is very overpriced. The only metal parts are the base and the center post. The things the boots hang on are plastic. Considering you can only hang 5 pairs of boots, it is really a lot of sugar for a cent. I got this to clean up the garage of all the farm boots, which are heavy and always pretty nasty. You have to grab the boots by the sole or ankle to put them on the hooks. Great. I really want to play in the chicken crap to get my boots on the rack.
Second thing you need to know is that the center post is in sections. One of those sections is longer than the other 4. Unfortunately the way the box is packed, that's the last one you came to. So my rack is too short on the bottom and the bottom pair of boots drags on the ground. I know, I could take it apart, but the thing is difficult to get sturdy and I'm not up for that.
Stability is OK, but the center post wobbles.
All in all I would never buy this. Too much money for not a very large benefit.

Just OK. This product is just OK in my mind. It seems sturdy enough to at least stack several boxes of shoes at a time. The box itself will hold one pair of shortish boots only, or 2 pairs of shoes. Unfortunately for me I would need a mountain of these to hold the shoes I have. Not sure what the price point on these is, but I think they aren't a really viable option for shoe storage.

Very Lightweight. First off there are no assembly instructions. Look at the box and work it out I guess. Which I did. For a few shelves, until I realized that it wasn't worth the effort to put together all those little connectors and pipes. Not very sturdy and nothing that I can use in my house. Was hoping since it said multi functional that it would be good for something other than shoes, but it wouldn't really  hold  a couple of boxes of wet noodles.

Pretty "Basic". These are plastic frames with a cheap finish. From a distance they don't look too bad. The corners are mitered well and they seem to be sturdy. I give away a lot of artwork and they will be useful for that, but by no means are they very expensive looking or particularly attractive.

Sort Of Works. After watching a lot of commercials I decided I needed one of these. I used it in my studio for cleaning up my drawing table. Had a fair amount of issues with it getting clogged up. It has a lot of suction and it grabs big and small things and you have to keep picking stuff of the bristles. I think it would be fine for use in kitchen drawers, but not so much where there is a combination of fine debris mixed with larger bits. The larger bits present a problem.

I Will Work. Interesting item.  Kind of weird how it works and folds up. Several of the bottoms of the legs were loose in the box on the one I got. Getting them on was tricky. It will do the job for a plastic piece of crap.

Wonky Shape. Interesting. I got a plate to review last week from this same set and manufacturer. I was 5 star impressed. This bowl, not so much. It isn't round and it is very wavy. It may be by design to look handmade, but in any event the shape is kind of odd and strange. Seems well made, just looks really wonky.

Not My Style. Kind of crude and rustic.  Has a rope wrapped handle that you don't really see in the picture.  Fairly large and of an undetermined style. No price listed, but I can guarantee it isn't worth it. Moderate quality. If it had a lid it would be a good birdcage. Actually I think I might put a vining plant in it.
Not Great. Poor value. You can get marbles like this at Micheals or JoAnns for a fraction of the price. Nothing at al special about these. Not smooth, lots of chill marks on them and inconsistent.

Worthless Assembly Instructions/ Faulty Design. This arrived several days ago and I finally assembled it today.

1. The box was severely damaged. Fed Ex had taped it back together, but the bottom insert of the drawer was damaged.
2. Assembling this according to the instructions, which are somewhat nebulous (no text, just pictures and arrows and little juvenile smiley faces), took the better part of 3 hours. So plan accordingly. I have a lot of experience with these kinds of things, so I'm no dummy. No issues with screws or holes. Everything did fit together once it was figured out.
3. The quality is about what you would expect for pressed "wood".
4. Crappy drawer construction. I would not overload the drawer, or put much weight on the upper section of this.
5. The extra USB ports are totally useless if you have a printer sitting in the only place it will fit. The cable won't even reach to the computer if you don't have tower. The USB ports were one of the reasons I got this. Bummer

To summarize, this is pretty much what you would expect for the money. Might last a few years if you don't overload it or try to move it around much.

Pretty Flimsy. I'm not in love with these bags. They are pretty flimsy and not well made. No reinforced bottoms to help them stand up. They are also very long and not too tall. This presents a problem if you use the self checkouts. These bags don't fit on the sensor well at all and hang out everywhere causing read errors.  Not the best shopping bags I have ever gotten.

Eh.... What is very hard to see in the picture is that these are not solid stainless cast as one piece. They have cheap plastic color bands on a separate handle and really look bad. The bag is nice enough to keep them all together and they will work for our annual fondue party. I don't expect them to have a long life expectancy.

Didn't Work Well For Me. I've been waiting to have a loaf of bread that these would fit on. They are really rather pre-shaped as if they had used a loaf of bread and then dipped it in the silicone. What I found is that if your bread didn't conform to the shape of this cap, it didn't really seal the end very well and the bread dried out. I really wanted this to work but was disappointed.

Cheap Imitation. This mop and bucket are a very poor imitation of the O'Cedar brand I currently have and love.  This has no foot pedal so you have to spin the mop by hand which doesn't really get it that dry. The handle, mop and bucket are really kind of flimsy. I got this to use outside because I didn't want to use one of my good ones for washing porches and siding. It might work OK because it doesn't matter so much if the mop is still pretty wet and drippy. The threads on this are also backwards, so be aware when you are putting it together. Counter clockwise. If you want a good bucket for house cleaning, get the O'Cedar.

What A Waste. Three stars is being generous for this. I needed a new mini chopper and thought I would take a chance on this one.
Pros:
It has an insert that you can use if you only have a small amount of something to chop

Cons:
Cheap, cheap, cheap
Be sure you inspect and clean the parts very well before the first use because there were all kinds of loose plastic strands in mine.
The cord wrap on the bottom is positively useless
It comes with a built in spatula. Why bother? It is is hard to get the spatula lined up in the storage place.
Said spatula storage place makes it impossible to store upright in a drawer, therefore taking up as much space laying down as a regular sized processor.

All in all I wish I had kept my Kitchen Aid and lived with it's quirks.

Difficult To Use. Where oh where to begin.. I'm not sure that even Mrs. Jetson would have used this.

Pros:
It has a very long cord that makes it easier to use without having to move from plug to plug.
Excellent suction and really picked up a lot of fur and dust.

Cons:
Poorly shipped. This is the only problem I ever have with Amazon. They don't ship large items very well. The outer box this came in was open and had been resealed and was crushed. The inner box with the vacuum was mangled and I had to slit open the whole box to get the vacuum out.

Very difficult to assemble. The instructions are fairly useless. One set on the hang tag suggests one assembly, the manual another. I have assembled 2 level bookcases without as much grief as this vacuum.

For something that is 99% plastic it is VERY heavy and difficult to maneuver. I banged into the legs of all my furniture trying to turn this. I thought that was one of the big selling points for Dyson was their ease of mobility. Not in my experience at all. The big ball does not allow it go under anything.

Emptying the dust bin is a nasty business.

To sum it up, there are a lot of less expensive vacuums with good suction out there. The execution of this machine is way too overwrought.
Does not appear to have any onboard storage for the attachments. Shows some in the diagrams, but I couldn't figure it out.

Not That Great. This really doesn't look a lot like the picture as far as color. It is a space suit silver metallic color. The handles are well attached. It doesn't keep it's shape very well. There is a sewn in wire around the top that is I guess supposed to help keep it round, but doesn't. Somehow I was expecting something sturdier and heavier and more functional. It will find a use, but not where anyone can see it.

YES It Slices, BUT.... I was fully prepared for this to not work at all. I make my own bacon and smoked turkey for sandwiches. Cutting the bacon is a pain and I thought I would try this. There are many limitations.

Pros:
It does slice. I partially froze my homemade bacon and it cut it very well

Cons:
Limited instructions. Not much help as far as putting it togther, and virtually none about getting it apart.

Very hard to use. The safety feature on this means that you have to depress 2 buttons and hold them while you are slicing. All this while trying to manage the carriage and feed your food into the blade.

The platform is barely large enough to slice anything meaningful. To do the bacon I had to take the moving parts out of the grooves to make my slab fit on the platform.

The setting for thickness needs to be constantly adjusted. It moves on it's own and before you know it you are getting thicker and thicker.

Exceptional hard to clean. This is the part that worries me the most. The part that folds up at the bottom doesn't come off. Food is trapped in that juncture between the platform and the machine/blade. No instructions on taking the blade off either. But there is a slot in the center hub to lock and unlock the lad. Use a screwdriver and then I used the screw driver to carefully release the blade. I wiped the not removable parts the best I could with hot soapy water on a cloth, and then finally took some clorox wipes and went over all the nooks and crannies.

Very cheaply constructed and I expect this to last no more than a year before the plastic parts crack or break.

All in all, it will cut, but not much more.

Interesting. This is an interesting item. Looks a lot like a tablecloth, or maybe a serape. Not much like a "towel". Not at all absorbent and not very soft. Very odd smell when it got wet. Very thin material.  Nice colors and pattern. The fringe is kind of flimsy. Might be nice as a beach blanket type thing. Overall it's just kind of well, interesting.

Flimsy. Unfortunately this is a failed experiment. I was hoping to use it in my guest closet where I store vacuum bags and parts. Kind of get everything together and off the floor.  This has a good Velcro strap at the top that fits over your rod or rail. That isn't the problem. The problem is the "shelves" themselves have not sturdiness. They are just cardboard and as soon as you start to put things on them, they bend. I didn't get more than a pack of bags and 2 brushes on it when the combined weight caused it to sag. I'm not sure what this would be intended for. Maybe ballet slippers, but not much more.
Just OK. I got white bins not the color pictured. They are low quality, but will work fine in kitchen and bathroom drawers. Easy to connect and a variety of configurations can be made with the set.

Strange  "Towels". These are different towels than I am used to. One side is terry cloth and the other side is smooth.  Not very plush by any means. Because the picture was poor and there was no description, I will tell you that these have a pale pink stripe on them. Had I known that I wouldn't have gotten them. These "towels" are more like a baby blanket than a bath towel and I think they should be described in that manner.  I really can't recommend these as towels, but if you need a baby shower item, these would work.
Sharp Edges. This is just like one my friend has except for the extremely sharp edge along one side.  Almost cut myself putting it into the dishwasher.

Another  Piece of Plastic. Once again an item delivered with no instructions. There are 3 miscellaneous plastic pieces included. Finally figured out that they are supposed to be dividers for the bins. The bins are so small that dividers seem unnecessary. very thin side panels. Not very sturdy. I'm hoping it will still work as a piece of display furniture on my art vending table.
Nothing Spectacular. Just a simple rubber dish drainer. The only thing exceptional is the ability to roll it up and close it. Who does that anyway?

Not Very Scented. These seem to be a good value for sure, but they are not very heavily scented.  In fact I couldn't really smell the scent at all until I put one in a warmer and melted it. They do seem to burn very cleanly. Might be fine for a gift, but not something I would buy.

Nifty Idea. UPDATE:

I DECIDED TO DEDUCT A STAR FOR THESE AFTER TRYING TO CLEAN ONE. IT IS NOT AN EASY PROCESS. ANY FOOD THAT COMES IN CONTACT WITH THE WAX IS STUCK FAIRLY WELL. iN COLD WATER THERE ISN'T MUCH TO DO TO CLEAN THEM. I CAN SEE A LOT OF ISSUES WITH FOOD CROSS CONTAMINATION USING THESE. THEY WILL WORK FOR HARD CHEESES, BUT I WON'T USE THEM FOR ANYTHING ELSE. NOT EVEN COVERING A BOWL.

Been wanting to try these for a long time. I opened the pack and wrangled loose the smallest sheet to wrap a piece of cheese in. This stuff is really sticky and stuck together. I tried to warm it a little I my hands to get it to be flexible as per the instructions. It conforms to whatever you are wrapping very well and it stays stuck closed. The downside is that you can't see through it, so if I wrap a bunch of cheese in these for instance, the only way to tell what's what is by the size or shape assuming I can remember which is what. Time will tell how well they hold up.

Small. I guess I missed the dimensions in the description. I have several waterfall type burners that are twice the size. This is not big and therefore the effect is diminished. Comes with cones and sticks since there is a place to burn a stick as well. Pointy tweezers which are extraneous. Boring color pallet.  Came backed in a padded envelope so the box was crushed. Luckily not broken.  Extremely boring. Wouldn't buy one on a bet.

Lovely Artwork. I am kind of bummed with this product. The enamelwork and art is very attractive and fun. The cup is a really nice size. The issues are in quality control. Imagine that? One tumbler seems thicker and better made than the other. Neither of the, are suitable for drinking out of due to the rims being rough in places from an over run of the enamel process.  I'll be using these for non drinking purposes only.

Some Issues. This has the potential to be a 5 star item it just falls a little short.

Pros:

Comfortable
Nice cover
Seems well made for the most part.

Cons:
The item I got will not fold completely flat. The headrest is stuck kind of folded over and no matter how I follw the instructions I can't get it loose.
This is very narrow. Only acceptable for a child, thin teenager or smallish woman. A full sized male or bigger woman is going to hang out on either side of this. Also not for very tall people.
The back is kind of sturdy without any support behind it, but it doesn't seem like it will stay in place for very long.
There is also a center of gravity issue with this. If you don't sit in it just right it rolls back and falls over which is dangerous. I was trying this out on a hard surface floor to see if it would move or stay in place, and it flipped me straight back into the coffee table.

Close, but no cigar folks.

Bark Is Peeling. These little goobers are a good idea, just not too well executed. They are a natural product I get that. Several of mine had lose bark on them that was coming off. I know I could glue it back, but that's kind of a pain. I painted one to use on my desk to hold art cards that I trade. The base is sturdy. They aren't particularly smooth on the surfaces if you are planning to wood burn or art on them.
Plastic Crap. Another crappy spatula even if it is Kitchen Aid. Will probably get about 6 months out of it before it ends up in the trash can.

Not The Best. I've been waiting to use this for just the right thing. I have a lot of Cornus kousa fruit on my trees and they need to have the seeds and skin removed to get the pulp for cooking. Normally I use a very old chinois strainer that was my grandmother's and work it through that. I was hoping that this would be a better solution. It was almost impossible to turn with the seeds that are in this fruit. I would imagine if you were doing something smoother it would be fine, but if it's already smooth, why would you?

Easy to assemble and it will be easy to clean. Just won't work well for me for this particular purpose. MIght be fine for seeding tomatoes but it really doesn't hold that much in the first place.

Needs Improvement. First let me say that this is a very well constructed machine. I have no problem with the grinder mechanism or container from a quality standpoint. I do think there are several things that would make it easier to use.

First off it needs a wider base. When you are grinding it is moving all over the counter because the top is heavier than the bottom.

Something to hold on to around the diameter would be helpful. I have decreasing hand strength and trying to hold the slick outer surface of this while grinding was a grind. LOL

It took me at least 7 minutes to grind enough for one cup of coffee in my Keurig. If you need to grind a lot, this isn't your machine.

Some guidance on the number you should use based on the coffee maker you have would be useful as well.

It would be nice if the handle flipped over for storage because as it is now it does take some space to store.

Stop With The Drawstring Bags!!. Packaging on all of this stuff ridiculous. Everything comes in a drawstring bag. What a waste. Anyway these gloves have potential if your hands are large enough. I have small hands and they don't fit well in the fingers ergo I don't have much claw control.  They work OK in loose mulch or soil as long as you keep pulling them up. Probably wouldn't buy them outright.

Nice Pot, Wonky Lid. Attractive cookware. Well made pot. I had to deduct a star because the lid I got is warped and does not fit the pot correctly or tightly. It rocks back and forth. Love the handles as they are easy to grip for older hands and they don't heat up. Perfect size for a batch of marinara, or a moderate soup or stock amount. This can go in the dishwasher which is fab, because the inside will clean and the outside is coated to prevent etching. If my lid fit, I would be giving 4 or more stars
Functional. Smallish basket would hold a hot dog and some fries maybe. Not that well made for long term use. I think I will use it for a small planter type idea I have.

See Through Thin. When someone says beach towel to me it evokes a certain expectation. Thick, soft, plush and absorbent. This is none of the above. You can read your phone through it. It is scratchy and barely dries off the smallest bit of water.  Big fail for me. I can not recommend this product.

Disappointing Finish Work. I will first say that this is one of the best constructed and heaviest items I've had to review in a long time. Well made for sure. Unfortunately it ends there. The hooks are all just slightly off center. Canted a it to the right or the left. It was spray stained and very unevenly at that. No hanging hardware, just 2 holes drilled through the top. The worst thing is the text at the top is totally not centered up between the hanging holes. This could have been an awesome product if more attention was given to the fit and finish.

Light Use. I would recommend this burner for infrequent light use only. It is not the best quality at all. It does heat up fast and hot. When I put an empty pot on it to test what it would hold, it started popping and creaking and pinging like crazy. Nothing in the pot, just a heavy duty stainless pan. Would probably be fine for a college dorm room or camping. I'm hoping it will work for me just as a warming burner during entertaining. Very short cord for safety and needs to be out at least 4 inches from the wall.  Worked OK on my island, but on a regular counter I'm not sure I would be too thrilled.

Couple of Problems. This works pretty well and seems to be heavy and well made. The issues I dislike are the fact that you can't see a fuel level anywhere.  Most importantly I was unable to get this to bend at any angle and the instructions that come with it are useless. I don't want to damage the torch, but it would be really nice if it bent the way it is supposed to.
Well Made But Fussy. I found this really hard to use. Hard to fill consistently and difficult to unmold. It's such a small little ball it isn't worth the trouble.
Flimsy. These seem to be kind of thin and flexible. I guess they will work for stirring coffee but that's about it. Don't think of using them for paint or resin like I planned to.

Pros and Cons. It looks good once it is together. The together part is the problem. The starter holes for the clamps that allow this to be put together and then taken apart, are marked, but aren't anywhere close to lining up with the holes in the clamps.  That little snafu causes a larger problem. This isn't a folding table in the normal manner. The top is actually a separate piece that needs to be totally removed so that you can fold in the sides. Then you can lay it flat and store the 2 pieces together. THEY ARE NOT CONNECTED.  Because the starter holes for the clamps don't line up, if there is variation in the clamp placement, the top is difficult to get on and off. In fact I didn't think I would be able to get the top on. It would connect to 3 of the 4 clamps. So I took it of and tried it in a different rotation and finally got the top on. That last connection is hard though.  Once it is together is is sturdy, but frankly it isn't easy to take apart and put together. If that's what you are looking for this isn't it.

Poor Engineering. I always have high hopes that these things will be better than they are. This rack is held together by ONE hinky screw that doesn't even go all the way through the metal because the pieces are bent and don't line up.  The picture shows this stacked with kindling too. In actuality it holds about 3 pieces of real wood.
Too Plain For My Plan. This is a really nice, well made mold. It just lacks detail. Would be fine for cake, but pretty plain for anything else.

All The Same. If you have used the old school sprouter lids you'll remember that they are different sizes based on the seeds you want to sprout. These have all the same kind of wire mesh in them which I suppose is OK if you are doing the same thing all the time.  The klugey little stands are kind of overkill.

No Instructions Included. This could have been a 5 star review if they would include some instructions on use besides a small diagram on the box. I figured it out, but it annoys me enough that I deduct stars when I have to do that. I plan to use this for making feta cheese in place of a large press.

Assembly Difficult. Just once I would like to  say that putting something from China together was easy. Unfortunately this isn't it. Lousy diagrams.  Took three times longer than it should have.  Once it's together it is pretty sturdy, but not overly big. Maybe good enough for kids, but not that terrific for an adult.

Very Small. These are about 8 inches long. I never knew they made them this small. They align well at the jaws and the lock that holds them together is good. Otherwise if you are expecting normal sized tongs these aren't it.

Pretty. I was hoping to use this as a planter. The baskets however are not fixed in place and swing back and forth. Easy to assemble and sturdy enough. Not sure I'd use this to store things in because if you overfill the baskets, things are going to fall out if it moves.

Very Hard To Use. I'd been wanting one of these for a long time. All the ads make it look so effortless. I decided to try mine out on some banana bread this morning. Tried to use it to cream the butter and sugar. Couldn't make it happen. Didn't work to mash and stir the bananas either. Frankly it was useless to me and I ended up getting the mixer out. Was going to try it on some bread dough that I did today as well, but decided it wasn't worth the mess.

The product itself is very sturdy and well made. I just don't have the hand strength at my age to get it to work.
Inconsistent Coating. I haven't tried these yet, but right upon opening, I discovered areas where the coating is flawed.

Could Be Wider. This is needs to be extra large in the width to carry anything more than a few sandwiches. Any container that may have leftovers or things like that would have be turned on it's side or else placed right in the very center of the bag which doesn't allow for it to be closed.  Disappointing.
It Works. About what you would expect for the price. The lid doesn't seat very well on the base, but it works.

Don't Throw Away Your Box Grater. This arrived today just as I was getting ready to shred some cabbage for slaw. I washed the parts an pieces and thought I would give it a try. What I know:

Skimpy directions on the box. What good is that if I plan to discard the box.
No clear pictures of what the cutting discs produce.
The grater turned my cabbage into mince.
It sticks well to the counter in fact so well that I almost broke the cheap plastic handle off doing a carrot.
No mention of whether it is dishwasher safe.

All in all I won't give up my bent up box grater for this gadget.

A Solid Three. So many issues...

The wand is too short. I'm 5'2" and If it's short for me, it's too short
The attachments don't have a home on the vacuum. They come in a little bag and you have to keep track of where you put them
The attachments are weak and lame. Not very robust at all.
The hose doesn't stay attached to the wand very well. This has pretty good suction so sometimes the floor brush gets stuck and the hose just comes off the wand.
The wheels get caught on things. Something about the dynamic or the placement of the wheels made this hard to drag around objects. It kept getting caught.
Emptying is a mess. As soon as you pop the bottom of the canister there is dust everywhere.

The good..
Has great suction. In fact so much that it was hard to use on my rubber matted studio floor. Kept wanting to pull up the floor even on low.

Issues. This is well constructed but there are some issues. The handles are way too small for anyone to get their fingers in there.  I was going to use this for a resin project, but the depth to the bottom of the handle isn't deep enough. The resin will just run out the handle. Not useful for my purposes.

Eh.... This is just OK. I don't like the way it fits in the base. Anytime something is engineered like that there is a weakness and a wobble.  This will work OK if you have tiny cups or small mugs. The way the hooks are laid out doesn't allow for a larger mug to hang on all the hooks without banging into whatever is hanging above or below it.

Pretty Small. I'm not really sure these are going to work for baking. They are way too small. Maybe holds 1/4 of a cup allowing for something to rise and not run over.  They are cute, but not functional.
Not Quite. Always looking for a good kitchen gadget. I have lots of ChefN products. This one falls quite short of the mark. Cheaply made. Hard to use. Hard to clean. I would not recommend.

Not Like The Picture. These do not fit together like the ones in the picture. There is about a one inch gap between the side piece that slides into the center piece. This means the shelves do no match up and are not the same width. The photo also shows that there are 3 pieces, 1 center and 2 sides, but I only got 2 pieces.  Not very useful and not well made.

Kind of Pale. Most of the flowers I got are really crinkled up from being stuffed in the packaging. The colors are also not as vibrant as the picture. These are double layered, so they don't lay very flat, and they have a place on the bottom that you could insert a stem if you wanted to. Some of the centers of the flowers are a really ugly color. ,I was hoping to use these in a fairly flat application, but will have to rethink.

Works Sort Of. This is just OK. I tried some rosemary the other night and it works, but you have to pull against the leaves and not with them to get them off. The direction they show in the picture doesn't work at all.

Not Really Very Absorbent. I washed these and used one today. I think they will need to be washed many times to get soft enough to be absorbent. Whatever kind of sizing is in these repels water. You can wring out the dish cloths pretty dry, but they still leave a lot of water behind when wiping a counter.

That Awful Smell. WOW! They warn you in the instructions that the first time you use this it will smell. Boy howdy. I finally had to turn it off and go to my regular stove because the smell was unbearable. It does get very hot and seems to be controllable. The knobs seem to me to be  oriented oddly. It's like they couldn't decide which way was up or down and just put them on at an angle. Easy to clean. Will use it for cooing outside to try to mitigate the awful odor.

Cheap and Tacky, But Pretty Sort Of. This is so cheaply made, I'm surprised it survived the shipping. It is pretty when the lights come on though.  In other words it will look good in the dark. Kind of like a bar at closing time. LOL

Engineering Problem. On first look these measuring spoons are a cooks dream come true. Everything included to make it easy for anyone who is math challenged. For instance a 2 tsp. measure. LOL.  Everyone needs one of those. (Ahem).. I digress. These are very heavy. Nicely made. The engineering problem being that the clip that is supposed to hold all this happiness together is a crappy piece of bent up metal that doesn't even begin to stay closed.  Could have been a big win. Now it's just a waste of space. I like the included leveler though. Very handy.

Plastic. I haven't had an electric can opener for years. I don't open many cans so a manual opener has been fine. Unfortunately I have advancing arthritis and manual is getting harder to achieve. I thought I'd try this. I am less than thrilled. it does work. It is almost entirely plastic and has no weight to it. One of the touted features is that you can hit the button and you don't have to hold the can or the opener. Yeah that works too, but the opener is so cheap and light that it shimmies all over the counter while it is opening. In the old days these used to have at least a metal mechanism. This one has a metal blade and the handle of it is plastic. When you push it down the whole thing kind of gives. Don't expect it will do well in the dishwasher although that is supposed to be another one of the many "benefits". I wouldn't recommend this at all and will only use it as a last resort.

Disappointing To Say The Least. Bought this based on the reviews and am now rather surprised that it was rated so high. The only thing I like about this ladle is that it hooks to the pan. I just finished canning some Sweet and Spicy Tiger Sauce and had the biggest mess I've ever made. This ladle DOES NOT fill an 8 ounce jar. It overfills it all over the place. It is also difficult to pour out of from the sides. I'll be going back to my old metal ladle and not making such a hot mess.

Looks Nice, But Cheap. I am giving this 5 stars for appearance and 2 for quality. Standard Chinese quality ceramic with a durability factor of next to nothing. It is attractive and a nice size. I like the seal around the lid, but  I've had things with that kind of seal before and they don't hold up well to continual use. Kind of surprised since I have been getting things from this manufacturer for a while now and the quality is usually better.

Hard To Use. I tried this a few weeks ago with potstickers. No joy. Tried it last night with empanadas. Not the greatest tool. The roller is very hard to get the knack of using and really isn't a time saver unless you have a long strip of dough. Otherwise it's easier to cut them with a ring mold. Unfortunately the largest ring mold in my set isn't big enough for the dumpling maker itself.  That brinks me to the second problem. after crimping everything sticks in there and you can't get it out. I tried a little flour, a little non stick spray. All in all it's a real pain in the butt to use. No instructions for how to make it work are included.

Somewhat Disappointing. I waited forever for this to get here so I could organize all my tea stash.  The product has proved disappointing on several levels. The compartments are a bit too small in width and length. A full box of 20 tea bags won't fit without stuffing them very tightly. Some packages like the Pukka teas are just a tad too wide for the space. I did figure out that if you put them in upside down you can get them in and out easier.  Having loaded it full I was not happy to find that it doesn't seal shut. Probably because the bags don't fit in there quite right and the lid doesn't have a latch of any kind. Poor design and execution.

How The Mighty Have Fallen. WOW, Very sad to see how far the Lenox name has fallen. In looking at the picture of this box my first impression was " it's a little plain but it will be better in person." Not so. It's butt ugly plain and if I were Lenox I would be embarrassed to put my name on it. The quality is OK but this sure could use a little spicing up as far as design is concerned.  I have some old pieces and there just is no comparison to this stuff in terms of quality or design.

About What You Would Expect From Sawdust and Glue. Where oh where to begin. I needed a functional piece of furniture for my artist studio. Someplace for a printer and a cutting machine etc. When I had the chance to get this from the Vine I went for it.

Pros:
Attractive from a distance.

Cons:

**Not at all white. The color is what I would call antique white. Matches well in my room.

**Poorly packaged. When UPS delivered it, there was packaging hanging out all over the torn up box. Fortunately it wasn't damaged.

**Assembly was interesting to say the least.

You definitely need 2 people and a power drill to put this together. The instructions are pictorial and assume a great amount of knowledge that the average person probably doesn't have. Like putting glue on the dowels before you insert them. No where does it tell you that. This took about 4 hours from start to finish. Be sure you assemble this very close to where you want it to land because it is the finest 130 pounds of sawdust and glue you will ever move.

**Has weight restrictions. In the instructions there are pretty clear weight limits for every part of this piece. Nothing should be set on top of it. No books. Nothing very heavy. About what you expect for something that is doweled, glued and screwed through poor quality particle board.

**Poor quality for the money. There are various qualities of particle board, some are quite sturdy. This is low end at best. I do not expect this to have a really long lifespan. Should probably not be moved around much as this will surely cause it to fall apart.

OK, With Issues. This product appears to be a really sturdy, functional over the sink organizer. There are, however, a few issues with assembly and quality. The side pieces are tubular stainless, but not very high quality. One of the big selling points is the adjustability of the item to fit most sink areas. One of my telescoping pieces fell apart as soon as I removed the bag, and the second one was jammed together so tightly I had to use a screwdriver to pry the tubing apart to get the center piece lose.
The protective scratch peel on the silverware holder was impossible to remove without scratching the stainless anyway and took longer to get off the whole rest of the assembly.
Versatile ability to set up the spacing and arrangement of the accessories. Be wary of overloading especially if you are putting breakables in the top basket.

They Work. These filters are fine, but it really annoys me that no one sells just the post motor filter. That's the one that's hard to clean and gets the dirtiest faster. After looking at it today it really is just a piece of felt, so from now on I will make my own.

Disappointing. I haven't burned candles in a long time, but I always bought Yankee. This one smells divine in the jar. I burned it for an hour yesterday and it burns fairly cleanly, but when burning I really didn't smell the scent much. Kind of disappointing for a candle that costs 30.00.

Overpriced. This product is well made, but very overpriced for plastic. There is a bag of "hardware" that comes with this. Some is not intuitive as to it's use. The descriptive pictures really don't show you much. I assume the rolls are removed from the box and inserted in the dispenser. There is a round hole in the acrylic panel that defies logic. I guess it is for sticking your finger in to remove the end with the magnets. Could be more user friendly.

Poor Quality. This is a beautiful mold. It does however have quality issues. Molds like this for cookies, are finely finished with no burrs or rough places to catch the dough. This one has many finishing flaws in the sanding of the design. Every one of those little burrs will make it very messy and hard to get out a perfectly finished cookie. If I have time, I may take my dremel and try to fix it, but not in time to use it this year. As always, you get what you pay for.

Really Small. Very small. Not worth the little bit of space it does take. Get a decent, well made dehumidifier and place it in a central location. You'll get a way better result. May work in a very tiny house or enclosed room, but it didn't make a very noticeable difference here.

Hard To Control. Not a big fan of this. First issue is the charging. It has a USB plug so it isn't convenient to charge. Second issue is that when you are using it on the handle it is difficult to keep it from bouncing all around. I thought this would work for my oversized, tiled shower, but the scrubbing pad isn't going to last long either.  It might be fine using it handheld, but that kind of defeats the purpose for me.

Lots of Do's and Don'ts. The first thing that struck me about this pan was the list of things that you shouldn't do to it. The first being no high heat because that will burn off the finish. Don't rap utensils on the edge. You can put it in the dishwasher, but don't. Heat it slowly. So many rules that it is unlikely I will use this very much.
It is well made, pretty heavy bottomed, and does clean up easily. I used it to do some sauteed vegetables and used a Calphalon lid that I had. It did clean up easily and if you don't cook much this is probably a good pan for you. I cook almost everyday/ 365 so I prefer cookware without all the caveats.

Works With Issues. At first I was sure this was going to burn out my mixer. Seems like a good tool to do that. Zero guidance or recipes about the consistency of the dough that is recommended. I had inadvertently used a 100 % whole wheat semolina. That was a mistake. This machine doesn't have the balls to extrude that kind of dough even if it is attached to a Kitchen Aid.  Going to try it again with regular semolina and see if that matters.  However, this  attachment is awful to clean. The dough is jammed in and the parts won't come undone. I had to soak it forever and thought I might have to get manly help to get it apart.  Not something I will use very often with the issues I have mentioned.

Functional. I do a lot of cooking. At the present I have old style heavy Calphalon cookware that is great, but can't go into the dishwasher or the warranty will be voided.  I generally stay away from anything nonstick, but I got this set for the occasional  lightweight use of warming up a sauce or doing some eggs. Some days there just isn't enough energy left to wash more dishes and these can go into the dishwasher and come out OK.  They are lightweight quality, but the lids are very nice and I will probably use them more than the actual pans. The additional plastic tools and the baking sheet are of such low quality, that they will be relegated to the trash, or a yard sale. All in all this set would be acceptable for light use for a new cook that didn't have anything else. They specifically state that they are for use on low to medium heat, so that alone would rule out most uses for a real cook

Somewhat Better Than The Original Version. I bought one of the original mini Keurigs for my husband's office. It was difficult and no matter what water you used, the coffee always tasted terrible. The new mini has at least resolved the flavor issue. It was kind of difficult to get it to work even after following the specific instructions to the letter. I finally had to unplug it, start over and eventually after raising and lowering the lid several times I got it do the first, cleansing brew. It spit and sputtered, groaned and growled, squealed and screeched, scared the crap out of the dog and then finally spit out some water. All in all a very frustrating and time consuming adventure. Put a pod in and repeated all the previous noises and was finally presented with a passable cup of coffee. Fortunately this is going in my art studio for winter use, because if I had to use it everyday I would probably have to shoot it.
I like the fact on this one that I can take out the water reservoir to fill and clean. The pod storage is stupid because you have to take it in and out to make the coffee. Still not a great design, but some moderate progress. Much smaller profile than the original, thinner and lighter for sure.

Cheaply Made. My first thought when I opened these is that they won't last long. Thin hinges, very cheaply made. If you overstuff the pie and force it shut it is sure to break. No use instruction for the lattice part of the pie and the description page isn't a great help.
Poor Quality. From a distance these are OK. Really cheaply made and they don't have glass, just some kind of film in the front. Very obviously plastic.
Not What I Wanted. I wanted to use these for a decor project, but they are really cheap looking and not a very good color.

Not Very Sturdy. I guess I'm always the critic. I grew up with Pyrex. These bowls are shaped like the little Pyrex custard bowls except they are pretty thin and not nearly as well made.  I will have to figure out a way to keep them separate because the Pyrex could go in the oven and these can't.

Pretty and Pathetic. In the broad daylight this tree is pathetic. Cheaply made and the branches are wrapped in plastic strips.  But you know what they say. Most things look better in the dark. Actually then it's kind of pretty. Comes with the top all bent over to fit the box so it requires a whole lot of messing with to get it into tree shape. Probably best to hide it in the daylight or it could scare the kids.

Epic Fail. I've been baking bread for the better part of 50 years. Never tried a Pullman loaf until today.  I used the recipe from King Arthur flour. The bread was good, the pan was a failure. You have to grease the pan so that you can get the bread out. That oil leaked out of the corners of the pan when it got hot and burned all over the oven, while the bread oozed out the top under the lid. Large mess!

Kind of Flat. These are nowhere as plump as they look in the picture. No amount of fluffing helps either. They were stuffed in a too small box and were almost impossible to remove without cutting the box open and damaging the contents.  Don't bother.

Just OK. About what you'd expect for cheap construction. Not too hard to put together, but some of the posts don't want to stay in the requisite holes. A rubber mallet is useful to get it all seated and level. Rolls OK. Didn't fit in the space I measured for it, so I don't know if I measured wrong or it's wider than they state.

Kind of 3.5 Stars. I have had a reading pillow for over 45 years. My original one finally succumbed to age and I've been looking for a replacement. This will do until something better comes along.

Pros:
Nice fabric and pattern. Very neutral.

Cons:
Impossible to get the headrest buttoned on. The button holes are too small I guess. Whatever reason, I messed with it for 15 minutes and finally gave up.

It is not very firm and supportive by any means. The old one I had was a beast. Stuffed full and firm. This is really wimpy. I use mine sometimes on my futon for watching TV and I can feel the wooden slats through this.

It is also kind of narrow. If you are a large person, you don't want this. I am 5 '2 and 150 and it works for me, but there isn't a lot of wiggle room.

It's OK, but could be better & too pricey for the quality. I purchased 4 white bookshelves (2 from Amazon and 2 from Walmart - Mainstays). I wanted only 2, but ended up with 3. Keep reading for the 'why'.

I purchased the Amazon (Furinno) ones first and quickly assembled one, but after finishing it, I was less than satisfied. It's the little things. The backboard was folded outward so the creases are more visible, which isn't good for a white bookshelf. Also, the shelf spacing is awkward. I decided to wait to assemble #2 and went to Plan B: Walmart bookshelves. (The sizes of the two products are within about an inch of each other on the measurements.) I figured I'd assemble a shelf and compare the two.

I was very satisfied with the Mainstays bookshelf because of the little things: 1) back panel folding was inward so the creases are more subtle, 2) the shelf spacing isn't so awkward, 3) little white caps were included to cover screws and cam locks, 4) all sides of the boards were covered white (expect the one facing the wall) including the top and bottom boards, and 5) very easy to assemble, clearly labeled parts, and clear instructions.

Finally, and this is the clencher for me, the price point for Mainstays is $29.88 (as of 4/25/21 in stores), whereas the Furinno shelves are nearly $60. The cheaper product looks better. I returned the unopened Furinno, but kept the one already assembled (too much trouble to disassemble and send back while also paying the $30 shipping costs). I'll use it in a less visible place. Now I have 3 shelves.

The Mainstays are in my living room and look lovely. They're certainly not genuine wood, but they are well made especially for the price.

Why 3 stars if I haven't said many positives about the product? The product is average at best, but Furrino's service is excellent - the shelves arrived 4 days ahead of the projected date, which I was very happy with, and they refunded my money for the one bookshelf, minus the shipping costs. But the product could be better, especially for the cost.

Insert in box (typed exactly as it is written)
IMPORTANT - READ ME
Hi, I'm your new mandoline slicer. Thank you for letting me be a part of your household :)
I can be used for slicing fruits and vegetables thinly and evenly which is great for Gratins or Salads.

I also let you do Julienne cuts which is great for Coleslaw and Stir-fry's.

Before you start cutting ensure that the slicer you have chosen is placed firmly into the small slots on the sides. This is to reduce the risk of the slicer plate slipping while you are slicing.

When working with me without the container start out by having the Mandoline (me) perpendicular (at a right-angle) to you. Do not be tempted to slice with "me" sideways. You'll have the best control over me by pushing the food in a forward motion.

Start out by creating a flat surface (on the piece of fruit or vegetable) for the blade to cut.

For example cut your potato down the middle with a knife to create a flat surface on the inside of the 2 halves.

Safety Comes First

To keep your hands and fingers safe we recommend either using the safety hand guard or a cut resistant glove to prevent you cutting yourselves as the blades are very sharp.

With starchy vegetables is important to lubricate the "runway" as when the starch oozes out of the vegetable it gets very slicky.

Then use consistent even strokes. This makes potato bake a very quick and easy dinner option.

To cut softer vegetables like a tomato apply a zig zag sawing motion gently back and forth. For Julienne vegetables swap inserts. Again start with a flat surface on your vegetable.

To get the most out of the "mincer" grater it is best used for Ginger, essential for any Asian dish and for fresh Ginger Tea.

Also great to zest any critus for dessert cooking.

It's usually a good idea to have a few extra veggies on hand when you're learning to use your mandoline so you can get the hang of the whole process.

And when you're done simply rinse me clean in warm water. I keep very neat and safe, away in my container until next time.

Do not place in boiling water or a dishwasher, the mandoline just needs a rinse off.

I will update my review as our use continues.

plastic tablecloth clips.
