Not my first air fryer, its OK. Maybe I'm just spoiled because I'm comparing this to an air fryer that I already love, but I found this one to be sub-optimal.
Air fryers, if you are unaware, are basically small high powered convection ovens that can simulate the effect of "frying" on certain types of food (like french fries). To do this, you need precise temperature controls and timing, since it happens rather quickly (a difference of a minute or two in the machine is significant). So one of the first things that turned me off to this one is the fact that the timer is a manual dial that WON'T LET YOU ADJUST THE TIME once you've set it. In other words, if you overcrank the time (say, to 10 min instead of 7), you can't turn it back down. You have to just wait out that amount of time until it finishes. That's a silly oversight if you ask me. My other air fryer, for contrast, has a digital display for the timer which can be adjusted at any time during the process. This one? You have to unplug it if you don't want it to continue running for the time you accidentally set.
Also the slotted tray insert comes out of the drawer rather easily, but the plastic tabs need to be lined up again for it to go back in (you have to push it with your thumb to slide it back into the open position). Just a silly nuisance that could have been avoided since I know other air fryers at similar price points don't have this issue.
As far as the food, it DOES work, as long as you preheat it first. And the first time you use it, of course, you should let it burn out for 30 min to avoid new appliance smell on your food. It's an alright air fryer, especially if you get it for a bargain sale price, but otherwise I feel like there are better models on the market with less quirks.

He even looks like he's struggling at first, and then the editor is like "nope, let's cut ahead some time!". The other included accessories such as the milk cup are cute, but honestly not necessary. If you have a milk frother, you're not going to pour it into this first to then pour into your coffee. And if you are using your milk straight, again, why pour it into this? For aesthetics? To serve? Maybe I'm just missing the point of it, and there aren't really instructions to clarify.
The actual press is the only part I like. Some die hards will tell you to only make it in glass but the metal container is perfectly fine IMO. The press is a little bit smaller than I'm used to, so it is only good for smaller portions of coffee, but the filter is interesting and easy to clean, which I liked.
All in all, its ok because it comes with so many things so it might make a cute gift, but I feel like you can get much higher quality versions of all the necessary components for not a lot more money. I'd rather buy a better grinder and bigger press separately, and skip the other things.

Looks good, a little wobbly. I feel bad giving this only 3 stars because it DOES work and looks great next to my stainless steel sink and faucet. I have an under-sink RO filter faucet as well which matches, so it just sort of completes the look in my kitchen. The only thing that gets on my nerves, however, is that the bottom seems to not be as flat as it should be. That is, it sort of rocks/teeters a little bit when touched, as if the bottom is curved slightly. As soon as you touch it to pump out some soap, you expect it to stay in place but it sort of moves a little like a loose appliance on the countertop. It's not the biggest deal, but I have a glass soap pump that doesn't do this. We wanted to replace it with this chrome one because it matches our sink better, but my wife and I actually prefer the one that doesn't rock back and forth.
I want to like this, and I might keep it for the looks, but I'm going to have to settle for "its just ok".

NOT a set of 3! Only ONE!. The description says this comes in a set of 3. But that is somewhat false advertising: the "three" here are the three parts of a single pan combo (the pan itself, a plastic lid and a grill insert), and it is NOT, in fact, a set of 3 pans as we were expecting.
That being said, the pan we did get from this is pretty great. We've used it for a few things so far, including 2 different kinds of deserts and it cleans up nicely and looks like new after each one (no more disposable 9x13 pans for messy dishes!). The grill rack is pretty cool for things like fish or meat, but the cover is just a plastic to preserve it, not oven safe for baking. So if you have a dish that requires being cooked while covered (lasagna for example), you'll need to use some aluminum foil or something similar instead of the included cover.

Its OK. I want to like these. I hate throwing away plastic bags. But honestly, I didn't like them as much as I hoped. I wanted to store ground coffee in one of the bags, but I noticed a plastic smell out of the box that I didn't want in my coffee. Washing the bag and letting it air out inside-out seemed to help, and after a few days I can say the bag now doesn't smell but I'm still wary of storing coffee in it. For things like storing cheese or sandwiches, I'd be ok with it. But it brings me to my next issue: Washing and drying plastic is hard to do without growing mold! You have to make sure you turn these really inside-out in order to get it to fully dry, and it could take a day or two to fully dry out enough that you can turn it back rightside-in to reuse.
At the end of the day, I don't think I'll be replacing disposable bags with this. But it's a good proof-of-concept at least.

Great product, but there are better versions out there. [[VIDEOID:7b675ea1597018da67f730c9556f03a3]] I've used other portable stools like this one before, we own some. Its very similar to the Slap Chop. I've owned a slap chop as seen on TV, and this is pretty much a new edition of the same product. I was hoping it would be somewhat improved from the original one made famous by infomercials, but sadly the same problems I had there exist here.
To be clear- for some things, it works great. chopping items without skin for example is pretty straight forward. But if you take a cucumber and try to slap it into chopped pieces, you end up with half of it still attached to the skin and the other half mushed into a pulp. There's a very fine line between too little chopping and too much. You also can't really control the size of the outcome very well. The idea is good and for certain things it will work well- chopping up hard boiled eggs for egg salad for example. Or Tuna with some peppers and spices, etc. But I was really hoping this would be good for israeli salad or pico de gallo, and it is just a little disappointing on that.

POWERFUL! But the battery system is weird. This product is super strong and perfect for moving large quantities of leaves. I've tried a few battery operated blowers before, and honestly they were never strong enough compared to their plug in or gas powered counterparts. The 453cfm rating on this one made me take notice, and I have to admit that this is the FIRST battery operated unit that I can confidently say is strong enough to replace a corded or gas option.
However, in order to achieve this, the unit requires 2 batteries. They are loaded up in tandem on the left and right of the back of the blower, and it requires both of them to be charged in order to work. This is a bit of an odd design, but I guess in order to reach the whopping amount of power necessary here, one battery pack isn't enough. The box comes with both necessary batteries, however it only comes with a single charger capable of charging only ONE battery at a time! This is a major downside. At full power, these batteries can easily run out of charge within 20-30 minutes. And then you have to charge not just one, but wait for it to finish and then charge the second battery! This is very frustrating and begs the question of why didn't they just include a charger for each battery?
If you get this blower, I strongly recommend buying a second charger, and perhaps a second set of batteries to swap. That would make it perfect. As of now, it's close but not quite what I could be.

Not quite the "poor man's mini split" I was hoping for- heat requires water removal!. Portable AC units are great for times a traditional window unit isn't an option. However, I was particularly interested in this one because of the supplemental HEAT function as well.
You see, I have a room that was added on to my home without attaching to the house's central HVAC. It is always noticeably hotter in the summer and colder in the winter in that room. I looked into installing an efficient mini-split unit which would solve this problem, however I could not justify the cost (thousands of dollars!).
This unit seemed like a possible work around: I can either pipe it to a window or drill a hole in my wall to pipe it out of (still much cheaper than a mini split!!), and have supplemental cooling AND heating!
Well, it turns out, using any mode other than cooling requires you to empty a water bucket. Dehumidify I understand, but I was surprised to learn that the heat pump mode (essentially running the AC in reverse) also fills with water and requires draining. There was not a lot of information about the heat mode before ordering it, and now I see why. It really does seem to be an afterthought, the cooling mode is the important feature. I'm disappointed because that mode was the only thing that stood out between this and other portable AC units I was looking at. It seems like still a good air conditioner if you've got a space that needs a portable one, but I wouldn't get it for the supplemental heating mode.

The alarm controls are a little hard to get used to; the buttons on the back aren't immediately intuitive so you need to learn how to shut off the alarm properly. But worse than that... THE ALARM ISN'T LOUD. My son is away for the summer and took this with him as an alarm clock only to find that the alarm is too soft, and there seems to be no way to adjust the volume in the directions. He's using it as a time piece only and will have to rely on his phone to wake him up. A little disappointed about that part.

Slim cans and small drinks only.. I got this thinking it would be useful to have a can insulator that also doubles as something to keep coffee hot / drinks cold. It DOES work for those purposes, but it wasn't until I tried it in person that I realized a normal sized can does not fit. A slim beer can? Sure. A regular Coke can? Nope.
That's ok, I'll just use it for coffee, right? Well, it's actually smaller than my other coffee insulated mugs/tumbler, we even have a Contigo tumbler that holds 16oz, whereas this seems to max out at 12. None of that is in the description otherwise I would have at least had more realistic expectations of what I was getting.
At the end of the day, it sort of ends up being a product that is pretty neat, but doesn't actually do anything useful to me. I don't buy skinny cans usually, and it isn't large enough to carry my drinks. If you want a smaller tumbler and buy skinny cans, I guess its ok.

Kind of unimpressed. I've ordered pillows online before, so I had a pretty realistic expectation, I think. These claim to be real down and are admittedly nice feeling to lay on- They come vacuum packed and flat like all the others I've tried, as well.
Here's the thing: Maybe I'm just used to down alternatives, but these did NOT seem to fluff back up as much as expected after removing from the plastic seal. In fact, they seem kind of 60-75% full compared to the pictures on the product description. I gave it a weekend to finish decompressing before trying again, I tried hand fluffing, but it still sort of feels like a pillow that has been used for a few years to me. Not what I was expecting.

Love the functionality, but some design flaws. This works really well for cleaning areas that are difficult to reach with a corded model (hallways and stairs in particular are difficult in my home). The carpet cleaning brush actually feels like it self-propels the unit forward which is cool, and the LED lights were particularly useful in spotting broken glass after a drinking cup had fallen and shattered. Works well on hardwood and carpet flooring (and unlike another review I read here, it doesn't leave any marks on our hardwood flooring- I'm not sure what that's about).
So why only 3 stars? For starters, the battery life doesn't seem that great. My home isn't that large, a modest 1,500 square feet, but the battery seems to struggle making it through an entire house cleaning in one shot. Twice we had to stop and charge it before we could finish. We have accepted that perhaps it is better to clean parts at a time rather than the entire house at once, but I'd have hoped this would last longer or at least come with a spare battery to swap and keep going.
Secondly, the collection cup is very easy to accidentally pop out and empty when you didn't want it to. That reference above to picking up glass that shattered? My son was using it to vacuum our stairs the same day and accidentally knocked the cup loose releasing all the debris all over the stair case, including some shards of glass that were still inside. If they made that part more secure and the battery life longer, I would gladly give this 5 stars. For now, I'd give it a three.

Don't expect much. We have four mostly-indoor pets, and now that it's almost spring, the shedding has gotten out of control. Our entire downstairs is wood flooring, and I did not want to pull out our large vacuum every day to pick up the fur. I bought this hoping it would help with light day-to-day vacuuming. It's compact and convenient enough, and I do love that it's cordless. The suction on it is TERRIBLE, though - really, really disappointing. When I leave it on the "bare floor" setting, the suction is only strong enough to suck the fur to the machine, but not into the canister (leaving me with a big clump of fur and debris on the outside of the vacuum's mouth, which is just gross). It's much more effective when I turn on the carpet setting and at least the rotating brush helps propel the fur into the canister, BUT, using the carpet setting wears the battery down significantly. I can only use this vacuum for about 15 minutes straight with the roller spinning before the battery gets drained and the vacuum basically begins to moan and sputter. Also, this is good enough to vacuum up fur and hair/dust, but does a poor job at sucking up anything with more mass - I can hardly get it to pick up stray cat food kibbles or even pine needles that the dogs have tracked in. I'm disappointed this isn't a slightly more robust vacuum, but I suppose the cheap price indicates what you can really expect from this.

A Decent Looking Bed, A Few Disappointments. I really like the looks of this bed if you squint a little and look at it from a ways off. I have owned a couple of very nice wrought iron beds and really liked the looks but they were higher quality than this one. I got a couple disappointments when I put it together. The biggest of which is that my rigid box spring could not fit the bed lengthwise. I ended up having to shift box springs around to get one that would fit the bed.

Set up was quick and easy. I'm not sure why this is called a snap bed, or why the video advertisement says the pieces snap into place. There is nothing that snaps, but it is an easy construction. 8 screws with the needed allen wrench included is nice. The pieces fit together fine, and while this is not the sturdiest bed I've owned, it is as good as most inexpensive head and foot boards that attach to a bed frame.

The finish is a painted on fake brushed nickel. There were two voids in the paint on mine and the threat that it can be scratched off. The welds are large and rough, perhaps that was a look they were going for, but they are amateurish enough to look less elegant. All in all, it's an OK bed, just not as good as I would have hoped from the photos and video.

All I really know is that I like freshly, consistently ground arabica beans that are brown. This is my first electric burr grinder. For as much coffee as I drink I really haven't bothered to learn much about making coffee. All I really know is that I like freshly, consistently ground arabica beans that are brown, not black. I seriously need to advance my knowledge beyond that. I will say that this grinder produces a fair amount of fine dust along with any coarseness of grounds, which I'm told is the sign of a cheap coffee grinder. OTOH it does a night-and-day better job than my previous, blade-chopping "grinder". I had to choose a new grinder in a hurry because my old one broke down.

Also the static cling on the plastic hopper is pretty bad. I do what I read in another review: I just shake the grounds (and dust) out of the hopper through its intake hole. That keeps mess to a minimum. I bought a refurbished one since I figure such a grinder will have received much more QC attention than a standard assembly-line example. I also got the extended protection plan, which buys me a few years' worth of maintenance, which at least forestalls this thing's date with a landfill (SIGH)... I hate buying disposable appliances/amusements, but I was overwhelmed with research on grinders ranging from $30 to $3,000. My plan is to use this grinder to simply defer the decision. I will use this for [I think 3 years?] after which I expect it to expire and nobody will be willing to fix it. At that point I will have accumulated enough knowledge to purchase a grinder that I can use my whole life, and somebody else can enjoy it when I'm gone. My next/final one will be a highly regarded, serviceable, conical burr grinder with a glass receptacle - that's all I know so far.

Now that I'm thinking about it, the purchase price seems good until I consider that I'm really just buying time to figure out which grinder I really want. I'm not proud of buying something that was clearly designed to be disposable.

EDIT 2016.05.20: I spent a week in Portland, and it pretty much ruined my life. Sampling the lifestyles there there has warped my mind like few things ever have. I now ride a bicycle pretty much everywhere I go - got rid of one car (share one with wife). I have lost all interest in chain restaurant food. After a week of swimming in really great coffee - culinary *experience* coffee - it's too hard to go back to my old, lower standards.

I finally started to read up on home roasting and brewing. I bought a Lido 3 hand grinder and I hacked my second popcorn roaster to add temp and fan controls (fire hazard - don't do it)! I found Kansas City's only top-tier coffee joint, Oddly Correct, and I bug them with questions. I've been to About the Coffee once and plan to take some classes there. I took the factory tour at Roasterie.

I think the Cuisinart was a good stepping stone for me. At the time I was hooked on "good" coffee but I wasn't interested enough to dump lots of hours into learning the whole process of making iteratively better coffee at home. This grinder is good in that it is reliable and consistent (from grind to grind). I put numbers on the coarseness dial with a fine Sharpie - returning to the click marked "6" will mean the same thing today that it did a year ago. A year ago my main problem with this grinder seemed like a quibble: it produces a lot of fine dust. Now that I'm beefing up my skills in taking coffee from green beans to finished drink, this shortcoming is becoming a limiter.

The static cling is annoying but I can totally live with that. I'm a hardcore coffee junkie now - to get my daily fix I would be stealing ratty old bicycles and smashing the front windows of pawn shops if it came to that. I see the extreme lengths to which some people go to get a better cup of coffee and I can totally imagining my own mental state degrading to the same level of obsession. Static cling is the least of my problems.

I'm satisfied that I took my coffee making as far as it can go with this grinder. At the time of purchase I thought it was a real step up - going from a blade type coffee chopper to a grinder with "burr" in the name - WOW haha! It's like all my hobbies - all I needed when starting out was to *think* I had good gear and the excitement carried me through. And to be fair this grinder was a huge step up from a blade type chopper. I'm happy for the experience I had with this Cuisinart grinder, but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone wanting to make good coffee.

I'm satisfied that I got my money's worth out of it - I bought a refurbished one with a 3-year warranty, which was the epitome of cheap reliability. I will continue to use it when a portable hand grinder is unsuitable (volume, time, broken arm, Japanese apartment with insufficient room to extend both elbows).

If you are currently satisfied with the coffee you drink at home and you just want a fast way to grind beans, then count yourself lucky and be happy with the Cuisinart grinder. This is luck on the order of maturing to adulthood without ever learning about war, famine, or the question of whether god exists.

Here is my advice to people who want the whole coffee experience - zen rituals of preparation, culinary exploration, etc. Plan to invest in an immersive hobby. Invest in the following order:

TIME: research, finding the best coffee joint in town, taking classes, plan a vacation around coffee tasting and learning. start by finding people who demonstrate their expertise by handing you a cup of the best coffee you've ever had. everyone can talk, but not everyone can roast and brew. those who can, can recommend books

BOOKS: get some real info. the internet is full of people who get all their info from the internet. At my current, novice level it is too hard for me to discern real experts from randos.

GEAR: roaster, grinder, brew gear.

Stay on guard for gear fetishism - it seems to affect a lot of coffee enthusiasts. Remember that you love *coffee* - not coffee *gear*. For me a reliable guide to gear and utility is to stand in a room, meditate for a minute, open my eyes, and ask, "What in here is ugly?" - and then get rid of the ugly things. Ugliness extends to every criterion: utility, aesthetics, undefined sensibilities. When used as my exclusive method - i.e. no "What's the best I can get?" or "What are the available choices?" - I end up with very good gear that works great and looks appropriate for my house. I end up with the *right* gear. A consort of good coffee gear is like an ad-hoc sculpture - perfection is achieved by removing that which doesn't belong. Adding more *stuff* is generally a step in the wrong direction.

Aggressively avoid advertising for coffee gear, which includes the pap that passes for journalism. It's like *Raiders of the Lost Ark*: one look and you will be destroyed.

Focus on one thing at a time. Probably stay in the area of brewing first, then move on to roasting. Progressively wean off the best, fresh-roasted beans in town to your own, home-roasted beans. Forget about incremental gear upgrades - spend your resources figuring out what you like (hands-on) and then do what it takes to acquire the necessary skills and gear. For me I don't really need flexibility or programmability or automation - I just want to consistently get the best results possible with a reasonable amount of time and effort. The Cuisinart grinder did that for me for a couple years, but because of my rising skill level, it is no longer suitable. It has become ugly, and as such must be relegated to storage.

Good luck on your quest into the magical, hidden world of coffee!

PowerFresh Steam Mop - not so great. Over the past several years, I have purchased several steam mops: Shark Pocket, Haan, Euroflex Monster and now this Bissell Power Fresh Steam Mop (purchased locally). I wanted a mop to put out nice hot steam that is hot enough to cut through stuff, swivel and ALSO fit under my kitchen cabinets.

This Power Fresh Steam Mop by Bissell DOES have a low head to fit under cabinets and it does swivel. Compared to the Euroflex Monster (steam temp is 212F per product specs), this Steam Fresh doesn't come close. Even on the hottest setting, the steam is less hot and abundant. (The Monster has steam from both the bottom and the front). Also, using the medium and highest settings left my floor SOGGY.

I was quite interested in the fresh scent disks for leaving that clean scent (yes, I know -- don't have to smell a fragrance to be clean). The scent to me was very minimal.

Pads: They are about the thinnish quality of the Shark and get soggy quickly. My floors aren't that dirty, but I have to use two or three (only 2 included) to do a medium-sized kitchen floor.
Handle: Sturdy, but they unit tips over easily.
Tank: Very small, but easy to refill.
Steam: Not very hot (compared to the Euroflex at 212F)- hold the mop over an area for 20 seconds to sanitize. Yikes .. takes ages to "santize" an entire floor.
Head Maneverability: Nice and low height.
Fresh Scent Disks: Barely noticeable (but might be my nose).

Bottom line: The steam only comes from one area on the bottom (as opposed to several jets). The clugging/chugging noise (normal, per instructions) is a bit annoying. I DO like the swivel head, and the fresh scent (such as it is). The low height makes it nice for cleaning under cabinets. The steam isn't that hot and one has to leave the mop over an area for 20 seconds to sanitize leaves much to be desired.

For Sanitizing and cleaning a large area, I'LL STICK TO MY EUROFLEX MONSTER. This will work for smaller areas.

More of a robotic sweeper than a vaccum. TL/DR (Conclusion): this unit really only does the job of eliminating routine light sweeping of floors. You will still need to get into corners with a broom. The dust bin needs emptying (very) frequently and the roller becomes clogged with lint quickly due to it's small diameter and width. The low height is great as it fits under most furniture. Daily automated program does not work properly. 2.5 stars. REALLY wish it had a smartphone app.

The price I paid, $109, was a great deal. The unit does a decent job of basic sweeping of floors on demand. It is capable of remembering obstacles, even though it is not really supposed to be able to map your home. If a new obstacle appears in its path, it will tap it, reverse, work it's way around it, and remember it is there for the duration of the cycle. It does seem to remember hard boundaries (walls, furniture), even though mapping is not supposed to be one of its features. I also purchased the magnetic boundary strip to keep it out of a specific area, and this works perfectly.

It does a decent job sweeping up dust and light particles, although it cannot quite reach all the way into corners with the brushes. The suction is not very strong unless you use the Max setting, but this depletes the battery rapidly. You will need to use the Max setting for some larger particles. The sweeping roller is not very long or wide and becomes clogged up with lint very easily, requiring a good cleaning about every third run or so. The dust bin is tiny, and requires emptying after every use in my small space, and likely several times if used in a larger area. The unit itself is gloss black on top and gets very dusty every time it is used, requiring frequent thorough dusting/cleaning. I did not bother purchasing the mop accessory, because online video reviews point out it is not really mopping, just the equivalent of dragging a wet cloth around on the floor, and is quite useless in this respect.

The primary reason I selected this model were the positive video reviews elsewhere conducted by an independent third party which brutally tests all robotic vacuums and records all tests on video. This model is the same mechanically as another top-selling robot which is simply private-labeled. This is apparently the OEM, and is significantly cheaper as a result.

By far the best feature is the low height/profile. This is the slimmest robotic vacuum I have ever seen. It is only 7.2cm tall! It can easily go under sofas, my media center, chairs, and most furniture with a wide enough opening for it to enter. It is also quite good at getting itself out of tight "traps" (i.e. behind furniture or under a couch with stuff there), but will stop if it becomes tangled or stuck, issuing a loud beep in the process. This is one reason I wish it had a smart phone app so it could alert you when it gets stuck.

What doesn't work:
1) The automation aspect does not function properly. I tried setting it up to go every day at the same time, and it did it for two days, then stopped without explanation. I tried again, and could not get it to hold the program. Then about 8 months later, following a brief power outage at home, it started automatically cleaning every day at the same time again, as though it had remembered the program or the feature had been re-enabled, but the time was not as previously set. When I tried to change the time, it seemed to save it, but it has failed to clean automatically on any day since. If I want it to run, I just grab the remote and hit "auto". Not such a big deal, really, but I wish it worked.

2) It cannot navigate any threshold with a height greater than about 3/8". This means in my house it cannot move from the hardwood in the living areas to carpet in bedrooms, etc. This is very frustrating. I have to give it a push if I want it to try to vacuum the carpet on the other side of the threshold. Which leads to number 3...

3) This unit is about 75% useless for vacuuming carpet. It will pick up surface debris, but that's it. If you want a proper vacuuming, you need to use a MUCH stronger vacuum. Even on Max suction mode, this does not do a deep cleaning (not even close), and the rotating brush becomes clogged with fibers very quickly due it's small diameter.

Conclusion: this unit really only does the job of eliminating routine light daily sweeping of floors. You will still need to get into corners with a broom. The dust bin needs emptying (very) frequently and the roller becomes clogged with lint quickly due to it's small diameter and width. The low height is great as it fits under most furniture. Daily automated program does not work properly.

Recommended? Yes, if it is on sale for about $100 (it frequently is). If I had paid $200, I would have been disappointed and may have returned it. Just keep your expectations realistic: this will sweep your hard floors and suck up the particles. That's it. If you have a lot of carpet, I would not recommend this unit.

Not as cool as it sounds. I absolutely hate washing greasy pans, so being a bacon-aholic, I had to find an easier way to get crispy bacon on the table ASAP or sooner. I've been using a microwave safe plate, and zapping the bacon for about 5 ½ minutes on 70% power, but couldn't resist trying out this product, just because.

Comparative results:

Bacon a la plate:
1. Put a paper towel on the plate
2. Put the Bacon on the paper towel
3. Put another paper towel on top
4. Zap at 70% power for 5 1/2 minutes
5. Remove top paper towel
6. Put bacon in another plate - ready to eat
7. Discard greasy bottom paper towel
8. Allow plate to cool, add dishwashing liquid and water for a few minutes
9. Wash as usual

Bacon a la gadget
1. Put bacon on grooved side of gadget
2. Put a paper towel on top (I hate cleaning splatters off microwaves too)
3. Zap at 70% power for 7 minutes
4. Zap again depending how it comes out
5. Remove top paper towel
6. Put bacon in another plate - ready to eat
7. Reserve gunky stuff at bottom of gadget if you're going to use it later
8. Apply generous quantities of dishwashing liquid and hot water, leave gadget to soak
9. Wash off whatever comes off, then leave to soak longer
10. Rinse, and soak again
11. Realize that sticky stuff isn't coming off the sides of the ridges or the inside rim of the gadget
12. Apply more detergent and use brute force with a brush to the problem areas
13. Remember to brush both sides of each ridge
14. Wash again

Summary:

For bacon without all the mess
Just use the microwave
There's no real need to use a pan
Unless it's fat you crave

All you need's a dinner plate
And two thick Bounty sheets
The rendered fat helps it to cook
Providing crispy treats

This gadget works, make no mistake
But it's too hard to clean
Use the flip side as a plate
And zap some quick cuisine

Amanda Richards, December 20, 2007

Thermos Funtainer 10oz insulates better. I recently bought my daughter the Thermos Funtainer 10oz with folding spoon to take soup to school for lunches, it was $16.99. It has worked well but I love all of my hydro flask water bottles so I was excited to try this. I tested them out this morning side by side. I started out by filling them both with hot tap water to warm up the metal insides while I boiled water. I dumped the tap water and then filled them both with boiling water (temp was 210 degrees). I sealed them tightly and left them on the counter for 4 hours. I then took the temperature of the water. The hydro flask water was 137 degrees and the Thermos Funtainer water was 151 degrees. I could actually see a small bit of steam coming out of the Thermos container and couldn’t see anything coming from the HydroFlask. The HydroFlask feels more substantial at first (it weighs 13 oz and the Thermos weighs 9oz), but the lid for the Thermos is bulkier and I guess that’s why the Thermos retains heat better.
Overall neither leak and my 6 year old can take off and put on the lid to both, so they are both easy enough for small kids to use. But when it comes to heat retention and price, Thermos wins.

Thoughts from a Gaggia Classic user. I’ve used a handful of espresso machines over the past few years ranging from cheap to expensive. This machine falls in the middle of both taste and price.
This machine is easy to use once you find the settings and pods you like, which took me about a month of trial and error. It heats up quickly and is pretty portable. You can get pretty consistent results, which is also nice. But the taste of the espresso and the milk foam simply don’t compare to my manual Gaggia Classic. I can get much better results from an extra 5 minutes with my Gaggia and quality espresso beans. Most pods I tried tasted bitter or weak until I found the single origin Rosabaya de Colombia, which has a decent flavor. I also struggled with the size of the Nespresso shots and the volume of milk. Whereas it’s simple to make a 16oz latte with a few tablespoons of espresso beans and my Gaggia, I found that using two Nespresso pods is a must to make a drink that size with the Creatista. I do one Ristretto shot and one Espresso shot to get enough espresso volume for a 16oz drink, but that makes the cost per drink upwards of $2. I was actually fairly impressed with the quality of the milk from the Creatista, but my main issue was the temperature. Even on its hottest setting the milk only got to 155 degrees. I typically manually froth my milk with my Gaggia to 160-170 degrees, which is about as hot as possible before giving it a burnt taste.
Overall I did find this machine superior to a Saeco super automatic machine I’ve tried that was three times as expensive. The display is simpler and the milk was better with this Creatista. If you can get over the cost of the pods and absolutely need to save another 5 minutes for each drink, this is the way to go. For me, I’d rather put in the extra time for a superior taste and lower cost.

Extremely Thin Material. I was very surprised by how thin this sheet set is.  If it lasts more than a month, I'll be even more surprised.

Enjoyed for years but cap is now wearing noticeably. I like this tumbler and have used it for a number of years.  I stopped using for reasons I can't remember.  After a few more years I started using it again.  It functioned without any problems all this time, but now, the rubber like material surrounding the cap has begun to wear noticeably - at the point where my thumb usually rests when twisting the cap on and off.  A nickel-sized piece has come loose. If I mash it back in, it will stick for a while until I have to mash it again.  I can't put it in the dishwasher because if I do, the piece will be forced off.  I'd request a replacement under Contigo's warranty program, but they don't cover return shipping - which would likely be a good chunk of what it cost to purchase a new one. Buying a new one is a more attractive option because shipping is free with Prime. Given this, the warranty is pretty much useless.  Some might say I shouldn't complain because I got years of use from the product.  But this ignores the material defect and the warranty shortcomings.  Anyway, that's my 2 cents.
Cake Keeper. It does not seal like the one my Mother had...  It will do until I can find another to replace it with...

Chef'n SleekStor Pinch Pour Prep Bowls. The were not exactly what I was expecting...  due to the material they are made of, they are better suited for liquids than dry spices/rubs, etc.  Got the green set for myself and the red set for my daughter-in-law...  Haven't heard from her regarding how she liked them...
Potato Peeler. Sorry but it didn't live up to my expectations...  It didn't seem to be as sharp as my old one...
Bread Loaf Bags. They don't work as expected...  have lost a lot of loaves due to molding...  got something different and have lost a lot less...
Oggi 3-Piece Acrylic Airtight Canisters, Mini .... Not what I expected... too small for my use, but my husband was able to find a use for them...
Pyrex Easy Grab 8-Inch Square Baking Dish .... Not really what I expected... bottom is smaller than top so getting things to fit is a bit of a pain ! ! !
Set of 2 BBQ Basting Mops with Wood Handle. Got them for a different sort of task...  they are a bit small for the new task but so far so good...
Crock Pot Liners. They don't work as well as others I have purchased...they seem to be smaller than most and are only sized good enough for my 2-3 quart crock-pot...
Hamilton Beach 49999A FlexBrew Single-Serve Coffeemaker. Not what we expected...  Husband was so disappointed that he won't use it...  when it breaks, we will try something different ! ! !
16 oz. Olive Oil Bottle Set. They will do...  they are much larger that expected and the rack is useless on my counter...  it is just gathering dust on top of the kitchen cabinet ! ! !
OXO Good Grips Pop-Up Steamer. It is okay...  does the job, but not exactly what I was looking for or expecting...  am looking for another - like I had before ! ! !

POOR Construction. This is exactly what I've been looking for to replace ones that lasted about 15 years. Upon receiving, I opened the zipper and the zipper tab came off in my fingers. Upon examination, I discovered that both ends of the zipper were unfinished. I had purchased 2 of these so I checked the other one and saw it was the same. I decided to keep them and to hand sew what was done incorrectly. These are perfect for lingerie and small delicates, but I'll be surprised if they last more than a year or 2.
Just as described!. This is ok for what it is.. plastic but the lights are cute.
Good basic unit. This is a good very basic unit, not terrible quality  but not stellar either. Average piece that fills a need..
Ok- but too expensive for what you get. I won’t but again-not worth the money
Just ok. Very thin and hard to get fold marks out. Ok. Not thick enough for my liking.:/
Ok :/. Pretty but wayyyyyyyy too small for the price.
Three Stars. Missing two of the 4 washers

Quality isnt really good.. I bought these for my step sister and they aren't terrible. I don't like what it is made up. It isn't absorbent. Like if you wash your hands you wouldn't be able to dry them off on it. They look nice and was a good price though. If you are trying to look good in it I' d recommend it, but if you are trying to cook with it, I wouldn't recommend it.
Disappointed. This pillow did not seem as good as the one I had previously. It is compressing more, almost as though it had been used.

Description is confusing/misleading. The items themselves ONE chain, ONE ant moat and ONE cleaning brush are fine. The description seemed to imply that there were three sets of each - that’s not the case. There is a single set of three for the price. 5 stars for the merchandise, 2 stars off for a confusing, possibly misleading description.

Great air purifier, but maybe not so smart. I’ve had mixed results with the “smart” features. The first P1 I bought was a total headache to get and keep connected. The second one has been no problem at all. As for the filtering ability - I’m pleased. It’s actually surprising what gets picked up by the P1. Example: In one room I also occasionally run an essential oil diffuser. Even before I notice any difference, the P1 senses the change, updates the PPM display and (on auto) increases the speed. This also happens when I spray air freshener nearby, even in an adjoining room.

Nice frame but there are some flaws.. The frame itself is really nice. The excessive staples on the back holding paper in place (to cover the metal hangers and such)are a bit ridiculous. I can’t get the staples out without scratching up the back of the frame. And there’s almost 20 staples!!! So that’s dumb.

Also- it’s not a glass front (no big deal) but the plastic covering has a crease in it... so it’s damaged. But I am too lazy to return it because I don’t want to wait.
I expected more.. Not super fluffy or high-quality, but I guess for the price I expected more.
One didn’t work. One of the shelves  was made incorrectly and won’t snap together.

has potential but seriously... stickers for 6 of the days. It's lacking in 'wow' factor. since it's not December yet my son hasn't gotten the chance to start opening the doors for each day but I did open the side of the box so I could slide out the cardboard holder and see everything inside. First off, the cars are great! They're everything I'd expect from Hot Wheels. The accessories are kind of cheap and some of them I have no clue what they even are, but I'm sure my son would figure it out so that's not an issue. What I was disappointed with was the stickers.... what a huge bummer to open a day in the advent calendar and see nothing more than a cheap, cheesy, little sticker. As a parent I don't want stickers all over everything in my home, and as a kid I wouldn't be thrilled with opening the door expecting something cool and seeing the sticker.

We normally buy the Lego Advent Calendars every year and my son loves them. Yes they're a bit more expensive but there's something interesting every single day (even if it is just an accessory for the item that was opened the day before) so in comparison to the Lego product I'd say Hot Wheels has a long way to go - but if you're kid likes Hot Wheels and little stickers than here you go.
hard to get it in there. That was a lot of work... and the kid I got this for I would have to change all the time, so this is too much work for what I need.

thick. I don't like these bags, too thick and have a bulky sliding color stick that seals the top closed, I can tell they would be good bags. strong bags but I like the bags that have the zips attached right on them so I can easily close my bags and not have to go looking for where I set my color stick.
soft but I didn't understand.... How does these work??? I'm used to getting two sheets and one that hugs the mattress, I couldn't figure them out, ended up just using pillow cases.

I couldn't figure it out on my own. I ended up having a friend come over and show me how this machine works. I like it, it saves food in the freezer longer but I don't think I will be using it much, too much of a pain to set up and do.

Arrived scuffed up but fixable with paint pens. Loved the look of this frame but was disappointed ted when it arrived scuffed up in all the raised parts which meant the white plastic underneath was showing.  After a little internal debate I decided to get brave and paint the design parts using rock painting paints I’d previously gotten.  The result is a fun frame that has a story all its own... the perfect display piece for our prized pictures.  Oh and don’t worry the glass/plastic photo covers are not broken, they’ve just shifted so aren’t sitting right.  Will be once we add photos.

very comfortable. I love the color and how soft the sheets are but I don't do zippers, so they ended up being put in the closet until I need them for our hide-a-bed.  The regular beds in the house are too heavy the put these on.

The seal isn't very good on the lid. The cup I received didn't have a very good seal on the lid. I had to adjust the rubber piece on it to get the lid to close and it still didn't fully close properly. it holds heat pretty well and keeps hot drinks heated for quite a while. I also noticed that the paint on the cup doesn't seem to be sealed very well so it might not hold up to being in the dishwasher.

small. I picked this up for one small child in my classroom, thought it would make a great break chair.  She really loves it and it's the right size, the only thing I don't like is it doesn't keep it's shape real well.  It really needed more stuffing.

really wanted to love it. I was so looking forward to this product coming to the house.  I ripped into it, carefully of course and was so disappointment in how cheap the handles are. It's hard to figure out where each knife goes. I have a cheaper knife block, still cost a lot but cheaper than this one was going to be getting rid of even though they are only 1 year old, but decided to keep the old and give the new away.

Tongs don’t stack up. After using these for quite sometime I can’t recommend the tongs that come in this set.
They are set so far apart you cannot grab anything with them, they simply have no grip. They won’t work with anything with any amount of weight to it at all.
If you are looking to only use them with salad you will be fine. Other than that, find another pair.

Stuck together right out of the box. All of these were so tightly stuck together in the box we had to pry them apart with a screwdriver. Needless to say it damaged one of the shelves, so their packaging leave a lot to be desired.
In all honesty these could have holes for optional hanging or magnetic use. Our fridge, turns out, doesn’t have enough clearance on the sides and that probably isn’t uncommon.
Most people wouldn’t have a choice but to use these elsewhere leaving you to have to drill holes or use the magnetic sticks on the wall. It would work but the aesthetic’s aren’t great.
I probably wouldn’t purchase this again knowing what I do. I would look for one that can be mounted multiple ways.
Wasn’t really pleased. Not really please with the durability of the product. Looks are deceiving.

Great but order extra. These worked great for us with the exception of a couple of bags. I loved the fact that they held a ton of stuff and the pump was easy to pack. Just be sure you order a few more than what you will need as a couple of ours didn’t seal and it left us short on bags.

Ok for omelets, can’t put much in it. Works ok, easy to over and under cook. Price point is good for what you are getting. If you’re looking for something fast and inexpensive this is definitely your choice. If you want something that can do a little more don’t get this particular model. Upgrade your choice to a little better product.

Does not fit Glad/Hefty 13 gallon bags.. Live the large opening but cannot get bags to fit. When  using the "arms" to hold the bag they won't stay in place to hold a 13 gallon bag. Good in theory but not in practice.
Good product. Did not stay up with suction alone

Works okay. I think these worked okay. there definitely could be better designs with these. It's definitely going to depend on what type of cords you have and how much length of them. Basically you just stuff the cords into them. The thing is, the way it is designed it is possible for it to come out. Also, because of the way it is, I think this would be easier for kids to figure out than some of the other safety products out there. They are a good value, but it does come with a price of a bit of functionality. No matter what, it is very important to keep cords out of kids' reach.

Sounded off. So something about this just seemed off. The music seemed too fast, and also not long enough compared to other similar products. It seemed repetative. It also had some scratches on the sides out of the box. I do like the idea of it and my husband and kids liked it. And it is very reasonable, so as long as you know what you are getting, can be a reasonable option.
Does Not Look Like It Was Painted. This may be on canvas, but it doesn't look painted, which makes me wonder why they bothered with the expense of canvas...

Not so easy. This was just not so easy to do. It takes a really long time to make a little ice cream. It can be frustrating and involves gong back and forth. Directions were not great.  love the idea and so do the kids, but I think there are other products that can do the same thing in a better way.

Works Fine, But The Design Is More Hype Than Function. Overall this works, but plastic isn't as good as glass, the two separate parts need to be cleaned separately, and the shape is awkward to hold.  Next time I'll buy a traditional Pyrex measuring glass instead.

Smaller Than Most, And Drawers Fall Easily. This is smaller than most sets like this, so if you're assuming it will fit next to you existing one, check the dimensions.

The drawers have to be balanced pretty well, otherwise they fall easily.

But overall it does hold toys and looks fine so 3 stars.

Cute idea, not executed great. This product was a little disappointing. My son loves the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles and he loves waffles, so I thought this would be great. unfortunately, it was not as good as I thought.

First the waffles came out super thin. They were literally half the size of the others from my normal waffle maker. One child actually thought they were pancakes instead of waffles they were so small. They had no room to become fluffy.

The image of the turtle was not super great. Yes, you could tell it was that, but it was not very clear.

It didn't have a timer, so it was hard to guess when it was done. It took longer than with my other one.

Overall, I have to say I'm a bit disappointed. It is fun for a TMNT fan, but I think the convenience and the fact that the regular ones make it so much better outweigh the one advantage of the TMNT image.

Looks Great, But The Lights Can Come Out. I've got kids...  They take the cups out and they break them.  If they were snug in there so they were hard to take out, that would be great, but they are so loose that they fall out if the wall is hit!  Only get this if you have no kids!!

Nice but not quite sturdy. So this is very attractive. It looks nice. I like that it fits in the corner. It is a nice wood.

The reason I gave it a middling review was because it is just not sturdy enough. Someone may fall if they are not used to it. Once you get used to it, you can be careful and not fall (we are going to keep it) but we just did have issues with it. I think it can be someone people can use, but you do have to be careful.
Picks up crumbs with ease. But only when you .... Picks up crumbs with ease.  But only when you remove the brush!  It doesn't have enough sucking power to work with the brush attached...

Muted gold. The sequins on this pillow are very muted. I suppose I thought it would be a lot shiner or sparkle a lot more. If you are looking for something that has a muted gold, then this can work for you. Because the sequins are a little rough, this is really more of a decorative pillow than one you would actually use. I had no problems with the quality. This would look nice on a sofa or with holiday decorations. You can only spot clean it; it is not to put in the machine. Overall, I wish it were a little more sparkly.

Too Long. Okay, I thought this was a good idea, but maybe something between this and the short ones I have now...  These aren't comfortable because they go past the elbows which makes it hard to bend your arm.

came with a lot of powder. These were really covered in powder. It was all over them. It kind of took away from them a lot. I would have had to have spent a while cleaning them before showing them off.

These artificial flowers didn't look quite real but they were decent quality otherwise.

Good Once Set Up. This was a lot of work to set up.  I expected a pre-made plastic thing, instead I got a pile of wood and screws with okay instructions.  Took about 15 minutes, which is way more time than I want to spend, so it took me months to get around to it.  Can you tell I'm a procrastinator yet?  Anyway, I'd look for something that comes premade if I were getting another one.

Pretty but a pain to open and close. I liked how it looked but it was a pain to open and close. I did manage it, but I had to push hard each time and it's just a hassle, especially with how often I change them. It worked fine, and once I got it opened or close it stayed that way. But just not sure it is worth dealing with it each time.
Three Stars. Ziplock bags still work better...

Broke quickly. This was a nice idea, but for us it broke quickly. It did not do what we needed it to do. It would be nice to have some extra storage. Perhaps we just got a bad one or for whatever reason it didn't work. I think it would depend on how you use it and what you put on it, but it definitely could have been stronger.

Decent. This chair was all right. It was decent. It was not the most cushioned but not terrible. It looks nice and my son liked it. It is nice that it reclines and has the colors. The pillow did end up ripping after not that long. I think the quality was kind of in the middle, not stupendous but not terrible. It wasn't too hard to put together. It looked like the picture.
Hard To Set Up And Not Straight. The lines are different lengths, so when you put it together some are straight and others are not.

Seemed flimsy. These were a bit disappointing. I could not believe how flimsy they seemed. They just really did not seem like they would hold up well. They were also a real pain to put together. It took me a while to get one lined up right and done. I would imagine someone who already has difficulty would find it impossible. For me, these just did not work.

Very, very hard. We were so disappointed in how hard this was. It just wasn't comfortable because it was so hard. If that is what you like, then perhaps it would work for you, but we will not be keeping it.

Otherwise the quality seemed okay. It wasn't too hard to put together. It seemed like decent quality. The size was good. The green was pretty and striking.

None of us found it was comfortable because of how hard it was.

Works Well, But Far Too Small. This is a decent soap dispenser, I'm happy with the foam and with how easy it is to use.  But it holds so little soap!  I've got 7 people with 2 bathrooms and this doesn't last a day!  So I'm not going to keep using it.

All right. These were all right. They just seemed a little more fake to me, as compared to some other ones I have recently got. I liked the purple one and put that one out, but the others were not as good for me. They are fine, they just look a little more artificial than some others. They did come in ok condition. It was nice to get four of them.

Hlaf were nice, half I didn't like. I was mixed on this. I liked the two dark green ones a lot. Those looked pretty, and I am going to keep those. I put them up.

The other two just didn't look good to me. They seemed faded and very unrealistic. I just didn't think they were attractive.

Overall, the qaulity was okay. You can put them all together or seperately. I do like fake plants overall since they stay the same and you don't have to worry about them.

Not as bright. So overall, I was disappointed in these. I liked one of them - the one that was very colorful. That one was bright and vibrant and very pretty. The others were really just so so. One of them really seemed faded. They just weren't close to as vibrant as the pictures. I will hang the one becuase I like it, but probably not the others. Otherwise they seem okay as far as being solid.

So-so-quality. We were disappointed in the quality of these. We've already had several come apart. For a product that kids may be using they really need to be better. They also seem kind of sparse. It is hard just to seperate them. The colors are fine. They just seem inexpensive and not particularly well made. You get a lot for what you pay and I guess you get what you pay for. If you want something really cheap and quick, they can still be an okay option but don't forget great quality.

Not very fluffy. This is a lot thinner than I thought it would be. I have other Vera Bradeley towels that I just love because they are so thick and absorbant and this is just a lot thinner than I thought. I don't really like the feel of it. It is pretty and the design is nice, and it works okay. It would be your preference of the fabric, but for me it wasn't great, especially considering the price point is high. It was just okay.

Attractive but not soft. As far as look, this is very nice. It is pretty and looks good. It goes along with many other items in this print. It seems to be very high quality, as most of their products are.

The porblem is in how it feels. It is really not soft. I was very disappointed. We have many blankets that are both beautiful and soft, so it was disappointing that this was only the first. It would look good as decor, but there are a lot better choices if you want to have something to use. So it depends on what you are using it for as to whether it would work for you.

Not The Greatest Chair of All Time. This chair was way harder to put together than most (I've put together a lot of chairs in my day).  Once together, it wasn't comfortable.  I have a bad back, and the lumbar support was all wrong.  So I gave it to my son, but he didn't like it either, so we donated it.

Pretty. Realize that you are just getting a thin plain piece of paper probably of the same quality that you could have printed it. But it was fine. The print itself is very pretty and nice. I love the saying. I have this in a larger canvas. As long as you know what you are getting, it is fine. Wish the pictures were less misleading.

All right. This painting is okay. It is a pretty good deal for a real painting, but it is not going to be close to what it looked like from the original painter. There wasn't anything inherently wrong with it, but I just felt underwhelmed. The colors weren't exactly the same and it was not as detailed. We will not be displaying it. So not a bad price for real work and I would imagine all will be different based on who you get to paint it, but for us just okay.
Need to have a 💧 catcher for wax.. The holders are nicely soldered. The glass is not beveled in the points.
Not secure. When I placed my little plate on the stand I was afraid it would topple over. Very flimsy.
I should have looked at the sizes. The product itself is very durable and easy to clean but I should have looked at the sizes. None of them are big enough to cover a full plate.

A little disappointed. I was so excited for this bundt cake pan but then u used it. It doesn't cook evenly. The cake came out if it easy but it was raw in the middle and just wouldn't cook. I figure I can use it as a jello mold because it didn't work for baking.

Didn't notice the spots!. Well it looks slightly different from the picture.  I didn't notice all the white spots on it from the website picture's.  It seems more white than grey. But I will be keeping it however because at least it's in a dark area of my room. Had I known that it was mostly white than grey though I wouldn't have bought it. Oh well live and learn!

Big piece of metal. Its too heavy. Everytime I get a paper towel it tumbles over. I literally have to hold the paper towel roll every time I need a paper towel in order to keep it from tumbling over. Not to mention I saw this $10 cheaper at Garden Ridge a few weeks after I purchased it. Not a happy camper.
Nice size. This was a nice size bowl but the coloring was not accurate. It was a light to medium brown. Returned it
Sharpe edges. Cute and functional......but edges are sharpe and could cut furniture, a child or a pet
Really nice faux fire. Really nice faux fire.  Bought it for our RV.  Like the option of no heat.....just faux embers.  Never received the extended warranty paperwork.
Three Stars. Love these.....even mounted in medicine cabinet in rv for cosmetics...just hope they don't come flying out the door
Nice novelty gift. Description says "Picture It On Canvas."  But further down in description says on metal.  It came on metal.  Nice novelty gift.
Nice valance.. Pattern a little bold. Nice valance, although wasn’t for me, so I returned it.
Disappointed. For some reason I thought I was repurchasing the JML Microfiber towels, NOPE. So sorry I bought these. Definitely not what Im used to. Would not recommend buying these.
Don’t love it, don’t hate it. You get what you pay for? Will use it, but I don’t recommend it and I would not buy it again.
Does not smell like palo santo. Do not recommend
eggs will stick, keep very well greased. Eggs stick.
but they are beautiful. I went and bought my own double sided .... Butterflies fell off double sided stickers, but they are beautiful. I went and bought my own double sided tape and used that.

Doesn't stay cold long. Cup doesn't even keep w
Ice from melting. Just a few hours in the house. It's not a very thick cup. If I could find the box I would send it back! Save your money and just go for the Yeti

very hwavy. I truthfully  can't  answer  all these questions  correctly.  But item arrived on time, BUT! it was so heavy I couldn't  move it inside. There would of been no way me a 5'6" 150lb woman could have put it together  alone. I ended up leaving it on my porch for  UPS  to pick back up and send back,but as heavy as it was it should have been sturdy.
Good quality but a little small. does a good job,but a little  small.

Won't stay put on cabinet  door. It's a nice stro g durable and thick hook and it looks great,but it just keeps falling off because it is so thick. I have solid oak cabinets so my cabinets  are well built and thick.

If you want to make a lot of tea it's great, but other wise water doesn't get into filter. Kettle is heat resistant and easy to clean, but in order to get water into filter you have to fill Kettle at least half way up and that's a lot of dried tea leaves. I guess if you want to make a whole Kettle it would work, but I only want enough to make 1 or to cups of hot tea.

Not all that impressed: "flimsy", and unsure it is "food-safe". Though I decided not to return this item, I think that it is awfully flimsy and the lid is pretty worthless. There are better quality Silicone products out there, and speaking of silicone, I suspect this item isnt 'pure' silicone, as you can see 'white' when you apply pressure with your fingernail (that is supposed to be a big indicator of other chemicals involved)…. so I am not so sure its totally food-safe when heated or microwaved. I'm using it as a bar-soap dish.

HEAVY....but more for 'forming' burgers -not 'flat bottom'. While this IS a very heavy quality iron press, I was deceived by the ad photos, as I believed it had a totally flat bottom. It does NOT! It has like a 1/3 inch 'lip", so it is "more for forming burgers" from a meat chunk(!).
I wanted something that totally pressed down my food in a frying pan....so I had to send this back

Love the cube sizes, but very hard to remove them!. Love-Hate relationship! :-) I LOVE the size of these large cubes, and the molds are easy to fill, but I HATE the difficulty in getting the cubes out! I found that filling the compartments up 1/2 way makes it a tad easier, but I bought this 'cuz I wanted the large full-sized cubes!
“Light blue” is actually dark bright blue. It’s a nice color, but will end up giving away to family with a different “blue” bathroom. I liked the look, soft and absorbent.
Three Stars. It's ok
Kinda disappointed. The item in the photo had the Brand name burned into the Stand BUT the product I got didn’t, I’m Disappointed.
Good looks, didn't last long.. Love the way it looked but one split at the seam not long after I had them.

Pretty, but not perfect. Looks pretty, design is as expected, not cartoony. Looks great really, the only thing is that some of the panels are not stretched taut so there's visible ripples, but not deep or anything.  Also not thrilled with the hardware, it's a bit flimsy so have to be careful when moving or shifting it, and especially when opening it to lay it out. It didn't break, but feels like it could if I'm not careful.

Wrong color but soft. Searched for months for this color, and when I finally get the package - these sheets are very dark forest green - not the Christmas look I was going for. But I’m keeping them, they are very soft so still like these.

Not easy to use. You would think there would be a setting on the dial that says something like "hot dogs" and "burgers" or "steaks" or something.. Anything.. an icon even... I was purely guessing on what temperature to cook anything, so I tried hot dogs and burned the hell out of them.  It's kind of a pain to remember to add water to the little plastic tray too, I almost forgot the one day. I honestly don't use this much, I've only tried it twice now. Food ended up in the trash because it was burned to a blackened crisp. Will have to do some research to figure out what temperature to cook foods on so I don't burn again. And I"m leaving a sticky note on this thing to remember to fill up the water tray. Who knows what would happen if you don't do that, but better to be safe.

Beautiful red, 82" long. Perfect red for the holidays. I wouldn’t say these are thermal insulated at all, or that they are sound proof or even total blackout curtains but they’re good for the low price. I can definitely feel the cold winds with these up so probably won’t keep them up for long… The grommets are plastic though which took me by surprise. Very light weight, good if you can’t hang real heavy drapes. Oh, and these are only 82" long, not 84" like the description says. I know they're cheap, but seriously? At least get the size right...

Fast shipping, less than high quality, easy to assemble. I ordered this for my teenager and she's happy with it, but I was a little disappointed in the quality. First, I want to say that aside from putting the mirror on, this was very easy to put together (yes, it comes in pieces). The legs for the table itself are just screwed on, and that's it. You do need 2 people to put the mirror together. The drawers are much smaller than they appear when looking at it. When you open a drawer the width of the drawer itself is about 2 inches smaller than the front face of the drawer, so you can't fit much in them. The stool is VERY small, and the legs beneath it seem like they are going to break right off, because they tend to angle inward slightly (probably because they are not cut well to fit when you screw on the legs) and there were several pulls of thread on the fabric, I had to cut them all off. It's ok. Filter lasts about a month.. Physically, what I don't like about this pitcher is that the little "handle" they put in the lid so you can lift it off is pointless. The lid snaps in, and the little groove you're supposed to grip to lift it off isn't nearly sufficient. So you end up sticking your finger in the end where the water comes out, which I don't really care about but someone might if they're very concerned about germs.
Secondly, the pitcher really doesn't filter much at a time. Even if you fill it once and then refill it again, the second time the water takes so long to filter that it's just easier to do it one at a time.

I like the way the water tastes when it's filtered. It's not for everyone. It's like how it tastes when you buy bottled water that's been "mineralized for taste", which really confuses me since this supposed to filter out most things. But whatever--I still like the taste of it.

However, I actually bought this not to drink with but to water my plants and fill my humidifier. I have a few sensitive plants that demand distilled water, rain water, or super filtered water like this (living in the desert prevents me from collecting rain water). Since I don't have to water my plants a lot I'll probably keep using it for that.

I was using it to fill my humidifier each night to prevent the "white dust" that can settle around humidifiers and also prevent hard water build up inside it. It was certainly effective, but I had to use so much water just to fill up my humidifier each night that I used up the filter fairly quickly. I filled the pitcher probably 3 times per day for my humidifier, plus add in a few extra fills for watering my plants, and the filter lasted about a month.

After about five weeks of using my humidifier with this pitcher, my humidifier started smelling fishy, which I thought was strange considering I had just cleaned it the week before. I ended up cleaning my humidifier multiple times and refilling it thinking it was my humidifier at fault, but I was wrong. I finally thought to smell the water that was filtered from the pitcher and it was the water that was smelling fishy. So obviously the filter had run its course. I tested with the TDS meter just to see what the filtered water was at, and it read 088.

Considering these filters cost over $12 a piece, I am not going to continue to use the pitcher to fill my humidifier. I'll just deal with the hard water consequences. I will continue to use it for my plants and I'll probably start drinking it since I liked the taste. I'll be interested to see how long a filter last doing that.

A Low-Res Disappointment. Our 14 year old family geek recently redid his room and has had his eye out for decorative stuff to use there. His taste is quirky enough that I didn't know if he would go for this tapestry or not. As soon as he saw it though, he was like "Yeah, let's get this." Sadly, the tapestry was a disappointment. Think of a Hi-Res and a Low-Res photo of the same object. The first tends to be rich in sharply defined details while the second looks like a more mushy version of the first. If you can't picture what I mean, just go to Google Images and use "hi res vs low res" as your search keywords. This tapestry is not as blurred as the most extreme examples but it did seem as mushy as some of the less extreme samples there. The fabric seemed pretty lightweight, and is thin enough that a light behind it washes out the image on the front. So this would need to be hung on a wall and not over a window or across a closet. Our 14 year old took the tapestry to use on his wall but only until he can find something better.

Fair To Middling For Me But Your Mileage May Vary. These bowls are solidly made and do work well in the microwave. As a 73 year old guy with some health problems though, I do have some issues with them. These issues may or may not apply to you.

The primary issue for me is that the stacked bowls are really stuck together hard. It takes quite a bit of effort for me to peel one bowl off the stack. If the bowls were any less durable, they would rip apart in the process. That's how hard I have to work at it. Prying an edge of a bowl up with a fingernail so I can grab it even hurts a bit.

A couple of other concerns turned out not to be issues at all, though a different hassle did pop up. I used a bowl to heat up a can of Campbell's Chunky Beef Stew. The bowl looked so shallow I wasn't sure it would hold the whole can's worth of stew but it did. If you've ever heated up any of Campbell's Chunky soups in a microwave, you know their soup has a tendency to bubble up and pop, splattering soup around your microwave. I wasn't sure the lid would stay on the bowl the first time I used it. Indeed, I had my fingers crossed that I wouldn't end up with a messy microwave. Well, the snap on lid stay firmly in place and my concern was groundless. That lid did raise another issue though. Taking the hot top off the bowl was another Ouch! to my fingertips.

My last issue with these bowls is one of practical finances. Given my age and health issues, washing dishes is an arduous task for me these days. So I use disposable dishes as much as possible. These bowls are too pricey for me to regularly use them as disposable products though.

Now all these issues are directly related to my age and my physical limitations. As such, they may or may not apply to you and only you can decide if they do or not. So read the other reviews to get a broader picture and make a decision based on your own situation. Good luck.

Solidly Built But With Some Design Issues. The tumbler itself seems solidly built and durable, which is nice. However, there are some design issues with it. The size of the tumbler is one of those issues. I wear a large in men's gloves and the cup is still a bit awkward for me to hold. Even worse, the outside of the tumbler gets slippery when wet. Most water bottles have a handle you can hold onto them with, but not this one. I haven't dropped it yet, but that seems to be just a matter of time.

The slider on the lid you push open to pour out liquids is easy to leave open without noticing you did. That lets bugs in and doesn't help with the insulation. Speaking of the insulation, it does not keep liquids cool for very long. Ice water will go from cold to mildly cool in an hour or so. There are plenty of insulated bottles on the market. This is not one I would get again.

Not As Nice As It Looks. The bottle arrived in a thin cardboard box that had been put inside a flimsy, plastic envelope. The upper corner of the box was smashed in when it arrived. The bottle itself wasn't broken but the rubber stopper inside the lid of the bottle had fallen out of place and the two piece infuser had come unscrewed and separated inside the bottle. That was not an auspicious beginning but things only went downhill from there.

The neoprene cover for the bottle smelled like burnt rubber that had gasoline squirted over it. Not something you want to smell when pouring liquids out of the infuser. After I took the cover off, the glass bottle was slippery and seemed like it would be easy to drop. Sadly, the glass had a fragile feel to it, as though it would shatter easily. Without the cover, the bottle also transmitted the temperature of whatever was inside directly to your hand. In my case, it was iced tea inside the bottle and that was fine. If it had been hot tea though, my hand might have automatically jerked back. In that case I would have found out just how fragile its glass actually was. All and all I was thoroughly unimpressed with this product.

Not Great, Not Terrible, But Okay. To make things easier for myself as an old guy, I use a lot of disposable plates, plastic silverware, and cups. So I have plenty of experience with disposable coffee cups. The best are sturdy and durable enough for repeated use. The worst are so flimsy, they feel like they will collapse in your hand the first time you use them. These cups sit firmly in the middle between those two extremes. The lids feel lightweight and flimsy. They also have to be firmly and carefully snapped into place. Otherwise, it looks like they are set in place but they really are not. That can be a painful mistake when dealing with hot liquids. The cups themselves are thin enough that you do need to use the sleeves in order to hold them when they are full of hot coffee. I have used better disposable cups that are thick enough to not need the extra insulation. Thicker cups also keep the coffee hot for longer than these cups do. Still, there are plenty of cheap, disposable cups that are much worse than these. So I give this product a firm, middle of the pack, 3 star rating.
