Pretty huge disappointment. I was pretty excited when I putting this vacuum together and reading the manual but... I’ve vacuumed my house once and was just more and more disappointed. I do want to say that I am the type of person that vacuums at least six days a week (sometimes twice a day, because toddlers) and I also detail with the vacuum at least every other day. I need a vacuum that does the job and does it efficiently. Maybe if you’re one of those people I’ve read about that vacuums once a week this would be ok for you. If you actually want a detailed clean, keep searching.

So let’s start with the good points:
I do like the idea of being able to take apart all of parts and wash them. And the idea of having a washable filter is great. It does work well on the floors, we have mostly wood and a few shorter pile rugs. The cord rewind is also a great feature (in theory) but I find that having to yank 25’ of cord out to be a little annoying already. The dusting accessory is nice and works well for house plants and shelves. And that’s it for the good parts... like I said, pretty huge disappointment.

Now the not so great parts (and there’s a lot of them, so buckle up and grab a snack):
The washable filter was originally what sold me on this particular vacuum but now that I’ve used it once (see pictures) I know I’m going to have to wash the filters at least once a week because hair and a ton of dirt gets directly to the filter. Which means ordering extra filters because they have to air dry and as I said before, I pretty much vacuum daily. I know understand WHY the whole vacuum needs to come apart for cleaning, hair gets stuck and wrapped around all over the ‘cyclone’ parts of the dirt cup. This vacuum doesn’t have a light! That’s my own fault for assuming it did, but I honestly didn’t know that modern vacuums didn’t just all have them. I find it incredibly annoying that I now have to switch on all the lights in every room to make sure I don’t miss anything. Even my super cheap stick vacuum has a light *facepalm*. Now let’s talk about these accessories... man o man what a HUGE letdown. Let’s start with this huge joke of an “extension” hose. It’s a foot long. That’s not much of an ‘extension’ in my book. I don’t know what kind of giant they have in the pictures but I’m 5’3” and I am now going to have to haul around a step stool to reach pretty much everything above my head. Using the crevice tool gives you another foot but you can’t use the other accessories on the end of it. And speaking of the crevice tool, if you’re using the extension hose there’s no where to put it so you have to carry it around while you use the other tools. The corner tool is the most awkward thing I have ever used and you have to stoop down into an awkward angle to use it. It’s just a weird design and not very user friendly at all. The ‘turbo pet eraser’ is another total letdown. Even the pressure from its own suction is enough to stop it completely. You have to have a very light touch while using it which means it’s actually pretty useless for getting the dog hair off the couch. It doesn’t work at all for pillows and couch covers because the fabric lifts up slightly and that’s enough to stop the brush head. Being that their whole advertisement scheme is based around being a pet friendly vacuum I’m left feeling pretty confused about that. The swivel feature is ok but kind of awkward to get used to and the roller can only fit about two inches under the furniture.

Overall, huge disappointment. I don’t know who they use for product testers that told them this thing was ready to go to market but they need to hire some people who have actually used a vacuum before; this thing is a disaster. I’m not sure if I’m going to go through the hassle of cleaning this thing to return it yet, but I’ll update if I do.

it comes with EASY Simple directions, Pictures, And a Phone number .

1. Grilled shrimp and scallops kabobs.
2. Teriyaki chicken wing’s.
3. Lemon pepper pork chop marinade.

The tube is connect in a little compartment under where the tumbler sits to suck the Air out.
Connect the tube to the tumbler, Turn the knob to Vacuum. It automatically will show the time, and will shut off when the time counts down.
Before sucking the air out and tumbling, I put allot of seasoning on my Chuck roast, even used the tenderize thingie I have by hand to put holes in the meat..
Then Putting it into the Tumbler to suck the air to infuse the spices.
Also the meat expands to let the seasoning all in.
After I put it on the Tumbler mode, as I believe this tenderizes the meat.
I was making a chuck roast for the crockpot..
When the tumbling stopped, I then put the roast into a hot Pan to Sear it, with Olive oil, Red Wine, & sliced thick mushrooms.
Added more garlic.

Before putting the roast into the newer slow cooker, I put in a large trader joe container of beef broth, potatoes, carrots, celery, & onions, along with the
drippings, more seasonings, and everything that was inside the Sear pan. Along with my chuck roast into the slow cooker for 8 hours.

After 8 hours, we ate it for dinner. We where expecting this roast to melt in our mouth!! Both my Husband and I didn't think this lived up to its potential,
Of a melt in your mouth roast, with tons of seasoning, and it was even kind of dry tasting, not as tender as expected, although covered with liquid etc while cooking.!!

Just want to mention, I have made this type of roast before, but Not often, although putting it inside the oven instead of the crock pot, and not using this
tumbler, it has been before , a melt in your mouth awesome roast.

I usually only make chicken breasts, which is white meat and is dryer then other parts that are dark meat. Never have I made dry chick breasts.

This is my 3rd day of this left over cooked roast sitting in my Frig. And today it finally tastes tender, & juicy.
I never had to let a chuck roast marinate after cooking for 3 days for it to taste like it now does.
This is my reason for giving this 3 stars..(maybe should have been 2 stars !)

That said, before when I make a Brisket, slow cooking, I let it sit in my frig for 3 days before eating it.

While it is o.k., there are other pots that are better.

Doesn't work for all 4x4's. I had to return these because my 4x4 snapshot pictures didn't fit. The faces close to the edges were cut off.  Also,because of the deep shadow box effect, a shadow was cast on much of the picture.  The actual product was o.k., but not for a 4x4 where the image went right to the sides.
It’s a good product. With art products
Loved the pattern. Loved the pattern. For the kitchen table. Fits well.  Could have a little more flannel but it’s good.
Seams visible. Seams in the finish are obvious unlike my older SM tumblers.

These are not nearly as good as the originals from a year ago. These are not nearly as good as the originals from a year ago. Disappointed. But still better than some candles out there. This company is frustrating because they cheapened their quality(time of burn and scent) - AND, they are constantly “out of candles”. Not talking about Premier Candle Corp unless they are the manufacturer which I don’t believe they are—talking about simply indulgent. BRING BACK THE ORIGINAL DEEP CANDLES with 1 wick and three amazing fragrances that you originally sold at Costco!!! I’d buy excessively!

Water/Pasta - 7 minutes. Fried or Scrambles -- about an hour.. I spent way to much time comparing single burners -- this one works just fine for the price. It boils my water for pasta or vegetables in about 7 minutes. The only problem I have is when I am making a scramble in the morning -- it turns off and on and it takes about 40 minutes to fry thinly shredded potatoes and another 15 after scrambling in the eggs. Almost an hour to make breakfast is a bit nuts. I'll be purchasing a different kind soon -- however, if you're not a breakfast person, it works well.

Way too big!. I should have read the dimensions better before ordering this. The good news is they had free shipping and free returns. It was incredibly user-friendly as far as it inflated quickly, but it was not all conducive to what I needed it for. It was also quite heavy and firm when I set it up to test it- I didn’t want to leave a bad review on a product I didn’t end up keeping. It may be great to keep in a second bedroom if you have extra storage space but there is nothing portable about this mattress.

Wish it lasted longer. This lunch bag is beautiful.  I only wish it lasted longer.  I was hoping to get at least a year out of it... But the inner insulation layer is already coming apart after about 4 months
good product but very difficult to clean.. good product but very difficult to clean.
Made well. This is made well but it's to soft, it says it's firm, my lower back sinks in laying on this, no support just like my Temper pedic mattress.
Wouldn’t buy ‼️. Snags on everything.

Should sell larger ones.. Like the design but for any bra with any padding only one will fit in at a time, the bags work better than these pop ups, if give them give stars if only more than one fit in.

This mattress only last about two years.. I bought this exact mattress about three years ago for half of what they charge now and the increase makes it to were I can't afford a new one so I strongly suggest looking at other mattresses but if you are really sold on this one I would buy the 10 year warranty.

Lighter & sweeter than the red nag champa. I love this brand, but not my favorite scent compared with either the red or the blue nag champa, which I use a lot for my home as a way it relax, meditate or room cleansing.  Too light and sweet for me.

Hmm, am I suppose to add something else with it? Too soft.. I usually use rice and this ash is soo soft that the incense just does not stay upright!  I am thinking of mixing this with rice, perhaps?  Very fine, but not functional.  I am a little disappointed.

Hmmm from 8 feet away, it is blurred!. I like the simple model with large screen and blue digits.  But I am not sure it is made for viewing from 8+ feet away as I thought it was my glasses!  Alas, we were disappointed that the digits are blurred, thank goodness, the digits are so large as we can still maki put the time from the settee.

Only for red wine and non screw tops. It does not work for all wine bottles either screw tops or white wine: just too big.  Otherwise for red wine, if you only plan to keep for another couple of days, great and easy to use.  Neat and compact versus larger vacuum contraptions we have at home. I only wished the cork was more flexible to use on smaller bottle necks.

Definately pungent when unlite!. I was very concerned with the very strong scent coming out of the unopened delivery box!  Definately agree with another writer that the raw inscence is very pungent, but after the first 10 seconds of being lite, the much more pleasant fragrance comes through,  very mellow, which I like to use in the latter half of e day.  More of energy cleansing than for meditation.  Not one of my favorites, but everyone to their own preference.  But great value.

No scent.. I love tealight candles.  This candle last a long time, but there was no scent to speak of.  Little disappointed, but love the candle last a little longer than ones I buy from a large chain store.

deflats a lot within 24 hours.. We thought with a light weight this airbed would be as good as an older one we have, but heaver.  The plus os that it is compact and it is not that high - approximately 22 inches.  So not great for elders who need a higher bed.  It dod input pretty quickly and there is a manual and electric option to deflat.  wasn't totally easy to get it back on the bag, but it did work eventually.  the one key negative wa that it dd not stay inflate for even 24 hours.  you need to pump it up every day, and I mean you really notice the deflation - much more than our older airbed.  This works if you need this in a pinch, but I wouldn't really use for guests if they were staying more than 3 days.  in the end we preferred out older airbed.

Does not fit all bottle size.. Fits champagne bottle not so much for red wine bottles.  Useful for keeping the fizz for 2 days maximum, or if a slow pour/few drinkers.  Well made and will last for a long time, not a cheap gimmick.

Long handles. Super long tongs, but super easy to use.  We have had issues with stiff joints in previous brands - not an issue here.  With the plastic, we prefer to hand wash.  Noticed with AmazonBasics kitchen tools that they use super long handles, which I am 2 minds with this extended length as it is cumbersome to fit in normal utensil drawers.

handles are TOO long.. What is up with the super long handles??  I dont love this feature.  It was hard to store and whilst I have hanging beam - they are too long.  I got them [they are not free] to minimize using utensils with plastic in my cooking - whilst this fulfills my needs - the freaking long handles.  That aside, easy to clean and can throw into dish washer - will take up more space.  good selection - love the pasta and the two flat 'spoons'.

Every other pasta, not spaghetti, falls short by 1 inch.. Does not work with spaghettis..this jar is tooo short. Disappointed as it was the reason I bought this for. Sorry, I am not slanting the pasta to fit in, too inefficient use of space.
However, for other pasta shapes. Works great. Be careful thta you don’t hold or grab by the lid, does come off despite its modest suction feature.

Still need to buy the mat for cookie dough.. With the holes, you still need the mat, as the cookie dough will melt through as it bakes.  Otherwise, a nice thin sheet that can be used for other baking like hot cross buns, which has a denser dough and will bake on this type of sheet.  With the holes, it does a good job as a cooling rack as well.

Simple plastic bin that is clear to see what you have in it.. Simple plastic container with non complicated snap on lid.  Not something I would put food directly into it, but I used it for my deli meat so everything is all in one place, where I keep the original wrapping on.  It gives vertical stacking in the fridge and hence you are not wasting any area of the fridge.  With the clear bin, you can see what you have and that is one thing I have in the fridge, cabinets: no more excess buying and you use what you ave.

Quick to heat, careful of exposed iron.. We used it to lightly roast spices, raw nuts. It does heat up quickly..so don’t touch the exposed iron.  The rubber handle does help, but being such a small pan, it was challenging not to touch the iron/exposed handle.  Eggs were quick to cook, and no sticking so far.  Cleaning is with soft side, as these non stick elements can be ‘cleaned’ off.

Big and not flexible for 90 deg bend in neck. I was a little surprised that the handle is the full sized that you see in regular spatulas.  It irked great at scooping at the bottom of jars and then ones in particular.  Where it didn’t worked for necks that have a 90 degree bend.  Game over.  Just a tad disappointed that it was a little too big for the general purpose, although I can see you will have a Very good grip.

Sturdy, but finish was somewhat lacking. It is definitely sturdy, but noticed a slight ‘defect’ in how the cane was binded.  Thankfully, it is nearer the top of the basket, And shouldn’t affect the esthetic of the top of the sourdough.  I always wash any new Banneton before first use, thereafter, you use a toothbrush to clear any flour.  I wouldn’t necessarily buy from this supplier again,,but at the price point, it is modestly cheaper aNd still give you the support for final proof.

Shame that the print says Brut. Slightly waxed on the inside and great to store brioche bread or any enriched bread.  The other bag wouldn’t fit anything with height.  Small loaves are acceptable.  What was disappointing was that it doesn’t say Bread; instead the print says ‘Brut’.  Not something to be used on a professional setting given the print, but okay for personal use or gifting baked goodies to family and friends.

Perfect for craft storage/organization. This set was perfect for my craft storage from beads to my sewing parts.  They are small enough and not too deep to keep everything easy to access.  The plastic thickness is perfect with a tiny give if you press really hard. The lids snap on tightly and are all good fit.  The lids imprint that they are safe for microwave and dishwasher, I am not testing either as I can’t belief the heat for dishwasher doesn’t have some negative effect all round.  I am super happy as I am so much more organized and see where everything is.

3.5 stars for few features, but accurate and light to hold. I like the hold function, but it was a little hit and miss when it will hold the temperature.  A great feature otherwise.  I like the temperature alarm setting for making jam, donuts and deep frying sensitive food.  Highly recommend you scan the instructions and keep it on your computer, as setting the temperature alarm wasn’t intuitive.  Very light to hold, and the metal spike folds safely into itself.  Does require a manual press to switch it on. Flat battery with auto shit off will preserve long life.

Practical and multifunctional. Lovely little set of pastry brushes and spatula.  I used the blue one to brush pizza sauce on a pizza, it stained it!  The rubber brittles are very soft that the larger one, I can use as pastry brush when making puff pastry and croissants pastry.  There are better ones thta don’t stain and comes off in the wash.  I hand wash all plastic tools, never trust they can withstand the heat.

Grip is okay, tad slippery. 2inch in length.  Plastic covering over metal clips.  Firm hold, best for chip bags, but tad slippery.  I wouldn’t use these for my flour bags.  I might use these for paperwork.  They are light and not difficult to open.

Easy to use. My first time using such a tool to make Polish/Russian/Turkish dumplings.  I was excited to try a new cultural experience.  Whilst we enjoyed trying the new foodie experience, many great YouTube’s recipes and demos.  I was a little cautious with the finish of the tool itself: not sure of what aluminum finish should look like, but I kept thinking it had another plastic layer I needed to peel off before use?  I decided to clean it by hand and not test it via dish washer.  I hover with 3.5 stars as I am not sure what the finish should be for this tool.  Thus far, it does wash easily.  Instructions were not in English, and I am assuming it is in Russian; not an issue given access via internet.

Raw finish - but more thAn just a ‘bamboo’ turner.. Something with  the new design of spoons, spatulas: they feel a little rough, not polished.  Whilst I like the Raw feel, there were some open ends, which were sealed once I started cooking with it.  I am kinda in two minds about it, but I do like the look, and the handle feels like a farmhouse cooking experience.  The handle is quite short though.

Wide lip saucepans: may not be an easy fit. Only wish the clip was wider: doesn’t fit as easily for wider lip saucepans.  In fact, with many of our fancy pans, this wasn’t fitting well.  I am sure I want to jam this on when the saucepan is hot.  Intuitively, it’s easy to figure out how to fit it on even though instructions are available.  The material is thick and did work well once it was placed on.

just tad of quality issue, but these jars work well.. a few came with a few chips at the next of the jars, and they were not as clear as I had hoped.  That said, it was good to get proper lids as well, but wished they had 1/2 and 1/2 as I thought it tad wasteful.  We use these jars to make salad dressing, transfer small amounts of pasta sauce from the original large jars, feeding the sourdough starter, and hence there are many greta uses.  The inside of the jar is not flat, but domes up, so  I couldn't use it as a tea light candle holder.

Nothing fancy or even nice imho.. Meh, more for students accommodation rather than anything fancy.  The blackout does work as long as your rods are close to the window.  I would say the material is value plus.  Nothing fancy at all.  Functional is best to describe these set of curtains.

3.5 stars. Perfect size and height for a foot stall. It’s not bulky looking and in design. Very comfortable to use. However: I get that you get what you pay for. Hence, you aren’t gonna get. Polished finished product. The legs were okay although the vanishing was little haphazard in places and since I got the darker wood, you can not see it unless you lift it up to your face, which I wouldn’t be doing; no instructions [here is my quick summary: the silver screws with the circle is for screwing the legs to the stool top; the gold ones are for the side panels to the legs; make sure the two circles are facing INWARDS; and don’t tighten everything until all the screws and wooden bolts are loosely in place]; and then my Allen key snapped when screwing the gold screws in- thankfully, I keep a few spare ones. An extra screw part is included in the pack.
The cover has a slight plastic protection on it - so wash with cold water. I will likely to make my own cover to replace the original one, although the original one is fine too. The cover is elasticated so very easy to slip on and off. There is a spongy cushion beneath the cover, which makes it very comfortable for the feet.

Okay for little kids [under 7], don’t recommend for adults and not for standing on.

The price point, it is functional for what we need without creating a bulky look.

Tad smaller and residual wax left unburnt.. It is a tad smaller than another brand we buy [ikea] and this one does not burn out all the wax; there is always a residual left, which I felt was wasteful.  The wick provides a low and slow burn, which is good.  This is expensive relative to other brands.

inconsistent quality for all their sized candles.  disappointed.. the wax burns way tooo fast and dripped all over the place.  and the quality is irractice - one candle was fine and the next one just collapsed with mess of wax everywhere.  we have noticed this inconsistent quality across many of amazon branded candles - regardless of the size.  disappointing as the brand is often very good.

Not blackout curtain,s .. I would not consider these as blackout curtains as it is single layer of material, and we tried them over our blinds.  It certainly added another layer of blackout, but still the room was not super dark - ie no light!  We could still see the furnitures in dawn light  However, it did help.  The color is nice, and the material is soft and easy to iron.

Pricy for a sticky mold. Disappointed.. I use this brand for cookie baking, and thought it would be great to use them for fluted cakes.  I used a muffin recipe that had oil in it, so I didn’t think I needed to oil the mould.  Wrong.  They were stuck and hmm, not happy.  I tried it again with a carrot cake mix, same issue.  Tried it 3rd time with light oiling of the mould: came out better.  Kinda expected a lot more of non stick feature of this mold. Not worth the high price.

Unimpressed. a lot of plastic for not a lot of action.. I have a mini Nespresso machine, and this 'mini' still looks significant against the Nespresso machine. I purchased the 're-usable' cups and it is very easy to use. However, I think this one bulky plastic for making straight forward coffee: just stick to your french press. there seems to be a lot of plastic and not much of it is that functional. You need to add water every time you want a full cup of coffee, but the coffee stated weak - so I decided to only fill half of the water tank to make the coffee. I wish there was a way to control the water volume/cup size of coffee. I am pretty unimpressed and stopped using it after a couple of attempts and we are back to the Nespresso machine.
like other says, you do notice there is additional 30 seconds of 'hot water' heating before the brew is ready. Not that extensive unless you are standing right in front of it.
I think if you love K-cups, this machine is relatively small to other K machines. However, if you are a Nespresso person, this will not work. I am considering returning this machine.

Too delicate for usage.. It feels very delicate.  In the end I decided i would use the cup and the strainer as a ‘teapot’, I removed the green plastic as I wasn’t sure about the ‘plastic + hot water’.  Once this was my set up, I was happy.  In fact the tea strainer was all I need, which defeats why I need the rest of it!

Shame about the gap around the spoon and the jar. I ended up returning this item, which I really didn’t want to...is because there is a gap around the spoon, which could led to flies coming in.  Unfortunately, we don’t live in a vacuum, and fruit flies etc have the smelling abilities to survive.  Otherwise, this would have been a keeper if there were a rubber sealant.
OK. Just like the original.

Does what it's supposed to do.. I wanted to say something nice about this machine.  Well .. it's HUGE on the kitchen cabinet!  It IS powerful and would probably emulsify a rock.  Wife and I decided we didn't like what it made.  Juices are probably good for you with everything blasted into a smooth puree.  I can't say the price is too high.  You want to see high?  Go price a Vita Mix!
It fit my smaller oval crock pot.. Just the right size.
I've had my recliner for a long time. I wish these were a little sturdier.  This is the third handle since I got my beloved recliner.
useable. a little too thin but ok for the price
ok. pretty thin, but good for hair after shampoo.
Lid doesn’t close properly. I bought the 32oz glass containers and I love it. But those ones are  bit different and the lid doesn’t close properly
Too firm.. Not what I was hoping for. It is too firm.

Too narrow for 2 different LG phones. I had hoped to use this by the bed in our travel trailer for my phone. Alas, the plastic box doesn't fit either of our current phones or even an old one. I have the LG V40 my husband has the LG Stylo 4 and both phones are too wide for this thing. The 3 year old Sony Xperia doesn't fit for the same reason.

The sticky pad does adhere completely to the travel trailer wall and it really holds well. We're using this for our toothbrushes over the sink instead. Thos fit fine and the clear plastic is easy to clean as well.

A toss up between which is worse....the original bad smell or this spray.. This spray does get rid of bad odors - particularly those found in the rest room. It works pretty quickly and has a manual push button spray nozzle - this allows you to control the amount of the Stinky Winky you actually use. Which is a good thing. The Stinky Winky itself is questionable with regard to its own scent. It has a combination of citronella and peppermint and eucalyptus and other stuff. All those things should smell fresh....yet....it's almost like a weird mix of bug repellant and those dried eucalyptus leaves you used to put in vases for decorating. I am going to reserve this stuff for the very worst smells only.

Best as decoration only. 16 months and already fraying. I bought these last year at the Biltmore Estate in one of the many gift shops on the grounds. The towels are very pretty and soft and for infrequent use or as decorative accents only, they are just fine. But....if you actually want to use them to dry wet hands just get something else. These aren't really absorbent and they aren't all that durable. After 16 months, 2 of the 4 have begun to show thin spots and fraying after coming out of the dryer.

Thin, cheap feeling and not good enough for regular use. Very, very thin! The grey color is gorgeous and the four pillow cases with the twin set was a nice bonus and the saving grace. These are strictly a back up set for unexpected guests and definitely NOT good enough quality for regular use. The sheets have a distinct polyester, cheap feel against the skin.

Polyester/cotton blend. Average softness compared to other poly blends. Loose threads after washing. First off do not mistake the description for actual 800 thread count "cotton". These are a blend - 55% cotton and 45% polyester to be exact. I am not a fan of this trend in bedding products of listing thread count in big, highlighted print on the label and then the tidbit about it being a blend in small print way below in the description. (Real 800 thread count cotton pillow cases usually cost three figures by the way)

For a polyester blend fabric, these pillow cases are of average quality. They are soft and feel ok against your face - they aren't scratchy or rough by any measure. Mine are standard size and our extra thick, shredded latex pillows fit without oozing out. After washing and drying them in a normal cycle with warm water and a set of sheets in a similar thread count blend, these pillow cases didn't shrink. However.... I do see a couple of little loose threads in the top, decorative hemstitch. So my bottom line is a one star deduction for silliness with phrasing and description and a one star deduction for overall quality versus value.

Very thin, pretty design, seem flimsy. I bought these for use by a friend in Afghanistan so he would have an extra set. I washed them before sending them on to him and they are very, very thin. The fabric is soft and should be pretty cool to the skin in the summer heat, but these are definately not going to be warm in the winter months. The other concern is the flimsy stitching along the edges - one washing and I had to clip some threads that had come loose. Not a good sign. The bottom line is these sheets will be fine for a few months, long term use & laundering will tear them up pretty quickly. I won't buy them again.

Any jostling tips this over and dumps everything off. At first glance, this looks like a great idea. It's more of a half finished idea that just almost works properly. It's easy to assemble and arrange the little brackets in whatever configuration you want. The caddy is also weighs next to nothing.

I was able to stack six different items on it including tin foil, different sizes of freezer bags and that plastic wrap. All of the various sizes and box shapes were accommodated by the hooks. However, every time we tried to remove an item to use, the entire caddy tips over. Picking it up to move to a different location was just a mess - everything slides off. I think I was better off just leaving our stuff in an extra drawer.

Suction cups are persnickety and bottom basket is short. The bronze color on this is pretty and trendy for lots of bathrooms right now and the finish is smooth all the way around - no rough or sharp edges. There are some limitations on where and how it can be used though. For example..... Our master shower has both marble and glass and a removable shower head. The suction cups absolutely will not adhere to the marble with any weight in the caddy - it just pops off and everything bounces out. The cups do stick to the glass wall, but of course, that's not where the shower head is located. Meanwhile, the removable shower head means the entire hose has to hang in front of the caddy to be accessible and that in turn, blocks things in the top basket of the caddy.

I moved this to our guest bathroom with slightly better luck. There's a standard attached showerhead in there and simple ceramic tiles so the caddy fits correctly and the suction cups are holding. Now there's a new problem. The top basket is tall enough for standard shampoo & conditioner bottles, but the bottom basket is very short. It only holds those small tubes of facial scrubs and whatnot - if you have more than two full size bottles of hair stuff, a shaving gel and shower gel/wash then you will still need more space. As a guest bath unit with small size versions of those things, this unit will suffice.

Unlevel out of the box, but functional with some tweaking.. I may have actually found a shower caddy that I can live with despite an actual manufacturer flaw. Taking this out of the package, I noticed that it wasn't level. It actually tilts a bit to one side and the shelves aren't level. See the photo.

It doesn't actually hang on my shower head properly because we have a marble ledge along the wall exactly where the suction cups are and it makes the entire unit bow out. Plus there's that whole uneven, tilting problem. Since it does hold the large size shampoo bottles, I found a work around.

I took pliers are turned the top hook a quarter turn around hung it on the shower glass wall using the suction cups on the glass. I had to think about placement of my items to keep stuff from sliding - pesky tilt. However, almost two weeks now and the suction cups are holding with no trouble & it's working fine. Nonetheless, the final production quality needs closer scrutiny.

Absolutely not useful for hand or glass drying. Survives the laundry - no shrinking or color bleeding. Grrr. Yet another dish towel that does not actually dry my hands after I wash them. This drives me crazy. I just want to wash my hands and dry them without my skin being damp afterwards. This a pretty towel and the blue stripes don't bleed in the wash, nor does it shrink. The edges are fully hemmed and it feels well made so one assumes that it should last for years. I guess it will in my house, because it's best suited as decoration or perhaps a bread basket liner rather than an actual useful daily kitchen towel.

Can't compete with the Ninja for smoothies & older Black & Decker is better on ice. Color me unimpressed by this blender. Technically, it works, but not well and not as well as my two year old Black & Decker XL Blast blender. I do like the glass jar and the measurements marked on it and I like the gold color. I do not like the way it works.

Case in point - the booklet specifically mentions making whipped cream. Now, as a sensible cook who KNOWS how to make real whipped cream (and I do often), I understand that more than 90 seconds in any blender will produce a curdled disaster instead of whipped cream. You make whipped cream with a hand mixer. But I tried with the blender because the book said I could. Yep...67 seconds to a gross curdled mess. See the photos.

Ice. I wanted to make a single frozen drink. Six regular square ice cubes were too much for this blender. It left two of the cubes completely whole and one broken in half. The other three were nicely crushed/pulverized and suitable for a margarita etc. Mind you, to get to that point took almost 3 full minutes including stopping to scrape the ice down with a spatula and mix it by hand. When I emptied the jar there was a thick layer of ice stuck under the blades.

Mixing just light, soft things is fine. Yogurt, juice, and a little canned pineapple mix easily - you will have to pull some of the pineapple out from under the blades. Honestly, I prefer my Nutri Ninja for smoothies and my old XL Blast blender for bigger blending jobs.

Not as substantial as other Mepra designs. Hard corners on then ends.. Sole is the third setting of flatware from Mepra that I am comparing and this one isn't quite as lovely as the Dolce Vita or Vintage designs have been. On its own, this flatware is very nice, especially when compared to the average, inexpensive mixed material stuff we all bought right out of college at wally world. Yet next to the other high quality, well made, 18/10 stainless forks & knives from Mepra there is a notable difference.

Each one of these pieces is lighter weight than the other designs and slightly smaller. The Sole pieces just don't feel as substantial. The look reminds me a bit of an arts & crafts style with the long carved lines and the finish is that beautiful, bright high shine. These have fared well in the dishwasher and are nice to eat breakfast with - the knife does a good job with a ham slice. However, the hard corners on the ends of each utensil can be a little...pokey as you eat, even the spoons will catch your wrist in a coffee cup.

Easy to cook with, beautiful red color. Loose, wobbly handle makes it risky to use when hot. Compared to my high end cookware, this pan is just as nice to cook with. I did a smoked sausage in it and nothing stuck or stained. Making a quick gravy wasn't a problem either - everything mixed and nothing burned on. I like the deep, candy apple red color and the size of the pan is really functional.

My problem is with the handle. Mine arrived loose and wobbly, enough so that I don't feel comfortable using it to lift the pan off the stove with food in it. I have had to use pot holders both times that I cooked with it. See my photo - the silver base of the handle twists where it's connected to the pan wall. That's unfortunate because I sort of like this thing.

Make sure you have enough, correct wiring for the power to this. Very, very difficult to put together. Be prepared for lots and lots of serious cursing inspired by pure frustration. This unit seems like a neat idea at first. It might be in limited circumstances. For me though, this has been a huge hassle.

It comes in an enormous, 150lbs box. Every piece is flat packed for easy shipping, but that translates to full construction from minute one for the end user. The instructions are fuzzy at best and the entire process is very complicated and time consuming. It took me a total of 6 hours over three days to get the thing put together - with a helper on the last day.

It isn't as solid or sturdy as I expected either. That might be poor construction on my part, I'm honestly not sure. The heater part might work fine, but like another reviewer noted, if you use the heat and a big tv and a cable box, you risk losing power or throwing a breaker. Make sure you have enough dedicated power in the spot you use this. I will have to relocate it if we intend to watch tv and use the heater at the same time. For now, it's basically a big bookshelf with a faux fireplace in the center in a guest room.

Works, but wastes 1/4 of the juice. Quiet and easily cleaned. Lots of parts. Let me just say up front, we aren't typically inclined to juice. I mean, we drink juice and we eat fruit, but we buy it ready made for many reasons. Not the least of which is convenience. This machine was my way of trying to do some stuff at home to save a bit of money and perhaps time when compared to the old hand juicers or buying it.

I was a little taken aback by the size of this machine - it's really big and next to our full size Kureig coffee machine it requires the same amount of counter space. That's a big footprint. Dragging it in and out of the pantry means handling several loose parts each time, but leaving it in place full time makes the kitchen look cluttered.

I have made several different juices with this and it handled everything easily. We have done orange and pineapple, mango and pineapple, papaya and grapefruit (gross), and just plain limes to mix with tequila later tonight. (Don't judge, who has time to squeeze a lime when there's drinking to be done?) You have to peel everything, remove the cores and the seeds and then you can put the fruit in the machine. Honestly, it's considerably less work to use an old hand juicer and less messy. Nonetheless, the juice tastes good - it does froth like crazy though. I'll give them credit, the motor is very quiet.

My issue here is the amount of wasted juice in the pulp catcher. Easily a quarter of the juice goes in the waste catcher rather your glass or pitcher. That irks me after all the work/time to clean, peel, cut and juice the fruit. Especially an entire pineapple! For our regular, daily consumption, this isn't worth the effort. I would rather just buy cut fruit and eat it on the go because it's faster, easier and I get all of it.

Easy to put together. Uncomfortable to sit in.. I got an identical chair a year ago from a different brand and this one gives me a matching pair for the dogs. These chairs look nice and the fabric is true grey linen texture. Putting it together is a simple matter of just attaching the four legs.

However, both are uncomfortable to sit in for more than a few minutes. The seat cushion is hard and there's no lumbar support at all. I would never expect guests to actually use these. My dogs flat out love the chairs. They curl up against the rounded back and have support on three sides - like a raised bolster bed. It let's the dogs have furniture of their own and leaves my good chairs and sofa free for people.

Unstructured and very thin material. Best for light items. If you're getting these for less than two bucks each, then they are decent bags. A penny more than that and they are overpriced. This is thin material and floppy with no internal structure of any sort. They won't stand up without being held so using them in a grocery store line is going be slower than it should be. There's also no bottom. I'm hesitant to use these for more than light weight items - snacks, frozen meals, toilet paper etc. I won't use them for canned goods or meats because I don't want to risk torn seams.

Not actual blackout drapes. Midweight material n a nice grey color. First off, these are not blackout drapes by any stretch of the imagination and I'm really tired of companies trying to pretend their product is better than it actually is. These drapes do reduce sunlight and exterior light that comes into the room, but they do not blackout all the light. See my photo.

The drapes themselves are a nice mid-weight velvet like material that is soft and thicker than a regular curtain. These do help block a little winter air due to the thickness and that's certainly good. The color is a nice grey that works with most color palettes.

Plastic interior. Ok with cold drinks, but not as good with hot drinks. I waffle every morning between carrying a mug of iced tea or a double cappuccino with me to the barn. I have a couple of very good go cups from Built NY that are great at keeping things hot or cold for a couple of hours.

This is the first "Bubba" mug we've tried and it's ok, but not a replacement for my Built NY cups. This is nice looking and it fits perfectly in my F150 cup holders and it's been fine in the top rack of the dishwasher. The interior is plastic, the only stainless steel is a decorative wrap on the exterior.

I will use this for iced tea and Dr Pepper over ice because it is fine at keeping cold drinks cool for a couple of hours - not cold, but cool. As for coffee, well... I have a 15 minute drive to the farm and another few minutes to get gates unlocked and parked etc. The coffee was fine and hot. However, after sitting for 35 minutes while I feed horses, my coffee was tepid. It's just not good for my needs with hot drinks.

Coffee is cold in 90 minutes. Iced tea stays cold a long time. I had hoped this cup would work for my husband when he's on the road and needs hot coffee. However, he has given it back to me after three days with the comment "nope". Apparently, the claim of keeping hot drinks hot for up to six hours is an exaggeration. After 90 minutes the coffee is actually cold. That's not good.

I will say that keeping sweet tea cold for three hours was no problem at all. The cup does fit in the cup holders of the F-150 truck and the rubber grip is definitely nice. This one doesn't slip out of my hand if I'm driving or walking. I'm just keeping this for cold drinks and still looking for a coffee cup for my husband.

Ugly and small. Nice as cat bowls. I just can't get past how ugly these bowls are. Ugly doesn't inhibit functionality, but it does mean I only have limited uses for them. They are also small - they certainly aren't big enough for a bowl of cereal or soup for an adult. However, these do make fine cat bowls for for dry food and water. They are easy to clean and seem close to indestructible.

Installation parts aren't finished or are broken. Ok for shoe storage. I wanted to love this little cubby bench, yet.... it's only partially functional due to poor materials. First, this is smaller by far than the photos lead you to expect. It's still a very functional size for our needs, but we're off. We'll use it for shoe storage near the front door and as a seat for two short dogs to perch on when we're walking into the house.

Assembly of this bench was ridiculous. There are multiple pegs that hold the base to the vertical shelf walls and the end pieces. These pegs snap in half like a matchstick with any pressure. Three arrived in my box already broken. Then you screw in and use a bolt thing to secure the rest of it. That was easy enough, but two of the holes weren't completely finished, so I had to re-drill them. The end result is that the entire unit is less stable than it should be and I will always be concerned about any weight on it causing a collapse. However, it will still serve as a shoe storage spot.

Not meant to hold anything heavy without additional bracing. I intended to use this cabinet as overhead storage for cups and bowls in a weekend cabin. However, the included pressed board hanger is way too flimsy. It might be fine for a short term install that won't involve any real weight being put inside. Instead, we ended up having to build a brace out of real wood and attaching it to wall studs. The cabinet itself looks nice, but I seriously doubt it will last more than a year or two before it begins to come apart.

Shrinks in the wash. Nice dark grey color. I don't care for the tub things on my feet so I'm using this as a cat bed instead. He actually loves this. The rug fabric is soft and the dark grey is a nice color. I've washed this in cold water and low heat in the dryer and it does shrink a bit. I'm of the opinion that it won't last long.

Very thin. Better a seat covers than throws. Well, there's a reason these are sold as a two pack. Each blanket is thin and just not as soft or cuddly as the normal fleece throws we have. They have survived a trip through the washer and dryer without shrinking. I'm actually using these blankets as seat covers on two armchairs for the dogs rather than as blankets.

Well constructed, comfy to walk on. Very greenish blue overall. Mmmmm...in person, this is definitely more green/blue than just blue. It's definitely more greenish than I thought or wanted. I'll have to relegate this rug to the prep area of the laundry room. The quality is excellent, which is what I expect from Mohawk. It's soft and feels nice under barefeet, but it's not super thick or fluffy.

Air flow is lower than our other cooler. I have a big swamp cooler like this one from Keystone that significantly out performs this one in a couple of ways. This one isn't bad, but it does not move much air despite the oscillating vent. I can feel the air flow from 25 feet away on the Keystone, but 12 feet away from this one and it loses it's oomph.

The thing with these evaporative coolers is they are only effective in limited climate situations. You need real air conditioning in East Texas due to the constant high humidity here, but out at the ranch in West Texas, these can help make you reasonably comfortable. The humidity averages 10 to 15% on most days out there and the evaporative action is noticeable. But again, this particular unit just isn't as cool as the other one - that may be because of the lower air flow, I'm not sure. However, I think it will be fine in conjunction with the other unit in our small cabin.

Very flashy and full of extra decorations that don't mix with a house cat. Well, this is ok and it is definitely big enough to be used under a large Christmas tree. However, it's just way too busy and bedazzled for my taste. In person there's a lot more going on than in the pictures. Sparkles, glitter, and a weird, fake fur trim glued to outside edge. It's an open invitation to our cat to come wreak havoc. I think we will just go back to our simple red skirt and call it good.

Open on bottom. This is not a storage bag, it's a clothing top cover. The bottom is completely open, so your things are exposed. I had intended to use this for winter coat storage in the loft of our cabin, but because of the open bottom, that won't work. It is handy if just wanted to protect stuff from dust in a regular closet.

Not really effective for calming. But...ok as treats. As treats these are good - all 8 dogs like them. I have two dogs who are nervous Nellies in thunderstorms and I tried these the other night to help them feel calmer. One dog did seem very slightly more relaxed, but still jumpy. The other dog.... absolutely zero effect on him. Still shaking, pacing and upset. I had to resort to half a Benadryl (per our vet, don't just randomly give your dogs OTC medications) and he was able to settle down and sleep a bit while the storm raged outside.

Sits low to the ground for a tv. This thing is reasonably simple for one person to put together. But it is heavy. It looks nice once it's all assembled. Unfortunately, it's short and our tv is way too close to the floor on it. We have rowdy dogs and it would be just a matter of time before they slammed into it and broke something.

Instead, I'm converting the shelves into wall shelves in a spare room. They will make a nice display area for photos and the like.

Random snacks and candy. Hmmmm. We just are not impressed with this box. It's fine as a basic gift for someone you don't know well or as a generic office type thing. There are snack size items we've all heard of - Chex Mix, popcorn,  Jelly Belly beans, Rice Krispies treat, box of Nerdz candy and other odds and ends like candles. Absolutely none of this stuff is interesting or special in the least. No way would I expect to see this offered for over twelve bucks.

Filter works well. Actual use is cumbersome. This is not as good as I expected. It filters the water and definitely does what it says. It's the day to day functionality that irritates me. It looks like a sizeable pitcher, close to a gallon, but it only holds half the water. The quantity is reduced be the length of the filter - mine will not process water after it reaches the bottom of the filter. This means I have to do the whole process twice to get an actual pitcher of purified water.

The other thing is the pour spout and lid. It flops open and can even fall out as you pour. If you hold it down and pour, that's fine, but it's a multi finger operation. There's no reason this lid can't have a little catch of some sort to prevent spilling.

Two strands don't work out of the box.. These are very tiny bulbs on a very thin, easily bendable string/line. They are a soft white, almost Amber color when out. I've used these on the top of a fence to illuminate the gate when needed after dark. They just sort of show the area they are on, but don't provide any real light - more of a nightlight effect. I could see using a few of these strings on a Christmas tree actually because they don't get hot.. Unfortunately, out of the six strings of lights in my box, only four actually work.

Works well on area rugs, only ok on bare floors. Makes a squealing noise. I'm a fan of stick vacs for daily quick removal of dog hair. I have a five year old Dirt Devil stick that's going strong, so I had high expectations for this one.

This has the ability to be a hand vac and a long cord and it weighs next to nothing. The bin is easy to remove and empty, but as with my older Dirt Devil, you have to pull out the dusty filter first. I dislike that detail, but it's not the end of the world.

This is actually good for area rugs - the brush spins fast enough to pull dog hair and whatnot out of the rug. Use on bare floors is so-so and I think the Bissell stick is better for bare floors and pet hair. My real issue is that this unit is very loud - louder than my Dyson cordless with it's more powerful motor. Additionally, there's a weird, high pitched squeal on my vacuum. It's enough to make me choose one of the other small vacuums that I already have on hand.

Ok midline quality polyester/cotton sheets. I love high quality linens and I don't mind spending real cash on the good stuff. We have legitimate 800 thread count cotton sheets that are awesome and have lasted years. These sheets don't even come close to the softness or overall quality of those. The so called 1000 thread count is marketing nonsense because these are not 100% cotton - they made of a combination of cotton and polyester.

I've run these through the washer and dryer twice and they are shedding fuzz like crazy. The sheets did soften a bit and they are comfortable to sleep on. The full elastic bottom sheet is a very nice touch and helps keep everything in place over a thick pillow top mattress. The thicker fabric makes these more suited for cooler weather than midsummer for us though. I wouldn't expect to pay more than fortyish bucks for this set.

I hate it, husband likes it a lot. Very firm. So this pillow has two different ratings in our home. A two star from me and a four stars from my husband....three star final compromise. It's very firm and way too solid for my tastes. I felt like I was sleeping with the arm of the sofa instead of an actual pillow. I definitely prefer my Caspar pillows. This thing is also hot for me and my neck just feels like I'm sleeping on a heater.

My husband, however, said it doesn't feel hot at all to him. He also likes the angle of it and feels like it gives him a bit of extra support. After ten nights, he is happy to continue using it in conjunction with his other, equally hard memory foam pillows.

Scarves or hats only.. This is a very light duty hook hanger. It's best used with things like scarves or hats. Leashes are a bit too heavy - it definitely won't hold handbags. Mine was missing the screws the box said were included. It still holds over the top of the door, but even with screws it would still be weak.

The red dye does bleed a bit in the wash, some shrinking. Generally decent for casual use.. There's something nice about using a cloth napkin instead of half a paper towel at dinner. It just feels a little more... grown up and certainly more responsible than wasting all that paper every year. These are cotton, so they are soft. Of course they also shrink because they are cotton. After running these through the laundry twice, several have shrunk and the red dye definitely bleeds, so be sure to wash them with other red colors. I think these napkins are fine for casual, every day use, but I would not depend on them for formal gatherings.

Thinner than others and they shed. These aren't as nice as the photos suggest.  At best, these are adequate towels like you might find in an older, midrange motel. They shed. A lot. Plus, the fabric is thinner than brand name towels in a similar price range. I'm using them as camper towels and they are good enough for that, but not as guest bath towels.

Veneer glued on plastic. Totally functional, but very basic.. RealVeneer is what the description and name ought to say rather than wood. I mean, technically, there is wood here, but it's just a wafer thin sheet glued on the bottom of the plastic tray. Like the thin roll out veneers over that cheap throw-away desk we all had in our freshman college dorm. Nonetheless, the tray in totality is perfectly functional.

It fits on the back of our guest toilet and holds a couple of extra rolls of toilet paper, a wipes container and two bottles of the Poo Pourri spray. My theory is that the items one might need ought to be handy and not hidden or hard to access....It is the bathroom after all. The lip on this tray is deep enough to keep everything from in place.

Holds a lot, weak adhesive. Updated review - dropped to 3 Stars

After a week on the wall, with a hairbrush, a tiny tube of eye cream, a tube of toothpaste and a stick of deodorant in the basket, it fell off the wall. The adhesive strip completely dried up and the whole kit and kaboodle fell to the floor. The second basket is still on the wall, but it has only tissues in it now because I don't trust it.

*****Original review below*****

*****You can never have enough little storage shelf things in an RV. These use an adhesive to attach to the walls rather than screws - a must in an RV since they are built so cheaply. The walls don't support nails etc.

The hooks to hold the shelf to the adhesive sticker are stuff and a bit difficult to attach, however, they do hold on. The adhesive is strong and attaches fast - we felt comfortable using the baskets in an hour.

Two days later, these are both still solidly attached and holding multiple small items - hooray for a cleared bathroom sink area! I have deodorant, skin lotion, eye cream, a small bottle of liquid Benadryl, bottle of aspirin and a bottle of allergy pills 8n one basket with no problems.

NOT blackout curtains. These are very pretty and easy to hang. However, I wanted what was advertised... BLACKOUT curtains. These are absolutely not blackout or even room darkening curtains. They are thin and just a single layer of fabric so the sunlight shines on in. As regular curtains, these are fine.

Filters are hard to find. Best for single, small room. Air purifiers are one the things where the old adage, "you get what ya pay for", is true. This is a decent, lower end purifier that does a decent job for a low price point. It's not going to deal with a ton of pollen or pet dander because it is just not big or powerful enough.

This purifier does fine a small space, like a home office or bedroom with minor air quality issues. It does have a timer and a so called sleep mode that runs a bit more quietly than the regular cycles. It is a bit quieter, but not a bunch. It does move a fair amount of air and that's good. My primary reason for the 2 star deduction is the inability to find replacement filters. These are not washable, so you need new ones when they get clogged, but they just aren't available.

Thick with rough, scratchy fabric. Ok. I love a thick, soft comforter on every bed and we have ten of them in different styles and fabrics. I change our linens twice a week minimum so they also need to be washer and dryer safe. This one is a decent comforter in many ways and sort of blah at the same time.

It's thick and well stuffed so I think it will be warm this winter and all the rope style hems are well made. That same fabric is scratchy and rough to the touch - even the dogs don't like napping on the bare comforter. I washed and dried this thing before using it and it's still stiff and scratchy. It's a good, basic comforter, but we have three others that are much better for about half the cost.

Nice under the cat food bowls. Fringe frays fast. If you need thick, sturdy placemats, then these probably aren't what you want. They are thin and almost see through. The fringe on the edges is pretty, but flimsy and will fray in the washing machine. However, I chose these to use under the cat food bowls only. For my purposes, these placemats are just the right size and keep the stray food off the counter. The cat doesn't mind the texture and I don't mind that the fringe is a little frayed after washing.

Heavy, dense bread, undercooked crusts. I love homemade bread and have been making all our bread for several years now. I started with a sub-fifty dollar machine and upgraded to a very fancy, high end bread machine. I still use my inexpensive first unit the most often actually. This unit is my 3rd bread maker and its definitely running third place to the others.

We made 4 different loaves over the last two days using 3 recipes - all ended with subpar results each time. The crusts were always too light on each setting and the light crust setting loaf wasn't completely cooked. One of the other loaves never rose fully - that could have been the yeast quality/quantity or the bread machine, I'm not sure.

I'm using tried and true recipes that we know make light, delicious breads and fresh ingredients including King Arthur bread flour. All four loaves were very, very dense and chewy. They reminded me of bagels in texture and chewiness. The double kneading wands create a dual ball of dough and I suspect that has something to do with the thick, heavy end product.

I'm going to fiddle with my recipes a bit and try this machine a few more times because there are several things to like about it. I like the large numbers and buttons on the front face - very easy to see. I also like that this machine puts out less direct heat while cooking than my other two. Its better insulated and the heat stays primarily inside where it should be.

It's ok, could be a lot better. I'm not thrilled with this unit, but I don't hate it either. I've used it twice with mixed results so far. The entire machine is unbalanced and I have to sort of slip something under one leg to make stay level for cooking.

As to the actual omelettes, they are edible and better than expected once you figure out the quantities. The first time we used 4 eggs, cheese, and ham and it was clearly too much. The middle never really cooked. I ended up throwing all of it in a skillet and just doing a scramble. The second batch, we used 2 eggs, cheese and ham and everything was done completely. Unfortunately, that's just a single serving for an adult, so you end up doing a second batch as well.

Doesn't cool as well as window units with lower BTUs. If you are looking at the 12,000 or even 14,000 BTU ac units to cool larger spaces, be aware that these portable machines aren't quite as capable as traditional window units of the same BTU measurements. I don't really understand why that's the case, but it is. We have a 640sqft weekend cabin with two window units in it - one is 8,000 BTU and the other is 10,000. They keep the cabin a very comfortable 72 degrees all summer - even when it's 96 degrees outside with a heat index of 104. So that's my base point for comparing this portable, 12,000 BTU machine to our existing set up.

This machine loses out to window units in a small space because it takes up floor space and still needs to occupy window space for the vent hose. Yes, it can be relocated to a different room if needed, but you still have to have a free window there and a three prong outlet - this is on wheels, but it weighs the same as a window unit.

As to the actual cooling ability....well that depends on your room size and insulation and the weather. I'm in East Texas with both high heat and high humidity so our heat index (misery factor) has been 102 to 105 for the past week. I first used this machine in the cabin living area - about 350sqft and the upper limit of this unit's ability. I normally have the 10,000 BTU window in that area. This machine does cool, but nowhere as effectively as the window unit - it never felt quite as comfortable as normal and we ended up going back to the window unit on the second day.

We moved this to the bedroom next - roughly 275sqft and cooled very effectively by an 8,000 BTU window air conditioner. The Midea portable did cool just as well and the room stayed at 72 degrees for three days of use. However, it required removing a small chair to accommodate this air conditioner and that's a big negative for me. Every inch counts in a small space.

For us, the window units are definitely more comfortable/cooler in the cabin and they certainly take less space and trouble. Yeah, window ACs are ugly and a portable can't be seen outside, but that is less important than being cool to us. I don't care what it looks like if it's 98 degrees outside and 72 in the cabin. In the end, this machine will be relegated to an emergency back up only.

Sheds everywhere every day. On one hand, I really like this blanket. On the other hand, it aggravates me a bit. It's very soft and feels great to snuggle under with a book. It's thin and not heavy at all.

However, the thing sheds. Constantly and we're finding fuzzy fibers on the dogs, the sofa, the floor and in the washer filter. It's obnoxious enough to make me consider just tossing it out before I bother to wash it again.

Weak suction cups, not great in shower, but perfect for barn storage use.. This is meant for the shower and while the mesh material is appropriate for a wet environment, the suction cups are weak. My unit holds fine as long as it is empty. The problem starts when I put stuff in it....you know, when I try to actually use it to hold things in the shower. The suction cups just slide down the glass or worse, pop off entirely and send the whole thing flying.

So, I have repurposed this for use in my horse barn. Hanging on a stall door it works pretty well to hold things like hoof picks, mane brushes, random rags and treat bags. The water friendly mesh can be hosed off to clean and dries quickly.

Not non stick at all. Not non-stick at all. We made cakes yesterday and used this pan and a regular meal nonstick pan. Guess which one stuck and had to be scraped out? This pan. You definitely need to use Pam or a swipe of oil before baking in this.

The pan weighs nothing, but is still stiff enough to hold its shape and not spill the batter. Baking was fine as well - no trouble with the hot oven and it cooled fast. We threw it in the dishwasher and it was just fine.

Literally turned me into a coffee drinker. Easy to use, easy to clean, and the milk froth is fluffy. [[VIDEOID:c0970f8faeb3219291fd414d42b0a60e]]
***Reduced to 3 Stars for magnet failure April 2, 2018****

Two weeks and the machine stopped working. It kept flashing a red warning that the bean hopper door was open even when it was obviously closed. No way to get past the warning and make coffee. I searched online and found out that this is a known, ongoing problem in these Saeco machines involving a cheap plastic part and a magnet. I carefully pulled every single coffee bean out of the hopper and the opening to the grinder and found two things mixed in with the beans - a tiny magnet and a piece of plastic that had snapped off the hopper door edge!! See the photos.

I was able to slip the magnet back in place and the machine works now, however....in order to stop this from happening again, I have to very slowly open the hopper, ensure the magnet is still in place, put a finger over it and then add new beans and slowly close the door over the magnet. Seriously??? A four figure price tag and it has plastic parts snapping off and falling into the coffee beans - ridiculous. Philips is the parent company here and they darn sure need better quality control.

Historically, I dislike coffee - it always tastes bitter and burned to my palate unless it's mixed into one of those pricey store bought milkshake things. My husband though has always been a coffee guy so I chose this espresso machine primarily for his benefit. As it turns out, I'm completely hooked on it and use it multiple times a day.

This machine is really attractive and looks nice in our kitchen and it fits perfectly in the spot the old Kuerig used to live (that thing and the K- cups are outta here!) The initial setup took me about 40 minutes plus another 20 minutes reading the book cover to cover and breaking the machine down so I could fully understand how it works. Only then did I try making a beverage and I haven't stopped since in a week. Heck, I'm drinking a chocolate cappuccino as I type this.

The bean hopper holds a lot of coffee beans and feeds them directly into the grinder and brews a cup of magic. The used grounds fall into a container in tight little circles to be disposed of later. Making a coffee that even I will love has proven astonishingly simple and consistent and that amazes me. The milk steamer/frother thingy is the reason. It's best with ice cold milk straight out of the fridge - also, chocolate milk works in it and makes a chocolate latte to die for! I'm sure coffee afficianados already know that trick, but as a first timer it was the best little surprise. (We drink only real, natural whole cow milk - no fake vegetable oil "milk like" stuff, so I can't speak to how the steamer works there.)

You can select the brew strength and type of drink you want from a super strong little espresso or cafe crema, to a mid strength full size cappuccino with a very light, fluffy foam that you can swirl a design in. My husband and my mother are very happy with the traditional versions and both prefer a very strong coffee from a dark roast bean. I'm incredibly happy with the light roast and a low medium strength with hot milk and a dash of sugar. It makes great tasting coffee with simple, generic beans too - so far we've been using an Amazon Basics dark roast bean and a light roast Columbian bean under the Wally world label, both costing less for two pounds of beans than a latte at a coffee shop.

You definitely want to keep an empty mug under the spouts when your made coffee is finished - the machine does a quick rinse off the milk nozzle and before it goes into sleep mode, it rinses the coffee nozzle. Because it's actually fresh grinding the beans, it's loud as it starts your drink - you aren't going to sneak around making cappuccino at 5am, you better plan on sharing with whomever you wake up. Bottom line is that the Picobaristo is reasonably easy to get the hang of for a first time user and it is simple to operate even half asleep at 5:30am.

Misspelling is driving me nuts. We are dog people through and through. Our kitchen curtains in our RV have dogs on them and our 6 dogs go almost everywhere we go. I love the sentiment of this towel because it is very true.... Every meal and bite we take, they are WATCHING us.
This towel is more decorative than useful. It's thin and still stiff are going through the laundry. Plus the use of the incorrect tense makes me not want to use this thing.

Rough, scratchy fabric. Meh. These are ok and they fit two pillows we already have on the sofa. The gold color is pretty brash and I don't want to look at it year round - perhaps during the Christmas holidays only. However, the texture on these cases is scratchy and rough. Definitely not meant for actually using as you sit.

Not up to adult weight. The listing says this step can hold up to 300lbs. I beg to differ. My husband is 216lbs and it make a cracking noise within seconds of him standing on it. I weigh significantly less and it still feels wobbly.

Basic cover. Meh. This is definitely not the best sofa cover. It's a basic cover that does the job adequately. It slides in place and uses those stupid push down stick thingys beneath the cushions. What that means is every time people or the dogs bounce onto the couch, the sticks slide up a bit until they come out entirely.  Our regular sofa covers use big elastic straps and can tie so they almost never slide. The color is nice and it does cover our sofa, but there are better choices for dog homes.

Easy to install,  but fragile. I thought this would add extra storage in our RV - free up the cabinet with my ridiculously oversized spice collection.  Its light enough for an RV installation  and super simple  with just 4 screws to attach. Unfortunately, the pieces are very thin and prone to cracking. The support rails that hold the screws cracked twice as I put it up. I was using a handheld screwdriver, not a drill. I'm using the shelf, but for the boxes of Advantix and Heartgard for the dogs instead of heavier spice bottles.

Not terribly stable. I want to love this hall rack. It looks nice and has lots of designated space for storage of random items. Unfortunately, this is not really sturdy and it wobbles. The connecting pieces are not strong themselves and that definitely leads to instability once this is put together.

I am using it in my office as a decorative piece for light jackets, extra shoes and my tote bag of files and field use laptop etc. I keep an extra pair of heels, mud boots and steel toe shoes in my office because I never know for sure where my day will take me. This unit handles that stuff fine and it hasn't fallen apart. However, if you have a busy home with kids tossing book bags and shoes etc on it multiple times a day, this thing may not survive long.

I can feel the coils. Good enough for a night or two guest mattress, but not as your every night bed.. Well... this is one of things where the old adage "you get what you pay for" definitely applies. This mattress is value priced for good reason. It's not terrible, but it's not something I want to sleep on more than a few hours at a time and certainly not on a regular basis. Nor would I ask anyone else to do so. The advertising description literally says "you never feel the coils" and that might very well be true if you add a feather bed topper or foam topper to the mattress before you lie on it. I can feel the coil springs in this on my back, stomach and side. Burned one loaf, two others were fine. Moves a lot while kneading. Not as good as my older maker. I have a very inexpensive ( under forty dollars) Sunbeam bread maker that's happily produced good bread a couple of times a week for almost four years. It's larger than this Hamilton Beach machine and significantly heavier. This machine is prettier with it's stainless and black color - it matches my big appliances.

As for the actual bread making, I think this one has it's good points, but in the end, my old machine is better overall. This one does have a handy little tool for removing the paddle from the fresh loaf and the included flour cup and tea/table spoon.

I made a simple, buttermilk sandwich loaf first and bacon cheddar bread the second time. Both are our standard, go-to breads here and I typically make one of each every week. The buttermilk bread on the light crust setting came out dense, moist and a little chewy as it should. The basic cycle here is actually about 14 minutes longer than with my old Sunbeam maker. The bacon cheddar bread on a medium crust setting didn't fare so well. Halfway through the bake cycle, smoke billowed out of the lid and I had to unplug the entire thing - the uncooked, slightly blackened bread went in the trash. There was nothing in the bottom of the machine to cause the burn, so I don't know what the problem was. I have since made another buttermilk bread without a repeat of the smoke.

My real issue with this bread maker is that it bounces, wobbles and walks all over the counters as it mixes and kneads the dough. This could present a serious safety problem if you have limited counter space or set it too close to the edge. It moves about 8 inches every time I use it. My old machine literally has never bounced or shifted one iota. So, because of the bounce and the smoke issue, I will only use this again as an emergency back up to my older bread maker.

Doesn't live up to the competition. Refills are pricey. This is in our guest bathroom. It won't be used a lot in there compared to our master bathroom or kitchen which is just as well. We have the Purell foaming soap dispenser in the kitchen and compared to it, this one just doesn't measure up.

This is a manual push rather than automatic via battery power, so it can end up with a messy handle if you have lots of traffic through the bathroom. This machine is bigger, far more complicated and delicate than my other espresso machine and it is significantly slower. This unit does hold more water, but fewer beans. This one does have a specific setting for iced brew, but it tastes exactly the same as when I just make a lungo over ice in the Saeco - so nothing special there.

In side by side use, the DeLonghi is significantly quieter than the Saeco and that's a plus early in the morning. However, it literally took seven minutes to brew a simple lungo from start to finish - my other machine had already finished and I was drinking that coffee before this one finished. My Saeco has its own pitcher and the machine forces the milk through the steamer and directly into the cup and then the coffee is added - you get a hot cup of coffee with hot milk and real foam all at the same time. That one thing is reason enough to put this machine in the closet as an emergency back up in the event our good Saeco dies.

Pressing the button to release steam is unnecessarily difficult.... [[VIDEOID:92802fd7aaa86092f4cb77c6f2a66f96]] We got this AFMAT steamer trough Vine, but we didn't like it at all, and ended up paying for the PurSteam. The main issue is the convoluted trigger button system. With your thumb, you have to slide up a child lock tab, then press down on the button. The tab has lines or grooves on them to help your thumb grip, but it's not enough, you need to push from the bottom edge of the tab where you can get a grip, then press down, but your thumb ends up hurting after awhile. With the Pursteam, the Child lock is a button you push to slide and unlock. Then you no longer have to deal with it. You simply press the trigger on the handle. The AFMAT requires your thumb to press up on the child lock tab at ALL TIMES during use. Hard to articulate, so please watch the video.

Both the AFMAT and the Pursteam provide you with essentially the same accessories, so it boils down to the triggering mechanism. The trigger on the Pursteam is a no brainer winner. Here is a link to the Pursteam: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B06XHXFHWG/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1

Having said all that, not everyone will struggle with the AFMAT, some can probably grip and slide the child lock tab just fine. For others, it will be a knack that they need to master. It is actually difficult enough already that you have to concentrate on how hard or light to press at your cleaning target, let alone having to do that and at the same time make sure your thumb keeps pressing up on the tab. You see if you get close to an oven knob, you don't want to press too hard, the steam will bounce off the knob, you need to lighten your press. In power tools, I guess this is equivalent to what's called variable speed. The Pursteam's trigger handle makes it so much easier to control this variable speed.

We are subtracting 2 stars for the unnecessarily difficult trigger system.

Good loft bed, but some shortcomings that prevented this from being 5-Stars.... THE GOOD:

THE BAD:

They get the job done, but this is not the best bang for your buck.... Holds your sodas perfectly. For double stacking, you can have 5 cans at the bottom, and 4 at the top. One of the stock photos show 7 cans at the bottom, but I believe those are smaller thinner cans. It gets the job done, but we'll have to knock 2 stars for not being price competitive.
