They don't give you enough magnets.... THE GOOD:
--------------
* Universally sized so it should work with most home washer and dryers.
* Keeps clothing from falling off the back.

THE BAD:
------------
* Not enough magnets. Sure they're earth magnets, but they're small and spaced too far apart. There needs to be more of them. I think the bottom should be one long strip of earth magnet. Actually, I bet you that it doesn't have to be earth magnets. It can be standard tape magnet, but if it's continuous and covers the entire bottom rails, I bet you that would be stronger than small earth magnets that are spaced far a apart.
* Moves easily. You can flick it with your fingers and the entire wall wobbles. Again, this is due to not having enough magnets.
* For best strength, DO NOT connect the middle. It just so happens that in my situation, I need to split the middle anyway because there is a shelf bracket in the way. But even if I didn't have this shelf bracket, I would still split the middle. The reason is because if you connect the entire thing, then the entire width will be much shorter than the entire width of both your washer and dryer. The top of washer and dryers machines will also vary in design, some have raised edges, which makes it tricky to make sure all the brackets are connected on the same raised level. So I just split it up. This way, it's easier to manipulate how and where I want the brackets to stick. This may sound confusing, but you'll see once you buy it.

Overall, this is a so-so product. Every day we're fixing the brackets cause it gets moved a lot. So it's doing it's job in terms of not letting your socks fall off the edges, but it is not sturdy. I will install extra earth magnets when I have the time. I'll go 3-Stars.

It's not height adjustable, so I don't get the point of this.... JAN. 15, 2022 UPDATE:
---------------------------
* Since my review, they've removed the stock photo I mentioned that I thought was misleading, that made me think the box was height adjustable. This is a nice box. Probably more suited for your children's room than for the garage. I just think paying a higher price for the collapsing feature doesn't make sense. I thought the price was tied to the "adjustable" feature. There is no such feature, and the stock photo has been removed.

ORGINAL REVIEW:
----------------------

THE GOOD:
--------------
* Spacious 42L at about 17.5 x 13 x 13.
* Stackable.. that's it, that's all that's good.

THE BAD:
-----------
* Their 6th stock photo mislead me. I thought this box was height adjustable. I got it because I thought if I had any issues with clearance, I can just lower the height of the box. That's not the case at all. That stock photo is just showing you how thin it is when it's shipped to you.
* Lots of parts... you got the main frame, you got the bottom plate, you got a bumper guard that goes over the frame to give it stability, then lastly, you got the lid. When I was putting it together, I was asking myself, "What's the point of all this if it's not adjustable? Why not just get a sturdy one piece box?"
* All these moving parts, all this foldability design does not benefit you at all. It only benefits the manufacture because it allows them to save space when they ship them out. Think about that... the only time you'll fold this up, is if you don't use it. But why are you buying a box if you're not going to use it? I thought this thing was adjustable. I was thinking, wow, what a cool invention! LOL! It turns out, it's not. The fact that it folds benefits nobody but the company that sells it. Or, those rare occasions where you need to take a bunch of these boxes to some location. Realistically, how many are you going to buy at $42 a pop? If you're buying 5 to 10, and you need to transport them somewhere, yeah I get the benefit, you need to pack flat. Oh wait, I just described the company's scenario, right? LOL! They are selling hundreds or thousands of units, they need to pack flat to save on shipping!
* Price, these are not cheap. They are charging us more for a nifty design that benefits them, not us. Think about that. LOL!

In my garage, there is no point to all these moving parts, which are all points of potential failure. There are more economical solutions that are one piece (two with lid), and more sturdy than this box. BTW, I've seen the baskets that collapses at Costco, but I don't think twice about them because they don't cost $42 a pop. I don't understand the point of this design, if you have to charge consumers more for it because really, it doesn't benefit them. So I think 3 stars is generous.

Stylish look, but useful for light duty ONLY .... Very mixed feelings about these.

First, what'd good:
== size -- they're perfect for getting that last bit of mustard from a jar or stirring a bowl of creamy dip for a vegetable tray
== appearance -- very classy looking: gray silicone heads and stylish stainless-steel handles
== the silicone heads can be removed for cleaning

Now, the problems:
== the silicone heads do not fit tightly onto the stainless steel handles, so if you're trying to get that last bit of jam or preserves (or anything sticky), the head will slip right off
== the spoon head is very pliable, so it can't be used for any "heavy lifting" or scraping with anything more than very light force.

I'll definitely get more use out of the mini spatula rather than the spoon -- it's just too flimsy to be useful for anything but the lightest duty. Before I could give this set more than 3 stars, there would need to be some serious redesign so that the heads don't slip off so easily, and they can be strengthened to allow for more versatile use. I think they're OK -- but nothing I could really recommend at this time.

Despite description, these DEFINITELY warp .... These pans are the perfect size for my toaster oven, but they warp terribly at 350F or higher (haven't tried them at lower temps yet, but I'm not hopeful). The warping is severe: 1.5" on one corner (will post a picture later ... ).

I can still use them for some uses, but not if the degree of warping will interfere with the evenness of the bake. They work great for reheating things like pizza or baking a few cookies, but I wouldn't use them with anything that has a significant amount of liquid as it probably wouldn't stay in the pan.

I'm giving them 3 stars -- they're OK, but it's obvious that whoever wrote the product info here had never used them for actually baking something. I can still use them for some things, so I won't return them.

The filter part of the press is looking a little worn, but then I usually take it apart to clean after every use. It makes a decent cup of coffee (don't let the "6-cup" designation fool you; this makes a maximum of about 28 oz of coffee, which is just over 2 standard-sized mugs), once you figure out how coarse/fine the grind needs to be.

I like the flat-topped plunger -- I have two other French presses, one with a "ball"-style plunger, the other with a small knob, and this one is definitely easier on the hand.

If you're looking for a small French press to try out the idea of French press coffee, this might be a good economical choice. But if you're looking for something to handle daily heavy usage, you might want to spend a few more $$ and get something larger and more substantial/sturdy.

High quality, but usefulness? maybe not so much .... I've owned a couple of other "handheld" spiral cutters and currently own the larger hand-crank Paderno spiral cutter. So I've had some experience with these devices and eat spiral "noodles" a couple of times a week.

First, if you've never owned a spiral cutter and you're thinking of trying one, this might be a good choice. Much better design than most handheld units, easier to set up and operate, etc. It's a bit pricier than the cheaper ones, but the better design makes it worth it. It handles softer veggies (zucchini, cucumbers) fairly well, but you do have to be careful of the diameter. Still, it might be a good intro to the sport/art of cutting veggie noodles

If, however, you have experienced the pleasures of a well designed "crank" style spiral cutter, you will be very disappointed in this. The size makes it difficult to do larger veggies (sweet potatoes, rutabagas, etc.) without serious paring down to fit the small opening. Also the effort needed to twist the holder with the veggie is not trivial. As someone with shoulder and hand arthritis, I had difficulty with this.

Even if you've never used a spiral cutter, it might be worth it to add a few bucks to the cost of this and go for the other Paderno hand crank cutter. It's so much easier to use and you'll have more options (with less waste) of veggies to cut. I've been using the larger Paderno cutter a couple of times a week now for about 6 months, and it's going strong with no sign of any failure. Paderno makes quality stuff, and this little cutter appears to fit my quality expectations for the brand. Pity it's not more useful/easier to use.

I'm giving this an "It's OK" rating -- 3 stars. Just not that useful for me; might be a good intro to veggie noodles for a novice.

Great bell, NO certificate of authenticiy. The bell itself is stunning, it's heavy and has a genuinely magical ring. I know my daughter will cherish it forever, and I am glad that I bought it. Some may think I'm being a little bit too particular taking away 2 stars because of a missing piece of paper, so I'll explain my rationale.  When my daughter asked Santa for a bell from his sleigh for Christmas I had a slight panic attack. How could I possibly get something like that?  Fortunately I decided to search on Amazon since they literally have everything and what do you know, I found it! There were 3 different bells I was interested in, and honestly the certificate of authenticity was what made this product stand out from the others. It seemed like the perfect touch. Including shipping, I paid over $40 for a bell. I truly don't mind spending the extra money to get something that will be cherished for a lifetime, and the quality of this bell exceeded all expectations. But when you spend that kind of money, you expect to get exactly what you paid for and exactly what is supposed to be in the package. I do plan on making my own certificate to put in the box and obviously a 5 year old will never know the difference, but there's no way to get a gold seal and I have no time to get nice paper to print it on. If you're buying this bell for a child, just know that you most likely will not receive the certificate of authenticity. If that matter to you then look elsewhere; but if it doesn't, then i'm sure you will be extremely happy with your purchase.

Inexpensive Duvet with Minor Quality Issues. This duvet came pretty quickly after ordering. The duvet cover is very thin, and appeared wrinkle-free, with clear buttons at one end and ties at each corner (on the inside), so you can tie the duvet to it.

As soon I'd opened it up, I'd decided to put it on the new, white down comforter that I had also purchased here on Amazon. After turning the duvet cover inside out and all four corners were tied to the comforter, I turned it all inside out (if you haven't learned to roll up a duvet and cover to put it on easier, check out a video on YouTube) and buttoned it up.

It looks pretty, but I had to sew part of the duvet cover, as the factory managed to miss a six inch portion at the top of the duvet cover that wasn't sewn. I was annoyed that right out of the gate there was an issue with quality, but I knew it wouldn't be an heirloom piece with the low thread count and the price I'd paid. The comforter was not that expensive, and I didn't have a lot of money to spend on a cover, but I just wanted to save the duvet from getting soiled with regular use. I think it will do the job but I suggest anyone buying this brand to do a quick quality check when your item comes in, so you can return it within the window. I'd not contacted the manufacturer because I don't have the time or energy to send it back, so I docked stars for a lack of quality control, instead.

Not what it’s cracked up to be.. I’ve owned a Bunn coffeemaker for years that was on its last leg. I decided to venture out and try something different and after watching YouTube reviews for 4 hours and reading reviews, I decided to take the plunge and buy this maker as it had the highest rated in the price range I was looking at I love my coffee and am by far not a coffee “connoisseur”. I just love a good strong cup of coffee to get my day going. I’m a Foldgers kind of gal occasionally who occasionally steps into the wild side and buys Starbucks coffee (already ground) and maybe some flavored coffee here and there.
So let’s get to the “beans” of this. The maker itself is flimsy. As most pots do, it “sticks” to the counter as you pull it out to fill the water. The first time I pulled it out, I pulled the whole top section off the machine. Yes, heart attack ensued thinking I broke it. After wrestling with it and getting it back together, I push a washcloth under it for easier gliding. One would think for that amount of $$ it wouldn’t come apart quite so easy and wouldn’t be plastic. You’re unable to put the top of the carafe on while the filter is still in place. It’s not a huge thing, but beware of steam burns when you’re dumping the hot grounds.
Next, when you dump the water from the thermos carafe into the maker, be prepared to have water all over your counter. As there isn’t a pour spout in the carafe it makes a huge mess. A pot of coffee is done in about 6 minutes which is nice. No waiting for 10-12 minutes. The coffee itself is, well a cup of coffee. I didn’t notice a huge difference from my Bunn, and I even ventured out and bought some fine ground Genevalia. The coffee is good and hot, which is where you can tell a significant difference from a Bunn. My Bunn temped at 165 and this one temps at 200 after a cycle completed. The thermos carafe does keep it warm, but not for an extended amount of time. Maybe an hour tops, but make sure you get the lid to the carafe on immediately when it’s done or a lot of heat is lost quickly. Now for my very least favorite thing about this maker. It states it’s a 8 cup coffee maker, which is true. BUT, one very grave point I breezed by in my research is the 8 cups is actually 8 5oz cups. Very few people I know, including myself, drink out of a 5oz coffee cup. Most coffee mugs are 10oz mugs, which means you get 4 regular sized cups of coffee from one carafe. This isn’t ideal when you’re jetting around getting ready for work and have to stop to make another pot.
To sum this up, I’m disappointed with this purchase and had I not have thrown the box away when I got it, I’d send it back and buy another Bunn.

Nice idea, but cheap execution. So there is a lot to like about this: it's stainless steel, has a nice aesthetic, and (my favorite!) comes with a little multi-purpose funnel that you can use to put powders/supplements in.

In terms of the bottle itself, my biggest gripes are (a) that the top doesn't close very easily. You have to push from the back of the circle part to get it to close. Or apply a little pressure upward under the front lip and then press down. If you pop the top and try to close it absentmindedly with 1 hand, it won't close. And (b) the cap doesn't screw on very smoothly. Not like my Blender Bottles, which are smooth. I haven't had any leaks, but not having a smooth screw-on makes me feel like it may not be screwed on properly (but it usually is).

The aesthetic of the bottle is great. It's a clean white color and the logo sticks off a little, which is a nice touch (i.e., it's not just a cheap screen printing application). The blender ball that comes with this is a little wider and flatter than the Blender Bottle ball, but it seems to work as well.

My favorite part, and the only piece that will be put into my regular use rotation is the funnel. Being able to take some pre-workout, or a scoop or protein/supplements to mix later is really useful. And much cleaner than putting a scoop of something in a ziplock bag (which has backfired on me before. RIP)

Overall, for $26, I like the stainless steel Blender Bottle more, which I also have. This one isn't bad by any means, but for the same price ($1 less, actually), you can get a higher quality bottle.

My biggest complaint is that the thermal containers don't screw on very smoothly, so it makes you wonder if the lid is aligned correctly (it usually is). I haven't had any leaks or anything, but it's a little annoying screwing the lids on. Secondly, there is a little bit of sloppy construction on the bag. I circled what I mean in one of my pics. Basic Clips that Work Pretty Well. The Marrywindix beach towel clips are basic, plastic clips. Nothing fancy, but they do work pretty well. They expand wide enough to clip onto fairly thick items, more so than a regular sized clothespin. They come in an assortment of bright colors, but they do have a cheap look to them. They look like something you would pick up at the dollar store or other discount store. They are not particularly sturdy feeling, but they don't fall apart at first use either.

*I received these clips from Marrywindix for the purpose of trying them out & reviewing. My thoughts & opinions are my own.

Not as Soft as Other Microfiber Sheets. First let me start by saying that I am a fan of microfiber sheets. Of course I love expensive high thread count cotton sheets, but in recent years I just haven't been able to justify spending that amount of money on them, so for the last 3 or 4 years I have been using microfiber sets. In general, microfiber sheets are soft (not quite as soft as the high thread count cotton) and long lasting (definitely don't become threadbare like the cotton ones). Now let me focus on these sheets. On the softness, they are soft, but I expected softer. I've had some microfiber sets that are super soft and these are not. They fit well on my Sleep Number mattress/bed. They easily go over all of the corners without coming up. The biggest issue that I have with these sheets is that the stripes go horizontally on the top sheet. The picture has the stripes going vertically, but because of the finished edge on the top sheet, the only way it goes is horizontally which is strange, but also frustrating. This may just be a manufacturing error and not representative of all of their striped sheet sets. I will use these because they are okay, but I would probably not repurchase these particular sheets.

Huge!. This is a huge! Much larger than I anticipated. It has to be assembled. It's really thin and wouldn't stay in the box shape well, so we had to tape it to keep it together. The opening where you put the cards tore within the first few cards that were deposited into it. It does hold a lot of cards, but it's not sturdy enough to save for another party.

Easy to Tip Over. This was quick and easy to assemble. Out of the box, it only took a few minutes for my husband to put it all together. The issue I have had with it is that the baskets can get knocked out of it a little to easily. My cat bunted the lower basket and one of the sides fell out its notch. It was easy to put back in place though.  It also doesn't have a very large weight capacity. If you put items in the top basket and nothing in the lower ones, it tips over. The handle is merely for decoration. If you pull on it, it falls apart. It doesn't push well either. It looks good and if you find the right spot for it, I think it can be a decent storage unit.

Comfortable, But Doesn't Quite Fit. We are in desperate need of a new mattress, but we're trying to delay that expense for the time being. I thought a memory foam topper might be a good temporary solution. It arrived compressed and expanded when the plastic covering was removed. There were no foul odors like some foam or plastic products. The mattress cover that comes with it is very nice and much better than the mattress cover I was using before. The cover easily fits over the topper and the mattress. Our bed is a regular king size, but this does not fit it. It hangs over the edge on one side and doesn't meet the edge of the other side. We turned it thinking that might be the problem, but we still had the same issues. Sleeping is very comfortable and it actually provided more cushion so when I turned during the night, my sore knee didn't hurt as much as it usually does. Another thing that I liked was that I didn't notice my husband's tossing and turning as much either. I struggled with how many stars to give it. I do like it, but the fact that it doesn't fit my bed is kind of annoying.

Easy to Assemble. We have an outdoor bar table that needed additional seating. While I realize these are steel and could rust if exposed to weather conditions, we are keeping these in the basement and taking them out to the patio as needed for the time being until we find some nice outdoor stools that we like. These were fairly easy to assemble. It comes with an Allen wrench and was put together within 20 minutes. My husband said he could have used his own tools which may have sped up things a little, but it was easy enough without. The stools ook nice and sleek. They aren't very comfortable for extended periods of sitting, but for short term sitting they are okay. One of the poles had a couple of dents on the lower piece. Depending on how much the chair is extended, the dents aren't noticeable because the upper piece covers it up.  Overall, these are decent and affordable stools.

Fun Idea. I love baking and trying out new cupcake flavors. I was excited to give this a try. It's a fun idea to make apple pie flavored cupcakes, but the end results are just so-so. It was easy to use the packets of flavoring, but the finished taste was too artificial. Of course, my family did eat them, but they all agreed that they didn't recommend getting them again. In addition to the flavor packets, the kit also includes disposable icing bags, icing tips and cupcake liners which are things we go through a lot of during baking season.

Pretty Basic. The Amazon Basic line is just that, pretty basic. I like the product line, but they're nothing fancy. Some of the items are surprises and better than expected, but some such as this one are just average or okay. This bench is a pressed wood kit that you have to assemble. Instructions were easy enough to follow. I ordered this to be used at the top of the basement stairs for our 21 year old son, who lives in the basement,  to use for his shoes and belongings. It's sturdy enough, but I've told him not to sit on it because he's a big guy. It is an improvement of having him leave his stuff on the floor at the top of the basement. The cushion is thin, but adequate. It attaches to the bench with vel-cro so it doesn't slide around. Overall, it's okay. It does the job.

Decent Frame. This frame allows you to hang it either horizontally or vertically. The back of the frame is secured with little metal tabs that have to be bent to remove the backing so you can insert your photo. I've had other frames with similar tabs and if you bend them too many times, they sometimes break off. That's okay as long as you still have enough others to hold the back in place. The frame is light weight. One of the four corners isn't glued all together completely, leaving a slight gap. Another of the corners has a spot where the paint is worn away or something. From a distance, it's not too noticeable.  Overall, it's a decent frame. I would compare them to the high end discount store ones, if that makes sense! The discount stores often have super cheap frames and then other frames that are more expensive. Their more expensive ones are not as nice as what you might find at a department store or other higher end store.

Clear Pocket is Nice. My daughter is going off to college in the fall and I thought these would be nice for protecting some of her nicer clothing. When I ordered them, I didn't pay attention to the actual measurements, but the description I got said "24''×32'' It is suitable for storing short coat, dress, sweater, T-shirt and child's clothes". In actuality, it won't fit all of the intended items because it's too short. We may be able to find some sweaters or short coats to put in them, but for most clothing items, these are way too short. Now, disregarding the length, the covers are made well. They material is very thin and light weight. The clear pocket is a nice feature so you can see what's inside without unzipping it. Overall, they're okay.

Took Much Longer to Bake. I was really excited to try these disposable baking pans. What a great idea! Unfortunately, I found them to be just okay. I tried baking a coffee cake. I used a recipe that I had used many times before. I did spray the pan before using. The recipe says to bake it for 30-40 minutes and to test it with a toothpick. After 30 minutes, almost the entire cake was still pretty liquid and it just jiggled. I added 10 more minutes, and there was barely any improvement. I kept adding an additional 7-9 minutes after each time I checked. After I had doubled the cooking time, I took a knife and inserted into the center and it was still batter consistency. The outer edges were lightly browned. I added a total of 10 more minutes before the center was mostly cooked. It was a little soft, but it wasn't batter like any more. I'm guessing it has to do with the material of the pan. Metal pans conduct heat whereas this one doesn't. In the end, my coffee cake was just okay. Of course we ate it, but it was a bit disappointing. I'm probably not going to try using them to bake anymore, but I do think they will work for something such as casseroles.

Well....... First of all, this book case is very heavy.  The good thing is, once we opened the box, there are smaller boxes inside so we could take the pieces in the house in multiple trips. The next thing we discovered, is that the ball bearings from one of the drawers had fallen out of slider/glider and fell all over the floor. Later during assembly, the glider/slider fell out of the drawer, too. So basically, one of our drawers doesn't open and close very well. Another issue is that there was a dent on one of the metal sides. All of those issues may have resulted during transit. Assembly took longer than expected. My husband puts together all kinds of furniture and is very handy. The directions were not always clear. For example, it we didn't know which way (up or down) to put the piece that the drawers go inside. My husband used his own tools such as an impact driver. From start to finish it took about two hours. The finished piece is sturdy and looks nice. The dented side faces the wall fortunately. Overall, it's okay.

Cute But Pretty Basic. This is a cute black collage style frame, but pretty basic. It is primarily a table top frame. There is one picture hanging hook on the back off one of the individual frames, but it would take 2 to hang properly. Plus the back that does have the picture frame also has the stand attached to it. The picture hanger is on the bottom (middle) of the frame and if you turned it around so you could utilize the hanger, then the stand part hangs down. I do plan to hang it up on the wall but I will use Command strips to do so. The frames are plastic and pretty sturdy. Two of the corners are not glued well and have a gap. It is a nice way to display a grouping of photos.

Weak Scent. I love burning scented candles. Unfortunately these candles are barely noticeable when they burn. I could barely even detect any scent when I practically put my nose in it.My family members agreed with me regarding the amount of scent or lack of it.  As far as burning, I haven't had any problems with them. They seem to be burning evenly and cleanly.

Pretty Pink Stripes. This towel is cute. I really like the pretty pink stripes. It's not a plush beach towel by any means, but it's not one of those super thin ones either. The size is fine and as expected. I wouldn't have bought this if I had been able to touch and feel it first because I prefer thicker, plush towels. This is the kind of the towel that I would send with my kids to camp because I wouldn't care if something happened to it. It's just okay in my opinion.

It Works!. I'm in my early fifties. I'm not having hot flashes yet, but I do find that I get too warm at night. I was excited to give this pillow case a try. I used to be one of those people who would frequently flip my pillow over during the night so I could have the cooler side. But over the last few years, I started using memory foam pillows that have a definitive right side, so I have gotten out of the habit of flipping my pillows in order to get the benefits of the memory foam. One side of this case is significantly cooler than the other. It's kind of fascinating to me how that works. The other side is softer and warmer. I have found that the cool side isn't continuous and it does reduce the amount of coolness rather quickly. I would estimate it to last for just a few minutes, but if you move your head to another spot, it's cool again.  I do like it when it's cool, but for the majority of the night, it's not.

Flawed. This is a plastic frame with mat. The frame itself is decent. It's light weight and looks good. It has hangers on the backside so you can hang it vertically or horizontally. One of the sets was flawed with a strange line through the glass. My husband thought at first that it was a piece of protective plastic film, but upon closer inspection, it was a flaw in the actual glass. It's not a crack. It's really odd and something we've never seen before. The other one was fine. I've included a picture. It's hard to see because of the reflection, but the line is in the middle from the top of the glass.

Nice Lantern, But Lights Don't Show Up Well. The lantern is actually really cute. The sugar skull punch out design looks nice. The finish on the lantern is even and well done. There's a little light at the bottom of the inside, but it doesn't produce enough light to show the punch out design well at all, even in total darkness. You can see the chin area of the skull, but not the top half, so the effect is pretty much lost. I've been playing around with different alternative lights to get a better lit image, but it's a little difficult because the interior bottom is not flat. I've had the most luck with a string of battery operated fairy lights. I think this would be a 4 or 5 star item with better light. A bonus would be if it included a timer feature (runs for 5 hours) or something like that on the light.

Cute Concept. I've always gone all out with Advent calendars for my kids. They're both in college now, but I still like making them for them. We used to have little cabinet type thing with drawers, but that really limited what I could put in them. These little bags give me more flexibility. The bags are decent. They're small but nicely made. The dates are just stickers and the stickers don't stick really well to the burlap bags. Plus, the little clothespins are more for decoration and can't hold much weight. Overall, I think this is a cute concept, but needs some improvements.

Cute But Not Made Well. I love decorating my home for Halloween. I thought this would look nice on the front door. It's cute, but not made very well. Mainly, it's the glue job that looks bad. There are large globs of dried glue around the edges that holds the lights in place. They look very messy. As someone who likes to make crafts, I would not be satisfied with something that looked like this. I'm very particular with my crafting. The picture in the description does show the glue, so I wasn't completely surprised. Rope is included and you have to attach it yourself. It does come with batteries, which is a plus. Overall, it's okay, but not outstanding.

Sums Up 2020!. This is a light weight, rubbery material ornament. It wasn't what I was expecting at all. With that being said, I think it's kind of cute and it definitely sums up 2020. There are 4 figures on mine with a little bit of space to personalize them on the hats. I haven't personalized them yet, but I plan to use a fine tip permanent marker as I have done on other ornaments and I don't foresee any problems. Each of the characters is wearing a face mask. The first zero in 2020 is a red covid symbol. The second zerio is a roll of toilet paper. Then there is also a bottle of hand sanitizer. It comes with a plain red ribbon to hang it. I do like it, but I wish it was made from a sturdier and nicer material.

Basic Toaster. This is a basic toaster, but that's not a bad thing. Some products have gotten so complicated over the years, that something as simple as making toast can be difficult. You can adjust the level of brownness and other standard & basic features that toast. It feels kind of flimsy. It's especially noticeable when pressing the lever to make the toast. There was a smell the first couple of uses, but the directions said that was normal. It's decent, just not great.

Good Size. This is a good size Christmas decoration for the wall or door. I found the paint job to be a bit messy - it's possible it was intentional, but I think it looks sloppy. I had to position the bow so it doesn't show the ties. It's okay, but it really looks like something I would see at the discount store. It's a little nicer than what I would find in the dollar store, but more like the $3 or $5 bins at Target.

Complete Set. This is a complete set of measuring cups and spoons. They are a mix of stainless steel and plastic. The stainless part feels sturdy. The plastic doesn't. It flexes easily and is not very rigid. It's easy to read the measurements. It seems to be dishwasher friendly.

Does the Job. My daughter wanted something to store her t-shirts in her closet. This does the job, but it's not a high quality item. Assembly is required. The directions were straight forward and easy to follow. The finished unit is a bit flimsy. It wil work for her t-shirts as long as she doesn't over stuff them. She does like that you can see inside without opening the drawers. Overall, it's just okay. We're not really sure how long it will last.

Under Whelmed. I wanted a nice neutral runner for the entry way. I was under whelmed by this. It's thin and too boring for the entry space. It would be fine for a more utilitarian purpose such as a laundry room or garage. The design is barely noticeable. I will keep looking.

Neat Design. We almost always have a bowl of pistachios out in the kitchen. Then next to it, we have a bowl for the shells. This is a neat design that streamlines that. This is supposed to be one unit, but mine arrived as two separate pieces. It looks like they were originally stapled together, but it didn't last during transport. The quality of the individual bowls is nice. I like the bamboo look.

Cute, But..... I love decorating for fall! This pair of lanterns is cute, but....... It was packed inside well, but it wasn't enough to survive the transport. The sides of the lantern are glass. They're not welded inside. Instead, it's like the glass in a picture frame. So when I was setting these up, both lanterns had at least one glass panel that I had to reinsert. The back panel on the smaller lantern was broken in one of the corners. There was a piece about the size of a lemon broken off. There was a large piece of glass as well as lots of small pieces all over the inside of the box. Luckily, this was the back panel, so it's not very noticeable. The decor pieces come inside a bag and you have to set it up your self. I'm not very good with that, so I did the best I could. I thought that there would be a flameless battery operated candle as shown in the pictures, but there's not. I kind of wish they had included a picture of what it "could" look like when you're done. Instead, I had to keep looking up the product description. I didn't use all of the decorations, they did provide a lot. I am happy with the way it looks. I am very concerned about storing it after the season so it doesn't break any further.

Okay. These candy pillows were just okay. They arrived compressed, but they never fully expanded. I followed the directions and put them in the dryer for a little while, but they still were misshapened. The material is soft. The construction is decent. I just found them to be underwhelming.

Arrived Broken. I was very excited to get this squirrel table. However, it arrived broken. The table top was split in half. My husband used wood glue and was able to fix it. There is an end piece that is included and requires you to attach it with screws that are included. We have it outside and have positioned a camera on it so we can see any visitors. So far, none have checked it out, but we just put it up last night.

Light Weight. This is set of 8 towels. It comes with 2 bath towels, 2 hand towels, and 2 wash cloths. The sizing is standard and they are comparable to other towel sizing. The towels are light weight and moderately fluffy. I was disappointed in the quality. They're okay, just not great. If saw these in person at the store, I probably wouldn't get them. However, if I was just starting out and these were the cheapest towels in the store, I would consider them. There were a lot of pulled threads on them which you can see in the picture. Overall, they're just okay.

Looks Nice. This is a basic twin comforter. The description says it's "ultra soft", but I don't think it feels very soft at all. It's not rough to the touch either, but it's not what I would consider soft. The planets look nice. It's more of a realistic space depiction rather than cutesy. The quality seems to be okay, but it has the over all look and feel of an inexpensive comforter.

Pieces Not Labeled. My husband is very handy and has put together all kinds of furniture pieces over the years. This one was not difficult, but it was a pain because the pieces were labeled! He had to keep holding individual pieces up and trying to match them up. The whole process took nearly an hour. The finished nightstand is decent. It's sturdy enough. It's a bit short and would be best for beds that are nearer to the ground. There are 2 drawers, but they don't use usual metal hardware that drawers use. The drawers open and close fine for now, but I do wonder how long they will hold up. A cheap screwdriver is provided, but my husband used his power tools instead. It's not a terrible nightstand, it's not a high quality one either. This would be a good fit for someone just starting out or a college student.

Rustic. This snowman wreath is rustic looking. It's basically 2 round wreaths connected together. The quality is okay, but it does seem a bit flimsy as far as their connection. There's a battery operated light included that's not attached, so you have to figure out how you would hang that on if you want to use it. Plus batteries are not included. Overall, it's fine, but it's just not my style.
Very Thin. These towels look nice, but they are very thin. They don't absorb a lot either. They remind me of tea towels. I was able to dry one pot before it became too saturated to dry another one.

Good Way to Display Pictures. My teenage daughter was really excited to hang this in her bedroom. She has one of those instant cameras and has been wanting something to hang up pictures on her wall. The concept this is cute, but the real product is just okay. It comes with straight wooden pieces that you have to assemble for the sides. The pieces have small wooden pegs that you have to fit into drilled holes. Most of them fit in pretty well, but some were a bit challenging to get in place. Then once you have the 3 wooden pieces together, you can still see where they were connected and it just doesn't look good. It would be nicer if the wooden sides were just one piece instead of three. The pictures in the product description do show the spaces between each piece. There are no instructions, so we did have to figure out which direction the wooden pieces went. It wasn't hard, but it did take some time. The pieces are painted white, but there were a few chips in the paint. The description calls it rustic white, so technically I can't argue with that. It's pretty large and takes up a good amount of wall space. There are 30 mini clothespins included. One of ours was broken, but we have others so it was easy to replace. There are some hanging holes for hanging it up, but I prefer to use adhesive strips which worked well. Overall, it's just okay. I would probably look for something similar at my local stores for that didn't require assembly.

Organic Cotton!. These little dish cloths are the size of a wash cloth. They are not full sized towels. They are fairly thin and don't have much texture to them. I prefer a little more texture in order to get stuck on food off of my dishes. The color assortment is nice and I love that they are made from organic cotton.

Didn't Help As Much As I Had Hoped. We have a sofa that sinks on one of the cushions. I had hoped that this would help. Unfortunately it didn't help as much as I had hoped. So I'm guessing our problem is the actual cushion not the foundation of the sofa where this would be more useful. This does require assembly. It's difficult to put together by yourself, so my husband and I did it together. It seems sturdy enough that it would do the job if the springs or base of your furniture was the cause of your sinking.

On the Thin Side. My nice, thick anti-fatigue mats were in desperate need of being replaced. They had gotten dinged up pretty badly over the last few years. Plus they were boring black. I saw these and thought that the grey color would look nice in my kitchen. They only look grey in natural light. When my LED kitchen lights are on, they look lavender in color. My kitchen is a green color and the lavender looking mats look awful! Plus, they are on the thin side and don't offer as much comfort and support as my old black ones. And for some reason, my cat has decided to use these as a scratching mat! She never did that with the old ones either. I am on the lookout for some new, thicker ones now.

Basic Bedding. This comforter set is basic bedding. It's nothing fancy. It's a black comforter that reverses to white. The fabric is not very soft. With that being said it's not scratchy either. It fits the bed as expected. It serves its purpose.

Light Weight. This is a cute, light weight, rustic wall piece. It has a fairly authentic chicken wire look to it. When my husband got his tools out to hang this, he wasn't sure what how to do it. It comes with the wall screws, but my unit was missing any hanging pieces attached to the shelf. I went and looked up the product description and the pictures showed two hangers and so did some of the other reviews. It seems like this one is not the norm.  So as of now, my husband hasn't decided how he's going to hang these. Overall, it's a nice unit. There's plenty of room in the basket portion. The towel rack is large enough for a bath towel. But with the missing hanging pieces, it's not an easy thing to install.

Great Cup!. See Update Below: I am trying to drink more water daily. Having pretty cups helps! I like the way this cup looks. It's very sturdy. It reminds me of the fancy Starbucks cups you can buy. The textured sides are easy to grip and hold. I am a fan!

Update: After just a few days of use, I started hearing water inside the double wall of this cup. I checked around the edges/rim and everything seemed fine. I then noticed that there was a crack on the interior wall. I have not dropped this cup and I have only hand washed it. I don't know if the crack was there when I got it or if it happened afterwards. Regardless, it's pretty annoying to have the water inside. It also doesn't sound very sanitary to me. My original rating was 5 stars, but I have changed it to 3. I probably should have given it 2 stars, but I really do like the cup.

Basic Kitchen Towels. These towels are basic, no frills kitchen towels. They remind me of the type you might buy at the grocery store. They are better than the ones you would get at the dollar store. The color is a nice, blue. They wash well and have a decent absorption quality. These are great for quick clean ups.

Fun to Read But Needs to be Proof Read!. We just hosted a small gathering for a good friend to celebrate his 50th birthday. I ordered this specifically for decoration at the event. It's a nice quality. I wasn't expected it to be a canvas print. I've ordered others like this that were just flat posters. It was definitely fun to read, but it needs to be proof read! There are a few places without proper spacing. Then in the sports section, 4 times the word "champion" is misspelled. Instead it says "champinos". The spacing problem is one thing, but spelling mistakes is really not acceptable.

Mine Didn't Have the Screen Print Image. When these first arrived, I thought that I had received buffalo plaid napkins instead of placemats. After reading the product description again, I decided that these were placemats, mine just didn't have the screen print image on them. Mine are just plain red & black buffalo plaid. They're a bit thin and fold really easily which is why I thought they were napkins. My husband didn't think they were napkins because the plaid was only on one side. They're pretty basic for a placemat, but they do look good on the table. And they do protect the table from food spills.

Pretty Print. While I do love the pretty print of this Vera Bradley storage bin, I'm not a fan of the design. It doesn't hold the round shape at all. I thought it might take some time since it was folded flat, but it's been at least a week and it's still in an awkward shape. I could see this being a useful storage item for a college student, but it's a little disappointing for this 50 something mom.

Not Very Cooling. I have been using cooling pillow cases for the last year or so. I saw these and thought it would be good to get a couple more. I use 3 pillows every night and only have 2 cooling ones. Right now I am using 2 of these and 1 of my original ones. These just don't seem to be as cool feeling as the others. My other ones are pretty cool when I first touch them. These are not. In fact, I sometimes have problems trying to figure out which side is the cooling side! None of the ones that I have used keep cool for very long.

Not What I Expected. This Christmas ornament was not at all what I was expecting. The pictures on the description led me to believe it was a 3-D chicken. Instead, it is a flat chicken. It's a color photo of a chicken (non-glossy) on wood. If you scroll through the product description, the very last thing it says in the 5th paragraph  is "Please note that this is a flat Christmas tree pendant, not three-". Obviously I didn't thoroughly read all of it or else I would have known. In all fairness, it is priced appropriately for what it is. I did have problems with the ribbon that was included. It was either stuck to the cardboard piece in the cello bag or it was caught on something because when I tried to remove it from the bag, it started fraying immediately. It was sticking to my arm and I had difficulties getting it off me. I can easily use my own ribbon or an ornament hanger, so that's not a big deal to me. My 3 star rating means this is okay. I don't love it, but I don't hate it either.

Disappointing. I found these framed dried flowers to be disappointing. Both of these had broken pieces of dried flowers sitting in the bottom of the frame. They're visible and it looks messy. I also thought the colors were too bright. The flowers in the product pictures were a bit more subdue. The pink one is really bright pink in person. I was hoping for the lighter colors because they would look better with my decor. .

Okay, but not Great. After being tired of undercooking several pans of brownies, I ordered this to help me make sure that my oven temperature was accurate. The numbers are small & hard to read, even with my reading glasses. We hang it from one of the racks and it gets easily knocked down a lot. Overall, it works, but it has some design flaws that don't make it the perfect oven thermometer for me.

Be careful!. I like the product a lot, but I don't know that I would recommend using the refill bag. Why? (1) The original purchase of DampRid comes in a small plastic bucket shaped like a small flower pot with a plastic grill on the top. If you are not careful and happen to knock over one of these little containers when the beads inside have turned to liquid, you will find that a strange, oily, toxic liquid spills all over and is not easy to clean-up. Similarly, when you empty the little container, you are told to pour the contents into the toilet. If you are not careful or should happen to dislodge the plastic grill, when you upend the little container, the inside liner will fall into the toilet. You will have to fish-out these items while being sure to flush to get that oily liquid out of the basin. (2) It is a toxic substance. Most of us with kids and pets are not fond of using toxic substances in our home unless absolutely necessary.

I do like DampRid but plan to dispose of the empty container rather than refill it due to the problems if a spill should happen or other accident.

Disappointing! Not as expected. I like OXO products, but, for the first time, I am disappointed in an OXO product. (1) If you look at the bottom of the chopper, you will see that the transparent cup fits into a black rubber seal that also serves as the base of the chopper. I have noticed that some commenters have written that this seal or gasket can be removed, but, if so, my hands are not strong enough to remove it. I can't get it off at all and previously assumed (before reading the comments) that it was permanently affixed to the transparent cup. The seal comes-up about 1/8" to form the base. I discovered that chopped bits of food were wedged down between the seal and sides of the transparent cup. These will not rinse out. If your hands are not strong enough to remove the seal (if it can be removed), you will have to figure-out a way to remove the trapped food either with a slender kitchen utensil or with your fingernail. (Sorry, I know it's gross!) I don't know whether or not I received a particularly badly made chopper or whether this is a design flaw. NOTE: See UPDATE below. (2) It takes a good amount of effort and time to chop the food. Even though the transparent cup shows that it will hold 1 cup, in reality you can only chop about 1/4 cup and then will need to empty the transparent cup. If you don't, the chopping blade does not have enough vertical space to operate well. It will take a fair amount of force to chop manually, so this gift is not ideal for a senior or anyone with limited mobility.

Like all OXO products, it is well made and seems sturdy. The blade did a good job of chopping the vegetables. As one commenter noted, however, you will have to chop the vegetables into small chunks to fit them inside the small transparent cup.

I plan to use the chopper (if I don't toss it) for celery, shallots, and similar kinds of items.

I have never owned a chopper before and so can't comment about this chopper in comparison to similar products. I do like the OXO brand, however, and was surprised to discover that this item has been disappointing.

UPDATE: Since writing the comment above, I discovered that the base with black rubber seal is easy to remove if I run it under very hot water and then punch the base lightly to push it out of the transparent cup. « Show Less
